column3: Polite for any woman about your mother's age, even a stranger: 阿姨，请问…. Children use it for their parents' women friends, and a hired cleaner or nanny is called 阿姨 too. A 阿 in front of a name or kinship term shows familiarity.
column4: 阿姨，请问洗手间在哪儿？
column5: 阿姨，請問洗手間在哪兒？
column6: Āyí, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr?
column7: Excuse me, auntie, where is the restroom?
column9: Polite for any woman about your mother's age, even a stranger: 阿姨，請問…. Children use it for their parents' women friends, and a hired cleaner or nanny is called 阿姨 too. A 阿 in front of a name or kinship term shows familiarity.

column3: Children greet any man about their father's age this way, and 叔叔好 is the standard greeting. Adults say it too when pointing a man out to a child. Only the father's side: a mother's brother is 舅舅. The mainland says shūshu; in Taiwan the reading of 叔 is shú, so shúshu.
column6: Háizimen jiào tā shūshu.
column7: The children call him uncle.
column9: Children greet any man about their father's age this way, and 叔叔好 is the standard greeting. Adults say it too when pointing a man out to a child. Only the father's side: a mother's brother is 舅舅. The mainland says shūshu; in Taiwan the reading of 叔 is shú, so shúshu.

column3: A respectful address to a man a little older than you, such as a stranger or a shop worker: 大哥，谢谢你. In a family the numbering goes on: 二哥, 三哥.
column6: Dàgē, xièxie nǐ bāngmáng.
column7: Brother, thanks for your help.
column9: A respectful address to a man a little older than you, such as a stranger or a shop worker: 大哥，謝謝你. In a family the numbering goes on: 二哥, 三哥.

column3: A friendly address to a woman a bit older than you, such as a shop owner or a neighbor: warmer and less formal than 女士. In a family the numbering goes on: 二姐, 三姐.
column6: Dàjiě, zhège duōshao qián?
column7: Ma'am, how much is this?
column9: A friendly address to a woman a bit older than you, such as a shop owner or a neighbor: warmer and less formal than 女士. In a family the numbering goes on: 二姐, 三姐.

column3: On the mainland, mostly in the north, a respectful address to a woman of your mother's age or older, common with neighbors and market sellers: 大妈，早上好. It sounds older than 阿姨. Taiwan says 阿姨 or 阿桑.
column6: Dàmā zài gōngyuán lǐ tiàowǔ.
column7: An older woman is dancing in the park.
column9: On the mainland, mostly in the north, a respectful address to a woman of your mother's age or older, common with neighbors and market sellers: 大媽，早上好. It sounds older than 阿姨. Taiwan says 阿姨 or 阿桑.

column3: On the mainland, mostly in the north, a respectful address to an elderly man, a stranger or a neighbor: 大爷，您慢走. Taiwan says 阿伯 or 伯伯. Its female counterpart is 大妈.
column6: Dàye zuò zài shù xià xià qí.
column7: An old man is sitting under a tree playing chess.
column9: On the mainland, mostly in the north, a respectful address to an elderly man, a stranger or a neighbor: 大爺，您慢走. Taiwan says 阿伯 or 伯伯. Its female counterpart is 大媽.

column3: The spoken, affectionate word a wife uses for her own husband: 我老公. In formal or written language use 丈夫. Its pair is 老婆.
column6: Wǒ lǎogong jīntiān jiābān.
column7: My husband is working overtime today.
column9: The spoken, affectionate word a wife uses for her own husband: 我老公. In formal or written language use 丈夫. Its pair is 老婆.

column3: The spoken, affectionate word a husband uses for his own wife: 我老婆. In writing and formal speech use 妻子; in polite talk about someone else's wife it is not used. Its pair is 老公. As a bound form, 婆 means grandmother or mother-in-law.
column6: Wǒ lǎopo zuòfàn hěn hǎochī.
column7: My wife's cooking is delicious.
column9: The spoken, affectionate word a husband uses for his own wife: 我老婆. In writing and formal speech use 妻子; in polite talk about someone else's wife it is not used. Its pair is 老公. As a bound form, 婆 means grandmother or mother-in-law.

column3: The neutral standard word, fine in speech and writing: 他的妻子. Its pair is 丈夫. Husbands often say 老婆 instead (wives say 老公).
column6: Tā de qīzi shì yī wèi yīshēng.
column7: His wife is a doctor.
column9: The neutral standard word, fine in speech and writing: 他的妻子. Its pair is 丈夫. Husbands often say 老婆 instead (wives say 老公).

column3: The neutral standard word, fine in speech and writing: 她的丈夫. Its pair is 妻子; the casual spoken word is 老公.
column6: Tā de zhàngfu zài yínháng gōngzuò.
column7: Her husband works at a bank.
column9: The neutral standard word, fine in speech and writing: 她的丈夫. Its pair is 妻子; the casual spoken word is 老公.

column3: The everyday word for a couple, also of yourselves: 我们是夫妻. Count them with 对: 一对夫妻. The set phrase 老夫老妻 is an old married couple.
column4: 他们是一对幸福的夫妻。
column5: 他們是一對幸福的夫妻。
column6: Tāmen shì yī duì xìngfú de fūqī.
column7: They are a happy married couple.
column9: The everyday word for a couple, also of yourselves: 我們是夫妻. Count them with 對: 一對夫妻. The set phrase 老夫老妻 is an old married couple.

column3: More formal and written than 夫妻, and used of other people's couples: 年轻夫妇, 这对夫妇. Counted with 对 too; it sounds stiff about yourselves.
column6: Zhè duì fūfù yǒu liǎng ge háizi.
column7: This couple has two children.
column9: More formal and written than 夫妻, and used of other people's couples: 年輕夫婦, 這對夫婦. Counted with 對 too; it sounds stiff about yourselves.

column3: A respectful word for someone else's wife, usually a person of standing: 总统夫人, 第一夫人, 李夫人. It is formal and mostly used of others, though a man may introduce his wife as 我夫人 in polite company.
column6: Zǒngtǒng fūren cānjiā le huìyì.
column7: The president's wife attended the meeting.
column9: A respectful word for someone else's wife, usually a person of standing: 總統夫人, 第一夫人, 李夫人. It is formal and mostly used of others, though a man may introduce his wife as 我夫人 in polite company.

column3: Only your son's son. A daughter's son is a different word, 外孙, and the granddaughter on the son's side is 孙女.
column6: Yéye dài sūnzi qù gōngyuán.
column7: Grandpa takes his grandson to the park.
column9: Only your son's son. A daughter's son is a different word, 外孫, and the granddaughter on the son's side is 孫女.

column6: Nǎinai zuì ài tā de sūnnǚ.
column7: Grandma loves her granddaughter most.

column3: Sisters as a group, older first; women also call close female friends 姐妹: 我的好姐妹, 姐妹们. For one sister you say 姐姐 or 妹妹, not 姐妹.
column6: Tāmen jiěmèi liǎ zhǎng de hěn xiàng.
column7: The two sisters look very much alike.
column9: Sisters as a group, older first; women also call close female friends 姐妹: 我的好姐妹, 姐妹們. For one sister you say 姐姐 or 妹妹, not 姐妹.

column3: Brothers of any age together: 兄弟三个. Men also use it as a friendly address to a buddy: 兄弟，来喝一杯. With 姐妹 it makes 兄弟姐妹, siblings. 弟 began as a picture of a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap; the wrapping meant order, which extended to a younger brother.
column4: 他们兄弟三个都喜欢踢足球。
column5: 他們兄弟三個都喜歡踢足球。
column6: Tāmen xiōngdì sān ge dōu xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
column7: The three brothers all like playing soccer.
column9: Brothers of any age together: 兄弟三個. Men also use it as a friendly address to a buddy: 兄弟，來喝一杯. With 姐妹 it makes 兄弟姐妹, siblings. 弟 began as a picture of a spear handle wrapped in a leather strap; the wrapping meant order, which extended to a younger brother.

column3: Doubling makes it fond and childlike: parents call a child of any age 宝宝, as in 宝宝乖, and partners use it too. 小宝宝 is a little baby.
column6: Bǎobao jīntiān yī suì le.
column7: The baby is one year old today.
column9: Doubling makes it fond and childlike: parents call a child of any age 寶寶, as in 寶寶乖, and partners use it too. 小寶寶 is a little baby.

column3: A fond name for a child or a partner: 宝贝，该睡觉了. It also names a cherished object: 这是我的宝贝. On mainland shopping sites, a product listing is also called 宝贝.
column6: Bǎobèi, gāi shuìjiào le.
column7: Darling, it's time to sleep.
column9: A fond name for a child or a partner: 寶貝，該睡覺了. It also names a cherished object: 這是我的寶貝. On mainland shopping sites, a product listing is also called 寶貝.

column3: The place your family comes from, such as your parents' village or city, which may not be where you live now. 回老家 is what many do at Spring Festival. It sounds more spoken and personal than 家乡.
column6: Guònián wǒ yào huí lǎojiā.
column7: I'm going back to my hometown for New Year.
column9: The place your family comes from, such as your parents' village or city, which may not be where you live now. 回老家 is what many do at Spring Festival. It sounds more spoken and personal than 家鄉.

column3: Only the groom at his wedding, paired with 新娘; together they are the 新人, the newlyweds. At the ceremony 新郎 and 新娘 are the titles of the day.
column6: Xīnláng jīntiān hěn jǐnzhāng.
column7: The groom is very nervous today.
column9: Only the groom at his wedding, paired with 新娘; together they are the 新人, the newlyweds. At the ceremony 新郎 and 新娘 are the titles of the day.

column3: The bride at her wedding, paired with 新郎. The warmer, more spoken form is 新娘子, and the two of them together are the 新人.
column6: Xīnniáng chuānzhe báisè de hūnshā.
column7: The bride is wearing a white wedding dress.
column9: The bride at her wedding, paired with 新郎. The warmer, more spoken form is 新娘子, and the two of them together are the 新人.

column3: The ceremony itself: 参加婚礼 "attend a wedding", 举行婚礼 "hold a wedding". Getting married, the act, is 结婚: 他们下个月结婚.
column4: 下个月我要参加朋友的婚礼。
column5: 下個月我要參加朋友的婚禮。
column6: Xià ge yuè wǒ yào cānjiā péngyou de hūnlǐ.
column7: Next month I'm going to a friend's wedding.
column9: The ceremony itself: 參加婚禮 "attend a wedding", 舉行婚禮 "hold a wedding". Getting married, the act, is 結婚: 他們下個月結婚.

column3: A formal or official word for children as a group, seen on signs and tickets: 儿童节, 儿童医院, 儿童票. In ordinary speech people say 孩子.
column4: 这个公园里有很多儿童。
column5: 這個公園裡有很多兒童。
column6: Zhège gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō értóng.
column7: There are many children in this park.
column9: A formal or official word for children as a group, seen on signs and tickets: 兒童節, 兒童醫院, 兒童票. In ordinary speech people say 孩子.

column3: Seen on tickets and in courses: 成人票, 成人教育. More formal than 大人, which parents and children say. As a verb phrase, 长大成人 is "to grow up". It also labels adult-only material.
column4: 他已经是成人了，可以自己决定。
column5: 他已經是成人了，可以自己決定。
column6: Tā yǐjīng shì chéngrén le, kěyǐ zìjǐ juédìng.
column7: He's an adult now and can decide for himself.
column9: Seen on tickets and in courses: 成人票, 成人教育. More formal than 大人, which parents and children say. As a verb phrase, 長大成人 is "to grow up". It also labels adult-only material.

column3: A polite word on signs and in service talk: 男士 for a men's department, 这位男士 "this gentleman". Its pair is 女士. Directly addressing a man, 先生 is the usual word.
column4: 请问这位男士需要什么？
column5: 請問這位男士需要什麼？
column6: Qǐngwèn zhè wèi nánshì xūyào shénme?
column7: Excuse me, what does this gentleman need?
column9: A polite word on signs and in service talk: 男士 for a men's department, 這位男士 "this gentleman". Its pair is 女士. Directly addressing a man, 先生 is the usual word.

column3: A polite word for a woman of any age you do not know: 这位女士. In speeches it pairs with 先生: 女士们，先生们. On signs and in shops it marks women's goods and rooms. Its pair is 男士.
column4: 这位女士是我们的经理。
column5: 這位女士是我們的經理。
column6: Zhè wèi nǚshì shì wǒmen de jīnglǐ.
column7: This lady is our manager.
column9: A polite word for a woman of any age you do not know: 這位女士. In speeches it pairs with 先生: 女士們，先生們. On signs and in shops it marks women's goods and rooms. Its pair is 男士.

column3: Always in this order, never reversed: 男女老少 "men, women, old and young", 男女平等 "equality of the sexes". It names both groups at once and often takes 都: 男女都可以.
column6: Nánnǚ dōu kěyǐ cānjiā bǐsài.
column7: Both men and women can enter the competition.
column9: Always in this order, never reversed: 男女老少 "men, women, old and young", 男女平等 "equality of the sexes". It names both groups at once and often takes 都: 男女都可以.

column3: Also a friendly or flattering address to a young woman, especially from shop and market staff: 美女，要不要看看？ Among friends it is a compliment; from a stranger it can sound pushy. Its pair is 帅哥.
column6: Měinǚ, nǐ yào mǎi shénme?
column7: Miss, what would you like to buy?
column9: Also a friendly or flattering address to a young woman, especially from shop and market staff: 美女，要不要看看？ Among friends it is a compliment; from a stranger it can sound pushy. Its pair is 帥哥.

column3: Said of men, usually with 很: 他很帅. A woman is 漂亮 or 美. It also means "cool" of anything stylish, such as a clean move: 这个动作很帅.
column6: Tā yòu gāo yòu shuài.
column7: He is tall and handsome.
column9: Said of men, usually with 很: 他很帥. A woman is 漂亮 or 美. It also means "cool" of anything stylish, such as a clean move: 這個動作很帥.

column3: A flattering address from shop staff or strangers to a young man, and a teasing compliment among friends. Its pair is 美女, and 哥 works as in 大哥.
column6: Shuàigē, yào bù yào jìnlái kànkan?
column7: Hey there, would you like to come in and have a look?
column9: A flattering address from shop staff or strangers to a young man, and a teasing compliment among friends. Its pair is 美女, and 哥 works as in 大哥.

column3: Spoken, and said warmly by someone older, of a man from his teens to about thirty: 这个小伙子. The same 伙 is in 伙伴.
column6: Zhège xiǎohuǒzi hěn yǒu lǐmào.
column7: This young man is very polite.
column9: Spoken, and said warmly by someone older, of a man from his teens to about thirty: 這個小夥子. The same 夥 is in 夥伴.

column3: Calling someone 胖子 to their face is rude; it is for a third person or friends joking. To describe, use the adjective: 他很胖. The same 子 makes 瘦子 for a thin person.
column4: 他以前是个胖子，现在很瘦。
column5: 他以前是個胖子，現在很瘦。
column6: Tā yǐqián shì ge pàngzi, xiànzài hěn shòu.
column7: He used to be fat, but now he is thin.
column9: Calling someone 胖子 to their face is rude; it is for a third person or friends joking. To describe, use the adjective: 他很胖. The same 子 makes 瘦子 for a thin person.

column3: It usually goes with 度过 or 回忆: 美好的童年, 童年的回忆. In speech, 小时候 "when I was little" is more common.
column4: 我的童年是在农村度过的。
column5: 我的童年是在農村度過的。
column6: Wǒ de tóngnián shì zài nóngcūn dùguò de.
column7: I spent my childhood in the countryside.
column9: It usually goes with 度過 or 回憶: 美好的童年, 童年的回憶. In speech, 小時候 "when I was little" is more common.

column3: For children of about three to six. A school level takes 上: 上幼儿园, then 上小学 and 上中学.
column6: Wǒ nǚ'ér zài shàng yòu'éryuán.
column7: My daughter goes to kindergarten.
column9: For children of about three to six. A school level takes 上: 上幼兒園, then 上小學 and 上中學.

column3: A warm, nostalgic word for the energetic years of youth, common in film and song titles: 青春的回忆. 青春期 is adolescence. For a young person, say 年轻. 春 itself can mean "youthful".
column4: 这是一部关于青春的电影。
column5: 這是一部關於青春的電影。
column6: Zhè shì yī bù guānyú qīngchūn de diànyǐng.
column7: This is a movie about youth.
column9: A warm, nostalgic word for the energetic years of youth, common in film and song titles: 青春的回憶. 青春期 is adolescence. For a young person, say 年輕. 春 itself can mean "youthful".

column3: A little more written than 好朋友: 我的好友, 多年的好友. On social apps 加好友 is "add a friend", and 好友 is the friends list.
column6: Wǒmen shì duōnián de hǎoyǒu.
column7: We have been close friends for many years.
column9: A little more written than 好朋友: 我的好友, 多年的好友. On social apps 加好友 is "add a friend", and 好友 is the friends list.

column3: Someone you do something with: 学习伙伴, 合作伙伴 "business partner". Also warm for a pet or tool that helps you: 好伙伴. Not for a romantic partner.
column6: Xiǎogǒu shì háizi de hǎo huǒbàn.
column7: The puppy is the child's good companion.
column9: Someone you do something with: 學習夥伴, 合作夥伴 "business partner". Also warm for a pet or tool that helps you: 好夥伴. Not for a romantic partner.

column3: Anyone the public knows, not only performers (those are 明星): writers, athletes and scientists too. It also appears in 名人名言 "famous sayings".
column6: Zhè wèi míngrén chángcháng shàng diànshì.
column7: This famous person is often on television.
column9: Anyone the public knows, not only performers (those are 明星): writers, athletes and scientists too. It also appears in 名人名言 "famous sayings".

column3: The poor as a group: 帮助穷人. Its opposite is 富人. For one person use the adjective: 他很穷.
column6: Tā bāngzhù guo hěn duō qióngrén.
column7: He has helped many poor people.
column9: The poor as a group: 幫助窮人. Its opposite is 富人. For one person use the adjective: 他很窮.

column3: A formal, written word, common in notices and news: 小区居民, 城市居民. 民 names a group of people in other words too: 市民, 村民, 网民.
column6: Xiǎoqū de jūmín dōu hěn yǒuhǎo.
column7: The residents of the neighborhood are all friendly.
column9: A formal, written word, common in notices and news: 小區居民, 城市居民. 民 names a group of people in other words too: 市民, 村民, 網民.

column3: Spoken, with three uses: "other people" in general (别学人家); "he, she, they" of someone you both know (人家已经走了); and a coy "I" (人家不想去嘛), cute and mostly said by women.
column6: Bié chǎo le, rénjia zài shuìjiào.
column7: Stop making noise, they are sleeping.
column9: Spoken, with three uses: "other people" in general (別學人家); "he, she, they" of someone you both know (人家已經走了); and a coy "I" (人家不想去嘛), cute and mostly said by women.

column3: It ends the names of many fruits and vegetables: 西瓜, 黄瓜, 南瓜, 冬瓜. On the internet, 吃瓜 "eat melon" means watching the gossip unfold.
column6: Zhège guā yòu dà yòu tián.
column7: This melon is big and sweet.
column9: It ends the names of many fruits and vegetables: 西瓜, 黃瓜, 南瓜, 冬瓜. On the internet, 吃瓜 "eat melon" means watching the gossip unfold.

column3: A whole one counts with 个 and a slice with 块: 一块西瓜. It is the classic summer fruit, and 瓜 ends many names: 黄瓜, 南瓜.
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ zuì ài chī xīguā.
column7: In summer I love eating watermelon most.
column9: A whole one counts with 個 and a slice with 塊: 一塊西瓜. It is the classic summer fruit, and 瓜 ends many names: 黃瓜, 南瓜.

column3: It counts with 根 for its long shape: 一根黄瓜. Eaten raw, as in 拍黄瓜, a cold smashed cucumber salad. In Taiwan the everyday cucumber is usually 小黄瓜.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī gēn huángguā.
column7: I want to buy a cucumber.
column9: It counts with 根 for its long shape: 一根黃瓜. Eaten raw, as in 拍黃瓜, a cold smashed cucumber salad. In Taiwan the everyday cucumber is usually 小黃瓜.

column3: It counts with 块: 一块豆腐. Kinds include 臭豆腐 "stinky tofu" and 麻婆豆腐. The idiom 吃豆腐 "eat tofu" means to flirt with or grope someone, so be careful with it.
column6: Dòufu shì yòng dòuzi zuò de.
column7: Tofu is made from soybeans.
column9: It counts with 塊: 一塊豆腐. Kinds include 臭豆腐 "stinky tofu" and 麻婆豆腐. The idiom 吃豆腐 "eat tofu" means to flirt with or grope someone, so be careful with it.

column3: Eaten boiled on the cob (煮玉米), as soup (玉米汤) or as porridge (玉米粥). Popcorn is 爆米花 and corn oil is 玉米油. 米 is any small grain: 小米 is millet.
column6: Xiàtiān de yùmǐ hěn tián.
column7: Summer corn is very sweet.
column9: Eaten boiled on the cob (煮玉米), as soup (玉米湯) or as porridge (玉米粥). Popcorn is 爆米花 and corn oil is 玉米油. 米 is any small grain: 小米 is millet.

column3: Fish and shellfish as food in general: 吃海鲜, 海鲜过敏 "a seafood allergy". 鲜 alone is "fresh", as in 新鲜.
column6: Wǒ duì hǎixiān guòmǐn.
column7: I am allergic to seafood.
column9: Fish and shellfish as food in general: 吃海鮮, 海鮮過敏 "a seafood allergy". 鮮 alone is "fresh", as in 新鮮.

column3: Usually used without a count (吃零食, 很多零食), or counted by the bag: 一包零食, 一袋零食. 零 means odd bits and small amounts, as in 零钱 "small change" and 零件 "a part".
column6: Háizimen dōu ài chī língshí.
column7: The children all love eating snacks.
column9: Usually used without a count (吃零食, 很多零食), or counted by the bag: 一包零食, 一袋零食. 零 means odd bits and small amounts, as in 零錢 "small change" and 零件 "a part".

column3: Staples like rice and wheat, a word of farming and national concern: 粮食生产, 浪费粮食. For food in general, say 食物; a meal is 饭.
column6: Nóngmín zhòng le hěn duō liángshi.
column7: The farmers grew a lot of grain.
column9: Staples like rice and wheat, a word of farming and national concern: 糧食生產, 浪費糧食. For food in general, say 食物; a meal is 飯.

column3: The botanical fruit of a plant, and in a figure the result of effort: 劳动果实, 胜利的果实. For fruit you eat, the everyday word is 水果.
column6: Zhè shì wǒmen nǔlì de guǒshí.
column7: This is the fruit of our hard work.
column9: The botanical fruit of a plant, and in a figure the result of effort: 勞動果實, 勝利的果實. For fruit you eat, the everyday word is 水果.

column3: Salt is counted by the spoon or a bit, not by pieces: 一勺盐, 一点盐. Kinds are named in front: 食盐, 海盐. The taste is 咸.
column6: Tāng lǐ zài fàng diǎnr yán.
column7: Add a little more salt to the soup.
column9: Salt is counted by the spoon or a bit, not by pieces: 一勺鹽, 一點鹽. Kinds are named in front: 食鹽, 海鹽. The taste is 鹹.

column3: You order it with 点: 点套餐, 午餐套餐. Any bundle of services sold at one price is also a 套餐: 手机套餐, 流量套餐. The 套 is the one in 一套衣服, a set.
column6: Wǒ yào yī ge tàocān.
column7: I'd like a set meal.
column9: You order it with 點: 點套餐, 午餐套餐. Any bundle of services sold at one price is also a 套餐: 手機套餐, 流量套餐. The 套 is the one in 一套衣服, a set.

column3: The cafeteria of a school, company or factory, plainer and cheaper than a restaurant (饭馆): 学校食堂, 在食堂吃饭.
column4: 中午我们在学校食堂吃饭。
column5: 中午我們在學校食堂吃飯。
column6: Zhōngwǔ wǒmen zài xuéxiào shítáng chīfàn.
column7: At noon we eat at the school cafeteria.
column9: The cafeteria of a school, company or factory, plainer and cheaper than a restaurant (飯館): 學校食堂, 在食堂吃飯.

column3: Food is 在冰箱里, or goes in with 放进冰箱. The 箱 is the same box as in 行李箱 and 邮箱. 冰 was first written as just 冫, and 水 was added later.
column6: Niúnǎi zài bīngxiāng lǐ.
column7: The milk is in the fridge.
column9: Food is 在冰箱裡, or goes in with 放進冰箱. The 箱 is the same box as in 行李箱 and 郵箱. 冰 was first written as just 冫, and 水 was added later.

column3: The everyday word for a flat dish to serve or eat from; something deeper is a 碗. Count it with 个: 一个盘子. Washing up is usually 洗碗.
column6: Qǐng bǎ pánzi fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
column7: Please put the plate on the table.
column9: The everyday word for a flat dish to serve or eat from; something deeper is a 碗. Count it with 個: 一個盤子. Washing up is usually 洗碗.

column3: Eaten with a spoon or drunk, counted with 杯 or 盒: 一杯酸奶. Flavors go in front: 草莓酸奶. In Taiwan the spoonable kind is 优格 and the drinkable kind 优酪乳.
column6: Wǒ zǎofàn hē le yī bēi suānnǎi.
column7: I had a glass of yogurt for breakfast.
column9: Eaten with a spoon or drunk, counted with 杯 or 盒: 一杯酸奶. Flavors go in front: 草莓酸奶. In Taiwan the spoonable kind is 優格 and the drinkable kind 優酪乳.

column3: Any fizzy soft drink, such as cola; the label or formal name is 碳酸饮料. 汽 is also explained as water and air together.
column6: Háizi xiǎng hē qìshuǐ.
column7: The child wants to drink soda.
column9: Any fizzy soft drink, such as cola; the label or formal name is 碳酸飲料. 汽 is also explained as water and air together.

column3: The default bottled water, counted with 瓶: 买一瓶矿泉水. The filtered kind sold beside it is 纯净水. 泉 shows water flowing from the source of a spring.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī píng kuàngquánshuǐ.
column7: Please give me a bottle of mineral water.
column9: The default bottled water, counted with 瓶: 買一瓶礦泉水. The filtered kind sold beside it is 純淨水. 泉 shows water flowing from the source of a spring.

column3: Filtered bottled water, sold beside 矿泉水; for water from the tap, 自来水. This is the mainland label; Taiwan bottles say 纯水 or 包装饮用水.
column4: 这瓶是纯净水，不是矿泉水。
column5: 這瓶是純淨水，不是礦泉水。
column6: Zhè píng shì chúnjìngshuǐ, bù shì kuàngquánshuǐ.
column7: This bottle is purified water, not mineral water.
column9: Filtered bottled water, sold beside 礦泉水; for water from the tap, 自來水. This is the mainland label; Taiwan bottles say 純水 or 包裝飲用水.

column3: On the mainland, boiled drinking water, often asked for as 一杯开水 and preferred by many to cold water; to boil it is 烧开水. In Taiwan 开水 is simply drinking water and may be cold or warm (冰开水, 温开水).
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi kāishuǐ.
column7: Please give me a glass of hot water.
column9: On the mainland, boiled drinking water, often asked for as 一杯開水 and preferred by many to cold water; to boil it is 燒開水. In Taiwan 開水 is simply drinking water and may be cold or warm (冰開水, 溫開水).

column3: The dry leaves you buy and brew: 一盒茶叶, 买茶叶. The drink itself is 茶. Kinds are named in front: 绿茶, 红茶.
column4: 这种茶叶是从云南来的。
column5: 這種茶葉是從雲南來的。
column6: Zhè zhǒng cháyè shì cóng Yúnnán lái de.
column7: This tea comes from Yunnan.
column9: The dry leaves you buy and brew: 一盒茶葉, 買茶葉. The drink itself is 茶. Kinds are named in front: 綠茶, 紅茶.

column3: Its 吧 is a sound borrowed from English "bar", not the suggestion particle. The same 吧 is in 网吧, the mainland word for an internet café; Taiwan says 网咖.
column4: 周末我们去酒吧听音乐。
column5: 週末我們去酒吧聽音樂。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù jiǔbā tīng yīnyuè.
column7: On weekends we go to a bar to listen to music.
column9: Its 吧 is a sound borrowed from English "bar", not the suggestion particle. The same 吧 is in 網吧, the mainland word for an internet café; Taiwan says 網咖.

column3: A straw is counted with 根: 一根吸管. The 管 is a tube or pipe, as in 水管, 血管 and 管子.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī gēn xīguǎn.
column7: Please give me a straw.
column9: A straw is counted with 根: 一根吸管. The 管 is a tube or pipe, as in 水管, 血管 and 管子.

column3: Breathe in or soak up. It is the verb in 吸气, 吸水, 吸烟, and in 吸引, which pulls attention or people toward something.
column6: Tā shēnshēn de xī le yī kǒu qì.
column7: He took a deep breath.
column9: Breathe in or soak up. It is the verb in 吸氣, 吸水, 吸煙, and in 吸引, which pulls attention or people toward something.

column3: Hot from chili, not from temperature: 辣椒, 不辣. When ordering you ask for 微辣 or 特辣. For hot weather or food that is hot to the touch, use 热 or 烫.
column4: 这个菜太辣了，我不能吃。
column5: 這個菜太辣了，我不能吃。
column6: Zhège cài tài là le, wǒ bù néng chī.
column7: This dish is too spicy, I can't eat it.
column9: Hot from chili, not from temperature: 辣椒, 不辣. When ordering you ask for 微辣 or 特辣. For hot weather or food that is hot to the touch, use 熱 or 燙.

column3: A second everyday sense is sore, aching from effort: 爬山后腿很酸. The taste meaning is in 酸奶 and 酸辣汤.
column6: Zhège píngguǒ tài suān le.
column7: This apple is too sour.
column9: A second everyday sense is sore, aching from effort: 爬山後腿很酸. The taste meaning is in 酸奶 and 酸辣湯.

column3: The usual complaint about food: 太咸了. 盐 is the thing and 咸 the taste. The opposite is 淡. Pickled vegetables are 咸菜.
column6: Tāng tài xián le.
column7: The soup is too salty.
column9: The usual complaint about food: 太鹹了. 鹽 is the thing and 鹹 the taste. The opposite is 淡. Pickled vegetables are 鹹菜.

column3: Beyond taste it means hard or painful: 吃苦 is to endure hardship, and 辛苦 is both "tiring" and what you say to thank someone for their work. 苦瓜 is bitter melon.
column6: Zhège yào hěn kǔ.
column7: This medicine is very bitter.
column9: Beyond taste it means hard or painful: 吃苦 is to endure hardship, and 辛苦 is both "tiring" and what you say to thank someone for their work. 苦瓜 is bitter melon.

column3: Weak in strength: 汤很淡 (the opposite of 咸), 淡茶, 淡蓝色 for pale colors, and 冷淡 for cool, indifferent feelings. 淡季 is the off season.
column6: Zhè wǎn tāng yǒudiǎnr dàn.
column7: This bowl of soup is a bit bland.
column9: Weak in strength: 湯很淡 (the opposite of 鹹), 淡茶, 淡藍色 for pale colors, and 冷淡 for cool, indifferent feelings. 淡季 is the off season.

column3: How much is packed in: 浓茶, 浓咖啡, 浓烟, and 感情很浓 for strong feeling. The opposite is 淡, as in 浓茶 against 淡茶 or 浓妆 against 淡妆.
column6: Zhè bēi kāfēi tài nóng le.
column7: This cup of coffee is too strong.
column9: How much is packed in: 濃茶, 濃咖啡, 濃煙, and 感情很濃 for strong feeling. The opposite is 淡, as in 濃茶 against 淡茶 or 濃妝 against 淡妝.

column3: Alone it praises the taste of fish, shellfish or soup: 汤很鲜. Mostly met in words: 新鲜, 海鲜 (seafood), 鲜花 (fresh flowers), 鲜红 (bright red).
column6: Zhè tiáo yú hěn xiān.
column7: This fish is very tasty.
column9: Alone it praises the taste of fish, shellfish or soup: 湯很鮮. Mostly met in words: 新鮮, 海鮮 (seafood), 鮮花 (fresh flowers), 鮮紅 (bright red).

column3: Fresh food, flowers and air: 新鲜蔬菜, 新鲜空气. It also means new and interesting, as in 新鲜事. A thing newly made is just 新, not 新鲜.
column6: Zhèlǐ de kōngqì hěn xīnxiān.
column7: The air here is fresh.
column9: Fresh food, flowers and air: 新鮮蔬菜, 新鮮空氣. It also means new and interesting, as in 新鮮事. A thing newly made is just 新, not 新鮮.

column3: The erhua form of 味道, used in northern speech, above all for smells: 烟味儿, 酒味儿, 香味儿. Taiwan and the south say 味道, which is also the written word.
column6: Zhège cài de wèir bùcuò.
column7: This dish tastes quite good.
column9: The erhua form of 味道, used in northern speech, above all for smells: 煙味兒, 酒味兒, 香味兒. Taiwan and the south say 味道, which is also the written word.

column3: The usual word for the window itself: 开窗户, 关窗户. For a service counter or a window on a screen, say 窗口.
column6: Qǐng bǎ chuānghu dǎkāi.
column7: Please open the window.
column9: The usual word for the window itself: 開窗戶, 關窗戶. For a service counter or a window on a screen, say 窗口.

column3: 台 is a raised flat place, as in 阳台, 台阶 and 讲台; here it is the ledge where flowerpots sit.
column6: Huā fàng zài chuāngtái shàng.
column7: The flowers are on the windowsill.
column9: 臺 is a raised flat place, as in 陽臺, 臺階 and 講臺; here it is the ledge where flowerpots sit.

column3: The same as 窗户, a spoken form, but 窗户 is at least as common. A service counter or a window on a screen is 窗口, not 窗子.
column6: Tā zhàn zài chuāngzi pángbiān.
column7: He is standing beside the window.
column9: The same as 窗戶, a spoken form, but 窗戶 is at least as common. A service counter or a window on a screen is 窗口, not 窗子.

column3: The balcony off an apartment, where laundry is hung up to dry (阳台上晒衣服) and plants are kept. Often glassed in and used for storage.
column6: Wǒmen zài yángtái shàng hē chá.
column7: We are drinking tea on the balcony.
column9: The balcony off an apartment, where laundry is hung up to dry (陽臺上曬衣服) and plants are kept. Often glassed in and used for storage.

column3: Stairs inside a building: 上楼梯, 下楼梯, 楼梯口. 走楼梯 means taking the stairs instead of the elevator. 梯 is explained as a wooden ladder.
column6: Xiǎoxīn lóutī, bié shuāidǎo.
column7: Watch the stairs, don't fall.
column9: Stairs inside a building: 上樓梯, 下樓梯, 樓梯口. 走樓梯 means taking the stairs instead of the elevator. 梯 is explained as a wooden ladder.

column3: Steps outside or at an entrance: 门前的台阶. Stairs inside a building are 楼梯. Figuratively, 给他一个台阶下 gives someone a way out of an embarrassing spot.
column6: Ménkǒu yǒu jǐ ge táijiē.
column7: There are a few steps at the door.
column9: Steps outside or at an entrance: 門前的臺階. Stairs inside a building are 樓梯. Figuratively, 給他一個臺階下 gives someone a way out of an embarrassing spot.

column3: You ride it with 坐 or 乘, or wait for it with 等电梯. An escalator is 自动扶梯, or 扶梯 for short, on the mainland and 手扶梯 in Taiwan. The 梯 is the one in 楼梯.
column6: Wǒmen zuò diàntī shàngqù ba.
column7: Let's take the elevator up.
column9: You ride it with 坐 or 乘, or wait for it with 等電梯. An escalator is 自動扶梯, or 扶梯 for short, on the mainland and 手扶梯 in Taiwan. The 梯 is the one in 樓梯.

column3: A large building, counted with 座: 一座大楼. It is named by use: 办公大楼, 教学大楼. In a building, 一楼 is the ground floor.
column6: Nà zuò dàlóu yǒu sānshí céng.
column7: That building has thirty floors.
column9: A large building, counted with 座: 一座大樓. It is named by use: 辦公大樓, 教學大樓. In a building, 一樓 is the ground floor.

column3: Going up the stairs or to a higher floor; 去 or 来 gives the direction: 上楼去, 上楼来. For climbing a hill, say 爬山. 上 is a short line above a long one.
column6: Tā mànmàn de shànglóu.
column7: He is going upstairs slowly.
column9: Going up the stairs or to a higher floor; 去 or 來 gives the direction: 上樓去, 上樓來. For climbing a hill, say 爬山. 上 is a short line above a long one.

column3: In an apartment block it is also the usual way to say you are going out for a moment: 下楼买东西, 下楼吃饭. 楼下 is "downstairs" as a place. 下 is a short line below a long one.
column6: Wǒ xiàlóu mǎi diǎn dōngxi.
column7: I'm going downstairs to buy something.
column9: In an apartment block it is also the usual way to say you are going out for a moment: 下樓買東西, 下樓吃飯. 樓下 is "downstairs" as a place. 下 is a short line below a long one.

column3: Light you see, from lamps, a stage or a window: 灯光很暗, 舞台灯光. The lamp itself is 灯, and sunshine is 阳光. 光 is explained as fire over a person's head.
column6: Fángjiān lǐ de dēngguāng hěn wēnnuǎn.
column7: The lamp light in the room is warm.
column9: Light you see, from lamps, a stage or a window: 燈光很暗, 舞臺燈光. The lamp itself is 燈, and sunshine is 陽光. 光 is explained as fire over a person's head.

column3: In speech people just say 灯: 开灯, 关灯. 电灯 sounds technical or a little old-fashioned. 电灯泡 is slang for a third wheel on a date.
column6: Qǐng bǎ diàndēng guān le.
column7: Please turn off the light.
column9: In speech people just say 燈: 開燈, 關燈. 電燈 sounds technical or a little old-fashioned. 電燈泡 is slang for a third wheel on a date.

column3: In northern China, central heating: a plant sends hot water to radiators (暖气片) for the winter, so you ask whether a building 有暖气. In the south and Taiwan people use a heater, 电暖器.
column4: 冬天屋里有暖气，很暖和。
column5: 冬天屋裡有暖氣，很暖和。
column6: Dōngtiān wū lǐ yǒu nuǎnqì, hěn nuǎnhuo.
column7: In winter there is heating indoors and it's warm.
column9: In northern China, central heating: a plant sends hot water to radiators (暖氣片) for the winter, so you ask whether a building 有暖氣. In the south and Taiwan people use a heater, 電暖器.

column3: The whole job of fitting out a home or shop: floors, walls, fixtures. 精装修 is fully finished, 毛坯房 a bare shell. Also a noun: 装修很漂亮.
column4: 我们的新房子正在装修。
column5: 我們的新房子正在裝修。
column6: Wǒmen de xīn fángzi zhèngzài zhuāngxiū.
column7: Our new house is being renovated.
column9: The whole job of fitting out a home or shop: floors, walls, fixtures. 精裝修 is fully finished, 毛坯房 a bare shell. Also a noun: 裝修很漂亮.

column3: Two uses: setting up or decorating a room or event (布置房间, 布置会场), and a teacher or boss assigning work (布置作业, 布置任务).
column4: 老师给我们布置了作业。
column5: 老師給我們佈置了作業。
column6: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen bùzhì le zuòyè.
column7: The teacher gave us homework.
column9: Two uses: setting up or decorating a room or event (佈置房間, 佈置會場), and a teacher or boss assigning work (佈置作業, 佈置任務).

column3: Alone it is mostly a measure word for boxed goods: 一箱水, 一箱书. As a thing it needs a partner: 冰箱, 行李箱, 邮箱, 保险箱. 箱 is explained as a bamboo box.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī xiāng shuǐ.
column7: I bought a case of water.
column9: Alone it is mostly a measure word for boxed goods: 一箱水, 一箱書. As a thing it needs a partner: 冰箱, 行李箱, 郵箱, 保險箱. 箱 is explained as a bamboo box.

column3: The general word for a big box or case, a suitcase included; 行李箱 is specifically luggage, and a small box is 盒子. 搬箱子, 打开箱子.
column6: Xiāngzi lǐ zhuāngmǎn le shū.
column7: The box is full of books.
column9: The general word for a big box or case, a suitcase included; 行李箱 is specifically luggage, and a small box is 盒子. 搬箱子, 打開箱子.

column3: On the mainland you 扔垃圾 or 倒垃圾; Taiwan says 丢垃圾. Also 垃圾桶, 垃圾分类. For poor quality it is a mild insult: 垃圾食品 is junk food, 垃圾邮件 spam.
column6: Qǐng bùyào luàn rēng lājī.
column7: Please don't throw trash around.
column9: On the mainland you 扔垃圾 or 倒垃圾; Taiwan says 丟垃圾. Also 垃圾桶, 垃圾分類. For poor quality it is a mild insult: 垃圾食品 is junk food, 垃圾郵件 spam.

column3: Cleaning a whole place; the object is the room, not the dirt: 打扫房间, and 打扫卫生 for "do the cleaning". Plain sweeping is 扫.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ yào dǎsǎo fángjiān.
column7: I'm going to clean the room this weekend.
column9: Cleaning a whole place; the object is the room, not the dirt: 打掃房間, and 打掃衛生 for "do the cleaning". Plain sweeping is 掃.

column3: Beyond floors, it means to scan: 扫码, 扫二维码. Also 扫雪, 扫地. To clean a whole room, use 打扫.
column6: Qǐng bǎ ménkǒu de xuě sǎo yīxià.
column7: Please sweep the snow at the door.
column9: Beyond floors, it means to scan: 掃碼, 掃二維碼. Also 掃雪, 掃地. To clean a whole room, use 打掃.

column3: Wiping with a cloth: 擦桌子, 擦黑板, 擦汗. Also putting on cream or polish: 擦药, 擦皮鞋. 擦干净 is wipe clean.
column6: Qǐng nǐ cā yīxià zhuōzi.
column7: Please wipe the table.
column9: Wiping with a cloth: 擦桌子, 擦黑板, 擦汗. Also putting on cream or polish: 擦藥, 擦皮鞋. 擦乾淨 is wipe clean.

column3: The verb is 做: 做家务, and 分担家务 for sharing the chores. Typical chores: 洗衣服, 做饭, 拖地. A written word, but also said in speech.
column6: Tā měitiān bāng māma zuò jiāwù.
column7: He helps his mother with the housework every day.
column9: The verb is 做: 做家務, and 分擔家務 for sharing the chores. Typical chores: 洗衣服, 做飯, 拖地. A written word, but also said in speech.

column3: The surface, indoors or out: 地面很滑, 擦地面. 地板 is the flooring material itself, and 地上 is the spoken "on the ground".
column6: Xià yǔ hòu, dìmiàn hěn huá.
column7: The ground is slippery after the rain.
column9: The surface, indoors or out: 地面很滑, 擦地面. 地板 is the flooring material itself, and 地上 is the spoken "on the ground".

column3: Below ground: 地下室, 地下停车场, 地下通道; the opposite is 地上. It also means underground in the secret sense: 地下工作, 地下乐队.
column6: Wǒmen de chē tíng zài dìxià.
column7: Our car is parked underground.
column9: Below ground: 地下室, 地下停車場, 地下通道; the opposite is 地上. It also means underground in the secret sense: 地下工作, 地下樂隊.

column3: A knitted top: 穿毛衣, 织毛衣 for knitting one. It is not a coat; outerwear is 外套. The 毛 is the one in 毛线, yarn. 毛 pictures a feather or hair.
column6: Tiān lěng le, nǐ gāi chuān máoyī le.
column7: It has turned cold, so you should wear a sweater.
column9: A knitted top: 穿毛衣, 織毛衣 for knitting one. It is not a coat; outerwear is 外套. The 毛 is the one in 毛線, yarn. 毛 pictures a feather or hair.

column3: You wear it with 戴 and take it off with 摘: 戴帽子, 一顶帽子. Figuratively, 扣帽子 is to pin a label on someone.
column6: Tā dàizhe yī dǐng hóng màozi.
column7: He is wearing a red hat.
column9: You wear it with 戴 and take it off with 摘: 戴帽子, 一頂帽子. Figuratively, 扣帽子 is to pin a label on someone.

column3: Socks are counted with 双 for a pair and 只 for a single sock, and the verb is 穿: 穿袜子, 穿上袜子. The 子 is only a noun suffix, as in 椅子.
column6: Wǒ de wàzi pò le.
column7: My socks have a hole.
column9: Socks are counted with 雙 for a pair and 隻 for a single sock, and the verb is 穿: 穿襪子, 穿上襪子. The 子 is only a noun suffix, as in 椅子.

column3: Any layer worn over other clothes, from a light jacket to a winter coat, counted with 件. A long heavy coat can also be called 大衣. 套 here is the cover slipped over, as in 手套.
column4: 外面冷，你带一件外套吧。
column5: 外面冷，你帶一件外套吧。
column6: Wàimiàn lěng, nǐ dài yī jiàn wàitào ba.
column7: It's cold outside, take a jacket.
column9: Any layer worn over other clothes, from a light jacket to a winter coat, counted with 件. A long heavy coat can also be called 大衣. 套 here is the cover slipped over, as in 手套.

column3: Counted with 条. Besides 戴围巾 you can say 围围巾, with 围 as the verb "to wrap around". 巾 is the cloth in 毛巾, 纸巾 and 餐巾 too.
column6: Māma sòng wǒ yī tiáo wéijīn.
column7: Mom gave me a scarf.
column9: Counted with 條. Besides 戴圍巾 you can say 圍圍巾, with 圍 as the verb "to wrap around". 巾 is the cloth in 毛巾, 紙巾 and 餐巾 too.

column3: Gloves and mittens alike, counted as a pair with 双 or 副 and put on with 戴: 戴手套, 摘手套.
column6: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, nǐ yào dài shǒutào.
column7: It's cold outside, you should wear gloves.
column9: Gloves and mittens alike, counted as a pair with 雙 or 副 and put on with 戴: 戴手套, 摘手套.

column3: 穿 alone describes the state (他穿红衣服), while 穿上 is the act of putting something on. The opposite is 脱下, and for a hat or glasses the pair is 戴上 and 摘下.
column6: Kuài chuānshang wàitào, wàimiàn hěn lěng.
column7: Put on a coat quickly, it's cold outside.
column9: 穿 alone describes the state (他穿紅衣服), while 穿上 is the act of putting something on. The opposite is 脫下, and for a hat or glasses the pair is 戴上 and 摘下.

column3: The verb for what sits on the head, face, neck or wrist: 戴帽子, 戴眼镜, 戴手套, 戴口罩, 戴手表. Clothes and shoes take 穿 instead. The oldest form was a picture of a person holding something on their head with both hands.
column6: Tā měitiān dōu dài màozi.
column7: He wears a hat every day.
column9: The verb for what sits on the head, face, neck or wrist: 戴帽子, 戴眼鏡, 戴手套, 戴口罩, 戴手錶. Clothes and shoes take 穿 instead. The oldest form was a picture of a person holding something on their head with both hands.

column3: For clothes, shoes and socks: 脱衣服, 脱鞋, usually with 下 (脱下外套). For glasses or a watch, 摘 is the natural verb. Also "to escape": 脱险.
column6: Jìn mén qǐng tuō xié.
column7: Please take off your shoes when you come in.
column9: For clothes, shoes and socks: 脫衣服, 脫鞋, usually with 下 (脫下外套). For glasses or a watch, 摘 is the natural verb. Also "to escape": 脫險.

column3: Counted with 副: 一副眼镜. You 戴 them on and 摘 them off. Sunglasses are 太阳镜 or 墨镜, and 镜 as a lens also appears in 望远镜 and 显微镜.
column4: 他戴着一副黑色的眼镜。
column5: 他戴著一副黑色的眼鏡。
column6: Tā dàizhe yī fù hēisè de yǎnjìng.
column7: He is wearing a pair of black glasses.
column9: Counted with 副: 一副眼鏡. You 戴 them on and 摘 them off. Sunglasses are 太陽鏡 or 墨鏡, and 鏡 as a lens also appears in 望遠鏡 and 顯微鏡.

column3: Counted with 把. 带伞 is to bring one, 打伞 or 撑伞 to hold it up. 雨伞 is the rain umbrella and 阳伞 the sun parasol.
column4: 今天会下雨，你带伞了吗？
column5: 今天會下雨，你帶傘了嗎？
column6: Jīntiān huì xiàyǔ, nǐ dài sǎn le ma?
column7: It will rain today, did you bring an umbrella?
column9: Counted with 把. 帶傘 is to bring one, 打傘 or 撐傘 to hold it up. 雨傘 is the rain umbrella and 陽傘 the sun parasol.

column3: Counted with 面: 一面镜子. You look at yourself in it with 照镜子, and 照 is also the verb for taking a photo.
column6: Tā zhèngzài zhào jìngzi.
column7: She is looking in the mirror.
column9: Counted with 面: 一面鏡子. You look at yourself in it with 照鏡子, and 照 is also the verb for taking a photo.

column3: The everyday word for a pocket on clothes (裤子口袋, 放进口袋里), and it also reaches a bag or sack. Said in speech more than written.
column6: Yàoshi zài wǒ de kǒudài lǐ.
column7: The key is in my pocket.
column9: The everyday word for a pocket on clothes (褲子口袋, 放進口袋裡), and it also reaches a bag or sack. Said in speech more than written.

column3: Mostly a measure word for what comes in a bag: 一袋米, 一袋面粉. As a thing it turns up inside words such as 口袋, 塑料袋 and 垃圾袋.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī dài dàmǐ.
column7: I bought a bag of rice.
column9: Mostly a measure word for what comes in a bag: 一袋米, 一袋麵粉. As a thing it turns up inside words such as 口袋, 塑料袋 and 垃圾袋.

column3: A "plastic bag": 一个塑料袋. 塑料 is "plastic" and 袋 "bag". In Taiwan the usual word is 塑胶袋. In shops you may be asked 要不要袋子？
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī ge sùliàodài.
column7: Please give me a plastic bag.
column9: A "plastic bag": 一個塑料袋. 塑料 is "plastic" and 袋 "bag". In Taiwan the usual word is 塑膠袋. In shops you may be asked 要不要袋子？

column3: Build and figure together, height included: 身材好 is a compliment on a good figure, 身材高大 and 身材矮小 describe size. For height alone, say 身高.
column6: Tā de shēncái hěn hǎo.
column7: She has a good figure.
column9: Build and figure together, height included: 身材好 is a compliment on a good figure, 身材高大 and 身材矮小 describe size. For height alone, say 身高.

column3: The spoken word for the belly: 肚子疼, 肚子饿 (hungry), 大肚子. 胃 is the stomach itself, the organ: 胃疼, 胃不舒服.
column6: Wǒ dùzi è le.
column7: I'm hungry.
column9: The spoken word for the belly: 肚子疼, 肚子餓 (hungry), 大肚子. 胃 is the stomach itself, the organ: 胃疼, 胃不舒服.

column3: The waist and lower back: 腰疼 is lower-back pain, while upper-back pain is 背疼. Also 弯腰, 腰带, and the middle of something tall, as in 山腰, the mountainside.
column6: Wǒ de yāo yǒudiǎnr téng.
column7: My lower back hurts a little.
column9: The waist and lower back: 腰疼 is lower-back pain, while upper-back pain is 背疼. Also 彎腰, 腰帶, and the middle of something tall, as in 山腰, the mountainside.

column3: The casual word for the head, sometimes joking: 摇脑袋, 脑袋疼. It can also mean brains: 脑袋聪明. In writing or neutral speech 头 is plainer.
column6: Tā yáo le yáo nǎodai.
column7: He shook his head.
column9: The casual word for the head, sometimes joking: 搖腦袋, 腦袋疼. It can also mean brains: 腦袋聰明. In writing or neutral speech 頭 is plainer.

column3: Teeth in everyday speech: 牙疼, 刷牙, 牙医, 牙膏. Counted with 颗. The more formal, medical word is 牙齿. It began as a picture of a pair of elephant tusks.
column6: Wǒ de yá hěn téng.
column7: My tooth hurts a lot.
column9: Teeth in everyday speech: 牙疼, 刷牙, 牙醫, 牙膏. Counted with 顆. The more formal, medical word is 牙齒. It began as a picture of a pair of elephant tusks.

column3: Counted with 根 or 块. 啃骨头 is to gnaw a bone, and 硬骨头 is a tough, unyielding person. The 头 is a suffix here, not "head".
column6: Gǒu xǐhuan chī gǔtou.
column7: Dogs like eating bones.
column9: Counted with 根 or 塊. 啃骨頭 is to gnaw a bone, and 硬骨頭 is a tough, unyielding person. The 頭 is a suffix here, not "head".

column3: A neutral, slightly medical word for the chest area: 胸部疼, 胸部手术. In speech people say 胸口 or just 胸. 部 marks a body part, as in 头部 and 腹部.
column6: Tā de xiōngbù shòushāng le.
column7: His chest was injured.
column9: A neutral, slightly medical word for the chest area: 胸部疼, 胸部手術. In speech people say 胸口 or just 胸. 部 marks a body part, as in 頭部 and 腹部.

column3: A body organ, and the word biology and medicine use: 器官移植, 内脏器官, 消化器官. 官 means government official too, but also organ of the body.
column6: Xīnzàng shì zhòngyào de qìguān.
column7: The heart is an important organ.
column9: A body organ, and the word biology and medicine use: 器官移植, 內臟器官, 消化器官. 官 means government official too, but also organ of the body.

column3: To breathe, as a verb or noun: 呼吸新鲜空气, 呼吸困难, 深呼吸. The two characters are opposites, out and in, put together to name the whole act.
column4: 在公园里可以呼吸新鲜空气。
column5: 在公園裡可以呼吸新鮮空氣。
column6: Zài gōngyuán lǐ kěyǐ hūxī xīnxiān kōngqì.
column7: In the park you can breathe fresh air.
column9: To breathe, as a verb or noun: 呼吸新鮮空氣, 呼吸困難, 深呼吸. The two characters are opposites, out and in, put together to name the whole act.

column3: A bound form: it appears in set words like 流泪, 泪水 and 眼泪 but is rarely said alone. It is literary, and fits emotional scenes.
column6: Tā gǎndòng de liú lèi le.
column7: She was moved to tears.
column9: A bound form: it appears in set words like 流淚, 淚水 and 眼淚 but is rarely said alone. It is literary, and fits emotional scenes.

column3: Tears with a more literary, emotional ring: 泪水流下来, 充满泪水. For a plain everyday statement people say 眼泪.
column4: 泪水从她的脸上流下来。
column5: 淚水從她的臉上流下來。
column6: Lèishuǐ cóng tā de liǎn shàng liú xiàlái.
column7: Tears ran down her face.
column9: Tears with a more literary, emotional ring: 淚水流下來, 充滿淚水. For a plain everyday statement people say 眼淚.

column3: The plain everyday word for tears, more common in speech than 泪水: 流眼泪, 擦眼泪. Count them with 滴: 一滴眼泪.
column6: Tā cā le cā yǎnlèi.
column7: He wiped his tears.
column9: The plain everyday word for tears, more common in speech than 淚水: 流眼淚, 擦眼淚. Count them with 滴: 一滴眼淚.

column3: Only for people (and animals): 身高一米八, and you ask 你身高多少? Buildings and mountains have a 高度 instead.
column6: Tā de shēngāo yǒu yī mǐ bā.
column7: He is 1.8 meters tall.
column9: Only for people (and animals): 身高一米八, and you ask 你身高多少? Buildings and mountains have a 高度 instead.

column3: Quoted in 公斤: 量体重, 体重增加, 控制体重. To ask, say 你多重? It is for a person's body; the weight of an object is 重量.
column6: Wǒ de tǐzhòng shì wǔshí gōngjīn.
column7: My weight is fifty kilograms.
column9: Quoted in 公斤: 量體重, 體重增加, 控制體重. To ask, say 你多重? It is for a person's body; the weight of an object is 重量.

column3: Muscle power only, not will or skill: 力气大, 没力气, 用力气. Heavy manual work is 力气活. Lasting energy is 精力 instead.
column4: 他力气很大，一个人搬得动。
column5: 他力氣很大，一個人搬得動。
column6: Tā lìqi hěn dà, yī ge rén bān de dòng.
column7: He is strong and can move it by himself.
column9: Muscle power only, not will or skill: 力氣大, 沒力氣, 用力氣. Heavy manual work is 力氣活. Lasting energy is 精力 instead.

column3: Energy to keep doing things, mental and physical: 精力充沛, 没有精力. It is stamina over time, unlike 力气, a burst of muscle strength.
column6: Wǒ méiyǒu jīnglì zài xuéxí le.
column7: I have no energy left to study.
column9: Energy to keep doing things, mental and physical: 精力充沛, 沒有精力. It is stamina over time, unlike 力氣, a burst of muscle strength.

column3: Used for traits passed from parent to child: 遗传病, 遗传基因. A property or a title is inherited with 继承, not 遗传.
column6: Zhè zhǒng bìng huì yíchuán.
column7: This illness can be inherited.
column9: Used for traits passed from parent to child: 遺傳病, 遺傳基因. A property or a title is inherited with 繼承, not 遺傳.

column3: Digesting food (消化不良, 不容易消化), and also taking in ideas: 消化新知识 is to absorb what you have learned.
column6: Chī tài duō bù róngyì xiāohuà.
column7: If you eat too much it is hard to digest.
column9: Digesting food (消化不良, 不容易消化), and also taking in ideas: 消化新知識 is to absorb what you have learned.

column3: Short and small, a little unflattering for people (身材矮小) and plain for buildings (矮小的房子). The opposite is 高大, and a short piece of string is 短, not 矮.
column4: 他的身材矮小，但是很有力气。
column5: 他的身材矮小，但是很有力氣。
column6: Tā de shēncái ǎixiǎo, dànshì hěn yǒu lìqi.
column7: He is small in build, but very strong.
column9: Short and small, a little unflattering for people (身材矮小) and plain for buildings (矮小的房子). The opposite is 高大, and a short piece of string is 短, not 矮.

column3: Fat of animals and meat (肥肉), and loose, baggy clothes (太肥了). Calling a person 肥 is blunt; 胖 is the usual word. It also means fertilizer and fertile, as in 化肥.
column6: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài féi le.
column7: These pants are too baggy.
column9: Fat of animals and meat (肥肉), and loose, baggy clothes (太肥了). Calling a person 肥 is blunt; 胖 is the usual word. It also means fertilizer and fertile, as in 化肥.

column3: Opposite of 强: 身体弱, 弱点, 弱者. One account sees a decorative bow that is functionally inferior; another, a bow that shakes because it is worn out.
column6: Tā shēntǐ hěn ruò, jīngcháng shēngbìng.
column7: She is physically weak and often ill.
column9: Opposite of 強: 身體弱, 弱點, 弱者. One account sees a decorative bow that is functionally inferior; another, a bow that shakes because it is worn out.

column3: A verb and its object, so 了 can split it: 发了烧, 发了三天烧. Bringing a fever down is 退烧. The slang 发烧友 is an enthusiast, such as an audio buff.
column6: Háizi fāshāo le, yào qù yīyuàn.
column7: The child has a fever and needs to go to the hospital.
column9: A verb and its object, so 了 can split it: 發了燒, 發了三天燒. Bringing a fever down is 退燒. The slang 發燒友 is an enthusiast, such as an audio buff.

column3: Feeling sick (我觉得恶心) and, as a strong everyday word, disgusting: 太恶心了! It can describe a person's behavior too. In this word 恶 is read ě; the reading è goes with evil.
column6: Wǒ zuò chuán huì juéde ěxīn.
column7: I feel sick when I take a boat.
column9: Feeling sick (我覺得噁心) and, as a strong everyday word, disgusting: 太噁心了! It can describe a person's behavior too. In this word 惡 is read ě; the reading è goes with evil.

column3: A verb and its object, so 打了针 or 打了一针. 打 is a light verb that suits many objects: 打伞, 打电话, 打针.
column6: Háizi zuì pà dǎzhēn.
column7: Children are most afraid of injections.
column9: A verb and its object, so 打了針 or 打了一針. 打 is a light verb that suits many objects: 打傘, 打電話, 打針.

column3: 做手术 serves both the surgeon and the patient: 医生给他做手术, 他做了手术. 动手术 is another way to say it, and 手术室 is the operating room.
column6: Tā xià zhōu yào zuò shǒushù.
column7: He is having an operation next week.
column9: 做手術 serves both the surgeon and the patient: 醫生給他做手術, 他做了手術. 動手術 is another way to say it, and 手術室 is the operating room.

column3: Mostly met in 治病, 治好 and compounds such as 治疗. 看病 is seeing a doctor, while 治 is the cure itself. The same character governs in 治国.
column6: Zhè zhǒng bìng hěn nán zhì.
column7: This illness is hard to cure.
column9: Mostly met in 治病, 治好 and compounds such as 治療. 看病 is seeing a doctor, while 治 is the cure itself. The same character governs in 治國.

column3: The formal word for treatment, a verb and a noun: 接受治疗, 治疗方法, 治疗效果. 疗 turns up in 医疗, 疗养 and 理疗 too.
column6: Tā zhèngzài yīyuàn jiēshòu zhìliáo.
column7: He is receiving treatment at the hospital.
column9: The formal word for treatment, a verb and a noun: 接受治療, 治療方法, 治療效果. 療 turns up in 醫療, 療養 and 理療 too.

column3: Medical care as a system or service, not one act: 医疗条件, 医疗保险, 医疗费用. For treating a particular illness, use 治疗.
column6: Zhèlǐ de yīliáo tiáojiàn hěn hǎo.
column7: The medical facilities here are very good.
column9: Medical care as a system or service, not one act: 醫療條件, 醫療保險, 醫療費用. For treating a particular illness, use 治療.

column3: Medicine as a field of study: 学医学, 医学院, 医学研究. Not the stuff you take, which is 药. The -学 ending names many fields, as in 化学 and 数学.
column6: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí yīxué.
column7: She studies medicine at university.
column9: Medicine as a field of study: 學醫學, 醫學院, 醫學研究. Not the stuff you take, which is 藥. The -學 ending names many fields, as in 化學 and 數學.

column3: The hospital department for illnesses treated without surgery, opposite 外科. You say 挂内科 to register there, and 内科医生 for the doctor.
column6: Qǐngwèn nèikē zài jǐ lóu?
column7: Excuse me, which floor is internal medicine on?
column9: The hospital department for illnesses treated without surgery, opposite 外科. You say 掛內科 to register there, and 內科醫生 for the doctor.

column3: A nurse of either sex: 当护士, 男护士, 护士长. 士 also ends words for trained or ranking people, as in 战士 and 博士.
column6: Hùshi gěi wǒ liáng le tǐwēn.
column7: The nurse took my temperature.
column9: A nurse of either sex: 當護士, 男護士, 護士長. 士 also ends words for trained or ranking people, as in 戰士 and 博士.

column3: A formal word for medicines as a group: 药物治疗, 药物过敏, 药物副作用. In speech, 药 alone is enough: 吃药.
column4: 这种药物有一些副作用。
column5: 這種藥物有一些副作用。
column6: Zhè zhǒng yàowù yǒu yīxiē fùzuòyòng.
column7: This medication has some side effects.
column9: A formal word for medicines as a group: 藥物治療, 藥物過敏, 藥物副作用. In speech, 藥 alone is enough: 吃藥.

column3: A routine check-up, often yearly through work or school: 做体检, 体检报告.
column4: 公司每年都让我们做体检。
column5: 公司每年都讓我們做體檢。
column6: Gōngsī měi nián dōu ràng wǒmen zuò tǐjiǎn.
column7: The company has us do a medical check-up every year.
column9: A routine check-up, often yearly through work or school: 做體檢, 體檢報告.

column3: A stay of rest and care to recover or keep one's health, often by the sea or in the mountains: 疗养院 is a sanatorium. It suggests weeks, not a hospital visit.
column4: 他在海边疗养了一个月。
column5: 他在海邊療養了一個月。
column6: Tā zài hǎibiān liáoyǎng le yī ge yuè.
column7: He recovered by the sea for a month.
column9: A stay of rest and care to recover or keep one's health, often by the sea or in the mountains: 療養院 is a sanatorium. It suggests weeks, not a hospital visit.

column3: A verb and its object: 想减肥, 在减肥, 减肥了. The result is said with 瘦: 瘦了五公斤. The diet itself is often 节食.
column4: 她最近在减肥，不吃晚饭。
column5: 她最近在減肥，不吃晚飯。
column6: Tā zuìjìn zài jiǎnféi, bù chī wǎnfàn.
column7: She is on a diet lately and skips dinner.
column9: A verb and its object: 想減肥, 在減肥, 減肥了. The result is said with 瘦: 瘦了五公斤. The diet itself is often 節食.

column3: To ease a problem without ending it: 缓解压力, 缓解疼痛, 缓解紧张. For solving it outright, use 解决.
column6: Tīng yīnyuè kěyǐ huǎnjiě yālì.
column7: Listening to music can relieve stress.
column9: To ease a problem without ending it: 緩解壓力, 緩解疼痛, 緩解緊張. For solving it outright, use 解決.

column3: To hurt on purpose or by effect, in body or feelings: 伤害别人, 伤害感情, 受到伤害. Getting hurt by accident is 受伤.
column6: Bùyào shānghài biérén de gǎnqíng.
column7: Don't hurt other people's feelings.
column9: To hurt on purpose or by effect, in body or feelings: 傷害別人, 傷害感情, 受到傷害. Getting hurt by accident is 受傷.

column3: A needle or pin, counted with 根: 缝衣针, 针线. It also gives 打针 and 针灸 (acupuncture), and the hands of a clock: 时针, 分针.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī gēn zhēn.
column7: Please give me a needle.
column9: A needle or pin, counted with 根: 縫衣針, 針線. It also gives 打針 and 針灸 (acupuncture), and the hands of a clock: 時針, 分針.

column3: You set it with 定 or 设 and it goes off with 响: 闹钟响了. Only for the clock that wakes you; a clock on the wall is 挂钟.
column6: Wǒ bǎ nàozhōng dìng zài liù diǎn.
column7: I set the alarm for six o'clock.
column9: You set it with 定 or 設 and it goes off with 響: 鬧鐘響了. Only for the clock that wakes you; a clock on the wall is 掛鐘.

column3: It is waking up, not getting up: 醒了 means your eyes are open, 起床 means out of bed. Common partners are 醒来, 睡醒 and 吵醒 (woken by noise).
column6: Wǒ jīntiān liù diǎn jiù xǐng le.
column7: I woke up already at six today.
column9: It is waking up, not getting up: 醒了 means your eyes are open, 起床 means out of bed. Common partners are 醒來, 睡醒 and 吵醒 (woken by noise).

column3: Clear in the mind, not just awake: 头脑清醒, and 清醒过来 for coming to after a faint or a night of drinking. It can also mean seeing things realistically: 清醒的认识.
column6: Hē le kāfēi, wǒ qīngxǐng duō le.
column7: After the coffee I am much more awake.
column9: Clear in the mind, not just awake: 頭腦清醒, and 清醒過來 for coming to after a faint or a night of drinking. It can also mean seeing things realistically: 清醒的認識.

column3: After a verb it says the action reached its goal: 睡着 (fall asleep), 找着, 猜着; 睡不着 is can't fall asleep. Alone it means to catch or touch, as in 着火 and 着凉 (catch a cold).
column6: Zuówǎn wǒ yīzhí shuì bù zháo.
column7: Last night I couldn't fall asleep at all.
column9: After a verb it says the action reached its goal: 睡著 (fall asleep), 找著, 猜著; 睡不著 is can't fall asleep. Alone it means to catch or touch, as in 著火 and 著涼 (catch a cold).

column3: 睡觉 is the activity of sleeping, 睡着 the moment you drop off: 我躺了一个小时才睡着. 睡不着 is the common way to say you can't sleep, and 睡着了 that someone is now asleep.
column6: Háizi yǐjīng shuìzháo le.
column7: The child has already fallen asleep.
column9: 睡覺 is the activity of sleeping, 睡著 the moment you drop off: 我躺了一個小時才睡著. 睡不著 is the common way to say you can't sleep, and 睡著了 that someone is now asleep.

column3: Lying down on something flat: 躺下, 躺在床上, and 躺着 for staying that way. Lying face down is 趴. On the internet 躺平 means opting out of the rat race.
column6: Tā tǎng zài shāfā shàng kàn diànshì.
column7: He is lying on the sofa watching TV.
column9: Lying down on something flat: 躺下, 躺在床上, and 躺著 for staying that way. Lying face down is 趴. On the internet 躺平 means opting out of the rat race.

column3: The verb is 做 and the measure word 个: 做了一个梦. It also stands for a hope or ambition: 梦想 is a dream you work toward, and 梦 alone can be a wish, as in 中国梦. The oldest forms show a person lying on a bed.
column6: Wǒ zuówǎn zuò le yī ge hǎo mèng.
column7: I had a good dream last night.
column9: The verb is 做 and the measure word 個: 做了一個夢. It also stands for a hope or ambition: 夢想 is a dream you work toward, and 夢 alone can be a wish, as in 中國夢. The oldest forms show a person lying on a bed.

column3: The dreamed thing comes straight after it, with no preposition: 我梦见你了, 梦见自己在飞. 做梦 names the experience of dreaming, 梦见 says what showed up in it.
column4: 我昨天梦见了我的奶奶。
column5: 我昨天夢見了我的奶奶。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān mèngjiàn le wǒ de nǎinai.
column7: Yesterday I dreamed about my grandmother.
column9: The dreamed thing comes straight after it, with no preposition: 我夢見你了, 夢見自己在飛. 做夢 names the experience of dreaming, 夢見 says what showed up in it.

column3: A verb and its object, so other words fit between: 做了一个梦, 做了个好梦. Said to someone, 你做梦! is "in your dreams", and 做梦都想… means wanting something badly enough to dream of it.
column6: Tā zuòmèng dōu xiǎng dāng yīshēng.
column7: He dreams of becoming a doctor, even in his sleep.
column9: A verb and its object, so other words fit between: 做了一個夢, 做了個好夢. Said to someone, 你做夢! is "in your dreams", and 做夢都想… means wanting something badly enough to dream of it.

column3: A verb and its object, so a number or 了 goes between: 刷了牙, 一天刷两次牙. The brush itself is 牙刷, the toothpaste 牙膏.
column6: Shuìjiào qián yào shuāyá.
column7: You must brush your teeth before going to bed.
column9: A verb and its object, so a number or 了 goes between: 刷了牙, 一天刷兩次牙. The brush itself is 牙刷, the toothpaste 牙膏.

column3: The thing, where 刷牙 is the action; counted with 把. The object comes first in brush names: 牙刷, 鞋刷, 锅刷 (pot brush).
column6: Wǒ wàng le dài yáshuā.
column7: I forgot to bring a toothbrush.
column9: The thing, where 刷牙 is the action; counted with 把. The object comes first in brush names: 牙刷, 鞋刷, 鍋刷 (pot brush).

column3: Counted with 条; it is the small face or hand towel, while a bath towel is 浴巾. 巾 is cloth in other words too: 围巾 scarf, 餐巾 napkin, 纸巾 tissue. 巾 began as a picture of a hanging piece of cloth.
column4: 请给我一条干净的毛巾。
column5: 請給我一條乾淨的毛巾。
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī tiáo gānjìng de máojīn.
column7: Please give me a clean towel.
column9: Counted with 條; it is the small face or hand towel, while a bath towel is 浴巾. 巾 is cloth in other words too: 圍巾 scarf, 餐巾 napkin, 紙巾 tissue. 巾 began as a picture of a hanging piece of cloth.

column3: Scrubbing with a brush or sponge: 刷牙, 刷鞋. Newer senses are 刷卡 (pay by card) and 刷手机 (scroll your phone). 刷碗 for washing dishes is northern mainland speech; in Taiwan and elsewhere it is 洗碗.
column6: Chīwán fàn, wǒ lái shuā wǎn.
column7: After the meal I'll wash the dishes.
column9: Scrubbing with a brush or sponge: 刷牙, 刷鞋. Newer senses are 刷卡 (pay by card) and 刷手機 (scroll your phone). 刷碗 for washing dishes is northern mainland speech; in Taiwan and elsewhere it is 洗碗.

column3: The general brush for scrubbing or painting, counted with 把. In the saying 有两把刷子, "he has two brushes" means he has real skill.
column6: Yòng shuāzi xǐ bēizi.
column7: Wash the cups with a brush.
column9: The general brush for scrubbing or painting, counted with 把. In the saying 有兩把刷子, "he has two brushes" means he has real skill.

column3: The everyday spoken verb: 抽一根烟, 不抽烟, 戒烟 (quit). On signs and warnings the same act is 吸烟.
column6: Qǐng bùyào zài zhèlǐ chōuyān.
column7: Please don't smoke here.
column9: The everyday spoken verb: 抽一根煙, 不抽煙, 戒煙 (quit). On signs and warnings the same act is 吸煙.

column3: The written form for signs and health warnings: 禁止吸烟, 吸烟区, 吸烟有害健康. People say 抽烟 when they talk about it; 二手烟 is secondhand smoke.
column6: Xīyān duì shēntǐ bù hǎo.
column7: Smoking is bad for your health.
column9: The written form for signs and health warnings: 禁止吸煙, 吸煙區, 吸煙有害健康. People say 抽煙 when they talk about it; 二手煙 is secondhand smoke.

column3: You write it with 写 or 记: 写日记, 记日记; counted with 本, and one day's entry is 一篇日记. 记 means record in other words too: 笔记 notes, 记录 a record.
column6: Wǒ měitiān wǎnshang xiě rìjì.
column7: I write in my diary every evening.
column9: You write it with 寫 or 記: 寫日記, 記日記; counted with 本, and one day's entry is 一篇日記. 記 means record in other words too: 筆記 notes, 記錄 a record.

column3: Covers the paper calendar and the app on a phone: 看日历, 手机日历. Kinds of paper ones are 台历 (desk) and 挂历 (wall).
column4: 日历上写着今天是五号。
column5: 日曆上寫著今天是五號。
column6: Rìlì shàng xiězhe jīntiān shì wǔ hào.
column7: The calendar says today is the fifth.
column9: Covers the paper calendar and the app on a phone: 看日曆, 手機日曆. Kinds of paper ones are 檯曆 (desk) and 掛曆 (wall).

column3: Both the action and the state: 放松一下 take a break, 放松肌肉, 放松心情. It also loosens things: 放松绳子, and 放松管制 is to ease controls. The opposite is 紧张 (tense).
column6: Zhōumò wǒ xiǎng fàngsōng yīxià.
column7: This weekend I want to relax a bit.
column9: Both the action and the state: 放鬆一下 take a break, 放鬆肌肉, 放鬆心情. It also loosens things: 放鬆繩子, and 放鬆管制 is to ease controls. The opposite is 緊張 (tense).

column3: Comfort of a place or object, in a slightly written style: 舒适的环境, 舒适的座位. For how a person feels, speech uses 舒服: 我不舒服 is "I don't feel well", never 不舒适.
column6: Zhè zhāng shāfā hěn shūshì.
column7: This sofa is very comfortable.
column9: Comfort of a place or object, in a slightly written style: 舒適的環境, 舒適的座位. For how a person feels, speech uses 舒服: 我不舒服 is "I don't feel well", never 不舒適.

column3: Stresses ease and lightness: 轻松的工作, 心情轻松, 轻轻松松 (with ease). It is also a verb, 轻松一下 (unwind a bit); 放松 stresses loosening tension, as in 放松肌肉.
column6: Zhè cì kǎoshì hěn qīngsōng.
column7: This exam was easy.
column9: Stresses ease and lightness: 輕鬆的工作, 心情輕鬆, 輕輕鬆鬆 (with ease). It is also a verb, 輕鬆一下 (unwind a bit); 放鬆 stresses loosening tension, as in 放鬆肌肉.

column3: Nearly always followed by a habit: 养成习惯, 养成好习惯, 养成…的习惯. Other objects are rarer but fit, such as 养成独立的性格 or 养成良好的作风; the sense is slow, repeated shaping.
column6: Tā yǎngchéng le zǎoqǐ de xíguàn.
column7: He has gotten into the habit of getting up early.
column9: Nearly always followed by a habit: 養成習慣, 養成好習慣, 養成…的習慣. Other objects are rarer but fit, such as 養成獨立的性格 or 養成良好的作風; the sense is slow, repeated shaping.

column3: The plain spoken word for any bug or worm; counted with 只, or 条 for a wormlike one. 昆虫 is the scientific insect. 虫 is the radical of many animal names, like 蚂蚁 and 蜜蜂.
column6: Huā shàng yǒu yī zhī xiǎo chóngzi.
column7: There is a little bug on the flower.
column9: The plain spoken word for any bug or worm; counted with 隻, or 條 for a wormlike one. 昆蟲 is the scientific insect. 蟲 is the radical of many animal names, like 螞蟻 and 蜜蜂.

column3: Animal tails: 摇尾巴, 一条尾巴. Figuratively 翘尾巴 (tail up) means getting cocky, and 夹着尾巴 (tail tucked) means keeping a low profile. 尾 is built from 尸 (a person) and 毛 (hair or feathers).
column6: Xiǎogǒu yáozhe wěiba.
column7: The puppy is wagging its tail.
column9: Animal tails: 搖尾巴, 一條尾巴. Figuratively 翹尾巴 (tail up) means getting cocky, and 夾著尾巴 (tail tucked) means keeping a low profile. 尾 is built from 尸 (a person) and 毛 (hair or feathers).

column3: A grove or small wood, as in 在树林里; 森林 is the big dense forest. 林 doubles 木 to give the idea of many trees.
column6: Wǒmen zài shùlín lǐ sànbù.
column7: We are walking in the woods.
column9: A grove or small wood, as in 在樹林裡; 森林 is the big dense forest. 林 doubles 木 to give the idea of many trees.

column3: Leaves of a tree, on it or fallen: 落叶 for a fallen one. 叶子 is the general word for any plant's leaf, and 树叶 is only for trees; counted with 片.
column6: Qiūtiān, shùyè dōu huáng le.
column7: In autumn the leaves have all turned yellow.
column9: Leaves of a tree, on it or fallen: 落葉 for a fallen one. 葉子 is the general word for any plant's leaf, and 樹葉 is only for trees; counted with 片.

column3: The leaf of any plant, from a tree to a cabbage; counted with 片. In compounds the 子 drops: 茶叶 tea leaves, 树叶 tree leaves, 菜叶 vegetable leaves.
column6: Zhè kē shù de yèzi hěn dà.
column7: This tree's leaves are very big.
column9: The leaf of any plant, from a tree to a cabbage; counted with 片. In compounds the 子 drops: 茶葉 tea leaves, 樹葉 tree leaves, 菜葉 vegetable leaves.

column3: The opposite is 紧: 太松 for a rope, belt or screw that is too loose. The pine tree, as in 松树 and 松子 (pine nut), is a different character that simplification made look the same.
column6: Zhè gēn shéngzi tài sōng le.
column7: This rope is too loose.
column9: The opposite is 緊: 太鬆 for a rope, belt or screw that is too loose.

column3: Counted with 棵. 松 gives other words from the tree: 松子 pine nut and 松鼠 squirrel. The pine stays green in winter, so it stands for endurance in poems and paintings.
column6: Shān shàng yǒu hěn duō sōngshù.
column7: There are many pine trees on the mountain.
column9: Counted with 棵. 松 gives other words from the tree: 松子 pine nut and 松鼠 squirrel. The pine stays green in winter, so it stands for endurance in poems and paintings.

column3: The big dense forest, as against a 树林: 森林公园, 保护森林; a rain forest is 热带雨林. 森 triples 木 to suggest a large number of trees.
column6: Zhè zuò shān shàng yǒu dà piàn sēnlín.
column7: This mountain has a large forest.
column9: The big dense forest, as against a 樹林: 森林公園, 保護森林; a rain forest is 熱帶雨林. 森 triples 木 to suggest a large number of trees.

column3: Plants as a class, the pair of 动物: 植物园 botanical garden, 植物油 vegetable oil, 植物人 a person in a vegetative state. 物 ends many words for a kind of thing: 食物, 礼物, 建筑物.
column6: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù xūyào hěn duō shuǐ.
column7: This plant needs a lot of water.
column9: Plants as a class, the pair of 動物: 植物園 botanical garden, 植物油 vegetable oil, 植物人 a person in a vegetative state. 物 ends many words for a kind of thing: 食物, 禮物, 建築物.

column3: Formal, for growing crops or trees on a scale: 种植蔬菜, 种植园, 种植面积. At home or in speech, 种 alone is the verb: 种花, 种菜.
column6: Zhèlǐ zhǔyào zhòngzhí cháyè.
column7: Mainly tea is grown here.
column9: Formal, for growing crops or trees on a scale: 種植蔬菜, 種植園, 種植面積. At home or in speech, 種 alone is the verb: 種花, 種菜.

column3: A verb with a plant: 种花, 种树, 种菜; 种田 and 种地 are to farm. It is the everyday word for planting, while 种植 is formal and for crops on a scale.
column6: Yéye zài yuànzi lǐ zhòng huā.
column7: Grandpa grows flowers in the yard.
column9: A verb with a plant: 種花, 種樹, 種菜; 種田 and 種地 are to farm. It is the everyday word for planting, while 種植 is formal and for crops on a scale.

column3: A verb and object, so 树开花了 and 开了花 both work. Figuratively 开花结果 (bloom, bear fruit) is for effort paying off.
column6: Chūntiān, shù shàng kāihuā le.
column7: In spring the trees are in blossom.
column9: A verb and object, so 樹開花了 and 開了花 both work. Figuratively 開花結果 (bloom, bear fruit) is for effort paying off.

column3: Real cut flowers, as gifts or decoration: 一束鲜花 is a bouquet, 一朵 one blossom. Artificial ones are 假花 and dried ones 干花.
column6: Tā sònggěi tā yī shù xiānhuā.
column7: He gave her a bouquet of fresh flowers.
column9: Real cut flowers, as gifts or decoration: 一束鮮花 is a bouquet, 一朵 one blossom. Artificial ones are 假花 and dried ones 乾花.

column3: Rivers in the south are mostly named 江, as in 长江 and 珠江, those in the north 河, as in 黄河. It also forms 江边 (riverside) and 江水.
column6: Zhè tiáo jiāng hěn kuān.
column7: This river is very wide.
column9: Rivers in the south are mostly named 江, as in 長江 and 珠江, those in the north 河, as in 黃河. It also forms 江邊 (riverside) and 江水.

column3: Land against sea or air: 陆地和海洋. 陆 is land in other words too: 登陆 to land ashore, 着陆 to touch down, and 大陆, a continent, which in Taiwan and Hong Kong is also the usual word for mainland China.
column4: 地球上陆地面积比海洋小。
column5: 地球上陸地面積比海洋小。
column6: Dìqiú shàng lùdì miànjī bǐ hǎiyáng xiǎo.
column7: Land covers less of the Earth than the ocean does.
column9: Land against sea or air: 陸地和海洋. 陸 is land in other words too: 登陸 to land ashore, 著陸 to touch down, and 大陸, a continent, which in Taiwan and Hong Kong is also the usual word for mainland China.

column6: Hǎishuǐ yòu xián yòu kǔ.
column7: Seawater is salty and bitter.

column3: Land as property or farmland: 一块土地, 土地面积, 土地使用权. For the ground you walk on, say 地面; for a country's territory, 领土.
column4: 农民需要土地来种粮食。
column5: 農民需要土地來種糧食。
column6: Nóngmín xūyào tǔdì lái zhòng liángshi.
column7: Farmers need land to grow grain.
column9: Land as property or farmland: 一塊土地, 土地面積, 土地使用權. For the ground you walk on, say 地面; for a country's territory, 領土.

column3: The shadow something casts; the reflection in water is 倒影. Figuratively it is a trace: 连个影子都没有 means not a trace of it. 影 also begins 电影 and 影响.
column6: Tàiyáng xià, wǒ de yǐngzi hěn cháng.
column7: In the sun my shadow is long.
column9: The shadow something casts; the reflection in water is 倒影. Figuratively it is a trace: 連個影子都沒有 means not a trace of it. 影 also begins 電影 and 影響.

column3: A formal word for the season, used in institutions and notices: 春季学期, 春季运动会. In speech it is 春天. Adding 季 to the other seasons works the same way.
column6: Chūnjì shì lǚyóu de hǎo shíhou.
column7: Spring is a good time to travel.
column9: A formal word for the season, used in institutions and notices: 春季學期, 春季運動會. In speech it is 春天. Adding 季 to the other seasons works the same way.

column3: Used in forecasts, schedules and sales: 夏季天气, 夏季大减价. In speech it is 夏天.
column6: Xiàjì chángcháng xià dàyǔ.
column7: It often rains hard in summer.
column9: Used in forecasts, schedules and sales: 夏季天氣, 夏季大減價. In speech it is 夏天.

column3: The written word for autumn: 秋季开学, 秋季学期. Speech says 秋天. It turns up in notices and programs for the season: 秋季运动会, 秋季旅游, 秋季招生.
column6: Xuéxiào qiūjì kāixué.
column7: School starts in the autumn.
column9: The written word for autumn: 秋季開學, 秋季學期. Speech says 秋天. It turns up in notices and programs for the season: 秋季運動會, 秋季旅遊, 秋季招生.

column3: The formal season word, often in set names: 冬季运动, 冬季奥运会 (Winter Olympics), 冬季施工. In speech it is 冬天.
column6: Běifāng de dōngjì hěn cháng.
column7: Winters in the north are long.
column9: The formal season word, often in set names: 冬季運動, 冬季奧運會 (Winter Olympics), 冬季施工. In speech it is 冬天.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 四季, 雨季, 旺季 (peak season), 淡季 (off season). Alone it counts a TV series' seasons: 第二季. It also gives 季度, a quarter of the year.
column4: 这部剧的第二季很好看。
column5: 這部劇的第二季很好看。
column6: Zhè bù jù de dì èr jì hěn hǎokàn.
column7: The second season of this show is very good.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 四季, 雨季, 旺季 (peak season), 淡季 (off season). Alone it counts a TV series' seasons: 第二季. It also gives 季度, a quarter of the year.

column3: Seasons in general, or the time when something is at its best: 哪个季节, 季节变化, 水果的季节. The named seasons are 春天 and the like.
column6: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan nǎge jìjié?
column7: Which season do you like best?
column9: Seasons in general, or the time when something is at its best: 哪個季節, 季節變化, 水果的季節. The named seasons are 春天 and the like.

column3: Written, for weather and climate: 寒冷的冬天, 气候寒冷, 寒冷刺骨. In speech 冷 does the job. 寒 is cold in 寒假 (winter vacation) and 寒流 (cold wave). 寒 was built as a person in a house, sleeping in the grass to protect from the cold.
column6: Běifāng de dōngtiān fēicháng hánlěng.
column7: Winter in the north is very cold.
column9: Written, for weather and climate: 寒冷的冬天, 氣候寒冷, 寒冷刺骨. In speech 冷 does the job. 寒 is cold in 寒假 (winter vacation) and 寒流 (cold wave). 寒 was built as a person in a house, sleeping in the grass to protect from the cold.

column3: Damp in a way you dislike, of air, rooms, walls or clothes: 天气潮湿, 阴暗潮湿. The opposite is 干燥. 湿 alone is just wet.
column6: Nánfāng de tiānqì hěn cháoshī.
column7: The weather in the south is very damp.
column9: Damp in a way you dislike, of air, rooms, walls or clothes: 天氣潮濕, 陰暗潮濕. The opposite is 乾燥. 溼 alone is just wet.

column3: The opposite is 干: 衣服湿了, 湿透了 (soaked), 湿度 (humidity). It also gives 湿巾, a wet wipe.
column4: 下雨了，我的衣服都湿了。
column5: 下雨了，我的衣服都濕了。
column6: Xià yǔ le, wǒ de yīfu dōu shī le.
column7: It rained and my clothes are all wet.
column9: The opposite is 乾: 衣服溼了, 溼透了 (soaked), 溼度 (humidity). It also gives 溼巾, a wet wipe.

column3: Lightning is 闪电 and a flash 闪光. As a verb it also means to dodge, 闪开 (get out of the way), and to strain a muscle: 闪了腰. 闪婚 is marrying in a flash. It pictures a person in a gate: a person running through a gate.
column6: Tiānkōng shǎn le yīxià.
column7: The sky flashed.
column9: Lightning is 閃電 and a flash 閃光. As a verb it also means to dodge, 閃開 (get out of the way), and to strain a muscle: 閃了腰. 閃婚 is marrying in a flash. It pictures a person in a gate: a person running through a gate.

column3: It counts with 道 (一道闪电) and sits next to 打雷 in storm talk: 又打雷又闪电. On its own 闪 is the verb to flash, as in 闪光灯, a camera flash.
column6: Wǒ kànjiàn yī dào shǎndiàn.
column7: I saw a flash of lightning.
column9: It counts with 道 (一道閃電) and sits next to 打雷 in storm talk: 又打雷又閃電. On its own 閃 is the verb to flash, as in 閃光燈, a camera flash.

column3: A verb-object, so the count goes inside: 打了一个雷. The rumble is 打雷 and the flash is 闪电; people say 打雷下雨 for a storm. 打 is a light verb that goes with many objects, as in 打电话.
column6: Wàimiàn zài dǎléi, nǐ pà ma?
column7: It's thundering outside. Are you afraid?
column9: A verb-object, so the count goes inside: 打了一個雷. The rumble is 打雷 and the flash is 閃電; people say 打雷下雨 for a storm. 打 is a light verb that goes with many objects, as in 打電話.

column3: The forecast word for the temperature falling, usually followed by advice to dress warmer: 大幅降温 is a sharp drop. The opposite is 升温, and the amount follows: 降温五度.
column4: 明天会降温，多穿点儿衣服。
column5: 明天會降溫，多穿點兒衣服。
column6: Míngtiān huì jiàngwēn, duō chuān diǎnr yīfu.
column7: It will get colder tomorrow, so wear more clothes.
column9: The forecast word for the temperature falling, usually followed by advice to dress warmer: 大幅降溫 is a sharp drop. The opposite is 升溫, and the amount follows: 降溫五度.

column3: A written, scenic word for ice and snow together: 冰雪运动 means winter sports, and 冰雪世界 a winter wonderland. In speech you say 冰 and 雪 separately. 冰 was first written as just 冫, and 水 was added later.
column6: Shān shàng de bīngxuě kāishǐ huà le.
column7: The ice and snow on the mountain are starting to melt.
column9: A written, scenic word for ice and snow together: 冰雪運動 means winter sports, and 冰雪世界 a winter wonderland. In speech you say 冰 and 雪 separately. 冰 was first written as just 冫, and 水 was added later.

column3: Putting something in the sun: 晒太阳 to sunbathe, 晒衣服 to dry laundry, 晒黑 to get tanned. Online it also means to post and show off: 晒照片, 晒幸福.
column6: Tāmen zài yángtái shàng shài yīfu.
column7: They are drying clothes on the balcony.
column9: Putting something in the sun: 曬太陽 to sunbathe, 曬衣服 to dry laundry, 曬黑 to get tanned. Online it also means to post and show off: 曬照片, 曬幸福.

column3: Dark of a place or a color: 房间很暗, 暗红色. The opposite is 亮. It also means hidden or secret: 暗中 is in secret and 暗恋 a secret crush.
column6: Fángjiān lǐ tài àn le, kāi dēng ba.
column7: It's too dark in the room. Let's turn on the light.
column9: Dark of a place or a color: 房間很暗, 暗紅色. The opposite is 亮. It also means hidden or secret: 暗中 is in secret and 暗戀 a secret crush.

column3: Both literal (a dark room) and figurative: corrupt or cruel conditions, as in 黑暗的社会, with 光明 as the opposite. For an ordinary dim room people usually say 很暗.
column6: Tā pà hēi'àn.
column7: He is afraid of the dark.
column9: Both literal (a dark room) and figurative: corrupt or cruel conditions, as in 黑暗的社會, with 光明 as the opposite. For an ordinary dim room people usually say 很暗.

column3: Two jobs: a verb for light or air getting through (透气, 透明), and a complement after a verb or adjective meaning thoroughly: 湿透, 看透, 熟透, 累透了.
column6: Yángguāng cóng chuānghu tòu jìnlái.
column7: Sunlight comes in through the window.
column9: Two jobs: a verb for light or air getting through (透氣, 透明), and a complement after a verb or adjective meaning thoroughly: 濕透, 看透, 熟透, 累透了.

column3: Bus, a loanword from English: 坐巴士. It is the usual word in Hong Kong and Singapore; in Taiwan a city bus is 公车. On the mainland, 公共汽车 or 公交车 is used for city buses, and 大巴 for coaches. Both 巴 and 士 are used only for their sounds.
column6: Wǒmen zuò bāshì qù jīchǎng.
column7: We take the bus to the airport.
column9: Bus, a loanword from English: 坐巴士. It is the usual word in Hong Kong and Singapore; in Taiwan a city bus is 公車. On the mainland, 公共汽車 or 公交車 is used for city buses, and 大巴 for coaches. Both 巴 and 士 are used only for their sounds.

column3: On the mainland, the coach used for tours and trips between towns (旅游大巴, 长途大巴), while a city bus is 公交车. In Taiwan a tour coach is 游览车 and a city bus 公车.
column6: Wǒmen zuò dàbā qù lǚyóu.
column7: We take a coach on our trip.
