column9: On the mainland, the coach used for tours and trips between towns (旅遊大巴, 長途大巴), while a city bus is 公交車. In Taiwan a tour coach is 遊覽車 and a city bus 公車.

column3: High-speed rail: 坐高铁, 高铁站. It is short for 高速铁路. 铁 means iron.
column4: 坐高铁去北京只要四个小时。
column5: 坐高鐵去北京只要四個小時。
column6: Zuò gāotiě qù Běijīng zhǐyào sì ge xiǎoshí.
column7: By high-speed train it takes only four hours to get to Beijing.
column9: High-speed rail: 坐高鐵, 高鐵站. It is short for 高速鐵路. 鐵 means iron.

column3: Names a scheduled flight by its number and time, not the aircraft: 航班号, 航班延误, 取消航班. The plane itself is 飞机.
column6: Zhège hángbān wǎndiǎn le.
column7: This flight is delayed.
column9: Names a scheduled flight by its number and time, not the aircraft: 航班號, 航班延誤, 取消航班. The plane itself is 飛機.

column3: Rarely used alone; it fills compounds about air travel: 航空公司, 航空邮件, 航空母舰. The airline's name often carries it, as in 中国国际航空.
column4: 这家航空公司的服务很好。
column5: 這家航空公司的服務很好。
column6: Zhè jiā hángkōng gōngsī de fúwù hěn hǎo.
column7: This airline's service is very good.
column9: Rarely used alone; it fills compounds about air travel: 航空公司, 航空郵件, 航空母艦. The airline's name often carries it, as in 中國國際航空.

column3: A bit dated: it names the engine-driven steamer, as against a sailing boat. Today people say just 船, and a cruise ship is 游轮.
column6: Wǒmen zuò lúnchuán guò jiāng.
column7: We take a ferry across the river.
column9: A bit dated: it names the engine-driven steamer, as against a sailing boat. Today people say just 船, and a cruise ship is 遊輪.

column3: The spoken word for a wheel on a car, suitcase or chair, counted with 个. 轮 also turns up in 轮船 and 轮椅, and the 子 is just a noun ending.
column6: Zhè liàng chē yǒu sì ge lúnzi.
column7: This car has four wheels.
column9: The spoken word for a wheel on a car, suitcase or chair, counted with 個. 輪 also turns up in 輪船 and 輪椅, and the 子 is just a noun ending.

column3: You use one with 坐 (坐轮椅) and push someone with 推: 推着轮椅. A plain chair is 椅子.
column6: Tā zuò lúnyǐ chūmén.
column7: He goes out in a wheelchair.
column9: You use one with 坐 (坐輪椅) and push someone with 推: 推著輪椅. A plain chair is 椅子.

column3: The formal word for a train, heard in station announcements, timetables and news: 高速列车, 列车员, 列车到站. In casual talk people say 火车.
column6: Lièchē mǎshàng jiù yào chūfā le.
column7: The train is about to leave.
column9: The formal word for a train, heard in station announcements, timetables and news: 高速列車, 列車員, 列車到站. In casual talk people say 火車.

column3: On the mainland it mostly means an electric bike or scooter (骑电动车, 电动车充电); an electric car is 电动汽车 or 新能源汽车. In Taiwan an electric scooter is 电动机车.
column6: Tā měitiān qí diàndòngchē shàngbān.
column7: He rides an electric scooter to work every day.
column9: On the mainland it mostly means an electric bike or scooter (騎電動車, 電動車充電); an electric car is 電動汽車 or 新能源汽車. In Taiwan an electric scooter is 電動機車.

column3: Counted with 次: 倒两次车, and 换乘 is the more formal word. This is mainland speech; in Taiwan people say 转车 or 换车. 倒 read dào means to go backward.
column4: 在这儿倒车，然后坐三号线。
column5: 在這兒倒車，然後坐三號線。
column6: Zài zhèr dǎochē, ránhòu zuò sān hào xiàn.
column7: Change here, then take line three.
column9: Counted with 次: 倒兩次車, and 換乘 is the more formal word. This is mainland speech; in Taiwan people say 轉車 or 換車. 倒 read dào means to go backward.

column3: A driving word, heard from navigation and reversing alarms: 倒车入库, 倒车影像, 倒车灯. The spoken warning is 倒车，请注意. 倒 read dǎo means to change (trains or buses).
column6: Dàochē de shíhou yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: Be careful when you reverse.
column9: A driving word, heard from navigation and reversing alarms: 倒車入庫, 倒車影像, 倒車燈. The spoken warning is 倒車，請注意. 倒 read dǎo means to change (trains or buses).

column3: Blocks a road, pipe or hole: 堵住, 路堵了, 下水道堵了. It is also a feeling of being stuffed up or upset: 心里堵得慌. 堵车 is the everyday traffic use.
column6: Qiánmiàn de lù dǔ le.
column7: The road ahead is blocked.
column9: Blocks a road, pipe or hole: 堵住, 路堵了, 下水道堵了. It is also a feeling of being stuffed up or upset: 心裡堵得慌. 堵車 is the everyday traffic use.

column3: A verb-object, so a length of time goes inside: 堵了两个小时的车. It is the stock excuse for being late: 路上堵车了. On the mainland 堵车 is the usual word; in Taiwan 塞车 is.
column6: Jīntiān zǎoshang lùshang dǔchē le.
column7: There was a traffic jam on the road this morning.
column9: A verb-object, so a length of time goes inside: 堵了兩個小時的車. It is the stock excuse for being late: 路上堵車了. On the mainland 堵車 is the usual word; in Taiwan 塞車 is.

column3: A "gas station": 去加油站, 加油站在哪里？ 加油 is "to add fuel", and also "keep it up!" as a cheer; 站 is a "station" or "stop". 站 has 立 "stand" and 占 for the sound.
column6: Qiánmiàn yǒu yī ge jiāyóuzhàn.
column7: There is a gas station ahead.
column9: A "gas station": 去加油站, 加油站在哪裡？ 加油 is "to add fuel", and also "keep it up!" as a cheer; 站 is a "station" or "stop". 站 has 立 "stand" and 占 for the sound.

column3: Used for aircraft, spacecraft and parachutes: 飞机降落, 安全降落, 降落伞. The opposite is 起飞; 着陆 is the more technical touch down.
column4: 飞机将在十分钟后降落。
column5: 飛機將在十分鐘後降落。
column6: Fēijī jiāng zài shí fēnzhōng hòu jiàngluò.
column7: The plane will land in ten minutes.
column9: Used for aircraft, spacecraft and parachutes: 飛機降落, 安全降落, 降落傘. The opposite is 起飛; 著陸 is the more technical touch down.

column3: The written, signpost word for going on foot: 步行街 is a pedestrian street and 步行十分钟 a ten-minute walk. In speech 走路 is more usual. 步 shows one foot placed in front of the other.
column4: 从这里步行到学校要二十分钟。
column5: 從這裡步行到學校要二十分鐘。
column6: Cóng zhèlǐ bùxíng dào xuéxiào yào èrshí fēnzhōng.
column7: It takes twenty minutes to walk from here to the school.
column9: The written, signpost word for going on foot: 步行街 is a pedestrian street and 步行十分鐘 a ten-minute walk. In speech 走路 is more usual. 步 shows one foot placed in front of the other.

column3: Usually put before a noun: 长途汽车, 长途电话, 长途飞行. The opposite is 短途.
column6: Wǒ bù xǐhuan zuò chángtú qìchē.
column7: I don't like taking long-distance buses.
column9: Usually put before a noun: 長途汽車, 長途電話, 長途飛行. The opposite is 短途.

column3: 下 shows the movement ending: something that was moving halts, as in 车停下了 or 请停下. Often 停下来. For parking a car, 停车 is the word. It also fits interrupting work: 停下手里的工作.
column6: Chē tūrán tíngxià le.
column7: The car suddenly stopped.
column9: 下 shows the movement ending: something that was moving halts, as in 車停下了 or 請停下. Often 停下來. For parking a car, 停車 is the word. It also fits interrupting work: 停下手裡的工作.

column3: A bend in a road or river, counted with 个 (这条路有很多弯), and an adjective: 弯弯的路. 弯路 is a detour, and 走弯路 also means taking the wrong path in life. 拐弯 is the spoken turn.
column6: Zhè tiáo lù yǒu hěn duō wān.
column7: This road has many bends.
column9: A bend in a road or river, counted with 個 (這條路有很多彎), and an adjective: 彎彎的路. 彎路 is a detour, and 走彎路 also means taking the wrong path in life. 拐彎 is the spoken turn.

column3: A verb-object, so you can say 转了个弯. It is what road signs and navigation say, as in 前方转弯; in speech 拐弯 is a close, more colloquial word.
column6: Qiánmiàn lùkǒu qǐng xiàng yòu zhuǎnwān.
column7: Please turn right at the next intersection.
column9: A verb-object, so you can say 轉了個彎. It is what road signs and navigation say, as in 前方轉彎; in speech 拐彎 is a close, more colloquial word.

column3: An ordinary town street, as against 马路 for a bigger road. It is also an administrative subdistrict, the lowest level of city government: 街道办事处.
column6: Zhè tiáo jiēdào hěn ānjìng.
column7: This street is very quiet.
column9: An ordinary town street, as against 馬路 for a bigger road. It is also an administrative subdistrict, the lowest level of city government: 街道辦事處.

column3: The built-up center, as against 郊区, the suburbs: 住在市区, 市区交通. 市中心 is the very heart of it.
column6: Wǒ jiā lí shìqū hěn yuǎn.
column7: My home is far from the city center.
column9: The built-up center, as against 郊區, the suburbs: 住在市區, 市區交通. 市中心 is the very heart of it.

column3: A "county", an administrative unit below the city or prefecture: 县城 "county town", 县长 "county chief". A village belongs to a 乡 which belongs to a 县.
column6: Zhège xiàn yǒu wǔshí wàn rénkǒu.
column7: This county has five hundred thousand people.
column9: A "county", an administrative unit below the city or prefecture: 縣城 "county town", 縣長 "county chief". A village belongs to a 鄉 which belongs to a 縣.

column3: Continent or "the mainland": 中国大陆 "mainland China", 亚洲大陆. In Taiwan and Hong Kong 大陆 means mainland China, by contrast. People on the mainland speak of 内地 or 国内 for the same.
column6: Tā shì cóng Zhōngguó dàlù lái de.
column7: He is from mainland China.
column9: Continent or "the mainland": 中國大陸 "mainland China", 亞洲大陸. In Taiwan and Hong Kong 大陸 means mainland China, by contrast. People on the mainland speak of 內地 or 國內 for the same.

column3: Used for a street, email or web address: 家庭地址, 电子邮件地址, 网址. A Chinese address runs from largest to smallest: city, district, street, number.
column4: 请把你的地址写在这里。
column5: 請把你的地址寫在這裡。
column6: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de dìzhǐ xiě zài zhèlǐ.
column7: Please write your address here.
column9: Used for a street, email or web address: 家庭地址, 電子郵件地址, 網址. A Chinese address runs from largest to smallest: city, district, street, number.

column3: Where you 寄信 and 寄包裹 or 取包裹. 邮 turns up in 邮票 (stamp), 邮件 (mail) and 邮箱 (mailbox), and 局 names an office, as in 警察局.
column6: Wǒ yào qù yóujú jì xìn.
column7: I'm going to the post office to mail a letter.
column9: Where you 寄信 and 寄包裹 or 取包裹. 郵 turns up in 郵票 (stamp), 郵件 (mail) and 郵箱 (mailbox), and 局 names an office, as in 警察局.

column3: Covers the service, the package and the courier: 寄快递, 取快递, 快递员, 快递柜. On the mainland it goes with online shopping; in Taiwan 宅配 is the everyday word for home delivery.
column6: Wǒ de kuàidì jīntiān dào le.
column7: My package arrived today.
column9: Covers the service, the package and the courier: 寄快遞, 取快遞, 快遞員, 快遞櫃. On the mainland it goes with online shopping; in Taiwan 宅配 is the everyday word for home delivery.

column3: 快递 is the service and 包裹 the item itself: 取包裹, 寄包裹. As a verb it is to wrap up: 包裹伤口. 包 alone also makes 书包, 钱包 and 面包. 包 pictured a fetus in the womb, or a swaddled baby.
column6: Yóujú tōngzhī wǒ qù qǔ bāoguǒ.
column7: The post office told me to pick up a parcel.
column9: 快遞 is the service and 包裹 the item itself: 取包裹, 寄包裹. As a verb it is to wrap up: 包裹傷口. 包 alone also makes 書包, 錢包 and 麵包. 包 pictured a fetus in the womb, or a swaddled baby.

column3: A school's sports field with a running track: 在操场上跑步. 操 also means drill, as in 早操 and 体操. A stadium is 体育场.
column6: Xuéshengmen zài cāochǎng shàng pǎobù.
column7: The students are running on the sports field.
column9: A school's sports field with a running track: 在操場上跑步. 操 also means drill, as in 早操 and 體操. A stadium is 體育場.

column3: General merchandise: it is found in 百货商店 or 百货公司 "department store", 日用百货 "daily goods". 百 is "hundred" and 货 "goods", so a hundred kinds of goods.
column4: 周末我们去百货商店买东西。
column5: 週末我們去百貨商店買東西。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù bǎihuò shāngdiàn mǎi dōngxi.
column7: At the weekend we go to the department store to shop.
column9: General merchandise: it is found in 百貨商店 or 百貨公司 "department store", 日用百貨 "daily goods". 百 is "hundred" and 貨 "goods", so a hundred kinds of goods.

column3: A formal, written word: 居住在上海, 居住条件, 居住证. In speech 住 is the common verb. 居 recurs in 居民 (resident) and 邻居 (neighbor).
column6: Tā yīzhí jūzhù zài Shànghǎi.
column7: He has always lived in Shanghai.
column9: A formal, written word: 居住在上海, 居住條件, 居住證. In speech 住 is the common verb. 居 recurs in 居民 (resident) and 鄰居 (neighbor).

column3: Both a verb and a noun, and it covers either direction: 移民到加拿大, 新移民. 民 marks a kind of people, as in 市民 and 农民, and 移 recurs in 移动.
column4: 他们打算移民到加拿大。
column5: 他們打算移民到加拿大。
column6: Tāmen dǎsuàn yímín dào Jiānádà.
column7: They plan to emigrate to Canada.
column9: Both a verb and a noun, and it covers either direction: 移民到加拿大, 新移民. 民 marks a kind of people, as in 市民 and 農民, and 移 recurs in 移動.

column3: Names the person (一位导游) and also the verb. 导 recurs in 领导 (leader) and 导航 (navigation), always leading someone.
column4: 导游带我们参观了古城。
column5: 導遊帶我們參觀了古城。
column6: Dǎoyóu dài wǒmen cānguān le gǔchéng.
column7: The guide took us around the old town.
column9: Names the person (一位導遊) and also the verb. 導 recurs in 領導 (leader) and 導航 (navigation), always leading someone.

column3: Strolling for pleasure with no strict aim: 逛街, 逛商店, 逛公园, even 逛淘宝 online. You may buy nothing, which is why it differs from 买东西.
column4: 我们在商场里逛了一下午。
column5: 我們在商場裡逛了一下午。
column6: Wǒmen zài shāngchǎng lǐ guàng le yī xiàwǔ.
column7: We strolled around the mall all afternoon.
column9: Strolling for pleasure with no strict aim: 逛街, 逛商店, 逛公園, even 逛淘寶 online. You may buy nothing, which is why it differs from 買東西.

column3: Climbing up to a high place, a bit formal: 登山, 登长城, 登上山顶. Also to publish (登报), to log in (登录) and to board a plane (登机, 登机牌).
column6: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎoshang dēng Chángchéng.
column7: Tomorrow morning we are climbing the Great Wall.
column9: Climbing up to a high place, a bit formal: 登山, 登長城, 登上山頂. Also to publish (登報), to log in (登錄) and to board a plane (登機, 登機牌).

column3: Sounds more like mountaineering than 爬山, the everyday word for going up a hill. 登山者 is a climber and 登山鞋 hiking boots.
column6: Tā de àihào shì dēngshān.
column7: His hobby is mountain climbing.
column9: Sounds more like mountaineering than 爬山, the everyday word for going up a hill. 登山者 is a climber and 登山鞋 hiking boots.

column3: What you look at: lakes, mountains, a town. 欣赏风景, 风景区 and 风景画. For a scene with feeling, see 情景. 景 also appears in 景色 and 景点 (a sight).
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng zhēn měi.
column7: The scenery here is really beautiful.
column9: What you look at: lakes, mountains, a town. 欣賞風景, 風景區 and 風景畫. For a scene with feeling, see 情景. 景 also appears in 景色 and 景點 (a sight).

column3: The customs of a place or a people, such as festivals, food and manners: 当地的风俗, 风俗习惯. A personal habit is 习惯, not 风俗, and 习俗 is a close near-synonym.
column4: 每个地方的风俗都不一样。
column5: 每個地方的風俗都不一樣。
column6: Měi ge dìfang de fēngsú dōu bù yīyàng.
column7: Every place has different customs.
column9: The customs of a place or a people, such as festivals, food and manners: 當地的風俗, 風俗習慣. A personal habit is 習慣, not 風俗, and 習俗 is a close near-synonym.

column3: A verb-object: 拍张照, 拍了很多照; ask a passerby 帮我们拍张照. 拍 is also the verb for filming: 拍视频, 拍电影. 照相 means the same.
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒmen pāizhào.
column7: Please take a photo of us.
column9: A verb-object: 拍張照, 拍了很多照; ask a passerby 幫我們拍張照. 拍 is also the verb for filming: 拍視頻, 拍電影. 照相 means the same.

column3: The lens of a camera, and a shot in a film: 一个镜头, 长镜头. Being on camera is 上镜头. Here 头 is only a noun ending.
column6: Qǐng kàn jìngtóu, xiào yī xiào.
column7: Look at the camera and smile.
column9: The lens of a camera, and a shot in a film: 一個鏡頭, 長鏡頭. Being on camera is 上鏡頭. Here 頭 is only a noun ending.

column3: A "photograph": 一张相片, 洗相片 "develop photos". 相 is read xiàng here, "appearance, picture", not xiāng. Taiwan uses 相片 a lot; on the mainland 照片 is more usual. 片 is a "piece, flat thing".
column6: Qiáng shàng guàzhe yī zhāng xiàngpiàn.
column7: A photograph is hanging on the wall.
column9: A "photograph": 一張相片, 洗相片 "develop photos". 相 is read xiàng here, "appearance, picture", not xiāng. Taiwan uses 相片 a lot; on the mainland 照片 is more usual. 片 is a "piece, flat thing".

column3: Used for rooms, tickets, tables and goods: 预订酒店, 预订机票, 提前预订. Don't mix it with 预定, which means to schedule something in advance. For an appointment with a person, use 预约.
column6: Wǒ yǐjīng yùdìng le jīpiào.
column7: I have already booked the flight.
column9: Used for rooms, tickets, tables and goods: 預訂酒店, 預訂機票, 提前預訂. Don't mix it with 預定, which means to schedule something in advance. For an appointment with a person, use 預約.

column3: A polite word for a guest's visit, used by shops and hotels: 欢迎光临 on the door, 欢迎再次光临 on leaving. Never use it of yourself.
column6: Huānyíng guānglín! Qǐngwèn jǐ wèi?
column7: Welcome! How many in your party?
column9: A polite word for a guest's visit, used by shops and hotels: 歡迎光臨 on the door, 歡迎再次光臨 on leaving. Never use it of yourself.

column3: Goes with a stretch of time, often a happy or hard one: 度过假期, 度过童年, 度过难关, 度过愉快的一天. Not for a single moment.
column4: 我们在海边度过了一个周末。
column5: 我們在海邊度過了一個週末。
column6: Wǒmen zài hǎibiān dùguò le yī ge zhōumò.
column7: We spent a weekend at the beach.
column9: Goes with a stretch of time, often a happy or hard one: 度過假期, 度過童年, 度過難關, 度過愉快的一天. Not for a single moment.

column3: A written word for on the way, placed after a place or a phrase with 的: 旅行途中, 在去机场的途中. In speech 路上 is more usual.
column4: 在去机场的途中，我们遇到了堵车。
column5: 在去機場的途中，我們遇到了堵車。
column6: Zài qù jīchǎng de túzhōng, wǒmen yùdào le dǔchē.
column7: On the way to the airport we ran into a traffic jam.
column9: A written word for on the way, placed after a place or a phrase with 的: 旅行途中, 在去機場的途中. In speech 路上 is more usual.

column3: A scene with feeling that you see or remember: 感人的情景, 想起当时的情景. For a landscape, say 风景. In textbooks 情景对话 is a dialogue set in a situation.
column4: 我还记得第一次见面的情景。
column5: 我還記得第一次見面的情景。
column6: Wǒ hái jìde dì yī cì jiànmiàn de qíngjǐng.
column7: I still remember the scene of our first meeting.
column9: A scene with feeling that you see or remember: 感人的情景, 想起當時的情景. For a landscape, say 風景. In textbooks 情景對話 is a dialogue set in a situation.

column3: What you do at a counter or on a form: 登记入住 is checking in at a hotel, 结婚登记 registering a marriage, and 登记处 the registration desk.
column6: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ dēngjì yīxià.
column7: Please register here.
column9: What you do at a counter or on a form: 登記入住 is checking in at a hotel, 結婚登記 registering a marriage, and 登記處 the registration desk.

column3: The last days of the month, common for deadlines, rent and pay: 月底前. The start is 月初. 底 marks the end of a period in 年底 too.
column6: Wǒ yuèdǐ yào bānjiā.
column7: I'm moving at the end of the month.
column9: The last days of the month, common for deadlines, rent and pay: 月底前. The start is 月初. 底 marks the end of a period in 年底 too.

column3: It names the quarters of a business year: 第一季度, 第二季度. Reports and economic news use it; in everyday talk people just say 三个月 for three months.
column4: 公司今年第一季度的收入增加了。
column5: 公司今年第一季度的收入增加了。
column6: Gōngsī jīnnián dì yī jìdù de shōurù zēngjiā le.
column7: The company's income rose in the first quarter this year.
column9: It names the quarters of a business year: 第一季度, 第二季度. Reports and economic news use it; in everyday talk people just say 三個月 for three months.

column3: A time word that goes before the verb. The measure word 个 sits between 上 and 月, and the same pattern gives 下个月 and 这个月; for weeks it is 上个星期.
column6: Wǒ shànggeyuè qù le Shànghǎi.
column7: I went to Shanghai last month.
column9: A time word that goes before the verb. The measure word 個 sits between 上 and 月, and the same pattern gives 下個月 and 這個月; for weeks it is 上個星期.

column3: A time word, so it goes at the start of the clause or before the verb: 下个月我要出差. The pair is 上个月 for last month and 这个月 for this month.
column6: Xiàgeyuè wǒ yào qù Běijīng.
column7: Next month I am going to Beijing.
column9: A time word, so it goes at the start of the clause or before the verb: 下個月我要出差. The pair is 上個月 for last month and 這個月 for this month.

column3: It means a long stretch, not an exact number: 多年前 is years ago, 多年来 is over the years, and 多年的朋友 is a friend of long standing. In 多, the two 夕 were once two pieces of meat, and one writer suggests that two pieces of meat meant a lot when meat was scarce.
column6: Tā zài zhèlǐ gōngzuò le duōnián.
column7: He has worked here for many years.
column9: It means a long stretch, not an exact number: 多年前 is years ago, 多年來 is over the years, and 多年的朋友 is a friend of long standing. In 多, the two 夕 were once two pieces of meat, and one writer suggests that two pieces of meat meant a lot when meat was scarce.

column3: A more formal way of saying 很多次. It goes before the verb (多次提醒) or after 过 (去过多次), and often turns up in news and reports.
column6: Wǒ qù guo nàlǐ duōcì.
column7: I have been there many times.
column9: A more formal way of saying 很多次. It goes before the verb (多次提醒) or after 過 (去過多次), and often turns up in news and reports.

column3: It follows the noun that names the period: 春节期间, 比赛期间, 学习期间. It covers a stretch of time with something going on, never a single moment.
column4: 春节期间，很多商店不开门。
column5: 春節期間，很多商店不開門。
column6: Chūnjié qījiān, hěn duō shāngdiàn bù kāimén.
column7: During the Spring Festival many stores are closed.
column9: It follows the noun that names the period: 春節期間, 比賽期間, 學習期間. It covers a stretch of time with something going on, never a single moment.

column3: It is the time allowed for something, in contracts, loans and homework: 超过期限, 在期限内, 没有期限. The exact end date is the 截止日期.
column4: 这份合同的期限是一年。
column5: 這份合同的期限是一年。
column6: Zhè fèn hétong de qīxiàn shì yī nián.
column7: The term of this contract is one year.
column9: It is the time allowed for something, in contracts, loans and homework: 超過期限, 在期限內, 沒有期限. The exact end date is the 截止日期.

column3: A step in a process, a project or a life: 第一阶段, 不同的阶段. 现阶段 means at this stage, and 进入…阶段 means to enter a stage.
column4: 这个项目已经进入第二阶段。
column5: 這個項目已經進入第二階段。
column6: Zhège xiàngmù yǐjīng jìnrù dì èr jiēduàn.
column7: This project has already entered its second stage.
column9: A step in a process, a project or a life: 第一階段, 不同的階段. 現階段 means at this stage, and 進入…階段 means to enter a stage.

column3: It sets the present against the past, and it is more written than 现在: 如今，很多人… Put it at the start of a sentence or before the verb.
column4: 如今，很多人都用手机付钱。
column5: 如今，很多人都用手機付錢。
column6: Rújīn, hěn duō rén dōu yòng shǒujī fù qián.
column7: Nowadays many people pay with their phones.
column9: It sets the present against the past, and it is more written than 現在: 如今，很多人… Put it at the start of a sentence or before the verb.

column3: It is also a modifier: 未来的计划, 未来几天 for the next few days. The opposite is 过去, and 将来 is the more spoken way to say in the future.
column6: Nǐ duì wèilái yǒu shénme dǎsuàn?
column7: What are your plans for the future?
column9: It is also a modifier: 未來的計劃, 未來幾天 for the next few days. The opposite is 過去, and 將來 is the more spoken way to say in the future.

column3: It marks the very start of a process: 最初的想法, or 最初， at the start of a sentence. In speech, 一开始 is more common.
column4: 最初，我一句中文也不会说。
column5: 最初，我一句中文也不會說。
column6: Zuìchū, wǒ yī jù Zhōngwén yě bù huì shuō.
column7: At first I couldn't say a word of Chinese.
column9: It marks the very start of a process: 最初的想法, or 最初， at the start of a sentence. In speech, 一開始 is more common.

column3: It follows a noun or a verb phrase: 睡觉之前, 三年之前. It is a shade more formal than 以前, and the opposite is 之后. In 前, an older form shows a foot on a boat moving forward.
column6: Shuìjiào zhīqián, wǒ xǐhuan kàn shū.
column7: Before going to bed, I like to read.
column9: It follows a noun or a verb phrase: 睡覺之前, 三年之前. It is a shade more formal than 以前, and the opposite is 之後. In 前, an older form shows a foot on a boat moving forward.

column3: It follows the phrase it modifies (下班之后, 三天之后) and can also open a sentence: 之后，我们… The opposite is 之前, and it is a bit more formal than 以后.
column4: 下班之后，我们去吃饭吧。
column5: 下班之後，我們去吃飯吧。
column6: Xiàbān zhīhòu, wǒmen qù chīfàn ba.
column7: After work, let's go and eat.
column9: It follows the phrase it modifies (下班之後, 三天之後) and can also open a sentence: 之後，我們… The opposite is 之前, and it is a bit more formal than 以後.

column3: It sets a limit on time, distance or number, and the limit itself counts: 三天以内, 一公里以内, 十岁以内. The opposite is 以外.
column6: Qǐng zài sān tiān yǐnèi wánchéng.
column7: Please finish it within three days.
column9: It sets a limit on time, distance or number, and the limit itself counts: 三天以內, 一公里以內, 十歲以內. The opposite is 以外.

column3: It follows the two things joined by 和 (医院和银行之间) or a plural noun (朋友之间). It gives a position, a relationship or a range.
column4: 学校在医院和银行之间。
column5: 學校在醫院和銀行之間。
column6: Xuéxiào zài yīyuàn hé yínháng zhījiān.
column7: The school is between the hospital and the bank.
column9: It follows the two things joined by 和 (醫院和銀行之間) or a plural noun (朋友之間). It gives a position, a relationship or a range.

column3: A general word for the activity of shopping: 购物中心, 网上购物, 去购物. For buying one particular thing, use 买.
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan zài wǎngshàng gòuwù.
column7: I like shopping online.
column9: A general word for the activity of shopping: 購物中心, 網上購物, 去購物. For buying one particular thing, use 買.

column3: It is more formal than 买 and suits websites, notices and writing: 购买机票, 在线购买, 购买力. The thing bought is usually of some value, or a service.
column4: 你可以在网上购买火车票。
column5: 你可以在網上購買火車票。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ zài wǎngshàng gòumǎi huǒchēpiào.
column7: You can buy train tickets online.
column9: It is more formal than 買 and suits websites, notices and writing: 購買機票, 在線購買, 購買力. The thing bought is usually of some value, or a service.

column3: It belongs to ads and signs rather than speech, where people say 卖: 房屋出售, 出售商品. The thing being sold is usually a house, a car or goods.
column6: Zhè tào fángzi zhèngzài chūshòu.
column7: This apartment is for sale.
column9: It belongs to ads and signs rather than speech, where people say 賣: 房屋出售, 出售商品. The thing being sold is usually a house, a car or goods.

column3: On its own it needs a verb or a modifier: 一批货, 进货 for stocking up, 发货 for shipping out. 货物 is cargo, and 货币 is currency.
column6: Zhè pī huò míngtiān jiù dào.
column7: This batch of goods arrives tomorrow.
column9: On its own it needs a verb or a modifier: 一批貨, 進貨 for stocking up, 發貨 for shipping out. 貨物 is cargo, and 貨幣 is currency.

column3: It is what signs and tags say: 特价商品, 今日特价. It can also be the predicate, as in 这件衣服特价. Compare 打折, where a share is taken off the price.
column6: Jīntiān zhè jiàn yīfu tèjià.
column7: This item of clothing is on sale today.
column9: It is what signs and tags say: 特價商品, 今日特價. It can also be the predicate, as in 這件衣服特價. Compare 打折, where a share is taken off the price.

column3: A verb and its object, so 打了折. A number goes before 折: 打八折 means 20% off, since you pay eight tenths. 打折扣 is also figurative, for falling short.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn xiànzài dǎzhé.
column7: This store has a sale now.
column9: A verb and its object, so 打了折. A number goes before 折: 打八折 means 20% off, since you pay eight tenths. 打折扣 is also figurative, for falling short.

column3: In prices, 折 counts tenths of the full price that you still pay: 七折 is 70%, so 30% off. Elsewhere it means to fold or break, as in 折纸 and 骨折. An older form of 折 was an axe cutting a tree in half.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu dǎ qī zhé.
column7: This item is 30% off.
column9: In prices, 折 counts tenths of the full price that you still pay: 七折 is 70%, so 30% off. Elsewhere it means to fold or break, as in 摺紙 and 骨折. An older form of 折 was an axe cutting a tree in half.

column3: A verb and its object, so 降了价. The opposite is 涨价, and 大降价 is a big sale. It also describes goods getting cheaper on the market, not only a store's sale. 降 pictures going down a hill, with 阝 as the hill.
column6: Zhè kuǎn shǒujī jiàngjià le.
column7: This phone has gone down in price.
column9: A verb and its object, so 降了價. The opposite is 漲價, and 大降價 is a big sale. It also describes goods getting cheaper on the market, not only a store's sale. 降 pictures going down a hill, with 阝 as the hill.

column3: It goes before a verb (高价购买, 高价出售) and often hints at paying more than it is worth. As a predicate, 'expensive' is 贵, and the opposite of 高价 is 低价.
column4: 他用高价买了一块手表。
column5: 他用高價買了一塊手錶。
column6: Tā yòng gāojià mǎi le yī kuài shǒubiǎo.
column7: He bought a watch at a high price.
column9: It goes before a verb (高價購買, 高價出售) and often hints at paying more than it is worth. As a predicate, 'expensive' is 貴, and the opposite of 高價 is 低價.

column3: It is the standard word on signs and ads: 免费的, 免费提供, 免费试用. In speech, 不要钱 is the casual way to say it costs nothing. 免 plus a noun means free of it, as in 免税.
column6: Zhèlǐ de tíngchē shì miǎnfèi de.
column7: Parking here is free.
column9: It is the standard word on signs and ads: 免費的, 免費提供, 免費試用. In speech, 不要錢 is the casual way to say it costs nothing. 免 plus a noun means free of it, as in 免稅.

column3: An "invoice, receipt" the official tax receipt: 开发票 "issue a receipt", 要发票 "ask for a receipt". 发 is "to issue", 票 a "ticket". Taiwan's 统一发票 also works as a lottery ticket.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ kāi yī zhāng fāpiào.
column7: Please issue me a receipt.
column9: An "invoice, receipt" the official tax receipt: 開發票 "issue a receipt", 要發票 "ask for a receipt". 發 is "to issue", 票 a "ticket". Taiwan's 統一發票 also works as a lottery ticket.

column3: It is what stores do: 促销活动, 促销价, 搞促销. It covers sales events, discounts and free gifts, all meant to get people to buy.
column6: Shāngchǎng zhèngzài gǎo cùxiāo huódòng.
column7: The mall is running a promotion.
column9: It is what stores do: 促銷活動, 促銷價, 搞促銷. It covers sales events, discounts and free gifts, all meant to get people to buy.

column3: The seller goes to the customer, so it can sound pushy: 推销产品, 推销保险, and 推销员 for a salesperson. 销售 is the neutral business word.
column4: 他想向我推销一个新产品。
column5: 他想向我推銷一個新產品。
column6: Tā xiǎng xiàng wǒ tuīxiāo yī ge xīn chǎnpǐn.

column9: The seller goes to the customer, so it can sound pushy: 推銷產品, 推銷保險, and 推銷員 for a salesperson. 銷售 is the neutral business word.

column3: The business word for selling, in volume and as a job: 销售额, 销售员, 做销售. It is neutral, unlike the pushier 推销.
column6: Tā zài yī jiā gōngsī zuò xiāoshòu.
column7: He works in sales at a company.
column9: The business word for selling, in volume and as a job: 銷售額, 銷售員, 做銷售. It is neutral, unlike the pushier 推銷.

column3: It works as a verb and as a modifier: 进口水果, 进口的. It is also the entrance of a place, and the opposite 出口 is both export and exit.
column6: Zhèxiē shuǐguǒ shì jìnkǒu de.
column7: This fruit is imported.
column9: It works as a verb and as a modifier: 進口水果, 進口的. It is also the entrance of a place, and the opposite 出口 is both export and exit.

column3: To choose by looking over several things: 挑一件, 挑颜色. It can also mean to find fault, as in 挑毛病.
column6: Nǐ zìjǐ tiāo yī jiàn ba.
column7: Pick one yourself.
column9: To choose by looking over several things: 挑一件, 挑顏色. It can also mean to find fault, as in 挑毛病.

column3: A careful, slightly more formal 挑: 仔细挑选, 挑选礼物. The 选 alone also means to elect, as in 选举.
column6: Tā zài rènzhēn de tiāoxuǎn shuǐguǒ.
column7: She is carefully choosing fruit.
column9: A careful, slightly more formal 挑: 仔細挑選, 挑選禮物. The 選 alone also means to elect, as in 選舉.

column3: To set things out so they stay there: 摆在桌子上, 摆整齐, 摆摊. A second sense is to swing or wave back and forth, as in 摆手.
column6: Tā bǎ shū bǎi zài zhuōzi shàng.
column7: He put the books on the table.
column9: To set things out so they stay there: 擺在桌子上, 擺整齊, 擺攤. A second sense is to swing or wave back and forth, as in 擺手.

column3: It goes before the noun: 二手车, 二手房, 二手书. 二手烟 is secondhand smoke, and 二手 is also used for secondhand information.
column6: Zhè liàng chē shì èrshǒu de.
column7: This car is secondhand.
column9: It goes before the noun: 二手車, 二手房, 二手書. 二手煙 is secondhand smoke, and 二手 is also used for secondhand information.

column3: A verb and its object, so 抽了一次奖. Shops and companies run it (参加抽奖, 抽奖活动), and whoever is lucky then 中奖.

column7: When you shop you can enter the prize draw.
column9: A verb and its object, so 抽了一次獎. Shops and companies run it (參加抽獎, 抽獎活動), and whoever is lucky then 中獎.

column3: A verb and its object, and it is luck: 中了一等奖. Winning a contest on merit is 获奖. The 中 here is the reading that means to hit a target or to win a prize.
column6: Tā zhòngjiǎng le, fēicháng gāoxìng.
column7: He won a prize and is very happy.
column9: A verb and its object, and it is luck: 中了一等獎. Winning a contest on merit is 獲獎. The 中 here is the reading that means to hit a target or to win a prize.

column3: It is given at Spring Festival, weddings and birthdays. The verb is 发 (发红包), and in chat apps 抢红包 is grabbing a digital one from a group. Context decides if it is a bonus or a bribe.
column4: 过年的时候，爷爷给孩子们红包。
column5: 過年的時候，爺爺給孩子們紅包。

column9: It is given at Spring Festival, weddings and birthdays. The verb is 發 (發紅包), and in chat apps 搶紅包 is grabbing a digital one from a group. Context decides if it is a bonus or a bribe.

column3: It has several everyday senses: a sign (招牌), a brand (牌子, 名牌), and a playing card or mahjong tile (打牌). The measure word is 张 for cards and 块 for signs.
column6: Tā shǒu lǐ yǒu yī zhāng hǎo pái.
column7: He has a good card in his hand.
column9: It has several everyday senses: a sign (招牌), a brand (牌子, 名牌), and a playing card or mahjong tile (打牌). The measure word is 張 for cards and 塊 for signs.

column3: It is the erhua form of 名牌: the 儿 only adds an r sound at the end, and the meaning is the same.
column6: Tā xǐhuan chuān míngpáir.
column7: He likes to wear brand-name clothes.
column9: It is the erhua form of 名牌: the 兒 only adds an r sound at the end, and the meaning is the same.

column3: The usual word for what a company makes: 新产品, 电子产品, 产品质量. For goods as things on sale in a shop, 商品 is the word. 品 is three 口, standing for various objects.
column4: 这家公司的产品卖得很好。
column5: 這家公司的產品賣得很好。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de chǎnpǐn mài de hěn hǎo.
column7: This company's products sell well.
column9: The usual word for what a company makes: 新產品, 電子產品, 產品質量. For goods as things on sale in a shop, 商品 is the word. 品 is three 口, standing for various objects.

column3: It stresses the inherent quality of a thing, or a person's character: 品质好, 优良的品质. For product quality Taiwan says 品质 every day, where the mainland more often says 质量.
column6: Zhè zhǒng chǎnpǐn de pǐnzhì hěn gāo.
column7: This product is of high quality.
column9: It stresses the inherent quality of a thing, or a person's character: 品質好, 優良的品質. For product quality Taiwan says 品質 every day, where the mainland more often says 質量.

column3: The everyday word for how good something is: 质量好, 质量差, 质量问题. In Taiwan 质量 is mostly physics, and quality is 品质; on the mainland it covers both.
column4: 这家店的东西质量很好。
column5: 這家店的東西質量很好。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
column7: The goods in this store are of good quality.
column9: The everyday word for how good something is: 質量好, 質量差, 質量問題. In Taiwan 質量 is mostly physics, and quality is 品質; on the mainland it covers both.

column3: Two everyday senses: material to build or make things with (建筑材料), and papers or information you hand in or study (准备材料, 学习材料). Context decides which one is meant.
column4: 这些材料是从国外进口的。
column5: 這些材料是從國外進口的。
column6: Zhèxiē cáiliào shì cóng guówài jìnkǒu de.
column7: These materials are imported from abroad.
column9: Two everyday senses: material to build or make things with (建築材料), and papers or information you hand in or study (準備材料, 學習材料). Context decides which one is meant.

column3: It is the raw input that is turned into a product: 食品原料, 原料价格. 材料 is broader and can be any material or even papers. 原 shows a spring bursting from a cliff-side.
column4: 这些面包的原料很新鲜。
column5: 這些麵包的原料很新鮮。
column6: Zhèxiē miànbāo de yuánliào hěn xīnxiān.
column7: The ingredients of this bread are very fresh.
column9: It is the raw input that is turned into a product: 食品原料, 原料價格. 材料 is broader and can be any material or even papers. 原 shows a spring bursting from a cliff-side.

column3: Plastic: 塑料袋, 塑料瓶 "plastic bottle", 塑料制品. In Taiwan, 塑胶 is the more common word. 塑 means "to mold" and has 土 "earth", clay, at the bottom; 料 is "material".
column6: Zhège bēizi shì sùliào zuò de.
column7: This cup is made of plastic.
column9: Plastic: 塑料袋, 塑料瓶 "plastic bottle", 塑料制品. In Taiwan, 塑膠 is the more common word. 塑 means "to mold" and has 土 "earth", clay, at the bottom; 料 is "material".

column3: It covers anything burned for energy, such as coal, gasoline or gas: 燃料价格, 清洁燃料. A fuel cell is 燃料电池.
column4: 汽车需要燃料才能开动。
column5: 汽車需要燃料才能開動。
column6: Qìchē xūyào ránliào cáinéng kāidòng.
column7: A car needs fuel before it can move.
column9: It covers anything burned for energy, such as coal, gasoline or gas: 燃料價格, 清潔燃料. A fuel cell is 燃料電池.

column3: A neutral or scientific word for burning (燃烧起来, 完全燃烧). It is also figurative, as in 热情燃烧. In daily talk, 烧 is more common. 燃 got its 火 later: it was first written 然, but 然 was borrowed for abstract senses.
column6: Huǒ zài lúzi lǐ ránshāo.
column7: The fire is burning in the stove.
column9: A neutral or scientific word for burning (燃燒起來, 完全燃燒). It is also figurative, as in 熱情燃燒. In daily talk, 燒 is more common. 燃 got its 火 later: it was first written 然, but 然 was borrowed for abstract senses.

column3: It is what you say when something catches fire: 房子着火了, 容易着火. A fire breaking out is also 起火. 着 here is read zháo and means to catch fire, not the particle zhe that marks an ongoing state.

column9: It is what you say when something catches fire: 房子著火了, 容易著火. A fire breaking out is also 起火. 著 here is read zháo and means to catch fire, not the particle zhe that marks an ongoing state.

column3: Heat is the common idea: 烧火, 烧水 for boiling water, 烧菜 for cooking dishes, and 发烧 for running a fever.
column6: Wǒ qù shāo diǎnr shuǐ.
column7: I'll go and boil some water.
column9: Heat is the common idea: 燒火, 燒水 for boiling water, 燒菜 for cooking dishes, and 發燒 for running a fever.

column3: The car fuel: 加汽油 to fill up, 汽油车. The other common fuel is 柴油 for diesel, and 加油 is the short way to say fill up. One view sees 汽 as water 氵 in the form of air 气.

column9: The car fuel: 加汽油 to fill up, 汽油車. The other common fuel is 柴油 for diesel, and 加油 is the short way to say fill up. One view sees 汽 as water 氵 in the form of air 气.

column3: A general noun for what a place or an organization has to use: 自然资源, 水资源, 人力资源, 资源丰富. It can also be non-material, like 学习资源.

column9: A general noun for what a place or an organization has to use: 自然資源, 水資源, 人力資源, 資源豐富. It can also be non-material, like 學習資源.

column3: The power supply of a device: 打开电源, 电源线, 电源插座, and 电源键 for the power button. 源 also means source in 水源 and 资源.

column9: The power supply of a device: 打開電源, 電源線, 電源插座, and 電源鍵 for the power button. 源 also means source in 水源 and 資源.

column3: Said twice, 宝宝, it is a pet name for a baby, and 宝贝 is what you call a darling child or sweetheart. Beyond people, it names valuables: 国宝 is a national treasure.
column6: Tā bǎ zhè běn shū dàng chéng bǎo.
column7: He treats this book as a treasure.
column9: Said twice, 寶寶, it is a pet name for a baby, and 寶貝 is what you call a darling child or sweetheart. Beyond people, it names valuables: 國寶 is a national treasure.

column3: The word for cut gems in jewelry, named by color: 红宝石 is a ruby and 蓝宝石 a sapphire. A diamond has its own word, 钻石, and carved jade is 玉.

column9: The word for cut gems in jewelry, named by color: 紅寶石 is a ruby and 藍寶石 a sapphire. A diamond has its own word, 鑽石, and carved jade is 玉.

column3: For what money can't buy: time, experience, advice, a chance (宝贵的机会). 宝贵意见 is the polite way to ask for or thank someone for their feedback. For a price tag, use 贵.

column7: Time is very precious.
column9: For what money can't buy: time, experience, advice, a chance (寶貴的機會). 寶貴意見 is the polite way to ask for or thank someone for their feedback. For a price tag, use 貴.

column3: The stone China prizes most, a symbol of beauty and purity, and common in names. Things made of it: 玉镯 a bracelet, 玉器 jade ware. A dot was introduced to tell it apart from 王. It is also read as three pieces of jade strung together on a string.

column9: The stone China prizes most, a symbol of beauty and purity, and common in names. Things made of it: 玉鐲 a bracelet, 玉器 jade ware. A dot was introduced to tell it apart from 王. It is also read as three pieces of jade strung together on a string.

column9: Besides the metal, it means golden, meaning the best period or chance: 黃金時間 is prime time and 黃金時代 a golden age. Gold jewelry is 黃金首飾.

column3: US dollars: 二十美金, 兑换美金. This is the spoken word, particularly in Taiwan and overseas communities. The mainland says 美元 in formal use. 美 "American" and 金 "money, gold". It is also used with other currencies as 日金 or 港金.

column3: A banking and finance word: 兑换外汇 to exchange currency, 外汇储备 a country's reserves, 外汇市场 the currency market. In daily talk, say the currency itself, like 美元.

column3: A verb for sending money to someone, usually by bank transfer: 汇钱, and 汇款 for the payment or remittance. In 汇合 it is people or streams joining up. 汇率 is the exchange rate.

column3: Goes with the currency: 人民币汇率, 美元汇率. The same 率 ends other rates: 利率 interest rate, 比率 ratio, 增长率 growth rate.

column9: Goes with the currency: 人民幣匯率, 美元匯率. The same 率 ends other rates: 利率 interest rate, 比率 ratio, 增長率 growth rate.

column9: The money itself, earned on savings or owed on a loan: 付利息 pay interest, 利息很高 high interest. 利率 is the rate, as a percentage; 利息 is the amount.

column3: A bonus from an employer, such as 年终奖金 at year end, or prize money in a contest. Verbs: 发奖金 to hand it out, 拿奖金 or 领奖金 to receive it.

column3: What a person or family legally owns, money and houses alike: 个人财产, 继承财产. 房产 is real estate in particular. 财富 is wealth in the sense of riches, not ownership.

column3: More written than 钱, and it can mean value that isn't money: 创造财富, 一笔财富, 知识就是财富. Unlike 财产, it is about riches, not legal ownership.

column9: More written than 錢, and it can mean value that isn't money: 創造財富, 一筆財富, 知識就是財富. Unlike 財產, it is about riches, not legal ownership.

column3: Both verb and noun: 投资股票 to invest in stocks, 一项投资 an investment. A person who invests is 投资者 or 投资人. The same 投 puts in money, casts a ballot and sends in a letter or manuscript.

column3: The legal state of a company: 申请破产 file for it, 宣布破产 declare it. A person can go broke too, in the sense of being ruined. A shop that just shuts down is 倒闭.

column3: Interests as something at stake or to gain: 国家利益, 保护利益, 利益冲突 conflict of interest. Not interest as a hobby, which is 兴趣, nor bank interest, which is 利息.

column9: Interests as something at stake or to gain: 國家利益, 保護利益, 利益衝突 conflict of interest. Not interest as a hobby, which is 興趣, nor bank interest, which is 利息.

column3: A financial word for what an investment or business brings in: 投资收益, 收益率 the rate of return. 收益 is what comes in, 利息 is a bank's interest, 利益 is what you have at stake.
column6: Zhège tóuzī de shōuyì bù gāo.
column7: The return on this investment is not high.
column9: A financial word for what an investment or business brings in: 投資收益, 收益率 the rate of return. 收益 is what comes in, 利息 is a bank's interest, 利益 is what you have at stake.

column3: To vouch for a person or back a loan: 为他担保, 担保人 the guarantor, 担保贷款. In speech, 我担保 is simply I guarantee it, as in 我担保他不会迟到.
column6: Wǒ kěyǐ wèi tā dānbǎo.
column7: I can vouch for him.
column9: To vouch for a person or back a loan: 為他擔保, 擔保人 the guarantor, 擔保貸款. In speech, 我擔保 is simply I guarantee it, as in 我擔保他不會遲到.

column3: Takes what you give in hope of a result: 付出努力, 付出时间, 付出代价 pay a price, and the pair 付出和回报. To pay a bill, say 付钱 or 付款 instead.
column4: 成功需要付出很多努力。
column5: 成功需要付出很多努力。
column6: Chénggōng xūyào fùchū hěn duō nǔlì.
column7: Success takes a lot of effort.
column9: Takes what you give in hope of a result: 付出努力, 付出時間, 付出代價 pay a price, and the pair 付出和回報. To pay a bill, say 付錢 or 付款 instead.

column3: Both a noun and a verb: 经济负担 a financial burden, 减轻负担 lighten the load. 负担得起 means can afford, and 负担不起 means can't.
column4: 学费对这个家庭是一个很大的负担。
column5: 學費對這個家庭是一個很大的負擔。
column6: Xuéfèi duì zhège jiātíng shì yī ge hěn dà de fùdān.
column7: Tuition is a heavy burden for this family.
column9: Both a noun and a verb: 經濟負擔 a financial burden, 減輕負擔 lighten the load. 負擔得起 means can afford, and 負擔不起 means can't.

column3: To use less of time, money, water, energy: 节省时间, 节省开支. In speech, 省 alone does the same: 省钱, 省时间. 节约 is a near-synonym that fits slogans and campaigns.
column6: Wǒmen yào jiéshěng yòng shuǐ.
column7: We must save water.
column9: To use less of time, money, water, energy: 節省時間, 節省開支. In speech, 省 alone does the same: 省錢, 省時間. 節約 is a near-synonym that fits slogans and campaigns.

column3: The formal letter itself, with its type in front: 录取通知书 admission letter, 入学通知书, 缴费通知书. 通知 is the act of notifying, or any notice. 书 as a document also ends 说明书 instructions.
column4: 他收到了大学录取通知书。
column5: 他收到了大學錄取通知書。
column6: Tā shōudào le dàxué lùqǔ tōngzhīshū.
column7: He received his university admission letter.
column9: The formal letter itself, with its type in front: 錄取通知書 admission letter, 入學通知書, 繳費通知書. 通知 is the act of notifying, or any notice. 書 as a document also ends 說明書 instructions.

column3: The opposite of 富 and 有钱: 穷人, 越来越穷. Trap: feeling sorry for someone, as in poor thing, is 可怜, not 穷. In a few spoken phrases it means pointlessly, as in 穷忙 busy for nothing.
column6: Tā xiǎoshíhou jiālǐ hěn qióng.
column7: His family was very poor when he was a child.
column9: The opposite of 富 and 有錢: 窮人, 越來越窮. Trap: feeling sorry for someone, as in poor thing, is 可憐, not 窮. In a few spoken phrases it means pointlessly, as in 窮忙 busy for nothing.

column3: What someone leaves behind at death, in money or in culture: 继承遗产, 文化遗产, 世界遗产. 财产 is what one owns in life; 遗产 is the estate or legacy passed on.
column4: 长城是重要的文化遗产。
column5: 長城是重要的文化遺產。
column6: Chángchéng shì zhòngyào de wénhuà yíchǎn.
column7: The Great Wall is an important cultural heritage.
column9: What someone leaves behind at death, in money or in culture: 繼承遺產, 文化遺產, 世界遺產. 財產 is what one owns in life; 遺產 is the estate or legacy passed on.

column3: Counts whole plants standing upright: 一棵树, 一棵白菜 a head of cabbage, 一棵草. Cut flowers are counted with 朵 or 枝 instead. It is said to come from 窠, a pit for growing plants.
column6: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu sān kē shù.
column7: There are three trees in the yard.
column9: Counts whole plants standing upright: 一棵樹, 一棵白菜 a head of cabbage, 一棵草. Cut flowers are counted with 朵 or 枝 instead. It is said to come from 窠, a pit for growing plants.

column3: Counts long, thin things: 一根筷子, 一根绳子, 一根头发. As a noun it is a root, as in 树根, and a basis in 根本 fundamental and 根据 on the basis of.
column6: Tā shǒu lǐ názhe yī gēn shéngzi.
column7: He is holding a piece of rope in his hand.
column9: Counts long, thin things: 一根筷子, 一根繩子, 一根頭髮. As a noun it is a root, as in 樹根, and a basis in 根本 fundamental and 根據 on the basis of.

column3: Counts items of something official or organized: 一项任务, 一项计划, 一项比赛, 一项规定. Never things you can pick up.
column4: 这是一项很重要的工作。
column5: 這是一項很重要的工作。
column6: Zhè shì yī xiàng hěn zhòngyào de gōngzuò.
column7: This is a very important piece of work.
column9: Counts items of something official or organized: 一項任務, 一項計劃, 一項比賽, 一項規定. Never things you can pick up.

column3: Counts households: 一户人家, 三户. As a noun, a household or an account: 户口 residence registration, 账户 account, 开户 to open an account. It is a picture of one half of a gate, a single door.
column4: 这个村子只有几十户人家。
column5: 這個村子只有幾十戶人家。
column6: Zhège cūnzi zhǐ yǒu jǐshí hù rénjiā.
column7: This village has only a few dozen households.
column9: Counts households: 一戶人家, 三戶. As a noun, a household or an account: 戶口 residence registration, 帳戶 account, 開戶 to open an account. It is a picture of one half of a gate, a single door.

column3: Counts a batch that arrives or is handled together: 一批货, 一批学生, 第一批 the first batch or wave. As a verb it approves or criticizes: 批准, 批评.
column6: Dì yī pī kèrén yǐjīng dào le.
column7: The first group of guests has arrived.
column9: Counts a batch that arrives or is handled together: 一批貨, 一批學生, 第一批 the first batch or wave. As a verb it approves or criticizes: 批准, 批評.

column3: Counts songs and poems: 一首歌, 一首诗. Films and books take other measure words. For the head, speech says 头 now; 首 lives on in 首都 capital and 首先 first of all. It began as a picture of an animal's head with a long mouth and horns.
column6: Tā wèi wǒ chàng le yī shǒu gē.
column7: He sang me a song.
column9: Counts songs and poems: 一首歌, 一首詩. Films and books take other measure words. For the head, speech says 頭 now; 首 lives on in 首都 capital and 首先 first of all. It began as a picture of an animal's head with a long mouth and horns.

column3: Counts something sudden that passes: 一阵风, 一阵雨, 一阵笑声, 一阵疼. Never a lasting state. 一阵子 is a stretch of time, a while.
column6: Tūrán guā qǐ le yī zhèn dàfēng.
column7: A strong gust of wind suddenly blew up.
column9: Counts something sudden that passes: 一陣風, 一陣雨, 一陣笑聲, 一陣疼. Never a lasting state. 一陣子 is a stretch of time, a while.

column3: A circle or ring, a social circle (朋友圈, 娱乐圈 the entertainment world), and a lap: 跑了三圈. As a verb it means to circle something on paper: 圈出来.
column6: Tā wéizhe cāochǎng pǎo le sān quān.
column7: He ran three laps around the sports field.
column9: A circle or ring, a social circle (朋友圈, 娛樂圈 the entertainment world), and a lap: 跑了三圈. As a verb it means to circle something on paper: 圈出來.

column3: Counts rounds and turns: 一轮比赛, 第二轮, 一轮明月. As a noun, a wheel: 轮子, 轮船. As a verb it is to take turns: 轮到你了, 轮流.
column6: Xià yī lún gāi nǐ shuō le.
column7: In the next round it is your turn to speak.
column9: Counts rounds and turns: 一輪比賽, 第二輪, 一輪明月. As a noun, a wheel: 輪子, 輪船. As a verb it is to take turns: 輪到你了, 輪流.

column3: Spoken, and after a pronoun: 咱俩, 你们俩, 他们俩. It already holds the number and the measure word, so never add 两个 or another number after it.
column4: 我们俩是从小一起长大的。
column5: 我們倆是從小一起長大的。
column6: Wǒmen liǎ shì cóng xiǎo yīqǐ zhǎng dà de.
column7: The two of us grew up together.
column9: Spoken, and after a pronoun: 咱倆, 你們倆, 他們倆. It already holds the number and the measure word, so never add 兩個 or another number after it.

column3: The plural of this, that and which: 这些, 那些, 哪些; also 一些 and 有些. After an adjective it softens a comparison: 快一些 a bit faster, 好一些 a bit better.
column6: Qǐng kuài xiē, wǒmen yào chídào le.
column7: Please hurry up, we are going to be late.
column9: The plural of this, that and which: 這些, 那些, 哪些; also 一些 and 有些. After an adjective it softens a comparison: 快一些 a bit faster, 好一些 a bit better.

column3: Counts a group of people, casual and sometimes negative, like a gang: 一伙人, 一伙小偷. It also appears in 伙伴 partner.
column4: 一伙年轻人在路边聊天。
column5: 一夥年輕人在路邊聊天。
column6: Yī huǒ niánqīngrén zài lùbiān liáotiān.
column7: A group of young people is chatting by the road.
column9: Counts a group of people, casual and sometimes negative, like a gang: 一夥人, 一夥小偷. It also appears in 夥伴 partner.

column3: Counts one game of chess or cards, or a match: 一局棋, 打了三局. As a noun, an office or bureau (邮局, 警察局) and a situation (结局 outcome, 局面). Context tells which.
column6: Wǒmen xià le yī jú qí.
column7: We played a game of chess.
column9: Counts one game of chess or cards, or a match: 一局棋, 打了三局. As a noun, an office or bureau (郵局, 警察局) and a situation (結局 outcome, 局面). Context tells which.

column3: Counts food served on a plate and board games: 一盘菜, 一盘饺子, 一盘棋. As a noun, a plate or a disc: 光盘, 硬盘 hard drive, 键盘 keyboard.
column6: Zhuōzi shàng fàngzhe yī pán shuǐguǒ.
column7: There is a plate of fruit on the table.
column9: Counts food served on a plate and board games: 一盤菜, 一盤餃子, 一盤棋. As a noun, a plate or a disc: 光盤, 硬盤 hard drive, 鍵盤 keyboard.

column3: A measure word for a dozen: 一打鸡蛋, 两打啤酒. The verb 打, as in 打电话 or 打球, is a different word.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī dá jīdàn.
column7: I bought a dozen eggs.
column9: A measure word for a dozen: 一打雞蛋, 兩打啤酒. The verb 打, as in 打電話 or 打球, is a different word.

column3: Opens a sentence as an exclamation of surprise or realization: 啊，是你！ At the end of a sentence it is a light-toned particle that adds feeling: 你好啊, 真好啊.
column6: Ā, wǒ wàng le dài yàoshi!
column7: Oh, I forgot to bring my key!
column9: Opens a sentence as an exclamation of surprise or realization: 啊，是你！ At the end of a sentence it is a light-toned particle that adds feeling: 你好啊, 真好啊.

column3: What 啊 becomes after a, e, i, o or ü: 你好呀, 快去呀, 哪儿呀. It softens a question or warms a command, and belongs to speech and chat more than to formal writing.
column6: Nǐ zěnme kū le ya?
column7: Why are you crying?
column9: What 啊 becomes after a, e, i, o or ü: 你好呀, 快去呀, 哪兒呀. It softens a question or warms a command, and belongs to speech and chat more than to formal writing.

column3: A sentence-ending particle that stands for 啊 after a word ending in n: 小心哪, 真难哪. Rare in writing, found in dialogue and speech.
column6: Dàjiā xiǎoxīn na!
column7: Everyone, be careful!
column9: A sentence-ending particle that stands for 啊 after a word ending in n: 小心哪, 真難哪. Rare in writing, found in dialogue and speech.

column3: Mostly in 打招呼, to greet someone in passing with a hello, a nod or a wave: 跟他打招呼. Also to look after guests (招呼客人) and to let someone know (招呼一声).
column4: 他向我打招呼，我没看见。
column5: 他向我打招呼，我沒看見。
column6: Tā xiàng wǒ dǎ zhāohu, wǒ méi kànjiàn.
column7: He called out a hello to me, but I did not see him.
column9: Mostly in 打招呼, to greet someone in passing with a hello, a nod or a wave: 跟他打招呼. Also to look after guests (招呼客人) and to let someone know (招呼一聲).

column3: More formal than 你好: it sends regards, often through someone, as in 代我问候你的家人, and fits letters and holiday messages. Said angrily about someone's relatives, as in 问候你全家, it is an insult.
column6: Qǐng dài wǒ wènhòu nǐ de fùmǔ.
column7: Please give my regards to your parents.
column9: More formal than 你好: it sends regards, often through someone, as in 代我問候你的家人, and fits letters and holiday messages. Said angrily about someone's relatives, as in 問候你全家, it is an insult.

column3: Both noun and verb: 送上祝福 send good wishes, 祝福你们 wish you well. Warmer and more formal than 祝 alone, which opens a plain wish: 祝你生日快乐.
column4: 我送给他们最好的祝福。
column5: 我送給他們最好的祝福。
column6: Wǒ sòng gěi tāmen zuì hǎo de zhùfú.
column7: I give them my very best wishes.
column9: Both noun and verb: 送上祝福 send good wishes, 祝福你們 wish you well. Warmer and more formal than 祝 alone, which opens a plain wish: 祝你生日快樂.

column3: Takes the person and often the reason: 称赞他勇敢. Neutral, between 夸 (casual speech) and 表扬 (public praise by a superior).
column6: Lǎoshī chēngzàn le tā de zuòwén.
column7: The teacher praised his essay.
column9: Takes the person and often the reason: 稱讚他勇敢. Neutral, between 誇 (casual speech) and 表揚 (public praise by a superior).

column3: Praise given in public by someone above: a teacher, boss or leader. Common as 受到表扬 to be commended. Between friends, 夸 or 称赞 sounds more natural.
column4: 老师在全班面前表扬了她。
column5: 老師在全班面前表揚了她。
column6: Lǎoshī zài quán bān miànqián biǎoyáng le tā.
column7: The teacher praised her in front of the whole class.
column9: Praise given in public by someone above: a teacher, boss or leader. Common as 受到表揚 to be commended. Between friends, 誇 or 稱讚 sounds more natural.

column3: Quiet, formal admiration for a quality, idea or work: 赞赏他的勇气, 值得赞赏. It is inner approval more than the open praise of 表扬.
column6: Wǒ hěn zànshǎng nǐ de yǒngqì.
column7: I greatly admire your courage.
column9: Quiet, formal admiration for a quality, idea or work: 讚賞他的勇氣, 值得讚賞. It is inner approval more than the open praise of 表揚.

column3: Usually about an idea, plan or proposal: 赞成这个办法, 举手赞成 vote in favor. The opposite is 反对. It means taking a side, more than 同意, which is simply to agree.
column6: Wǒ zànchéng nǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
column7: I agree with your idea.
column9: Usually about an idea, plan or proposal: 贊成這個辦法, 舉手贊成 vote in favor. The opposite is 反對. It means taking a side, more than 同意, which is simply to agree.

column3: Companies sponsor events, teams and shows: 赞助商 is the sponsor and 赞助费 the money. For a gift to charity or a school, 捐赠 or 捐款 is the word, not 赞助.
column4: 这家公司赞助了这次比赛。
column5: 這家公司贊助了這次比賽。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī zànzhù le zhè cì bǐsài.
column7: This company sponsored the competition.
column9: Companies sponsor events, teams and shows: 贊助商 is the sponsor and 贊助費 the money. For a gift to charity or a school, 捐贈 or 捐款 is the word, not 贊助.

column3: Both a noun (面带微笑) and a verb (对人微笑). A faint, polite smile, gentler than 笑; it fits service, photos and calm warmth. 微 is "micro-" in 微波炉 (microwave) and 微信 (WeChat).
column6: Tā duì wǒ wēixiào le yīxià.
column7: She gave me a little smile.
column9: Both a noun (面帶微笑) and a verb (對人微笑). A faint, polite smile, gentler than 笑; it fits service, photos and calm warmth. 微 is "micro-" in 微波爐 (microwave) and 微信 (WeChat).

column3: The look on a face: 没有表情 is expressionless. In chat it is also emoji and stickers: 表情包 is a sticker pack, and 发个表情 sends one.
column6: Tā de biǎoqíng hěn yánsù.
column7: His expression is very serious.
column9: The look on a face: 沒有表情 is expressionless. In chat it is also emoji and stickers: 表情包 is a sticker pack, and 發個表情 sends one.

column3: Alone it is mostly 赏月 and 赏花, enjoying something beautiful; 欣赏 is the everyday word for appreciating art, music or a person. It is also a reward from someone above, as in 奖赏.
column4: 老板赏了他一个大红包。
column5: 老闆賞了他一個大紅包。
column6: Lǎobǎn shǎng le tā yī ge dà hóngbāo.
column7: The boss gave him a big red envelope as a reward.
column9: Alone it is mostly 賞月 and 賞花, enjoying something beautiful; 欣賞 is the everyday word for appreciating art, music or a person. It is also a reward from someone above, as in 獎賞.

column3: The object is built in, so it splits: 毕了业, 毕不了业. You graduate from a school with 从…毕业, or put the school first: 大学毕业. The diploma is 毕业证, the ceremony 毕业典礼.
column6: Tā míngnián dàxué bìyè.
column7: He graduates from university next year.
column9: The object is built in, so it splits: 畢了業, 畢不了業. You graduate from a school with 從…畢業, or put the school first: 大學畢業. The diploma is 畢業證, the ceremony 畢業典禮.

column3: Also the word for recent graduates on the job market: 应届毕业生. The ending 生 turns a field into a kind of student, as in 研究生, 留学生 and 新生 (new student).
column6: Jīnnián de bìyèshēng hěn duō.
column7: There are many graduates this year.
column9: Also the word for recent graduates on the job market: 應屆畢業生. The ending 生 turns a field into a kind of student, as in 研究生, 留學生 and 新生 (new student).

column3: One level above 专科 (junior college) and below 研究生. People say 读本科 for studying it, 本科生 for the student, and 本科毕业 for finishing it.
column6: Tā zài Běijīng dú běnkē.
column7: He is studying for his bachelor's degree in Beijing.
column9: One level above 專科 (junior college) and below 研究生. People say 讀本科 for studying it, 本科生 for the student, and 本科畢業 for finishing it.

column3: Covers master's and doctoral students alike; 硕士 and 博士 name the two degrees. On the mainland 读研 and 考研 (taking the entrance exam) are the short forms; in Taiwan a graduate school is a 研究所, so people say 念研究所.
column6: Tā zhèngzài dú yánjiūshēng.
column7: She is studying for a graduate degree.
column9: Covers master's and doctoral students alike; 碩士 and 博士 name the two degrees. On the mainland 讀研 and 考研 (taking the entrance exam) are the short forms; in Taiwan a graduate school is a 研究所, so people say 唸研究所.

column3: A university rank, used as a title after a surname (王教授) and for addressing someone. Below it come 副教授 (associate professor) and 讲师 (lecturer). It is not for a school teacher, who is 老师. 教 combines a child 子 with 攵, a teaching cane that stands for authority.
column6: Tā shì dàxué de jiàoshòu.
column7: He is a university professor.
column9: A university rank, used as a title after a surname (王教授) and for addressing someone. Below it come 副教授 (associate professor) and 講師 (lecturer). It is not for a school teacher, who is 老師. 教 combines a child 子 with 攵, a teaching cane that stands for authority.

column3: Counted with 个: 三个学分. You 修学分 (take credits), 拿学分 (earn them) or are 学分不够 (short of credits). It is not 分数, which is the grade or mark you get on a test.
column6: Zhè mén kè yǒu sān ge xuéfēn.
column7: This course is worth three credits.
column9: Counted with 個: 三個學分. You 修學分 (take credits), 拿學分 (earn them) or are 學分不夠 (short of credits). It is not 分數, which is the grade or mark you get on a test.

column3: The school year, running from autumn to summer, not the calendar year; 学期 is half of it. New 学年 start in September, and 第二学年 is the second year of study. 年 was originally a word for a harvest and later came to mean a year.
column6: Xīn xuénián jiǔ yuè kāishǐ.
column7: The new school year begins in September.
column9: The school year, running from autumn to summer, not the calendar year; 學期 is half of it. New 學年 start in September, and 第二學年 is the second year of study. 年 was originally a word for a harvest and later came to mean a year.

column3: A syllabus and schedule term: 四十个学时 is forty class hours in all. For one lesson period in everyday talk people say 课时, and for how long you studied, 学习时间.
column4: 这门课一共有四十个学时。
column5: 這門課一共有四十個學時。
column6: Zhè mén kè yīgòng yǒu sìshí ge xuéshí.
column7: This course has forty class hours in all.
column9: A syllabus and schedule term: 四十個學時 is forty class hours in all. For one lesson period in everyday talk people say 課時, and for how long you studied, 學習時間.

column3: Mostly before other nouns: 学术研究, 学术会议, 学术论文, and 学术界 for the academic world. It also stands alone: 学术上, 搞学术. It is about scholarship and research, not plain school study.
column6: Tā zài xuéshù shàng hěn yǒu chéngjiù.
column7: He has achieved a great deal in scholarship.
column9: Mostly before other nouns: 學術研究, 學術會議, 學術論文, and 學術界 for the academic world. It also stands alone: 學術上, 搞學術. It is about scholarship and research, not plain school study.

column3: A learned person 有学问, not just 有知识. Also a subject that takes real skill: 做饭也是一门学问 (counted with 门). 做学问 is to pursue scholarship.
column6: Tā shì ge hěn yǒu xuéwèn de rén.
column7: He is a very learned man.
column9: A learned person 有學問, not just 有知識. Also a subject that takes real skill: 做飯也是一門學問 (counted with 門). 做學問 is to pursue scholarship.

column3: Goes with 写 (write), 交 (hand in), 发表 (publish) and 答辩 (defend): 毕业论文 is the graduation thesis. 论 is the same one as in 讨论 and 理论.
column6: Tā zhèngzài xiě bìyè lùnwén.
column7: He is writing his graduation thesis.
column9: Goes with 寫 (write), 交 (hand in), 發表 (publish) and 答辯 (defend): 畢業論文 is the graduation thesis. 論 is the same one as in 討論 and 理論.

column3: Verbs: 放寒假 (the break begins), 过寒假, 寒假作业 (homework). Its pair is 暑假, and it comes around the Spring Festival. Leave of absence is 请假. This 假 is read jià; as fake or false it is read jiǎ. 寒 is drawn as a person in a house, sleeping in the grass to protect from the cold.
column6: Hánjià wǒ xiǎng huí jiā.
column7: During the winter break I want to go home.
column9: Verbs: 放寒假 (the break begins), 過寒假, 寒假作業 (homework). Its pair is 暑假, and it comes around the Spring Festival. Leave of absence is 請假. This 假 is read jià; as fake or false it is read jiǎ. 寒 is drawn as a person in a house, sleeping in the grass to protect from the cold.

column3: 放暑假 is when it begins; its pair is 寒假. The 暑 is summer heat, as in 中暑 (heatstroke) and 暑期 (the summer period).
column6: Shǔjià nǐ yǒu shénme dǎsuàn?
column7: What are your plans for the summer vacation?
column9: 放暑假 is when it begins; its pair is 寒假. The 暑 is summer heat, as in 中暑 (heatstroke) and 暑期 (the summer period).

column3: Short for 期中考试, so 准备期中 and 期中成绩 mean the exam and its result. Its pair is 期末, and 期初 is the start of term. A school word, not for the middle of other things.
column6: Zhè cì qīzhōng, wǒ kǎo de bùcuò.
column7: This midterm, I did well.
column9: Short for 期中考試, so 準備期中 and 期中成績 mean the exam and its result. Its pair is 期末, and 期初 is the start of term. A school word, not for the middle of other things.

column3: Final-exam time: 期末考试, 期末复习, 期末成绩. 末 also ends 周末, 月末 and 年末. Its pair is 期中. 末 is a tree with a stroke on its top, implying the meaning of apex; 本 puts the stroke at the bottom, at the roots.
column4: 期末快到了，我要好好复习。
column5: 期末快到了，我要好好複習。
column6: Qīmò kuài dào le, wǒ yào hǎohāo fùxí.
column7: The end of term is near; I must review properly.
column9: Final-exam time: 期末考試, 期末複習, 期末成績. 末 also ends 週末, 月末 and 年末. Its pair is 期中. 末 is a tree with a stroke on its top, implying the meaning of apex; 本 puts the stroke at the bottom, at the roots.

column3: Verbs: 发试卷 (hand out), 交试卷 or just 交卷 (hand in), 改试卷 (grade). 卷子 is the spoken form, and 考试 is the exam as an event rather than the sheet.
column6: Qǐng bǎ shìjuàn jiāo gěi lǎoshī.
column7: Please hand the exam paper to the teacher.
column9: Verbs: 發試卷 (hand out), 交試卷 or just 交卷 (hand in), 改試卷 (grade). 卷子 is the spoken form, and 考試 is the exam as an event rather than the sheet.

column3: A volume of a set or a chapter-like part: 第三卷, 上卷, 下卷. It is also the paper in 试卷 and 考卷. The idea behind 卷 is bending, and a reel of books.
column6: Zhè tào shū yīgòng yǒu sān juàn.
column7: This set of books has three volumes in all.
column9: A volume of a set or a chapter-like part: 第三卷, 上卷, 下卷. It is also the paper in 試卷 and 考卷. The idea behind 卷 is bending, and a reel of books.

column3: The answer to a question: 标准答案 (the standard answer), 参考答案 (the key), 对答案 (check answers together). It is the thing itself; the act of answering is 回答 or 答.
column6: Zhè dào tí de dá'àn shì shénme?
column7: What is the answer to this question?
column9: The answer to a question: 標準答案 (the standard answer), 參考答案 (the key), 對答案 (check answers together). It is the thing itself; the act of answering is 回答 or 答.

column3: A verb-object compound: 点了名, 点过名. It is roll call in class, and naming someone in public, often to criticize: 被点名批评. 名 is drawn as a crescent moon 夕 over a mouth 口: to say one's own name to identify oneself in the dark.
column6: Lǎoshī měitiān shàngkè xiān diǎnmíng.
column7: Every day the teacher takes attendance before class.
column9: A verb-object compound: 點了名, 點過名. It is roll call in class, and naming someone in public, often to criticize: 被點名批評. 名 is drawn as a crescent moon 夕 over a mouth 口: to say one's own name to identify oneself in the dark.

column3: To pass an exam or reach a standard, normally 60 points: 及格线 is the pass line, 不及格 fails. For passing a review or a vote, 通过 is used instead. It is verb plus object: 及不了格. 及 is a hand 又 grabbing a person 人.
column6: Zhè cì kǎoshì wǒ jígé le.
column7: I passed this exam.
column9: To pass an exam or reach a standard, normally 60 points: 及格線 is the pass line, 不及格 fails. For passing a review or a vote, 通過 is used instead. It is verb plus object: 及不了格. 及 is a hand 又 grabbing a person 人.

column3: The standard exam item is 填空题, next to 选择题 (multiple choice). It also means filling a vacancy or filling a gap on a form. This 空 is read kòng, the reading for space and free time, not kōng.
column6: Qǐng zài kuòhào lǐ tiánkòng.
column7: Please fill in the blank inside the brackets.
column9: The standard exam item is 填空題, next to 選擇題 (multiple choice). It also means filling a vacancy or filling a gap on a form. This 空 is read kòng, the reading for space and free time, not kōng.

column3: 抄作业 is copying homework to cheat, and 抄袭 is plagiarizing. For honest copying, such as notes, 抄笔记 is fine. It is not photocopying, which is 复印. The raid sense, 抄家, is rare.
column6: Bùyào chāo biérén de zuòyè.
column7: Don't copy other people's homework.
column9: 抄作業 is copying homework to cheat, and 抄襲 is plagiarizing. For honest copying, such as notes, 抄筆記 is fine. It is not photocopying, which is 複印. The raid sense, 抄家, is rare.

column3: Copying out by hand, for practice or a record: 抄写生词, 抄写三遍. It is neutral, with no hint of cheating; that is 抄 alone or 抄袭.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē cí chāoxiě sān biàn.
column7: Please copy these words out three times.
column9: Copying out by hand, for practice or a record: 抄寫生詞, 抄寫三遍. It is neutral, with no hint of cheating; that is 抄 alone or 抄襲.

column3: Verb and noun: you 参考 a book for your own view, and 仅供参考 is "for reference only". Common partners: 参考书, 参考资料, 参考答案.
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ cānkǎo zhè běn shū.
column7: You can consult this book.
column9: Verb and noun: you 參考 a book for your own view, and 僅供參考 is "for reference only". Common partners: 參考書, 參考資料, 參考答案.

column3: The school or company admits you, so the school is the subject or you use 被: 被录取. 录取通知书 is the admission letter and 录取分数线 the cutoff score. 取 is a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: to take the ear of fallen prey, a rite of hunters mentioned in the Rites of Zhou.
column6: Tā bèi Běijīng Dàxué lùqǔ le.
column7: He was admitted to Peking University.
column9: The school or company admits you, so the school is the subject or you use 被: 被錄取. 錄取通知書 is the admission letter and 錄取分數線 the cutoff score. 取 is a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: to take the ear of fallen prey, a rite of hunters mentioned in the Rites of Zhou.

column3: Right on the dot: 准时到, 准时开会, or 他很准时. The 准 is the one in 准确 and 准备. Close to 按时, which is more about meeting a schedule.
column6: Qǐng dàjiā zhǔnshí dào.
column7: Please, everyone, be on time.
column9: Right on the dot: 準時到, 準時開會, or 他很準時. The 準 is the one in 準確 and 準備. Close to 按時, which is more about meeting a schedule.

column3: Goes before the verb: 按时上班, 按时吃药, 按时完成. It means keeping to a schedule or deadline, while 准时 is hitting the exact moment of arrival or starting.
column6: Qǐng ànshí chī yào.
column7: Please take your medicine on time.
column9: Goes before the verb: 按時上班, 按時吃藥, 按時完成. It means keeping to a schedule or deadline, while 準時 is hitting the exact moment of arrival or starting.

column3: The late one is the subject: 我迟到了, 迟到十分钟. Leaving early is 早退. For a train or flight running late, say 晚点, not 迟到.
column6: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ chídào le.
column7: Sorry, I am late.
column9: The late one is the subject: 我遲到了, 遲到十分鐘. Leaving early is 早退. For a train or flight running late, say 晚點, not 遲到.

column3: Late trains, planes and buses: 火车晚点, 航班晚点. Also colloquial for "a bit later": 我晚点给你打电话. For a person who is late, say 迟到.
column6: Huǒchē wǎndiǎn le èrshí fēnzhōng.
column7: The train was twenty minutes late.
column9: Late trains, planes and buses: 火車晚點, 航班晚點. Also colloquial for "a bit later": 我晚點給你打電話. For a person who is late, say 遲到.

column3: The new time follows 到: 推迟到下周. The thing put off is the object. The opposite is 提前 (move earlier). For events and deadlines 延期 is similar.
column6: Huìyì tuīchí dào xià zhōu.
column7: The meeting has been postponed to next week.
column9: The new time follows 到: 推遲到下週. The thing put off is the object. The opposite is 提前 (move earlier). For events and deadlines 延期 is similar.

column3: Used as a whole verb: 延期了, 延期举行. Typical subjects are 比赛, 会议, 考试 and deadlines, and the reason often comes first: 因为…延期. Close to 推迟. 延 began as 彳 walking and 止 a foot, with the sense to travel far.
column6: Bǐsài yīnwèi xià yǔ yánqī le.
column7: The match was postponed because of rain.
column9: Used as a whole verb: 延期了, 延期舉行. Typical subjects are 比賽, 會議, 考試 and deadlines, and the reason often comes first: 因為…延期. Close to 推遲. 延 began as 彳 walking and 止 a foot, with the sense to travel far.

column3: Makes something last longer or reach farther: 延长时间, 延长假期. 延期 and 推迟 instead move it to a later date, so do not use 延长 for a postponed meeting.
column6: Huìyì yáncháng le bàn xiǎoshí.
column7: The meeting was extended by half an hour.
column9: Makes something last longer or reach farther: 延長時間, 延長假期. 延期 and 推遲 instead move it to a later date, so do not use 延長 for a postponed meeting.

column3: Before a verb it means at the last moment: 临时决定, 临时有事. Before a noun it means temporary: 临时工, 临时住所. 临时抱佛脚 is to cram at the last minute. 临 is drawn as a person looking down at some objects.
column6: Wǒ línshí yǒu shì, bù néng qù le.
column7: Something came up and I cannot go.
column9: Before a verb it means at the last moment: 臨時決定, 臨時有事. Before a noun it means temporary: 臨時工, 臨時住所. 臨時抱佛腳 is to cram at the last minute. 臨 is drawn as a person looking down at some objects.

column3: Goes before the verb: 事先通知, 事先准备. Its opposite is 事后 (afterward). 提前 is about moving a time earlier, 事先 about doing something before the event. 先 is a foot 止 over a person 儿, to go forward.
column6: Yǒu shì qǐng shìxiān gàosu wǒ.
column7: If something comes up, tell me beforehand.
column9: Goes before the verb: 事先通知, 事先準備. Its opposite is 事後 (afterward). 提前 is about moving a time earlier, 事先 about doing something before the event. 先 is a foot 止 over a person 儿, to go forward.

column3: Formal and written, for news and announcements: 即将出发, 即将到来. In speech use 快要 or 就要. It always comes before a verb. 即 is a food vessel 皀 and a kneeling person 卩, coming near to eat.
column6: Fēijī jíjiāng qǐfēi.
column7: The plane is about to take off.
column9: Formal and written, for news and announcements: 即將出發, 即將到來. In speech use 快要 or 就要. It always comes before a verb. 即 is a food vessel 皀 and a kneeling person 卩, coming near to eat.

column3: A written word for an experience in the past: 我曾去过. It is usually followed by 过, and the fuller 曾经 is the common form. To negate it, 没 plus 过 is everyday, and 不曾 or 未曾 is written. 曾 began as a picture of a cooker for steaming food, and was later borrowed for its sound to mean once already.
column6: Wǒ céng zài Běijīng zhù guo liǎng nián.
column7: I once lived in Beijing for two years.
column9: A written word for an experience in the past: 我曾去過. It is usually followed by 過, and the fuller 曾經 is the common form. To negate it, 沒 plus 過 is everyday, and 不曾 or 未曾 is written. 曾 began as a picture of a cooker for steaming food, and was later borrowed for its sound to mean once already.

column3: Goes before the verb: 他依然很忙. More written than 还是 or 仍然, and often after a time phrase. 依然如故 means unchanged from before. 依旧 is a close match.
column4: 十年过去了，他依然没变。
column5: 十年過去了，他依然沒變。
column6: Shí nián guòqù le, tā yīrán méi biàn.
column7: Ten years have passed and he is still the same.
column9: Goes before the verb: 他依然很忙. More written than 還是 or 仍然, and often after a time phrase. 依然如故 means unchanged from before. 依舊 is a close match.

column3: A collective: you do not count it, so for one item say 词 or 单词. Typical phrases: 词汇量 (vocabulary size), 扩大词汇量, 词汇丰富.
column6: Tā de cíhuì hěn fēngfù.
column7: His vocabulary is very rich.
column9: A collective: you do not count it, so for one item say 詞 or 單詞. Typical phrases: 詞彙量 (vocabulary size), 擴大詞彙量, 詞彙豐富.

column3: The rules, not the language itself, which is 语言. Typical phrases: 语法错误, 语法点 (a point of grammar), 学语法, 汉语语法.
column6: Hànyǔ yǔfǎ bù tài nán.
column7: Chinese grammar is not too hard.
column9: The rules, not the language itself, which is 語言. Typical phrases: 語法錯誤, 語法點 (a point of grammar), 學語法, 漢語語法.

column3: The sound system and how you pronounce: 语音标准. Also a chat voice message: 发语音, 语音消息, 语音通话. The pronunciation of one word is usually 发音. 音 is 言 with an extra stroke inside its mouth 口, likely representing partially closed or muffled vocalization.
column6: Tā de yǔyīn hěn biāozhǔn.
column7: His pronunciation is very standard.
column9: The sound system and how you pronounce: 語音標準. Also a chat voice message: 發語音, 語音消息, 語音通話. The pronunciation of one word is usually 發音. 音 is 言 with an extra stroke inside its mouth 口, likely representing partially closed or muffled vocalization.

column3: Spoken language as opposed to 书面语 (the written one). 英语口语 and 口语考试 are speaking skills, and 口语化 describes a casual, chatty style.
column6: Tā de Yīngyǔ kǒuyǔ hěn hǎo.
column7: Her spoken English is very good.
column9: Spoken language as opposed to 書面語 (the written one). 英語口語 and 口語考試 are speaking skills, and 口語化 describes a casual, chatty style.

column3: Letters of any alphabet: 拼音字母, 大写字母 (capital), 小写字母 (lowercase), 首字母 (initial). A Chinese character is a 字, never a 字母.
column6: Yīngyǔ yǒu èrshíliù ge zìmǔ.
column7: English has twenty-six letters.
column9: Letters of any alphabet: 拼音字母, 大寫字母 (capital), 小寫字母 (lowercase), 首字母 (initial). A Chinese character is a 字, never a 字母.

column3: Covers round and square brackets (方括号). 号 names other punctuation marks too: 句号, 逗号, 问号, 引号.
column6: Qǐng bǎ dá'àn xiě zài kuòhào lǐ.
column7: Please write the answer in the brackets.
column9: Covers round and square brackets (方括號). 號 names other punctuation marks too: 句號, 逗號, 問號, 引號.

column3: Marks and signs on a page or keyboard: 标点符号 (punctuation), 数学符号, 符号表. A road sign or logo is a 标志. Also figurative: 文化符号.
column6: Zhège fúhào shì shénme yìsi?
column7: What does this symbol mean?
column9: Marks and signs on a page or keyboard: 標點符號 (punctuation), 數學符號, 符號表. A road sign or logo is a 標誌. Also figurative: 文化符號.

column3: Something you can see that stands for a thing: 交通标志, 公司标志 (logo). 符号 is a written or abstract mark. As a verb, 标志着 means "marks": 标志着新阶段的开始.
column4: 这个标志表示禁止停车。
column5: 這個標誌表示禁止停車。
column6: Zhège biāozhì biǎoshì jìnzhǐ tíngchē.
column7: This sign means no parking.
column9: Something you can see that stands for a thing: 交通標誌, 公司標誌 (logo). 符號 is a written or abstract mark. As a verb, 標誌著 means "marks": 標誌著新階段的開始.

column3: Written and formal: tests (阅读理解), skills and habits (阅读习惯, 阅读量). In speech, 看书 or 读书 are usual. 读 passed from to say aloud to to recite and then to read.
column4: 我每天晚上阅读半小时。
column5: 我每天晚上閱讀半小時。
column6: Wǒ měitiān wǎnshang yuèdú bàn xiǎoshí.
column7: Every evening I read for half an hour.
column9: Written and formal: tests (閱讀理解), skills and habits (閱讀習慣, 閱讀量). In speech, 看書 or 讀書 are usual. 讀 passed from to say aloud to to recite and then to read.

column3: Things put together in order or made up: 编书, 编程序, 编故事. 编借口 is to invent an excuse, 编辫子 to braid hair, and 编辑 an editor or to edit.
column6: Tā biān le yī běn cídiǎn.
column7: He compiled a dictionary.
column9: Things put together in order or made up: 編書, 編程序, 編故事. 編借口 is to invent an excuse, 編辮子 to braid hair, and 編輯 an editor or to edit.

column3: As a verb, 成 names the target language: 翻译成英语. As a noun it is the person, so 他是翻译 works. It covers written translation and live interpreting alike.
column4: 请把这句话翻译成英语。
column5: 請把這句話翻譯成英語。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhè jù huà fānyì chéng Yīngyǔ.
column7: Please translate this sentence into English.
column9: As a verb, 成 names the target language: 翻譯成英語. As a noun it is the person, so 他是翻譯 works. It covers written translation and live interpreting alike.

column3: Turning a flat thing over: 翻页, 翻书 (to leaf through a book), 翻身 (to turn over in bed). 翻山 is to climb over a mountain, and 翻译 turns words into another language.
column6: Qǐng fān dào dì shí yè.
column7: Please turn to page ten.
column9: Turning a flat thing over: 翻頁, 翻書 (to leaf through a book), 翻身 (to turn over in bed). 翻山 is to climb over a mountain, and 翻譯 turns words into another language.

column3: An account of what happened or what something is like, so it suits reports and test answers: 描述情况, 描述过程. Also a noun: 一段描述. For vivid, literary portrayal, see 描写.
column4: 请描述一下你看到的情况。
column5: 請描述一下你看到的情況。
column6: Qǐng miáoshù yīxià nǐ kàndào de qíngkuàng.
column7: Please describe what you saw.
column9: An account of what happened or what something is like, so it suits reports and test answers: 描述情況, 描述過程. Also a noun: 一段描述. For vivid, literary portrayal, see 描寫.

column3: Said of authors and artists portraying a person, place or feeling: 描写人物, 描写景色. Where 描述 reports facts, 描写 paints a picture. Also a noun: 心理描写.
column4: 这篇文章描写了乡村的生活。
column5: 這篇文章描寫了鄉村的生活。
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng miáoxiě le xiāngcūn de shēnghuó.
column7: This article portrays life in the countryside.
