column9: Said of authors and artists portraying a person, place or feeling: 描寫人物, 描寫景色. Where 描述 reports facts, 描寫 paints a picture. Also a noun: 心理描寫.

column3: Often used for something hard to put into words: 无法形容, 难以形容. 用…形容 names the word you describe it with, and 形容词 is an adjective.
column4: 这个词可以用来形容天气。
column5: 這個詞可以用來形容天氣。
column6: Zhège cí kěyǐ yòng lái xíngróng tiānqì.
column7: This word can be used to describe the weather.
column9: Often used for something hard to put into words: 無法形容, 難以形容. 用…形容 names the word you describe it with, and 形容詞 is an adjective.

column3: You explain a word, a reason or an action: 解释原因, 向他解释. Also a noun: 他的解释很清楚. 不用解释了 means there is no need to make excuses.
column6: Qǐng nǐ jiěshì yīxià zhège cí.
column7: Please explain this word.
column9: You explain a word, a reason or an action: 解釋原因, 向他解釋. Also a noun: 他的解釋很清楚. 不用解釋了 means there is no need to make excuses.

column3: Counted with 首: 一首诗. Common partners are 唐诗, 写诗 and 读诗. 诗歌 is poetry in general, while 诗 can be a single poem.
column6: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan zhè shǒu shī.
column7: This poem is my favorite.
column9: Counted with 首: 一首詩. Common partners are 唐詩, 寫詩 and 讀詩. 詩歌 is poetry in general, while 詩 can be a single poem.

column3: Said of a recognized poet, past or present: 唐代诗人, 著名诗人. Someone who only writes a poem now and then is not usually called one; you say 会写诗 instead.
column6: Lǐ Bái shì yǒumíng de shīrén.
column7: Li Bai is a famous poet.
column9: Said of a recognized poet, past or present: 唐代詩人, 著名詩人. Someone who only writes a poem now and then is not usually called one; you say 會寫詩 instead.

column3: Tales of gods and the start of the world: 希腊神话, 中国神话. Also figurative: something too good to be true, or a legendary feat (创造了神话). An invented children's story is a 童话.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge gǔlǎo de shénhuà.
column7: This is an ancient myth.
column9: Tales of gods and the start of the world: 希臘神話, 中國神話. Also figurative: something too good to be true, or a legendary feat (創造了神話). An invented children's story is a 童話.

column3: An invented story for children: 童话故事, 安徒生童话. 童话般的 describes something dreamlike and too perfect: 童话般的世界. Compare 神话, the old tales of gods.
column4: 她给女儿讲了一个童话。
column5: 她給女兒講了一個童話。
column6: Tā gěi nǚ'ér jiǎng le yī ge tónghuà.
column7: She told her daughter a fairy tale.
column9: An invented story for children: 童話故事, 安徒生童話. 童話般的 describes something dreamlike and too perfect: 童話般的世界. Compare 神話, the old tales of gods.

column3: A formal word for a substantial written work with an author: 一部著作, 学术著作, and 著作权 for copyright. 作品 is broader and covers art, music and film too.
column6: Zhè wèi zuòjiā yǒu hěn duō zhùzuò.
column7: This writer has produced many works.
column9: A formal word for a substantial written work with an author: 一部著作, 學術著作, and 著作權 for copyright. 作品 is broader and covers art, music and film too.

column3: Before a noun, usually with 的: 著名的作家, 著名景点, 世界著名. More formal than 有名, and used of people, places and works with a wide reputation.
column4: 北京是著名的旅游城市。
column5: 北京是著名的旅遊城市。
column6: Běijīng shì zhùmíng de lǚyóu chéngshì.
column7: Beijing is a famous tourist city.
column9: Before a noun, usually with 的: 著名的作家, 著名景點, 世界著名. More formal than 有名, and used of people, places and works with a wide reputation.

column3: Both noun and adjective: 这部电影是经典, 经典作品, 经典歌曲. It praises what has lasted. 经典案例 is a textbook case, and in the old sense it means the Confucian classics. 典 pictures official books on a table.
column4: 这部电影已经成为经典。
column5: 這部電影已經成為經典。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng yǐjīng chéngwéi jīngdiǎn.
column7: This film has become a classic.
column9: Both noun and adjective: 這部電影是經典, 經典作品, 經典歌曲. It praises what has lasted. 經典案例 is a textbook case, and in the old sense it means the Confucian classics. 典 pictures official books on a table.

column3: The past of a country, a thing or a field: 中国历史, 有两千年的历史, and the school subject 历史老师. It is not "story": for that say 故事. 史 originally indicates the act of taking notes.
column4: 这座城市有两千年的历史。
column5: 這座城市有兩千年的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu liǎng qiān nián de lìshǐ.
column7: This city has a history of two thousand years.
column9: The past of a country, a thing or a field: 中國歷史, 有兩千年的歷史, and the school subject 歷史老師. It is not "story": for that say 故事. 史 originally indicates the act of taking notes.

column3: Goes before a year: 公元2000年. For BC, 前 follows and the year comes last: 公元前221年. A textbook style; in speech people just say the year. In Taiwan the usual term is 西元, on the mainland 公元.
column4: 这座塔建于公元七世纪。
column5: 這座塔建於公元七世紀。
column6: Zhè zuò tǎ jiànyú gōngyuán qī shìjì.
column7: This pagoda was built in the seventh century AD.
column9: Goes before a year: 公元2000年. For BC, 前 follows and the year comes last: 公元前221年. A textbook style; in speech people just say the year. In Taiwan the usual term is 西元, on the mainland 公元.

column3: Mostly a history word. In Chinese history it runs from the Opium Wars to about 1919, and 现代 comes after it. Seen in 近代史 and 近代化.
column6: Zhè zuò lóu shì jìndài jiànzào de.
column7: This building was built in modern times.
column9: Mostly a history word. In Chinese history it runs from the Opium Wars to about 1919, and 現代 comes after it. Seen in 近代史 and 近代化.

column3: Noun and adjective: 保持传统, 传统文化, 传统节日, 传统的方法. Used of customs, food, medicine and clothes. 统 is the same 统 as in 系统 and 统一.
column4: 春节是中国的传统节日。
column5: 春節是中國的傳統節日。
column6: Chūnjié shì Zhōngguó de chuántǒng jiérì.
column7: The Spring Festival is a traditional Chinese holiday.
column9: Noun and adjective: 保持傳統, 傳統文化, 傳統節日, 傳統的方法. Used of customs, food, medicine and clothes. 統 is the same 統 as in 系統 and 統一.

column3: The subject is a book or document: 书上记载着…. Also a noun: 历史记载. Compare 记录, which is a record of data or events; 记载 is what a text says. 载 is read zǎi in this word on the mainland, and zài in Taiwan.
column6: Shū lǐ jìzǎi le hěn duō gùshi.
column7: The book records many stories.
column9: The subject is a book or document: 書上記載著…. Also a noun: 歷史記載. Compare 記錄, which is a record of data or events; 記載 is what a text says. 載 is read zǎi in this word on the mainland, and zài in Taiwan.

column3: The subject is the thing that spreads, with no object: 故事流传, 广为流传, 流传了几百年. Rumors circulate this way too. To say someone hands something down, use 传 or 传承.
column4: 这个故事流传了几百年。
column5: 這個故事流傳了幾百年。
column6: Zhège gùshi liúchuán le jǐ bǎi nián.
column7: This story has been passed down for hundreds of years.
column9: The subject is the thing that spreads, with no object: 故事流傳, 廣為流傳, 流傳了幾百年. Rumors circulate this way too. To say someone hands something down, use 傳 or 傳承.

column3: Something begun earlier goes on, often with 到 and a time or place: 延续到今天. Goes with 传统, 习惯, 生命. 延 also lies behind 延长 and 延期.
column4: 这种习惯一直延续到今天。
column5: 這種習慣一直延續到今天。
column6: Zhè zhǒng xíguàn yīzhí yánxù dào jīntiān.
column7: This custom has continued to this day.
column9: Something begun earlier goes on, often with 到 and a time or place: 延續到今天. Goes with 傳統, 習慣, 生命. 延 also lies behind 延長 and 延期.

column3: Network, and in daily speech "the internet": 网 "net" plus 络 "web, network". Used for 网络游戏, 网络安全, 网络不好 "the connection is bad", 上网络. 网 is a picture of a net, and 络 has 纟 "thread". Taiwan says 网路 instead.
column6: Xiànzài de wǎngluò hěn fāngbiàn.
column7: Today's internet is very convenient.
column9: Network, and in daily speech "the internet": 網 "net" plus 絡 "web, network". Used for 網絡遊戲, 網絡安全, 網絡不好 "the connection is bad", 上網絡. 網 is a picture of a net, and 絡 has 糹 "thread". Taiwan says 網路 instead.

column3: What you give someone to type or click: 把网址发给我, 输入网址. 网站 is the site itself and 网址 its address. 址 never stands alone; it is also in 地址 and 住址.
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de wǎngzhǐ.
column7: Please tell me your web address.
column9: What you give someone to type or click: 把網址發給我, 輸入網址. 網站 is the site itself and 網址 its address. 址 never stands alone; it is also in 地址 and 住址.

column3: A product name, with no measure word. It is also the word for a message, counted with 条, and for the account: 发了一条微信, 微信号, 微信支付. People use it as a verb too: 微信我一下.
column6: Wǒmen yòng Wēixìn liáotiān ba.
column7: Let's chat on WeChat.
column9: A product name, with no measure word. It is also the word for a message, counted with 條, and for the account: 發了一條微信, 微信號, 微信支付. People use it as a verb too: 微信我一下.

column3: The object is the thing you download: 下载软件, 下载音乐. The opposite is 上传. 载 is read zǎi in this word; in Taiwan the reading is zài.
column4: 我在网上下载了一首歌。
column5: 我在網上下載了一首歌。
column6: Wǒ zài wǎngshàng xiàzài le yī shǒu gē.
column7: I downloaded a song online.
column9: The object is the thing you download: 下載軟件, 下載音樂. The opposite is 上傳. 載 is read zǎi in this word; in Taiwan the reading is zài.

column3: To log in: 登 "go up" plus 录 "record". The object is the account or website: 登录账号, 登录网站. Taiwan often says 登入 instead. The reverse is 退出 or 注销. 登 shows two feet 癶 climbing, which suits "going up" to a site.
column6: Qǐng xiān dēnglù nǐ de zhànghào.
column7: Please log in to your account first.
column9: To log in: 登 "go up" plus 錄 "record". The object is the account or website: 登錄帳號, 登錄網站. Taiwan often says 登入 instead. The reverse is 退出 or 註銷. 登 shows two feet 癶 climbing, which suits "going up" to a site.

column3: Usually counted with 组 or 项: 一组数据. Also 大数据, 数据库, 分析数据. 数字 is a digit, while 数据 is collected figures. 据 is also in 根据 and 证据.
column6: Zhèxiē shùjù hěn zhòngyào.
column7: These data are very important.
column9: Usually counted with 組 or 項: 一組數據. Also 大數據, 數據庫, 分析數據. 數字 is a digit, while 數據 is collected figures. 據 is also in 根據 and 證據.

column3: Digital: 数 "number" plus 码 "code". Before a noun: 数码相机 "digital camera", 数码产品 "digital products". Used for consumer electronics in mainland China; Taiwan prefers 数位. Also the number itself in some uses.
column6: Tā xǐhuan mǎi shùmǎ chǎnpǐn.
column7: He likes to buy digital gadgets.
column9: Digital: 數 "number" plus 碼 "code". Before a noun: 數碼相機 "digital camera", 數碼產品 "digital products". Used for consumer electronics in mainland China; Taiwan prefers 數位. Also the number itself in some uses.

column3: A verb-object, so other words go between: 充满电, 充了电, 充一会儿电. 没电 means the battery is dead, and 充电宝 is a power bank.
column6: Shǒujī méi diàn le, wǒ yào chōngdiàn.
column7: My phone is out of battery, I need to charge it.
column9: A verb-object, so other words go between: 充滿電, 充了電, 充一會兒電. 沒電 means the battery is dead, and 充電寶 is a power bank.

column3: The plug-in unit: 手机充电器. A cable alone is 充电线 and a power bank is 充电宝. 器 ends many words for devices: 计算器, 吸尘器.
column6: Nǐ yǒu shǒujī chōngdiànqì ma?
column7: Do you have a phone charger?
column9: The plug-in unit: 手機充電器. A cable alone is 充電線 and a power bank is 充電寶. 器 ends many words for devices: 計算器, 吸塵器.

column3: Headphones, earphones: 耳 "ear" plus 机 "machine". 戴耳机 "wear", 插耳机 "plug in". 耳 is a picture of an ear.
column6: Wǒ dàizhe ěrjī tīng yīnyuè.
column7: I am listening to music with headphones on.
column9: Headphones, earphones: 耳 "ear" plus 機 "machine". 戴耳機 "wear", 插耳機 "plug in". 耳 is a picture of an ear.

column3: Settings, to set up: 设 "establish" plus 置 "place". As a noun, the settings menu in an app: 在设置里. As a verb: 设置密码 "set a password". 置 has 罒 "net" over 直, and appears in 位置 "position". In Taiwan both are used, 设定 more often.
column4: 你可以在设置里改语言。
column5: 你可以在設置裡改語言。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ zài shèzhì lǐ gǎi yǔyán.
column7: You can change the language in the settings.
column9: Settings, to set up: 設 "establish" plus 置 "place". As a noun, the settings menu in an app: 在設置裡. As a verb: 設置密碼 "set a password". 置 has 罒 "net" over 直, and appears in 位置 "position". In Taiwan both are used, 設定 more often.

column3: Used for computers (操作系统), organizations (教育系统) and the body (消化系统). 系统地学习 means to study systematically. 系 alone is also a university department: 中文系.
column6: Diànnǎo de xìtǒng xūyào gēngxīn.
column7: The computer's system needs an update.
column9: Used for computers (操作系統), organizations (教育系統) and the body (消化系統). 系統地學習 means to study systematically. 系 alone is also a university department: 中文系.

column3: Procedure, computer program: 程 "course" plus 序 "order". As a program: 写程序, 安装程序, 程序员 "programmer". As a procedure: 手续程序. The Taiwan word for a program is more often 程式. 程 has 禾 "grain", from the old use of measuring.
column6: Zhège chéngxù hěn hǎoyòng.
column7: This program is very easy to use.
column9: Procedure, computer program: 程 "course" plus 序 "order". As a program: 寫程序, 安裝程序, 程序員 "programmer". As a procedure: 手續程序. The Taiwan word for a program is more often 程式. 程 has 禾 "grain", from the old use of measuring.

column3: Usually a tool, machine or program is the object: 操作电脑, 操作简单. Also the steps of a procedure: 操作步骤, 操作手册. 操作系统 is an operating system.
column6: Zhè tái jīqì hěn róngyì cāozuò.
column7: This machine is very easy to operate.
column9: Usually a tool, machine or program is the object: 操作電腦, 操作簡單. Also the steps of a procedure: 操作步驟, 操作手冊. 操作系統 is an operating system.

column3: On a computer: 复制链接, 复制和粘贴. Not the same as 抄, which is copying by hand. The same 复 means "repeat" in 复印 and 复习, and "complex" in 复杂.
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ fùzhì zhè duàn huà.
column7: You can copy this passage.
column9: On a computer: 複製鏈接, 複製和粘貼. Not the same as 抄, which is copying by hand. The same 複 means "repeat" in 複印 and 複習, and "complex" in 複雜.

column3: The everyday sense is replying to a message, email or comment: 回复邮件, 请尽快回复. The recover sense is rare and written; for health or order, say 恢复.
column6: Wǒ hái méi huífù tā de yóujiàn.
column7: I have not yet replied to his e-mail.
column9: The everyday sense is replying to a message, email or comment: 回復郵件, 請盡快回復. The recover sense is rare and written; for health or order, say 恢復.

column3: Said of machines and software: 智能手机, 智能家居, 人工智能 on the mainland; Taiwan says 智慧型手机 and 人工智慧. Not said of people; for a smart person use 聪明.
column4: 现在人人都有智能手机。
column5: 現在人人都有智能手機。
column6: Xiànzài rénrén dōu yǒu zhìnéng shǒujī.
column7: Everyone has a smartphone now.
column9: Said of machines and software: 智能手機, 智能家居, 人工智能 on the mainland; Taiwan says 智慧型手機 and 人工智慧. Not said of people; for a smart person use 聰明.

column3: Counted with 张: 一张光盘. 光盘 is the mainland word; Taiwan says 光碟. 光盘行动 is the "clean your plate" campaign: you leave nothing on the plate. 光 also means used up, and 盘 is a plate.
column6: Zhè zhāng guāngpán shì xīn mǎi de.
column7: This CD is newly bought.
column9: Counted with 張: 一張光盤. 光盤 is the mainland word; Taiwan says 光碟. 光盤行動 is the "clean your plate" campaign: you leave nothing on the plate. 光 also means used up, and 盤 is a plate.

column3: 片 marks flat, thin things and films: 照片, 名片, 卡片, 动画片. 唱片 is a record or album; today an album is usually called 专辑.
column6: Tā shōují le hěn duō jiù chàngpiàn.
column7: He has collected many old records.
column9: 片 marks flat, thin things and films: 照片, 名片, 卡片, 動畫片. 唱片 is a record or album; today an album is usually called 專輯.

column3: Typical verbs: 输入密码, 设置密码, 忘记密码, 修改密码. Also a cipher, as in 摩斯密码, and figuratively the key to something: 成功的密码. 密 is "secret" in 保密 but "dense" in 密集. 密 is explained as hidden in the mountains: secret, intimate.
column6: Qǐng shūrù nǐ de mìmǎ.
column7: Please enter your password.
column9: Typical verbs: 輸入密碼, 設置密碼, 忘記密碼, 修改密碼. Also a cipher, as in 摩斯密碼, and figuratively the key to something: 成功的密碼. 密 is "secret" in 保密 but "dense" in 密集. 密 is explained as hidden in the mountains: secret, intimate.

column3: A number that identifies something in a series: 手机号码, 电话号码, 号码牌. For a quantity, use 数字 or 数. 号 follows a number for room numbers and dates.
column6: Nǐ de shǒujī hàomǎ shì duōshao?
column7: What is your cell phone number?
column9: A number that identifies something in a series: 手機號碼, 電話號碼, 號碼牌. For a quantity, use 數字 or 數. 號 follows a number for room numbers and dates.

column3: A formal word for measuring or testing something specific, often in a lab: 检测结果, 水质检测, 核酸检测. 检查 is the general word for a check or inspection.
column6: Tā qù yīyuàn zuò le jiǎncè.
column7: He went to the hospital for a test.
column9: A formal word for measuring or testing something specific, often in a lab: 檢測結果, 水質檢測, 核酸檢測. 檢查 is the general word for a check or inspection.

column3: A school or company sports meet, with many events at once: 开运动会, 校运动会. 会 here is a gathering, as in 开会 and 晚会. One match is a 比赛, not a 运动会.
column6: Xuéxiào xià zhōu kāi yùndònghuì.
column7: The school holds its sports meet next week.
column9: A school or company sports meet, with many events at once: 開運動會, 校運動會. 會 here is a gathering, as in 開會 and 晚會. One match is a 比賽, not a 運動會.

column3: Short for 亚洲运动会, with the host city first: 杭州亚运会. The Olympics follow the same pattern: 奥运会. 亚 for Asia is read yǎ in Taiwan.
column4: 亚运会每四年举行一次。
column5: 亞運會每四年舉行一次。
column6: Yàyùnhuì měi sì nián jǔxíng yī cì.
column7: The Asian Games are held every four years.
column9: Short for 亞洲運動會, with the host city first: 杭州亞運會. The Olympics follow the same pattern: 奧運會. 亞 for Asia is read yǎ in Taiwan.

column3: Name the sport first: 游泳运动员, 足球运动员. 选手 is a contestant in a particular contest. The ending 员 makes people by role: 演员, 服务员, 队员.
column6: Tā shì yī míng yóuyǒng yùndòngyuán.
column7: He is a competitive swimmer.
column9: Name the sport first: 游泳運動員, 足球運動員. 選手 is a contestant in a particular contest. The ending 員 makes people by role: 演員, 服務員, 隊員.

column3: Scores are read with 比 between the numbers: 二比一, 三比零. 分 is a point, as in 得分, to score.
column6: Xiànzài de bǐfēn shì èr bǐ yī.
column7: The score is now two to one.
column9: Scores are read with 比 between the numbers: 二比一, 三比零. 分 is a point, as in 得分, to score.

column3: Both the sport (体操比赛) and a short drill done together, like 广播体操 in schools. 操 is the exercise itself: 早操 is morning exercises and 操场 the field where you do them.
column6: Tā cóng xiǎo liàn tǐcāo.
column7: She has trained in gymnastics since she was little.
column9: Both the sport (體操比賽) and a short drill done together, like 廣播體操 in schools. 操 is the exercise itself: 早操 is morning exercises and 操場 the field where you do them.

column3: A verb-object: 去健身, 健身房 for a gym, 健身教练 for a trainer. It is for health and shape, not competition. 健 is also in 健康.
column6: Tā měitiān zǎoshang jiànshēn.
column7: He works out every morning.
column9: A verb-object: 去健身, 健身房 for a gym, 健身教練 for a trainer. It is for health and shape, not competition. 健 is also in 健康.

column3: To exercise, to train: 锻 "forge metal" plus 炼 "refine". Both pieces come from metalworking, so the word means toughening your body or skills: 锻炼身体, 锻炼能力. The second syllable is a falling tone: liàn. More general than 健身.
column4: 每天锻炼身体对健康有好处。
column5: 每天鍛鍊身體對健康有好處。
column6: Měitiān duànliàn shēntǐ duì jiànkāng yǒu hǎochù.
column7: Exercising every day is good for your health.
column9: To exercise, to train: 鍛 "forge metal" plus 鍊 "refine". Both pieces come from metalworking, so the word means toughening your body or skills: 鍛鍊身體, 鍛鍊能力. The second syllable is a falling tone: liàn. More general than 健身.

column3: The object is what you earn, not an opponent: 赢得尊重, 赢得信任, 赢得掌声, 赢得比赛. A little formal. To simply win a game, say 赢: 我们赢了.
column6: Tā yíngdé le dàjiā de zūnzhòng.
column7: He won everyone's respect.
column9: The object is what you earn, not an opponent: 贏得尊重, 贏得信任, 贏得掌聲, 贏得比賽. A little formal. To simply win a game, say 贏: 我們贏了.

column3: Literary, and mostly in compounds: 获得, 获奖, 获胜, 获取. Alone it takes an object like a prize: 获过很多奖. In speech, 得 or 拿到 do the same job.
column4: 这位科学家一生获过很多奖。
column5: 這位科學家一生獲過很多獎。
column6: Zhè wèi kēxuéjiā yīshēng huò guo hěn duō jiǎng.
column7: This scientist won many prizes in his life.
column9: Literary, and mostly in compounds: 獲得, 獲獎, 獲勝, 獲取. Alone it takes an object like a prize: 獲過很多獎. In speech, 得 or 拿到 do the same job.

column3: A verb-object, so the 奖 can be split: 获过奖, 获了一等奖. Before a noun it means prize-winning: 获奖作品, 获奖者. In speech 得奖 is just as common.
column6: Tā de xiǎoshuō huòjiǎng le.
column7: His novel won a prize.
column9: A verb-object, so the 獎 can be split: 獲過獎, 獲了一等獎. Before a noun it means prize-winning: 獲獎作品, 獲獎者. In speech 得獎 is just as common.

column3: Seen in 一等奖, 得奖, 奖金 (bonus) and 奖学金 (scholarship). Also a verb: 奖励. Counted with 个 or 项.
column6: Tā dé le yī děng jiǎng.
column7: He won first prize.
column9: Seen in 一等獎, 得獎, 獎金 (bonus) and 獎學金 (scholarship). Also a verb: 獎勵. Counted with 個 or 項.

column3: Noun and verb: 面对挑战, 接受挑战, 挑战自己, 挑战世界纪录. 很有挑战性 describes something demanding. 挑 is read tiǎo here, to stir up, but tiāo when it means to choose, as in 挑选.
column4: 学汉字对我是一个挑战。
column5: 學漢字對我是一個挑戰。
column6: Xué Hànzì duì wǒ shì yī ge tiǎozhàn.
column7: Learning Chinese characters is a challenge for me.
column9: Noun and verb: 面對挑戰, 接受挑戰, 挑戰自己, 挑戰世界紀錄. 很有挑戰性 describes something demanding. 挑 is read tiǎo here, to stir up, but tiāo when it means to choose, as in 挑選.

column3: For efforts, plans, experiments and teams: 实验失败了, 失败的原因. The opposite is 成功. A person who flunks an exam says 没通过 or 不及格. 失 also means lose in 失业 and 失望.
column6: Zhè cì shíyàn shībài le.
column7: This experiment failed.
column9: For efforts, plans, experiments and teams: 實驗失敗了, 失敗的原因. The opposite is 成功. A person who flunks an exam says 沒通過 or 不及格. 失 also means lose in 失業 and 失望.

column3: Long, hard effort toward a goal, said with admiration: 为梦想奋斗, 努力奋斗, 奋斗目标. It belongs in speeches and slogans more than in talk about everyday tasks. 斗 is read dòu when it means to fight, but dǒu as a dry measure for grain.
column6: Tā wèi mèngxiǎng fèndòu le shí nián.
column7: He has strived for his dream for ten years.
column9: Long, hard effort toward a goal, said with admiration: 為夢想奮鬥, 努力奮鬥, 奮鬥目標. It belongs in speeches and slogans more than in talk about everyday tasks. 鬥 is read dòu when it means to fight, but dǒu as a dry measure for grain.

column3: Goes with contests, debates and fights: 竞争激烈, 激烈的讨论, 激烈地争论. It is not for a person's own feelings; use 激动 for those. The 激 in it is built on water and can describe water that swashes.
column6: Bǐsài fēicháng jīliè.
column7: The match is very intense.
column9: Goes with contests, debates and fights: 競爭激烈, 激烈的討論, 激烈地爭論. It is not for a person's own feelings; use 激動 for those. The 激 in it is built on water and can describe water that swashes.

column3: The everyday word for a cartoon, and the shorter 动画 is just as common. 片 marks a film or show, as in 纪录片 and 恐怖片.
column6: Háizimen dōu ài kàn dònghuàpiàn.
column7: All the children love watching cartoons.
column9: The everyday word for a cartoon, and the shorter 動畫 is just as common. 片 marks a film or show, as in 紀錄片 and 恐怖片.

column3: Covers a part in a play, film or game (演主要角色, 游戏角色) and a role in life: 在家庭中的角色, 扮演重要角色.
column4: 他在电影里演主要角色。
column5: 他在電影裡演主要角色。
column6: Tā zài diànyǐng lǐ yǎn zhǔyào juésè.
column7: He plays the lead role in the film.
column9: Covers a part in a play, film or game (演主要角色, 遊戲角色) and a role in life: 在家庭中的角色, 扮演重要角色.

column3: The look given to something on purpose: 造型独特, 造型可爱, for objects, characters and hairstyles. 型 means a type or form in many words, such as 发型 and 血型.
column4: 这个杯子的造型很特别。
column5: 這個杯子的造型很特別。
column6: Zhège bēizi de zàoxíng hěn tèbié.
column7: The shape of this cup is very special.
column9: The look given to something on purpose: 造型獨特, 造型可愛, for objects, characters and hairstyles. 型 means a type or form in many words, such as 髮型 and 血型.

column3: A decorative design on cloth, wallpaper, tiles or packaging: 花朵图案, 条纹图案, 图案设计. A picture that shows something is 图画, not this.
column4: 这件衣服上有漂亮的图案。
column5: 這件衣服上有漂亮的圖案。
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu shàng yǒu piàoliang de tú'àn.
column7: There is a pretty pattern on this garment.
column9: A decorative design on cloth, wallpaper, tiles or packaging: 花朵圖案, 條紋圖案, 圖案設計. A picture that shows something is 圖畫, not this.

column3: Mostly a building block: 红色, 特色, 脸色 (the look on someone's face). On its own it is the color of cloth or dye, as in the example, and in speech it can also mean lecherous (很色, 好色). Everyday speech says 颜色 for color. The character depicts a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, and was later borrowed to mean color.
column6: Zhè kuài bù de sè hěn zhèng.
column7: The color of this cloth is very true.
column9: Mostly a building block: 紅色, 特色, 臉色 (the look on someone's face). On its own it is the color of cloth or dye, as in the example, and in speech it can also mean lecherous (很色, 好色). Everyday speech says 顏色 for color. The character depicts a hand pressing down on a kneeling person, and was later borrowed to mean color.

column3: More literary than 颜色. It is the colors of a painting or scene (色彩丰富, 色彩鲜艳) and, figuratively, a flavor or tinge: 民族色彩, 神秘色彩. 彩 is also in 彩虹 and 彩色.
column6: Zhè fú huà de sècǎi hěn fēngfù.
column7: The colors in this painting are very rich.
column9: More literary than 顏色. It is the colors of a painting or scene (色彩豐富, 色彩鮮豔) and, figuratively, a flavor or tinge: 民族色彩, 神秘色彩. 彩 is also in 彩虹 and 彩色.

column3: A set phrase in which the numbers only mean many kinds. It goes before 的 and a noun, or stands alone as a predicate: 五颜六色的气球, 衣服五颜六色.
column4: 花园里开着五颜六色的花。
column5: 花園裡開著五顏六色的花。
column6: Huāyuán lǐ kāizhe wǔyánliùsè de huā.
column7: Flowers of every color bloom in the garden.
column9: A set phrase in which the numbers only mean many kinds. It goes before 的 and a noun, or stands alone as a predicate: 五顏六色的氣球, 衣服五顏六色.

column3: A physical scale model (飞机模型, 建筑模型) or an abstract one (数学模型). The same 模 is in 模仿 and 模特, a fashion model.
column6: Tā zuò le yī ge fēijī móxíng.
column7: He made a model airplane.
column9: A physical scale model (飛機模型, 建築模型) or an abstract one (數學模型). The same 模 is in 模仿 and 模特, a fashion model.

column3: The characteristic style of a work, person or period: 写作风格, 装修风格, 穿衣风格. 风 means manner or custom in 作风 and 学风 too.
column6: Tā xǐhuan jiǎndān de fēnggé.
column7: She likes a simple style.
column9: The characteristic style of a work, person or period: 寫作風格, 裝修風格, 穿衣風格. 風 means manner or custom in 作風 and 學風 too.

column3: Used for tides (涨潮, 退潮), for damp air or things (潮湿), and in speech for trendy: 很潮, 潮牌. The trendy sense is slangy and mostly about clothes and young people. It is derived from 朝, the word for morning, and its tide began as the rising tide in the daytime.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn cháo.
column7: This piece of clothing is very trendy.
column9: Used for tides (漲潮, 退潮), for damp air or things (潮濕), and in speech for trendy: 很潮, 潮牌. The trendy sense is slangy and mostly about clothes and young people. It is derived from 朝, the word for morning, and its tide began as the rising tide in the daytime.

column3: A broad current in society or fashion that is hard to resist: 时代的潮流, 跟上潮流, 潮流品牌. 趋势 is a plainer tendency, as in 发展趋势.
column6: Niánqīngrén xǐhuan gēn shàng cháoliú.
column7: Young people like to keep up with trends.
column9: A broad current in society or fashion that is hard to resist: 時代的潮流, 跟上潮流, 潮流品牌. 趨勢 is a plainer tendency, as in 發展趨勢.

column3: The peak of a story, film, match or event: 进入高潮, 迎来高潮. Its opposite is 低潮, a low point or slump.
column6: Diànyǐng de gāocháo hěn jīngcǎi.
column7: The climax of the film is very exciting.
column9: The peak of a story, film, match or event: 進入高潮, 迎來高潮. Its opposite is 低潮, a low point or slump.

column3: Done by hand rather than by machine (手工蛋糕, 手工制作), and also the activity of making crafts: 做手工. Its opposite is 机器.
column6: Zhè shì shǒugōng zuò de dàngāo.
column7: This is a handmade cake.
column9: Done by hand rather than by machine (手工蛋糕, 手工製作), and also the activity of making crafts: 做手工. Its opposite is 機器.

column3: Spoken. It points to a place ahead (路前头, 走在前头) and to what came earlier in a text or talk: 前头说过了. The pair is 后头; 前面 is the neutral, written choice. 头 makes a place word in 里头 and 外头 too.
column6: Lù qiántou yǒu yī jiā shāngdiàn.
column7: There is a shop ahead on the road.
column9: Spoken. It points to a place ahead (路前頭, 走在前頭) and to what came earlier in a text or talk: 前頭說過了. The pair is 後頭; 前面 is the neutral, written choice. 頭 makes a place word in 裡頭 and 外頭 too.

column3: Spoken. It points to a place behind (站在我后头) and to later time: 后头再说, 后头还有. The pair is 前头; 后面 is the neutral, written choice.
column6: Tā zhàn zài wǒ hòutou.
column7: He stands behind me.
column9: Spoken. It points to a place behind (站在我後頭) and to later time: 後頭再說, 後頭還有. The pair is 前頭; 後面 is the neutral, written choice.

column3: The place phrase for the stage or platform, with 台下 for the audience. The saying 台上一分钟，台下十年功 says a minute on stage takes ten years of practice.
column6: Tā zhàn zài táishàng jiǎnghuà.
column7: He stands on the stage and speaks.
column9: The place phrase for the stage or platform, with 臺下 for the audience. The saying 臺上一分鐘，臺下十年功 says a minute on stage takes ten years of practice.

column3: Spoken. After a person: what they hold (手里拿着书) or what is in their possession or control: 钱在他手里, 决定权在你手里.
column6: Tā shǒulǐ názhe yī běn shū.
column7: He is holding a book in his hands.
column9: Spoken. After a person: what they hold (手裡拿著書) or what is in their possession or control: 錢在他手裡, 決定權在你手裡.

column3: Literally what is in the eyes (眼里都是泪水); figuratively what someone notices or cares about: 他眼里只有工作. 眼里容不得沙子 is said of someone who cannot tolerate a flaw.
column6: Tā yǎnli dōu shì lèishuǐ.
column7: Her eyes are full of tears.
column9: Literally what is in the eyes (眼裡都是淚水); figuratively what someone notices or cares about: 他眼裡只有工作. 眼裡容不得沙子 is said of someone who cannot tolerate a flaw.

column3: Takes no measure word: 路的两边, 河的两边. It is also the two parties in a matter: 两边都有道理. 边 is the side in 左边, 右边 and 旁边.
column6: Lù de liǎngbiān dōu yǒu shù.
column7: There are trees on both sides of the road.
column9: Takes no measure word: 路的兩邊, 河的兩邊. It is also the two parties in a matter: 兩邊都有道理. 邊 is the side in 左邊, 右邊 and 旁邊.

column3: The bottom of a thing (杯底, 鞋底, 海底), and the end of a month or year: 月底, 年底. 底下 is underneath, and 心里没底 is feeling unsure. 底 is the bottom or foundation of a building, which is why it has 广.
column6: Bēizi de dǐ pò le.
column7: The bottom of the cup is broken.
column9: The bottom of a thing (杯底, 鞋底, 海底), and the end of a month or year: 月底, 年底. 底下 is underneath, and 心裡沒底 is feeling unsure. 底 is the bottom or foundation of a building, which is why it has 广.

column3: Mostly in compounds for the end of a period: 周末, 期末, 年末. 月末 and 月底 both mean the end of a month; 末 is a little more formal. 末 is a tree 木 with an extra stroke marking its top.
column6: Tā zài shíyuè mò huíguó.
column7: He returns to his country at the end of October.
column9: Mostly in compounds for the end of a period: 週末, 期末, 年末. 月末 and 月底 both mean the end of a month; 末 is a little more formal. 末 is a tree 木 with an extra stroke marking its top.

column3: A measure word for spots and places (三处错误, 一处风景), and a place in compounds: 好处, 到处, 住处, 办事处.
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu sān chù cuòwù.
column7: There are three mistakes here.
column9: A measure word for spots and places (三處錯誤, 一處風景), and a place in compounds: 好處, 到處, 住處, 辦事處.

column3: Where something is (座位的位置, 停车位置) and also a place in a ranking or in someone's mind: 放在重要的位置. The 位 is the same as in 座位 and 车位.
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de wèizhi.
column7: Please tell me where you are.
column9: Where something is (座位的位置, 停車位置) and also a place in a ranking or in someone's mind: 放在重要的位置. The 位 is the same as in 座位 and 車位.

column3: Of an organization or object: 公司内部, 内部结构. In 内部资料 or 内部消息 it means for insiders only. Its opposite is 外部.
column6: Gōngsī nèibù yǒu hěn duō guīdìng.
column7: There are many rules within the company.
column9: Of an organization or object: 公司內部, 內部結構. In 內部資料 or 內部消息 it means for insiders only. Its opposite is 外部.

column3: Names the gap between two things: 隔一条街 in space, 隔两天 in time. It is also a barrier: 隔着窗户看, 隔音, 隔壁 for next door.
column6: Wǒ jiā hé gōngsī gé yī tiáo jiē.
column7: My home is one street away from the company.
column9: Names the gap between two things: 隔一條街 in space, 隔兩天 in time. It is also a barrier: 隔著窗戶看, 隔音, 隔壁 for next door.

column3: To part things with something in between: 用墙隔开, 把A和B隔开, 被河隔开. For quarantine or isolation, say 隔离 instead.
column4: 一堵墙把两个房间隔开了。
column5: 一堵牆把兩個房間隔開了。
column6: Yī dǔ qiáng bǎ liǎng ge fángjiān gékāi le.
column7: A wall separates the two rooms.
column9: To part things with something in between: 用牆隔開, 把A和B隔開, 被河隔開. For quarantine or isolation, say 隔離 instead.

column3: As a plain word it means square: 方桌, 方的. Mostly it is a building block for side, party, place or way: 对方, 双方, 地方, 方法, 方面, 南方.
column6: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì fāng de.
column7: This table is square.
column9: As a plain word it means square: 方桌, 方的. Mostly it is a building block for side, party, place or way: 對方, 雙方, 地方, 方法, 方面, 南方.

column3: Distance: 距 "be apart from" plus 离 "leave". Between two places or times: 距离学校很近, 保持距离. It works as a noun (一段距离) and as a preposition-like verb (我家距离学校很近). 距 has 足 "foot" and 巨 for sound.
column6: Wǒ jiā jùlí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
column7: My home is very close to the school.
column9: Distance: 距 "be apart from" plus 離 "leave". Between two places or times: 距離學校很近, 保持距離. It works as a noun (一段距離) and as a preposition-like verb (我家距離學校很近). 距 has 足 "foot" and 巨 for sound.

column3: Room that can be used or filled: 空间不够, 储存空间; and figuratively room to grow: 发展空间, 想象空间. A room in a house is 房间, not this.
column4: 这个房间的空间太小了。
column5: 這個房間的空間太小了。
column6: Zhège fángjiān de kōngjiān tài xiǎo le.
column7: The space in this room is too small.
column9: Room that can be used or filled: 空間不夠, 儲存空間; and figuratively room to grow: 發展空間, 想象空間. A room in a house is 房間, not this.

column3: Spare time or an empty spot: 有空, 没空, 抽空 for making time, 空位 for a vacant seat. 你有空吗 is the usual way to ask if someone is free.
column6: Nǐ míngtiān yǒu kòng ma?
column7: Are you free tomorrow?
column9: Spare time or an empty spot: 有空, 沒空, 抽空 for making time, 空位 for a vacant seat. 你有空嗎 is the usual way to ask if someone is free.

column3: Strong emotion, happy or sad, often to tears or shaking: 激动得哭了, 情绪激动. 兴奋 is happy excitement, 感动 is being touched by kindness, and for contests use 激烈.
column4: 听到这个消息，他很激动。
column5: 聽到這個消息，他很激動。
column6: Tīng dào zhège xiāoxi, tā hěn jīdòng.
column7: Hearing the news, he was very moved.
column9: Strong emotion, happy or sad, often to tears or shaking: 激動得哭了, 情緒激動. 興奮 is happy excitement, 感動 is being touched by kindness, and for contests use 激烈.

column3: Happy, energetic excitement that can keep you up: 兴奋得睡不着. As an adverb it takes 地: 兴奋地说.
column4: 孩子们兴奋地跑了出来。
column5: 孩子們興奮地跑了出來。
column6: Háizimen xīngfèn de pǎo le chūlái.
column7: The children ran out excitedly.
column9: Happy, energetic excitement that can keep you up: 興奮得睡不著. As an adverb it takes 地: 興奮地說.

column3: Disappointment when hopes are not met. The person or thing goes after 对: 我对他很失望; 让人失望 is disappointing. 失 means lose in 失业, 失败 and 失眠 too. 望 began as a person standing up and looking off into the distance.
column6: Kǎoshì méi guò, wǒ hěn shīwàng.
column7: I failed the exam and am very disappointed.
column9: Disappointment when hopes are not met. The person or thing goes after 對: 我對他很失望; 讓人失望 is disappointing. 失 means lose in 失業, 失敗 and 失眠 too. 望 began as a person standing up and looking off into the distance.

column3: Verb and object, so 吃了一惊 and 大吃一惊 for a big start. The cause comes first: 听到…很吃惊. It is surprise or shock, not fear. 吃 also means to suffer or absorb, as in 吃亏 and 吃苦.
column4: 听到他结婚了，我很吃惊。
column5: 聽到他結婚了，我很吃驚。
column6: Tīng dào tā jiéhūn le, wǒ hěn chījīng.
column7: I was shocked to hear he got married.
column9: Verb and object, so 吃了一驚 and 大吃一驚 for a big start. The cause comes first: 聽到…很吃驚. It is surprise or shock, not fear. 吃 also means to suffer or absorb, as in 吃虧 and 吃苦.

column3: The relief of a release after something satisfying: 玩得很痛快, 痛快地哭一场. Of a person it means frank and decisive: 他说话很痛快, 痛快点! 痛 also means deeply or thoroughly, as in 痛哭 and 痛恨.
column6: Xǐ le ge rè shuǐzǎo, zhēn tòngkuài.
column7: A hot bath: how satisfying!
column9: The relief of a release after something satisfying: 玩得很痛快, 痛快地哭一場. Of a person it means frank and decisive: 他說話很痛快, 痛快點! 痛 also means deeply or thoroughly, as in 痛哭 and 痛恨.

column3: Pleased with yourself after a success, and often a little smug: 得意洋洋, 得意地笑, 得意忘形 for getting carried away. If you only mean happy, say 高兴.
column6: Tā kǎo le mǎnfēn, hěn déyì.
column7: He got a perfect score and is very pleased with himself.
column9: Pleased with yourself after a success, and often a little smug: 得意洋洋, 得意地笑, 得意忘形 for getting carried away. If you only mean happy, say 高興.

column3: Annoyed, or to annoy someone: 别烦我, 烦死了, 心烦, 烦人. It is the base of 麻烦 and 烦恼, and 好烦 is common in speech.
column6: Bié fán wǒ, wǒ zài gōngzuò.
column7: Don't bother me; I am working.
column9: Annoyed, or to annoy someone: 別煩我, 煩死了, 心煩, 煩人. It is the base of 麻煩 and 煩惱, and 好煩 is common in speech.

column3: About hurry and pressure, not fear. 别着急 is the phrase you hear most, said to calm someone down; 急死我了 and 着什么急 are also common. 担心 is worry about what might go wrong.
column6: Bié zháojí, mànmàn shuō.
column7: Don't worry, speak slowly.
column9: About hurry and pressure, not fear. 別著急 is the phrase you hear most, said to calm someone down; 急死我了 and 著什麼急 are also common. 擔心 is worry about what might go wrong.

column3: Worry about what could go wrong. The object can follow directly (担心你, 担心他的健康) or be a clause: 担心他迟到. The opposite is 放心. 担 also means take on, as in 担任.
column6: Māma hěn dānxīn nǐ.
column7: Mom worries a lot about you.
column9: Worry about what could go wrong. The object can follow directly (擔心你, 擔心他的健康) or be a clause: 擔心他遲到. The opposite is 放心. 擔 also means take on, as in 擔任.

column3: For what is gone: a time or a person who has died, as in 怀念童年, 怀念过去. It is warm and a little literary. 想念 is for someone you cannot see right now. 怀 also holds a thought or a child in 怀疑 and 怀孕.
column4: 我很怀念小时候的生活。
column5: 我很懷念小時候的生活。
column6: Wǒ hěn huáiniàn xiǎoshíhou de shēnghuó.
column7: I fondly remember life when I was little.
column9: For what is gone: a time or a person who has died, as in 懷念童年, 懷念過去. It is warm and a little literary. 想念 is for someone you cannot see right now. 懷 also holds a thought or a child in 懷疑 and 懷孕.

column3: To miss someone or a place you cannot be with: 想念家人, 想念家乡. It works in speech, letters and messages. For the past, use 怀念. One 2021 study reads 念 as an upside-down mouth over a heart: to listen to one's heart.
column6: Wǒ hěn xiǎngniàn wǒ de jiārén.
column7: I miss my family very much.
column9: To miss someone or a place you cannot be with: 想念家人, 想念家鄉. It works in speech, letters and messages. For the past, use 懷念. One 2021 study reads 念 as an upside-down mouth over a heart: to listen to one's heart.

column3: Feeling for someone who is badly off: 同情他, 同情心 for compassion, 博取同情 for angling for sympathy. It can carry a little pity. To agree with someone, use 同意.
column6: Dàjiā dōu hěn tóngqíng tā.
column7: Everyone feels sorry for him.
column9: Feeling for someone who is badly off: 同情他, 同情心 for compassion, 博取同情 for angling for sympathy. It can carry a little pity. To agree with someone, use 同意.

column3: Looking forward to something good, a little formal: 期待你的来信, 期待见面. 令人期待 is exciting to look forward to. In casual speech, 等不及 is "can't wait".
column6: Wǒ qīdài nǐ de láixìn.
column7: I look forward to your letter.
column9: Looking forward to something good, a little formal: 期待你的來信, 期待見面. 令人期待 is exciting to look forward to. In casual speech, 等不及 is "can't wait".

column3: Takes a clause: 我怀疑他在说谎 is a suspicion that it is so. 怀疑他不来 usually means I suspect he is not coming, not that I doubt it. 疑 began as a man with a cane looking around with his mouth wide open, not knowing where to go.
column6: Wǒ huáiyí tā zài shuōhuǎng.
column7: I suspect he is lying.
column9: Takes a clause: 我懷疑他在說謊 is a suspicion that it is so. 懷疑他不來 usually means I suspect he is not coming, not that I doubt it. 疑 began as a man with a cane looking around with his mouth wide open, not knowing where to go.

column3: Urgent and strongly felt, said of needs, wishes and tasks: 迫切的需要, 迫切地希望. It is written and formal; for a person in a hurry, 着急.
column4: 我们迫切需要你的帮助。
column5: 我們迫切需要你的幫助。
column6: Wǒmen pòqiè xūyào nǐ de bāngzhù.
column7: We urgently need your help.
column9: Urgent and strongly felt, said of needs, wishes and tasks: 迫切的需要, 迫切地希望. It is written and formal; for a person in a hurry, 著急.

column3: A calm, quiet scene or state of mind, a bit poetic: 宁静的夜晚, 内心宁静, 宁静的生活. For everyday quiet, say 安静.
column6: Yèwǎn de cūnzi hěn níngjìng.
column7: The village is very peaceful at night.
column9: A calm, quiet scene or state of mind, a bit poetic: 寧靜的夜晚, 內心寧靜, 寧靜的生活. For everyday quiet, say 安靜.

column3: Free of disturbance, for a surface, a mood or a life: 平静的湖面, 心情平静, 平静地说. 平静下来 is to calm down. 宁静 paints a peaceful scene; 平静 is the absence of agitation.
column6: Húmiàn hěn píngjìng.
column7: The surface of the lake is very calm.
column9: Free of disturbance, for a surface, a mood or a life: 平靜的湖面, 心情平靜, 平靜地說. 平靜下來 is to calm down. 寧靜 paints a peaceful scene; 平靜 is the absence of agitation.

column3: Said of a bored person (我好无聊) or a dull thing (这部电影很无聊). Of a joke or behavior it means pointless or silly. 聊 alone is to chat, as in 聊天.
column4: 周末一个人在家很无聊。
column5: 週末一個人在家很無聊。
column6: Zhōumò yī ge rén zài jiā hěn wúliáo.
column7: It is boring to be home alone on weekends.
column9: Said of a bored person (我好無聊) or a dull thing (這部電影很無聊). Of a joke or behavior it means pointless or silly. 聊 alone is to chat, as in 聊天.

column3: The thing goes after 对: 对中国历史感兴趣. The degree goes before 感: 很感兴趣, 不太感兴趣. It cannot take an object directly. 对…有兴趣 means the same.
column4: 我对中国历史很感兴趣。
column5: 我對中國歷史很感興趣。
column6: Wǒ duì Zhōngguó lìshǐ hěn gǎnxìngqù.
column7: I am very interested in Chinese history.
column9: The thing goes after 對: 對中國歷史感興趣. The degree goes before 感: 很感興趣, 不太感興趣. It cannot take an object directly. 對…有興趣 means the same.

column3: A lasting liking or hobby: 对…有兴趣, 兴趣爱好, 培养兴趣, 没兴趣. 没兴趣 is blunt in speech. 兴 is read xìng here, but xīng in 兴奋, where it goes with rising and starting. 趣 is built on walking, to hasten towards an object of interest.
column6: Nǐ yǒu shénme xìngqù àihào?
column7: What are your hobbies and interests?
column9: A lasting liking or hobby: 對…有興趣, 興趣愛好, 培養興趣, 沒興趣. 沒興趣 is blunt in speech. 興 is read xìng here, but xīng in 興奮, where it goes with rising and starting. 趣 is built on walking, to hasten towards an object of interest.

column3: The pleasure found in an activity or a way of life, often followed by 的: 生活的乐趣, 享受乐趣. It names the enjoyment itself; for something that is fun to do or watch, say 有趣. Here 乐 is read lè; it is read yuè in 音乐, where it means music.
column4: 读书给我带来很多乐趣。
column5: 讀書給我帶來很多樂趣。
column6: Dúshū gěi wǒ dàilái hěn duō lèqù.
column7: Reading brings me a lot of pleasure.
column9: The pleasure found in an activity or a way of life, often followed by 的: 生活的樂趣, 享受樂趣. It names the enjoyment itself; for something that is fun to do or watch, say 有趣. Here 樂 is read lè; it is read yuè in 音樂, where it means music.

column3: Said of a thing, a story or a person: 很有趣, 有趣的故事. 有意思 is the more common way to say it in speech; 有趣 sounds a touch more written. Pattern: 有 plus a noun makes an adjective of having that quality, as in 有用, 有名, 有趣.
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒuqù.
column7: This book is very interesting.
column9: Said of a thing, a story or a person: 很有趣, 有趣的故事. 有意思 is the more common way to say it in speech; 有趣 sounds a touch more written. Pattern: 有 plus a noun makes an adjective of having that quality, as in 有用, 有名, 有趣.

column3: Spoken. Of an activity, it is fun and absorbing (玩游戏很有劲儿); of a person, it means strong (他很有劲儿). The opposite is 没劲, boring or dull.
column6: Wán yóuxì hěn yǒujìnr.
column7: Playing the game is a lot of fun.
column9: Spoken. Of an activity, it is fun and absorbing (玩遊戲很有勁兒); of a person, it means strong (他很有勁兒). The opposite is 沒勁, boring or dull.

column3: Usually a good thing: a place or event full of people and sound, as in 街上很热闹 or 热闹非凡. It is not just loud; for noise that bothers you, say 吵. It is also a verb: 热闹一下 means to liven things up.
column4: 过年的时候，街上很热闹。
column5: 過年的時候，街上很熱鬧。
column6: Guònián de shíhou, jiē shàng hěn rènao.
column7: At New Year the street is very lively.
column9: Usually a good thing: a place or event full of people and sound, as in 街上很熱鬧 or 熱鬧非凡. It is not just loud; for noise that bothers you, say 吵. It is also a verb: 熱鬧一下 means to liven things up.

column3: A general word for disturbing things: to make noise or a fuss (别闹了), to joke around, or to come down with an illness: 闹肚子 means to have an upset stomach. 闹笑话 is to make a fool of yourself.
column6: Bié nào le, wǒ zài xiě zuòyè.
column7: Stop making noise; I am doing my homework.
column9: A general word for disturbing things: to make noise or a fuss (別鬧了), to joke around, or to come down with an illness: 鬧肚子 means to have an upset stomach. 鬧笑話 is to make a fool of yourself.

column3: Luck as chance, good or bad: 运气好, 运气不好, and 碰运气 for trying your luck. 走运 is the verb for being in luck.
column6: Jīntiān wǒ yùnqi hěn hǎo.
column7: I am very lucky today.
column9: Luck as chance, good or bad: 運氣好, 運氣不好, and 碰運氣 for trying your luck. 走運 is the verb for being in luck.

column3: You blow one up: 吹气球. The measure word is 个; 热气球 is a hot-air balloon.
column4: 孩子手里拿着一个红气球。
column5: 孩子手裡拿著一個紅氣球。
column6: Háizi shǒulǐ názhe yī ge hóng qìqiú.
column7: The child is holding a red balloon.
column9: You blow one up: 吹氣球. The measure word is 個; 熱氣球 is a hot-air balloon.

column3: Honest in what a person says and does: 诚实的孩子, 诚实回答. 老实 is close but leans toward plain and well-behaved, while 诚实 is about not lying.
column6: Tā shì yī ge chéngshí de háizi.
column7: He is an honest child.
column9: Honest in what a person says and does: 誠實的孩子, 誠實回答. 老實 is close but leans toward plain and well-behaved, while 誠實 is about not lying.

column3: Honest in a plain, simple way, so it can also hint at naive: 老实人 is a decent but unworldly person. 老实说 opens a frank remark, and 老老实实 means honestly and steadily.
column6: Tā hěn lǎoshi, cóng bù shuōhuǎng.
column7: He is honest and never lies.
column9: Honest in a plain, simple way, so it can also hint at naive: 老實人 is a decent but unworldly person. 老實說 opens a frank remark, and 老老實實 means honestly and steadily.

column3: A written, abstract word for keeping your word and being reliable, said of businesses, institutions and people alike: 讲诚信, 诚信经营.
column6: Zuò shēngyi yào jiǎng chéngxìn.
column7: Business needs honesty and good faith.
column9: A written, abstract word for keeping your word and being reliable, said of businesses, institutions and people alike: 講誠信, 誠信經營.

column3: Said of a person or an act that faces danger or difficulty: 勇敢的战士, 勇敢地面对. 敢 alone is the verb dare (不敢, 敢不敢), which 勇敢 is not. One analysis of 敢 shows a hand using a capturing tool to hunt a wild boar.
column6: Tā shì yī ge yǒnggǎn de rén.
column7: He is a brave person.
column9: Said of a person or an act that faces danger or difficulty: 勇敢的戰士, 勇敢地面對. 敢 alone is the verb dare (不敢, 敢不敢), which 勇敢 is not. One analysis of 敢 shows a hand using a capturing tool to hunt a wild boar.

column3: The noun: 有勇气, 鼓起勇气 (to pluck up courage). 勇敢 describes the person; 勇气 is the quality they have, so say 她很勇敢 but 她有勇气.
column6: Tā yǒu shuō zhēnhuà de yǒngqì.
column7: She has the courage to tell the truth.
column9: The noun: 有勇氣, 鼓起勇氣 (to pluck up courage). 勇敢 describes the person; 勇氣 is the quality they have, so say 她很勇敢 but 她有勇氣.

column3: A trait of character: 善良的人, 心地善良. It is about a good heart that wishes others no harm, not about good manners. 善 alone also means good at, as in 善于.
column6: Tā shì yī ge shànliáng de nǚhái.
column7: She is a kind-hearted girl.
column9: A trait of character: 善良的人, 心地善良. It is about a good heart that wishes others no harm, not about good manners. 善 alone also means good at, as in 善於.

column3: Which sense depends on what it describes: a person is generous or relaxed in manner (举止大方), while clothes or a design are tasteful and not showy (款式大方). The opposite of generous is 小气.
column6: Tā duì péngyou hěn dàfang.
column7: She is very generous to her friends.
column9: Which sense depends on what it describes: a person is generous or relaxed in manner (舉止大方), while clothes or a design are tasteful and not showy (款式大方). The opposite of generous is 小氣.

column3: Said of someone who readily helps or takes part: 热心人, 热心帮助. 热情 is more about a warm welcome to guests; 热心 is eagerness to help.
column6: Línjūmen dōu hěn rèxīn.
column7: The neighbors are all very helpful.
column9: Said of someone who readily helps or takes part: 熱心人, 熱心幫助. 熱情 is more about a warm welcome to guests; 熱心 is eagerness to help.

column3: Nice for a child (天真的笑容), but mildly critical for an adult, who is too trusting and unrealistic: 你太天真了.
column6: Háizi de xiàoróng hěn tiānzhēn.
column7: The child's smile is so innocent.
column9: Nice for a child (天真的笑容), but mildly critical for an adult, who is too trusting and unrealistic: 你太天真了.

column3: Mild and often affectionate, of a child who plays tricks or won't listen: 调皮捣蛋 means to be up to mischief. In this word 调 is read tiáo; as diào it is read in 调查, an investigation. In speech, 皮 alone can also mean naughty, as in 这孩子真皮.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn tiáopí.
column7: This child is very naughty.
column9: Mild and often affectionate, of a child who plays tricks or won't listen: 調皮搗蛋 means to be up to mischief. In this word 調 is read tiáo; as diào it is read in 調查, an investigation. In speech, 皮 alone can also mean naughty, as in 這孩子真皮.

column3: Carelessness from not paying attention, as in a mistake on an exam: 太粗心了, 粗心大意. The opposite is 细心, which is careful and attentive.
column6: Tā zuò tí zǒngshì hěn cūxīn.
column7: He is always careless when doing the exercises.
column9: Carelessness from not paying attention, as in a mistake on an exam: 太粗心了, 粗心大意. The opposite is 細心, which is careful and attentive.

column3: Blunt: teasing with a friend, rude to a stranger. It covers slow brains (我太笨了) and clumsy hands (笨手笨脚). For a bulky, heavy thing, 笨重.
column6: Wǒ tài bèn le, yòu zuòcuò le.
column7: I am so stupid; I got it wrong again.
column9: Blunt: teasing with a friend, rude to a stranger. It covers slow brains (我太笨了) and clumsy hands (笨手笨腳). For a bulky, heavy thing, 笨重.

column3: Praise for a person who gets things done well, especially at work: 能干的人, 精明能干. It is said of people, not of things. Here 干 is read gàn, to do; it is read gān, dry, in 干燥.
column6: Tā shì ge nénggàn de rén.
column7: She is a capable person.
column9: Praise for a person who gets things done well, especially at work: 能幹的人, 精明能幹. It is said of people, not of things. Here 幹 is read gàn, to do; it is read gān, dry, in 乾燥.

column3: Staying calm and clear-headed under pressure: 保持冷静, 冷静思考. It describes the mind, not the weather. 冷静下来 means to calm down.
column6: Yùdào wèntí yào lěngjìng.
column7: When you meet a problem, stay calm.
column9: Staying calm and clear-headed under pressure: 保持冷靜, 冷靜思考. It describes the mind, not the weather. 冷靜下來 means to calm down.

column3: Both a noun (有自信) and an adjective (他很自信), and positive. For too much of it, say 自大 or 骄傲. 自 began as a picture of a nose; folk etymology links that to self through people pointing at their noses.
column6: Tā duì zìjǐ hěn zìxìn.
column7: He is very confident in himself.
column9: Both a noun (有自信) and an adjective (他很自信), and positive. For too much of it, say 自大 or 驕傲. 自 began as a picture of a nose; folk etymology links that to self through people pointing at their noses.

column3: Used of morals, character and goals, always positive and a little formal: 高尚的品德. It is not about social class or taste; for refined taste say 高雅.
column6: Tā yǒu yī kē gāoshàng de xīn.
column7: He has a noble heart.
column9: Used of morals, character and goals, always positive and a little formal: 高尚的品德. It is not about social class or taste; for refined taste say 高雅.

column3: Works before another verb: 专心听讲, 专心学习. A person can be 很专心 or 不专心. The opposite is 分心, to get distracted. One account of 专 is a hand turning a spindle or spinning wheel, and the idea came to be bundling several things into one.
column6: Shàngkè yào zhuānxīn tīngjiǎng.
column7: In class you must listen attentively.
column9: Works before another verb: 專心聽講, 專心學習. A person can be 很專心 or 不專心. The opposite is 分心, to get distracted. One account of 專 is a hand turning a spindle or spinning wheel, and the idea came to be bundling several things into one.

column3: Describes a person or idea with nothing hidden or complicated, with a hint of naive: 想法单纯. Before a verb it narrows the reason: 不能单纯靠运气.
column6: Tā de xiǎngfǎ hěn dānchún.
column7: Her way of thinking is very simple.
column9: Describes a person or idea with nothing hidden or complicated, with a hint of naive: 想法單純. Before a verb it narrows the reason: 不能單純靠運氣.

column3: Effort without a promise of success: 我会尽力 is a polite I will do what I can, not a guarantee. It is also a set phrase, 尽力而为. Here 尽 is read jìn; as jǐn it is read in 尽量, as much as possible.
column6: Wǒ huì jìnlì bāng nǐ.
column7: I will do my best to help you.
column9: Effort without a promise of success: 我會盡力 is a polite I will do what I can, not a guarantee. It is also a set phrase, 盡力而為. Here 盡 is read jìn; as jǐn it is read in 盡量, as much as possible.

column3: Silence where speech is expected: 保持沉默, 沉默了很久. 沉默寡言 describes a person who says little. For a quiet place, say 安静.
column6: Tā chénmò le hěn jiǔ.
column7: He stayed silent for a long time.
column9: Silence where speech is expected: 保持沉默, 沉默了很久. 沉默寡言 describes a person who says little. For a quiet place, say 安靜.

column3: An adverb before the verb, usually with 地: 默默地工作, 默默地付出. It often describes quiet effort made without seeking credit, but it can also be plain silence, as in 默默地看着.
column4: 她默默地帮助了很多人。
column5: 她默默地幫助了很多人。
column6: Tā mòmò de bāngzhù le hěn duō rén.
column7: She quietly helped many people.
column9: An adverb before the verb, usually with 地: 默默地工作, 默默地付出. It often describes quiet effort made without seeking credit, but it can also be plain silence, as in 默默地看著.

column3: Used only before a noun, as in English dear: 亲爱的朋友 is a standard letter opening. Between couples, 亲爱的 on its own is darling.
column6: Qīn'ài de péngyou, nǐ hǎo!
column7: Dear friend, hello!
column9: Used only before a noun, as in English dear: 親愛的朋友 is a standard letter opening. Between couples, 親愛的 on its own is darling.

column3: About closeness of feeling between people: 亲密的朋友, 关系亲密, 亲密接触. 亲密无间 means extremely close. For close in distance, say 近.
column6: Tāmen shì qīnmì de péngyou.
column7: They are close friends.
column9: About closeness of feeling between people: 親密的朋友, 關係親密, 親密接觸. 親密無間 means extremely close. For close in distance, say 近.

column3: Care for things that need looking after: 爱护公物, 爱护环境, and also children or animals. It is common on signs (请爱护花草) and never romantic.
column6: Qǐng àihù gōnggòng cáiwù.
column7: Please take care of public property.
column9: Care for things that need looking after: 愛護公物, 愛護環境, and also children or animals. It is common on signs (請愛護花草) and never romantic.

column3: A verb-object that is mostly used as an adjective: 爱国精神, 爱国者. It is common in official and formal speech.
column6: Tā shì yī ge àiguó de rén.
column7: He is a patriotic person.
column9: A verb-object that is mostly used as an adjective: 愛國精神, 愛國者. It is common in official and formal speech.

column3: Warmer and more formal than 喜欢. The object can be a person, animal or thing: 喜爱音乐. It is often passive: 深受喜爱, 受到大家的喜爱.
column4: 孩子们都喜爱这只小狗。
column5: 孩子們都喜愛這隻小狗。
column6: Háizimen dōu xǐ'ài zhè zhī xiǎogǒu.
column7: The children all love this puppy.
column9: Warmer and more formal than 喜歡. The object can be a person, animal or thing: 喜愛音樂. It is often passive: 深受喜愛, 受到大家的喜愛.

column3: A verb-object, so 分了手 and 和女朋友分手 (no object directly after). Mostly about lovers ending a relationship, but it can mean people parting company.
column6: Tāmen qùnián fēnshǒu le.
column7: They broke up last year.
column9: A verb-object, so 分了手 and 和女朋友分手 (no object directly after). Mostly about lovers ending a relationship, but it can mean people parting company.

column3: Both a noun (一个约会) and a verb (他们约会了). About people it usually means a romantic date; for a doctor's or business appointment, use 预约.
column6: Tāmen zhōumò yǒu yī ge yuēhuì.
column7: They have a date this weekend.
column9: Both a noun (一個約會) and a verb (他們約會了). About people it usually means a romantic date; for a doctor's or business appointment, use 預約.

column3: Being with people over time, as colleagues or housemates: 和同事相处, with 得 after it to say how it goes: 相处得很好. Here 处 is read chǔ, to get along with; as chù it means place, as in 到处.
column6: Wǒ hé tóngshì xiāngchǔ de hěn hǎo.
column7: I get along very well with my colleagues.
column9: Being with people over time, as colleagues or housemates: 和同事相處, with 得 after it to say how it goes: 相處得很好. Here 處 is read chǔ, to get along with; as chù it means place, as in 到處.

column3: The people gather, so the subject is usually friends or family: 聚一聚, 聚在一起. It appears in 聚会, 聚餐 (a meal together) and 团聚 (a family reunion).
column4: 好久不见，我们聚一聚吧。
column5: 好久不見，我們聚一聚吧。
column6: Hǎojiǔ bù jiàn, wǒmen jù yī jù ba.
column7: Long time no see; let's get together.
column9: The people gather, so the subject is usually friends or family: 聚一聚, 聚在一起. It appears in 聚會, 聚餐 (a meal together) and 團聚 (a family reunion).

column3: A social gathering of friends, classmates or family: 同学聚会, 参加聚会. It can also be a verb. It is less formal than 宴会, a banquet.
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen yǒu yī ge jùhuì.
column7: We have a get-together this weekend.
column9: A social gathering of friends, classmates or family: 同學聚會, 參加聚會. It can also be a verb. It is less formal than 宴會, a banquet.

column3: About dealing with people socially: 很会交际, 交际能力. 社交 is a close word. 交 alone can mean to make friends.
column6: Tā hěn huì jiāojì.
column7: He is good at socializing.
column9: About dealing with people socially: 很會交際, 交際能力. 社交 is a close word. 交 alone can mean to make friends.

column3: A caring visit to someone you look in on: elders, the sick, people you care for (看望父母, 看望病人), or a leader visiting staff. For a business call say 拜访, and for a place say 参观. 望 was originally written as a person standing up and looking off into the distance.
column6: Wǒ qù yīyuàn kànwàng péngyou.
column7: I am going to the hospital to visit a friend.
column9: A caring visit to someone you look in on: elders, the sick, people you care for (看望父母, 看望病人), or a leader visiting staff. For a business call say 拜訪, and for a place say 參觀. 望 was originally written as a person standing up and looking off into the distance.

column3: Mostly about a service coming to the customer's home: 上门服务, 医生上门, 送货上门. It can also mean to call on someone: 上门拜访.
column6: Yīshēng shàngmén gěi tā kànbìng.
column7: The doctor came to his home to treat him.
column9: Mostly about a service coming to the customer's home: 上門服務, 醫生上門, 送貨上門. It can also mean to call on someone: 上門拜訪.

column3: For flat things: 薄纸, 薄被子, 薄衣服. A thin rope is 细 and a thin person is 瘦. The opposite is 厚.
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn báo.
column7: This book is very thin.
column9: For flat things: 薄紙, 薄被子, 薄衣服. A thin rope is 細 and a thin person is 瘦. The opposite is 厚.

column3: For flat things with layers: 厚书, 厚被子, 厚衣服, and 厚度 for thickness. A thick rope or finger is 粗. In 厚道 and 深厚 it is generous or deep. The opposite is 薄.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài hòu le.
column7: This garment is too thick.
column9: For flat things with layers: 厚書, 厚被子, 厚衣服, and 厚度 for thickness. A thick rope or finger is 粗. In 厚道 and 深厚 it is generous or deep. The opposite is 薄.

column3: For long round things: 粗绳子, 粗手指, 粗腿. A thick flat thing is 厚. It also means rough: 粗糙, a gruff voice, 粗心. The opposite is 细.
column6: Zhè gēn shéngzi hěn cū.
column7: This rope is very thick.
column9: For long round things: 粗繩子, 粗手指, 粗腿. A thick flat thing is 厚. It also means rough: 粗糙, a gruff voice, 粗心. The opposite is 細.

column3: For thin round or fine things: 细绳子, 细雨, 细沙. A thin flat thing is 薄. It also means careful: 仔细, 细心. The opposite is 粗.
column6: Tā de shǒuzhǐ yòu xì yòu cháng.
column7: Her fingers are slender and long.
column9: For thin round or fine things: 細繩子, 細雨, 細沙. A thin flat thing is 薄. It also means careful: 仔細, 細心. The opposite is 粗.

column3: For width: 宽马路, 肩膀很宽, and 三米宽 after a number. It also means loose (宽松) and lenient (宽大). The opposite is 窄.
column6: Zhè tiáo lù hěn kuān.
column7: This road is very wide.
column9: For width: 寬馬路, 肩膀很寬, and 三米寬 after a number. It also means loose (寬鬆) and lenient (寬大). The opposite is 窄.

column3: Larger and more literary than 宽: land, sea, sky, or a broad mind: 宽广的草原, 心胸宽广. A road or a room is just 宽.
column6: Cǎoyuán fēicháng kuānguǎng.
column7: The grassland is extremely vast.
column9: Larger and more literary than 寬: land, sea, sky, or a broad mind: 寬廣的草原, 心胸寬廣. A road or a room is just 寬.

column3: Shallow water (河很浅) and pale colors (浅色, 浅蓝). It also means slight in knowledge or experience (经验浅) and easy to grasp (浅显). The opposite is 深.
column6: Zhè tiáo hé hěn qiǎn.
column7: This river is very shallow.
column9: Shallow water (河很淺) and pale colors (淺色, 淺藍). It also means slight in knowledge or experience (經驗淺) and easy to grasp (淺顯). The opposite is 深.

column3: Only for abstract things: 深厚的友谊, 深厚的感情, 深厚的基础. For water or a hole, say just 深.
column4: 他们之间有深厚的友谊。
column5: 他們之間有深厚的友誼。
column6: Tāmen zhījiān yǒu shēnhòu de yǒuyì.
column7: There is a deep friendship between them.
column9: Only for abstract things: 深厚的友誼, 深厚的感情, 深厚的基礎. For water or a hole, say just 深.

column3: Round: 圆形, 圆桌, 月亮圆了 for a full moon. It also means complete and satisfying in 圆满, as in 圆满成功.
column6: Jīnwǎn de yuèliang yòu dà yòu yuán.
column7: The moon tonight is big and round.
column9: Round: 圓形, 圓桌, 月亮圓了 for a full moon. It also means complete and satisfying in 圓滿, as in 圓滿成功.

column3: A strong, rather formal word, best with abstract nouns: 巨大的变化, 巨大的压力, 巨大的成功. For an ordinary big bag or box, 很大 is the natural word.
column4: 这个城市发生了巨大的变化。
column5: 這個城市發生了巨大的變化。
column6: Zhège chéngshì fāshēng le jùdà de biànhuà.
column7: Huge changes have taken place in this city.
column9: A strong, rather formal word, best with abstract nouns: 巨大的變化, 巨大的壓力, 巨大的成功. For an ordinary big bag or box, 很大 is the natural word.

column3: Only goes before a noun, for events, machines and companies: 大型活动, 大型商场. It can't be a predicate, so you can't say 这个很大型. Opposite 小型.
column6: Zhè shì yī chǎng dàxíng yǎnchū.
column7: This is a large-scale show.
column9: Only goes before a noun, for events, machines and companies: 大型活動, 大型商場. It can't be a predicate, so you can't say 這個很大型. Opposite 小型.

column3: Before a noun, it puts the thing in a size class: 小型公司, 小型汽车, 小型音乐会. Opposite 大型. A plain small thing is just 小.
column6: Tā kāi le yī jiā xiǎoxíng gōngsī.
column7: He opened a small company.
column9: Before a noun, it puts the thing in a size class: 小型公司, 小型汽車, 小型音樂會. Opposite 大型. A plain small thing is just 小.

column3: Before a noun, for a recently developed kind of product or idea: 新型材料, 新型手机. Like 大型, it only modifies a noun. The opposite is 老式.
column6: Zhè shì yī zhǒng xīnxíng shǒujī.
column7: This is a new type of phone.
column9: Before a noun, for a recently developed kind of product or idea: 新型材料, 新型手機. Like 大型, it only modifies a noun. The opposite is 老式.

column3: Seen almost only in compounds: 血型, 发型, 脸型, 类型. It is rarely used on its own. It was an earthen mold, so it came to mean form and pattern.
column6: Tā chuān de hěn yǒu xíng.
column7: He dresses very stylishly.
column9: Seen almost only in compounds: 血型, 髮型, 臉型, 類型. It is rarely used on its own. It was an earthen mold, so it came to mean form and pattern.

column3: Colloquial in the north: 这个箱子很沉 for a heavy box, where 重 is the everyday word everywhere. 沉重 is for burdens and moods. Also in 沉默 and 沉睡.
column6: Shítou chén dào le shuǐdǐ.
column7: The stone sank to the bottom of the water.
column9: Colloquial in the north: 這個箱子很沉 for a heavy box, where 重 is the everyday word everywhere. 沉重 is for burdens and moods. Also in 沉默 and 沉睡.

column3: A written word for weight you feel more than lift: 心情沉重, 沉重的负担, 脚步沉重. For a box or bag, say 沉 or 重.
column6: Tā de xīnqíng hěn chénzhòng.
column7: He feels heavy at heart.
column9: A written word for weight you feel more than lift: 心情沉重, 沉重的負擔, 腳步沉重. For a box or bag, say 沉 or 重.

column3: Rare on its own; you meet it in 尺子, 尺寸 and 卷尺, and as a traditional unit, 一尺长. One explanation is a hand with the thumb and middle finger stretched out to measure a length of ten cun.
column6: Tā yòng chǐ huà le yī tiáo xiàn.
column7: He drew a line with a ruler.
column9: Rare on its own; you meet it in 尺子, 尺寸 and 卷尺, and as a traditional unit, 一尺長. One explanation is a hand with the thumb and middle finger stretched out to measure a length of ten cun.

column3: The ordinary word for a school ruler: 一把尺子, 借尺子. 把 is its measure word. A tape measure is 卷尺.
column6: Qǐng bǎ chǐzi jiè gěi wǒ.
column7: Please lend me your ruler.
column9: The ordinary word for a school ruler: 一把尺子, 借尺子. 把 is its measure word. A tape measure is 卷尺.

column3: For a size you can measure, of clothes, shoes or furniture: 量尺寸, 尺寸合适, 尺寸太大. A sense of what is proper is 分寸, not this.
column6: Zhè shuāng xié de chǐcun bù héshì.
column7: These shoes are not the right size.
column9: For a size you can measure, of clothes, shoes or furniture: 量尺寸, 尺寸合適, 尺寸太大. A sense of what is proper is 分寸, not this.

column3: Centimeter: 厘 is a hundredth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 一百八十厘米. Taiwan usually says 公分. Read límǐ. A millimeter is 毫米, and a meter is 米.
column4: 他的身高一百八十厘米。
column5: 他的身高一百八十釐米。
column6: Tā de shēngāo yībǎi bāshí límǐ.
column7: He is 180 centimeters tall.
column9: Centimeter: 釐 is a hundredth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 一百八十釐米. Taiwan usually says 公分. Read límǐ. A millimeter is 毫米, and a meter is 米.

column3: Millimeter: 毫 is a thousandth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 五毫米. 毫 has 毛 "hair" beneath a top part: the finest hair. Taiwan also says 公厘. In general speech centimeters are used for everyday size.
column4: 这块板的厚度是五毫米。
column5: 這塊板的厚度是五毫米。
column6: Zhè kuài bǎn de hòudù shì wǔ háomǐ.
column7: This board is five millimeters thick.
column9: Millimeter: 毫 is a thousandth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 五毫米. 毫 has 毛 "hair" beneath a top part: the finest hair. Taiwan also says 公釐. In general speech centimeters are used for everyday size.

column3: Milliliter: 毫 "thousandth" plus 升 "liter". After a number: 五百毫升. The drink bottle sizes you see on packages: 500毫升. 升 is the liter; Taiwan also says 公升.
column6: Zhè píng shuǐ yǒu wǔbǎi háoshēng.
column7: This bottle of water holds five hundred milliliters.
column9: Milliliter: 毫 "thousandth" plus 升 "liter". After a number: 五百毫升. The drink bottle sizes you see on packages: 500毫升. 升 is the liter; Taiwan also says 公升.

column3: In areas the unit is 平方米, and home sizes are given that way (一百平方米); in speech it is often cut to 平方. Compare 立方, the cube.
column6: Sān de píngfāng shì jiǔ.
column7: The square of three is nine.
column9: In areas the unit is 平方米, and home sizes are given that way (一百平方米); in speech it is often cut to 平方. Compare 立方, the cube.

column3: The average sits before the verb: 平均每天睡七个小时. Also an adjective (平均分数) and 'evenly' (平均分配).
column4: 他每天平均睡七个小时。
column5: 他每天平均睡七個小時。
column6: Tā měitiān píngjūn shuì qī ge xiǎoshí.
column7: On average he sleeps seven hours a day.
column9: The average sits before the verb: 平均每天睡七個小時. Also an adjective (平均分數) and 'evenly' (平均分配).

column3: Follows the number: 两倍, 三倍, with 是…的 for comparison. 增加了两倍 is ambiguous (doubled or tripled?), so 是我的两倍 is the safer pattern.
column6: Tā de niánjì shì wǒ de liǎng bèi.
column7: He is twice my age.
column9: Follows the number: 兩倍, 三倍, with 是…的 for comparison. 增加了兩倍 is ambiguous (doubled or tripled?), so 是我的兩倍 is the safer pattern.

column3: Here it is the verb of measuring with a tool: 量身高, 量体温, 量尺寸, often doubled as 量一量. The noun for an amount is a different word, as in 数量, 质量, 大量.
column6: Qǐng yòng chǐ liáng yi liáng.
column7: Please measure it with a ruler.
column9: Here it is the verb of measuring with a tool: 量身高, 量體溫, 量尺寸, often doubled as 量一量. The noun for an amount is a different word, as in 數量, 質量, 大量.

column3: The number a scale gives for an object: 重量是十公斤. For a person's weight, say 体重.
column4: 这个箱子的重量是十公斤。
column5: 這個箱子的重量是十公斤。
column6: Zhège xiāngzi de zhòngliàng shì shí gōngjīn.
column7: This box weighs ten kilograms.
column9: The number a scale gives for an object: 重量是十公斤. For a person's weight, say 體重.

column3: Mostly in compounds like 测试, 测量, 预测. Alone it takes the thing measured or a quantity: 测体温, 测血压.
column6: Qǐng nǐ cè yīxià tǐwēn.
column7: Please take your temperature.
column9: Mostly in compounds like 測試, 測量, 預測. Alone it takes the thing measured or a quantity: 測體溫, 測血壓.

column3: More technical than 量: land, distances, instruments (测量工具). At home, a person's height is just 量身高.
column6: Gōngrén zhèngzài cèliáng zhè kuài dì.
column7: The workers are surveying this plot of land.
column9: More technical than 量: land, distances, instruments (測量工具). At home, a person's height is just 量身高.

column3: Both verb and noun, for a skill or for a machine or program: 汉语水平测试, 测试软件. Less official than 考试, a school exam.
column6: Míngtiān yǒu Hànyǔ cèshì.
column7: There is a Chinese test tomorrow.
column9: Both verb and noun, for a skill or for a machine or program: 漢語水平測試, 測試軟件. Less official than 考試, a school exam.

column3: The exact code of a product, asked when buying, repairing or ordering: 什么型号, 手机型号. 型 alone is only the kind.
column6: Zhège shǒujī shì shénme xínghào?
column7: What model is this phone?
column9: The exact code of a product, asked when buying, repairing or ordering: 什麼型號, 手機型號. 型 alone is only the kind.

column3: Spoken pattern: 极了 after an adjective, as in 好极了, 累极了. Before an adjective it is more written: 极好, 极大, and 极其 is stronger still.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng měi jí le.
column7: The scenery here is extremely beautiful.
column9: Spoken pattern: 極了 after an adjective, as in 好極了, 累極了. Before an adjective it is more written: 極好, 極大, and 極其 is stronger still.

column3: A written intensifier before an adjective or verb: 极其重要, 极其困难. Stronger than 很 or 非常, and it never follows the word, unlike 极了.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì jíqí zhòngyào.
column7: This matter is extremely important.
column9: A written intensifier before an adjective or verb: 極其重要, 極其困難. Stronger than 很 or 非常, and it never follows the word, unlike 極了.

column3: Before an adjective or verb, meaning more than usual for the occasion: 格外高兴, 格外冷. It compares with the norm, so it often follows a time phrase.
column6: Jīntiān de tiānqì géwài hǎo.
column7: The weather today is especially good.
column9: Before an adjective or verb, meaning more than usual for the occasion: 格外高興, 格外冷. It compares with the norm, so it often follows a time phrase.

column3: Mostly a criticism of words, acts or demands that cross a line: 太过分了, 过分的要求. For too much of a physical thing, use 太 instead.
column6: Tā shuō de yǒudiǎn guòfèn.
column7: What he said was a bit much.
column9: Mostly a criticism of words, acts or demands that cross a line: 太過分了, 過分的要求. For too much of a physical thing, use 太 instead.

column3: Positive and formal; it pairs with abstract nouns: 充分的准备, 充分的理由. As an adverb: 充分利用 (make full use of). Not used for water or food.
column6: Nǐ yào zuòhǎo chōngfèn de zhǔnbèi.
column7: You must make ample preparation.
column9: Positive and formal; it pairs with abstract nouns: 充分的準備, 充分的理由. As an adverb: 充分利用 (make full use of). Not used for water or food.

column3: An adjective and adverb: 彻底解决, 彻底改变, 彻底打扫. It also works for bad things: 彻底失败.
column6: Fángjiān yào chèdǐ dǎsǎo yīxià.
column7: The room needs a thorough cleaning.
column9: An adjective and adverb: 徹底解決, 徹底改變, 徹底打掃. It also works for bad things: 徹底失敗.

column3: Spoken pattern 非…不可 (also 非要…不可): must, will insist, as in 他非要去不可. Also 'non-' in 非法 and 非常.
column6: Tā fēi yào qù bùkě.
column7: He insists on going.
column9: Spoken pattern 非…不可 (also 非要…不可): must, will insist, as in 他非要去不可. Also 'non-' in 非法 and 非常.

column3: Goes before a verb or number: 几乎每天, 几乎没有. With 不 or 没 it means hardly or almost never. Elsewhere 几 is jǐ, as in 几个, for how many or several.
column6: Wǒ jīhū měitiān dōu pǎobù.
column7: I run almost every day.
column9: Goes before a verb or number: 幾乎每天, 幾乎沒有. With 不 or 沒 it means hardly or almost never. Elsewhere 幾 is jǐ, as in 幾個, for how many or several.

column3: Nearly always in negatives: 不会轻易放弃, 不要轻易相信. It means too easily or without much thought, and is rare in positive sentences.
column6: Tā bù huì qīngyì fàngqì.
column7: He will not give up easily.
column9: Nearly always in negatives: 不會輕易放棄, 不要輕易相信. It means too easily or without much thought, and is rare in positive sentences.

column3: Introduces the extreme case at the end of a list or a rise: 他忙得甚至忘了吃饭. Often followed by 都 or 也: 甚至连…都….
column6: Tā máng de shènzhì wàng le chīfàn.
column7: He was so busy that he even forgot to eat.
column9: Introduces the extreme case at the end of a list or a rise: 他忙得甚至忘了吃飯. Often followed by 都 or 也: 甚至連…都….

column3: Use it when the result runs against what the first part leads you to expect: 药吃了，病反而重了. For plain contrast, 但是 is the word.
column6: Yǔ méiyǒu tíng, fǎn'ér gèng dà le.
column7: The rain did not stop; it got even heavier.
column9: Use it when the result runs against what the first part leads you to expect: 藥吃了，病反而重了. For plain contrast, 但是 is the word.

column3: Goes before the verb: 大多是…. With a noun, use 大多数: 大多数人. It states what most of a group is. 多 began as two pieces of meat.
column4: 这里的学生大多是外国人。
column5: 這裡的學生大多是外國人。
column6: Zhèlǐ de xuésheng dàduō shì wàiguórén.
column7: The students here are mostly foreigners.
column9: Goes before the verb: 大多是…. With a noun, use 大多數: 大多數人. It states what most of a group is. 多 began as two pieces of meat.

column3: Before a number or 多少: 总共十个, 总共多少钱. It adds everything up. 一共 means the same and is more common in speech.
column6: Wǒmen zǒnggòng yǒu shí ge rén.
column7: There are ten of us in all.
column9: Before a number or 多少: 總共十個, 總共多少錢. It adds everything up. 一共 means the same and is more common in speech.

column3: Points to a few exceptions in a larger group: 个别学生, 个别情况. As an adverb it means one by one: 个别谈话, a talk with each person alone.
column4: 个别学生没有完成作业。
column5: 個別學生沒有完成作業。
column6: Gèbié xuésheng méiyǒu wánchéng zuòyè.
column7: A few students did not finish the homework.
column9: Points to a few exceptions in a larger group: 個別學生, 個別情況. As an adverb it means one by one: 個別談話, a talk with each person alone.

column3: Goes before a noun, with no 的: 各个方面, 各个班. It treats a group member by member. The shorter 各 sits in set words: 各国, 各位.
column6: Gègè bān dōu cānjiā le bǐsài.
column7: Every class took part in the contest.
column9: Goes before a noun, with no 的: 各個方面, 各個班. It treats a group member by member. The shorter 各 sits in set words: 各國, 各位.

column3: The rest after you have named some: 其余的人. For others in general, 其他 is the word.
column6: Qíyú de rén dōu huí jiā le.
column7: The rest of the people all went home.
column9: The rest after you have named some: 其餘的人. For others in general, 其他 is the word.

column3: An adverb before the verb, for rules and notices that allow no exceptions: 学生一律穿校服, 一律免费.
column6: Xuésheng yīlǜ chuān xiàofú.
column7: All students wear the school uniform without exception.
column9: An adverb before the verb, for rules and notices that allow no exceptions: 學生一律穿校服, 一律免費.

column3: Two everyday senses: a bill or list (菜单, 名单, 订单; 买单 is what you call out to pay) and single or one only (单人间, 单身, 单号, 简单).
column6: Qǐng zài zhè zhāng dān shàng qiānmíng.
column7: Please sign this form.
column9: Two everyday senses: a bill or list (菜單, 名單, 訂單; 買單 is what you call out to pay) and single or one only (單人間, 單身, 單號, 簡單).

column3: Before a verb, apart from others: 单独行动, 单独谈话. 一个人 is the plain spoken 'by oneself'; 单独 stresses being separate.
column6: Tā xǐhuan dāndú lǚxíng.
column7: He likes to travel alone.
column9: Before a verb, apart from others: 單獨行動, 單獨談話. 一個人 is the plain spoken 'by oneself'; 單獨 stresses being separate.

column3: A written adverb before a verb: 独自生活, 独自一人. It often carries a tone of loneliness or independence.
column6: Tā dúzì yī rén qù le Běijīng.
column7: She went to Beijing all by herself.
column9: A written adverb before a verb: 獨自生活, 獨自一人. It often carries a tone of loneliness or independence.

column3: A single member against the group: 个体差异. In China 个体户 is a self-employed business owner. Mostly written or technical.
column6: Měi ge gètǐ dōu bùtóng.
column7: Every individual is different.
column9: A single member against the group: 個體差異. In China 個體戶 is a self-employed business owner. Mostly written or technical.

column3: Before a measure word or noun: 无数颗星星, 无数次. It is exaggeration for 'very many', not a literal count.
column6: Tiān shàng yǒu wúshù kē xīngxing.
column7: There are countless stars in the sky.
column9: Before a measure word or noun: 無數顆星星, 無數次. It is exaggeration for 'very many', not a literal count.

column3: Often with abstract nouns: 无限的可能, 无限期, 无限感激; also 无限大. The opposite is 有限.
column4: 孩子的想象力是无限的。
column5: 孩子的想像力是無限的。
column6: Háizi de xiǎngxiànglì shì wúxiàn de.
column7: A child's imagination is boundless.
column9: Often with abstract nouns: 無限的可能, 無限期, 無限感激; also 無限大. The opposite is 有限.

column3: 时间有限, 能力有限; 有限公司 is a limited company. 我的能力有限 is a modest way to say what you can't do. The opposite is 无限.
column6: Wǒ de shíjiān yǒuxiàn.
column7: My time is limited.
column9: 時間有限, 能力有限; 有限公司 is a limited company. 我的能力有限 is a modest way to say what you can't do. The opposite is 無限.

column3: Mostly in 丰富多样 and nouns like 多样性, 多样化. It can take 的 before a noun (多样的文化, 多样的形式) but, unlike 多种, not sit straight before one.
column6: Chéngshì de shēnghuó fēngfù duōyàng.
column7: City life is rich and varied.
column9: Mostly in 豐富多樣 and nouns like 多樣性, 多樣化. It can take 的 before a noun (多樣的文化, 多樣的形式) but, unlike 多種, not sit straight before one.

column3: Goes straight before a noun: 多种颜色, 多种方式. 多样 describes variety, while 多种 counts kinds.
column4: 这里有多种颜色可以选择。
column5: 這裡有多種顏色可以選擇。
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu duōzhǒng yánsè kěyǐ xuǎnzé.
column7: There are various colors to choose from.
column9: Goes straight before a noun: 多種顏色, 多種方式. 多樣 describes variety, while 多種 counts kinds.

column3: Follows the group noun directly and names one member: 原因之一, 四大发明之一, 最大的城市之一. The group always comes first.
column4: 北京是中国最大的城市之一。
column5: 北京是中國最大的城市之一。
column6: Běijīng shì Zhōngguó zuì dà de chéngshì zhīyī.
column7: Beijing is one of China's largest cities.
column9: Follows the group noun directly and names one member: 原因之一, 四大發明之一, 最大的城市之一. The group always comes first.

column3: Fractions: the bottom number comes first, so 三分之一 is one third. 百分之五十 is fifty percent and 二分之一 is a half.
column6: Sān fēnzhī yī de xuésheng méi lái.
column7: One third of the students did not come.
column9: Fractions: the bottom number comes first, so 三分之一 is one third. 百分之五十 is fifty percent and 二分之一 is a half.
