column3: Covers both the person and the field: 她是会计, 学会计. A 会计师 is a certified accountant. 会 is read kuài here, as a bound form for reckoning accounts.
column6: Tā shì gōngsī de kuàijì.
column7: She is the company's accountant.
column9: Covers both the person and the field: 她是會計, 學會計. A 會計師 is a certified accountant. 會 is read kuài here, as a bound form for reckoning accounts.

column3: 师 ends names of skilled professions: 老师, 医师, 工程师. 当律师 is to become a lawyer, 请律师 to hire one.
column6: Tā shì yī míng lǜshī.
column7: He is a lawyer.
column9: 師 ends names of skilled professions: 老師, 醫師, 工程師. 當律師 is to become a lawyer, 請律師 to hire one.

column3: Secretary: 秘 "secret" plus 书 "writing". Someone who handles letters and schedules for a boss: 秘书长 "secretary-general". 秘 is mì here, as in 秘密.
column4: 秘书把文件放在桌子上。
column5: 秘書把文件放在桌子上。
column6: Mìshū bǎ wénjiàn fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
column7: The secretary put the document on the table.
column9: Secretary: 祕 "secret" plus 書 "writing". Someone who handles letters and schedules for a boss: 祕書長 "secretary-general". 祕 is mì here, as in 祕密.

column3: A verb-object, so it splits: 加了班, 加班到很晚, 经常加班. Overtime pay is 加班费.
column6: Wǒ jīnwǎn yào jiābān.
column7: I have to work overtime tonight.
column9: A verb-object, so it splits: 加了班, 加班到很晚, 經常加班. Overtime pay is 加班費.

column3: A verb-object word, so 了 goes inside: 办了事. For errands and official business at an office or counter, and 办事处 is such an office. It also describes how someone works: 办事认真, 办事效率.
column6: Wǒ xiàwǔ yào qù yínháng bànshì.
column7: I am going to the bank this afternoon to take care of something.
column9: A verb-object word, so 了 goes inside: 辦了事. For errands and official business at an office or counter, and 辦事處 is such an office. It also describes how someone works: 辦事認真, 辦事效率.

column3: The post follows directly: 担任班长, 担任翻译, 担任经理. A formal word for taking on a role with duties; for an ordinary job in speech, 当 or 做 is plainer, as in 当老师.
column6: Tā dānrèn bānzhǎng.
column7: He serves as the class monitor.
column9: The post follows directly: 擔任班長, 擔任翻譯, 擔任經理. A formal word for taking on a role with duties; for an ordinary job in speech, 當 or 做 is plainer, as in 當老師.

column3: Pay and benefits together: 待遇好, and 待遇面议 in job ads, where the amount is settled in talks. The pay alone is 工资. It can also mean how people are treated: 平等的待遇.
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de dàiyù hěn hǎo.
column7: This company has good pay and benefits.
column9: Pay and benefits together: 待遇好, and 待遇面議 in job ads, where the amount is settled in talks. The pay alone is 工資. It can also mean how people are treated: 平等的待遇.

column3: Verb and noun: 他失业了, 失业率. The word is about losing a job; quitting is 辞职, and being let go is 被辞退. The person is 失业者.
column6: Tā qùnián shīyè le.
column7: He lost his job last year.
column9: Verb and noun: 他失業了, 失業率. The word is about losing a job; quitting is 辭職, and being let go is 被辭退. The person is 失業者.

column3: It comes before a noun: 业余爱好, 业余时间 (spare time), 业余选手 (a non-professional player). The opposite is 专业, a professional or specialized one.
column6: Tā de yèyú àihào shì huàhuà.
column7: His hobby is painting.
column9: It comes before a noun: 業餘愛好, 業餘時間 (spare time), 業餘選手 (a non-professional player). The opposite is 專業, a professional or specialized one.

column3: A whole field of work: 哪个行业, 服务行业, 教育行业. The 业 is the same one as in 企业, 营业 and 失业, which all concern business and work. 行 is read háng in this word (a line of business, a row) and xíng when it means to walk.
column6: Tā zài jiàoyù hángyè gōngzuò.
column7: He works in the education industry.
column9: A whole field of work: 哪個行業, 服務行業, 教育行業. The 業 is the same one as in 企業, 營業 and 失業, which all concern business and work. 行 is read háng in this word (a line of business, a row) and xíng when it means to walk.

column3: Identity, status: 身 "person" plus 份 "portion". Who one is: 身份证 "ID card", 他的身份是老师 "he is a teacher". Also capacity: 以老师的身份 "as a teacher". Taiwan writes 身分 more often. Read shēnfèn.
column6: Tā de shēnfèn shì lǎoshī.
column7: He is a teacher by profession.
column9: Identity, status: 身 "person" plus 份 "portion". Who one is: 身份證 "ID card", 他的身份是老師 "he is a teacher". Also capacity: 以老師的身份 "as a teacher". Taiwan writes 身分 more often. Read shēnfèn.

column3: Standing in society: 社会地位, 地位高 or 地位低. It also gives how important something is: 占重要地位. A seat is 座位, and 位 is the place that makes up the word.
column6: Nǚxìng de dìwèi yuè lái yuè gāo.
column7: Women's status is getting higher and higher.
column9: Standing in society: 社會地位, 地位高 or 地位低. It also gives how important something is: 佔重要地位. A seat is 座位, and 位 is the place that makes up the word.

column3: 员 marks a person in a job, as in 服务员, 运动员 and 营业员. For a person who works in a shop, 店员 is the plainer, more general word.
column6: Shòuhuòyuán zài zhěnglǐ huòjià.
column7: The sales clerk is arranging the shelves.
column9: 員 marks a person in a job, as in 服務員, 運動員 and 營業員. For a person who works in a shop, 店員 is the plainer, more general word.

column3: Model (fashion): a loanword from English "model", with 儿 ending: mótèr. 当模特儿 "work as a model". The 儿 ending is northern; Taiwan says 模特儿 and the last syllable is neutral. Without the 儿, 模特 is the same word.
column6: Tā xiǎng dāng mótèr.
column7: She wants to be a model.
column9: Model (fashion): a loanword from English "model", with 兒 ending: mótèr. 當模特兒 "work as a model". The 兒 ending is northern; Taiwan says 模特兒 and the last syllable is neutral. Without the 兒, 模特 is the same word.

column3: Handed over with both hands, as a polite gesture: 递名片, 交换名片. Also a phone contact card sent to someone: 电子名片.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de míngpiàn.
column7: This is my business card.
column9: Handed over with both hands, as a polite gesture: 遞名片, 交換名片. Also a phone contact card sent to someone: 電子名片.

column3: You write it (写简历) and send it in (投简历, 发简历). 简 is brief, as in 简单 and 简称, and 历 is past experience, as in 经历 and 学历: a brief record of your background.
column6: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de jiǎnlì fā gěi wǒ.
column7: Please send me your résumé.
column9: You write it (寫簡歷) and send it in (投簡歷, 發簡歷). 簡 is brief, as in 簡單 and 簡稱, and 歷 is past experience, as in 經歷 and 學歷: a brief record of your background.

column3: Noun and verb: 参加面试, 通过面试, 去面试. The interviewer is 面试官. A written test is 笔试, and a reporter’s interview is 采访, not 面试.
column6: Míngtiān wǒ yǒu yī ge miànshì.
column7: I have an interview tomorrow.
column9: Noun and verb: 參加面試, 通過面試, 去面試. The interviewer is 面試官. A written test is 筆試, and a reporter’s interview is 採訪, not 面試.

column3: The thing applied for follows directly: 申请签证, 申请奖学金, 申请大学. The form is 申请表. It goes to an office or institution, and is not a request to a friend.
column6: Wǒ shēnqǐng le yī suǒ dàxué.
column7: I applied to a university.
column9: The thing applied for follows directly: 申請簽證, 申請獎學金, 申請大學. The form is 申請表. It goes to an office or institution, and is not a request to a friend.

column3: Short courses for a job: 参加培训, 新员工培训, 培训课. A trainer is 培训师, and 受训 is to receive training. 培 is used for banking up earth around plants and also for training people.
column6: Gōngsī gěi xīn yuángōng péixùn.
column7: The company trains its new staff.
column9: Short courses for a job: 參加培訓, 新員工培訓, 培訓課. A trainer is 培訓師, and 受訓 is to receive training. 培 is used for banking up earth around plants and also for training people.

column3: A course you sign up for: 报培训班, 英语培训班. It covers adult skills and children’s interest classes alike; for remedial classes in school subjects, 补习班 is the usual word.
column4: 我报了一个英语培训班。
column5: 我報了一個英語培訓班。
column6: Wǒ bào le yī ge Yīngyǔ péixùnbān.
column7: I signed up for an English training class.
column9: A course you sign up for: 報培訓班, 英語培訓班. It covers adult skills and children’s interest classes alike; for remedial classes in school subjects, 補習班 is the usual word.

column3: Raising people and qualities over a long time: 培养兴趣, 培养人才, 培养习惯. A short course is 培训; 培养 is the slow raising. It also grows cells and bacteria in a lab.
column4: 父母要培养孩子的兴趣。
column5: 父母要培養孩子的興趣。
column6: Fùmǔ yào péiyǎng háizi de xìngqù.
column7: Parents should cultivate their children's interests.
column9: Raising people and qualities over a long time: 培養興趣, 培養人才, 培養習慣. A short course is 培訓; 培養 is the slow raising. It also grows cells and bacteria in a lab.

column3: Mostly plants and animals: 培育新品种 (a new variety), 培育花苗. In writing it carries over to people and ideals: 培育人才. More formal than 培养, and rarer in speech.
column4: 这所学校培育了很多人才。
column5: 這所學校培育了很多人才。
column6: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào péiyù le hěn duō réncái.
column7: This school has nurtured many talents.
column9: Mostly plants and animals: 培育新品種 (a new variety), 培育花苗. In writing it carries over to people and ideals: 培育人才. More formal than 培養, and rarer in speech.

column3: A lucky chance that comes along: 抓住机遇, 难得的机遇. Often paired with 挑战: 机遇与挑战. 机会 is the everyday chance; 机遇 sounds larger and rarer.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge nándé de jīyù.
column7: This is a rare opportunity.
column9: A lucky chance that comes along: 抓住機遇, 難得的機遇. Often paired with 挑戰: 機遇與挑戰. 機會 is the everyday chance; 機遇 sounds larger and rarer.

column3: How things will turn out for someone: 前途光明, 前途无量 (a limitless future), 没有前途. Said of a person, a job, a field or a company.
column6: Tā de qiántú yī piàn guāngmíng.
column7: His future is bright.
column9: How things will turn out for someone: 前途光明, 前途無量 (a limitless future), 沒有前途. Said of a person, a job, a field or a company.

column3: A knack or technique in doing something: 写作技巧, 沟通技巧, 说话的技巧. 技术 is technical skill or technology, as in a trade or engineering, not a knack.
column6: Xiězuò xūyào yīxiē jìqiǎo.
column7: Writing needs some technique.
column9: A knack or technique in doing something: 寫作技巧, 溝通技巧, 說話的技巧. 技術 is technical skill or technology, as in a trade or engineering, not a knack.

column3: Skill earned by practice: 熟练工人, 熟练掌握 (to have mastered). For being familiar with a person or a place, 熟悉 is the word, not 熟练.
column6: Tā dǎzì hěn shúliàn.
column7: She types very skillfully.
column9: Skill earned by practice: 熟練工人, 熟練掌握 (to have mastered). For being familiar with a person or a place, 熟悉 is the word, not 熟練.

column3: A verb must follow: 善于沟通, 善于学习. It describes a talent or habit. 擅长 means nearly the same but can also take a noun directly: 擅长数学.
column6: Tā shànyú hé rén jiāoliú.
column7: She is good at communicating with people.
column9: A verb must follow: 善於溝通, 善於學習. It describes a talent or habit. 擅長 means nearly the same but can also take a noun directly: 擅長數學.

column3: Mental ability that can be tested or trained: 智力测验, 开发智力. IQ is 智商. To call a person clever, say 聪明.
column4: 这个游戏可以锻炼智力。
column5: 這個遊戲可以鍛鍊智力。
column6: Zhège yóuxì kěyǐ duànliàn zhìlì.
column7: This game can train the mind.
column9: Mental ability that can be tested or trained: 智力測驗, 開發智力. IQ is 智商. To call a person clever, say 聰明.

column3: The word of news and policy for any size of business: 国有企业, 私营企业, 企业家 (entrepreneur). In chat about where you work, 公司 is the plainer word. In Taiwan, 企 in this word is read qì.
column4: 这家企业有一千名员工。
column5: 這家企業有一千名員工。
column6: Zhè jiā qǐyè yǒu yīqiān míng yuángōng.
column7: This company has a thousand employees.
column9: The word of news and policy for any size of business: 國有企業, 私營企業, 企業家 (entrepreneur). In chat about where you work, 公司 is the plainer word. In Taiwan, 企 in this word is read qì.

column3: A body that does a particular job: 金融机构, 研究机构, 政府机构. Wider than 公司, since a bank, a school or an agency all count.
column4: 他在一个国际机构工作。
column5: 他在一個國際機構工作。
column6: Tā zài yī ge guójì jīgòu gōngzuò.
column7: He works at an international organization.
column9: A body that does a particular job: 金融機構, 研究機構, 政府機構. Wider than 公司, since a bank, a school or an agency all count.

column3: A large building or engineering project: 建筑工程, 重点工程. An engineer is 工程师. A project in an office or lab is usually 项目.
column4: 这个工程要三年才能完成。
column5: 這個工程要三年才能完成。
column6: Zhège gōngchéng yào sān nián cái néng wánchéng.
column7: This project will take three years to complete.
column9: A large building or engineering project: 建築工程, 重點工程. An engineer is 工程師. A project in an office or lab is usually 項目.

column3: A project with a plan: 新项目, 项目经理, 项目组. Also an event in a sports meet: 比赛项目. 项 alone counts tasks and studies, as in 一项研究.
column4: 我们正在做一个新项目。
column5: 我們正在做一個新項目。
column6: Wǒmen zhèngzài zuò yī ge xīn xiàngmù.
column7: We are working on a new project.
column9: A project with a plan: 新項目, 項目經理, 項目組. Also an event in a sports meet: 比賽項目. 項 alone counts tasks and studies, as in 一項研究.

column3: Contract: 合 "join" plus 同 "same". A legal agreement: 签合同, 劳动合同 "work contract", 合同到期. Written and binding. Taiwan says 合约 or 契约. The second syllable is neutral in speech: hétong.
column6: Qǐng zài hétóng shàng qiānzì.
column7: Please sign the contract.
column9: Contract: 合 "join" plus 同 "same". A legal agreement: 簽合同, 勞動合同 "work contract", 合同到期. Written and binding. Taiwan says 合約 or 契約. The second syllable is neutral in speech: hétong.

column3: The size of an organization, event or effort: 规模大, 扩大规模, 具有一定规模. It is not used for the size of an object like a table.
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de guīmó hěn dà.
column7: This company is very large.
column9: The size of an organization, event or effort: 規模大, 擴大規模, 具有一定規模. It is not used for the size of an object like a table.

column3: It comes before a verb or noun: 大规模生产, 大规模投资. It fits plans, campaigns and production. The opposite is 小规模.
column6: Zhèngfǔ kāishǐ dàguīmó jiànshè.
column7: The government began large-scale construction.
column9: It comes before a verb or noun: 大規模生產, 大規模投資. It fits plans, campaigns and production. The opposite is 小規模.

column3: How fast and well work gets done: 工作效率, 效率高, 提高效率. The result itself is 效果, not 效率. 率 is read lǜ here, meaning a rate; read shuài it means to lead or command.
column6: Tā gōngzuò xiàolǜ hěn gāo.
column7: He works very efficiently.
column9: How fast and well work gets done: 工作效率, 效率高, 提高效率. The result itself is 效果, not 效率. 率 is read lǜ here, meaning a rate; read shuài it means to lead or command.

column3: Here it means to draw a line or mark off: 划线, 划重点. It is also the last character of 计划 and 规划, both meaning a plan.
column4: 请在这个词下面划一条线。
column5: 請在這個詞下面劃一條線。
column6: Qǐng zài zhège cí xiàmiàn huà yī tiáo xiàn.
column7: Please draw a line under this word.
column9: Here it means to draw a line or mark off: 劃線, 劃重點. It is also the last character of 計劃 and 規劃, both meaning a plan.

column3: A worked-out plan to act on: 设计方案, 解决方案 (a solution), 三个方案. More detailed than 计划, and you can choose between several.
column6: Wǒmen tǎolùn le sān ge fāng'àn.
column7: We discussed three plans.
column9: A worked-out plan to act on: 設計方案, 解決方案 (a solution), 三個方案. More detailed than 計劃, and you can choose between several.

column3: To put a law, plan or policy into effect: 实施计划, 全面实施. A written, official word. A new rule can start by itself: 开始实施. For an order from above, 执行 is also used.
column4: 新规定下个月开始实施。
column5: 新規定下個月開始實施。
column6: Xīn guīdìng xià ge yuè kāishǐ shíshī.
column7: The new rules take effect next month.
column9: To put a law, plan or policy into effect: 實施計劃, 全面實施. A written, official word. A new rule can start by itself: 開始實施. For an order from above, 執行 is also used.

column3: Said of a shop or restaurant that is open: 营业时间 (opening hours), 开始营业, 停止营业. A shop clerk is 营业员. The sign 营业中 means open.
column4: 商店早上九点开始营业。
column5: 商店早上九點開始營業。
column6: Shāngdiàn zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ yíngyè.
column7: The shop opens at nine in the morning.
column9: Said of a shop or restaurant that is open: 營業時間 (opening hours), 開始營業, 停止營業. A shop clerk is 營業員. The sign 營業中 means open.

column3: It comes before a noun: 商务舱 (business class), 商务旅行, 商务会议. A word for offices and travel; a single deal or trade is 生意.
column4: 他这次去北京是商务旅行。
column5: 他這次去北京是商務旅行。
column6: Tā zhè cì qù Běijīng shì shāngwù lǚxíng.
column7: His trip to Beijing this time is a business trip.
column9: It comes before a noun: 商務艙 (business class), 商務旅行, 商務會議. A word for offices and travel; a single deal or trade is 生意.

column3: Both the agent and the agency: 房产中介, 找中介, 中介费 (the fee). Most often it means real estate, but it works for any go-between. It is also a verb, to link two sides.
column4: 我通过中介找到了房子。
column5: 我通過中介找到了房子。
column6: Wǒ tōngguò zhōngjiè zhǎodào le fángzi.
column7: I found the house through an agent.
column9: Both the agent and the agency: 房產中介, 找中介, 中介費 (the fee). Most often it means real estate, but it works for any go-between. It is also a verb, to link two sides.

column3: To keep something going as it is: 维持秩序, 维持生活 (to make a living), 维持现状. It needs an object. The 维 in 维持, 维护 and 维修 is the same one.
column6: Tā kào dǎgōng wéichí shēnghuó.
column7: He makes a living by doing odd jobs.
column9: To keep something going as it is: 維持秩序, 維持生活 (to make a living), 維持現狀. It needs an object. The 維 in 維持, 維護 and 維修 is the same one.

column3: To defend or keep up something valued: 维护权利, 维护和平, and also systems and equipment: 系统维护, 设备维护. 维修 is the repair of something broken.
column6: Wǒmen yào wéihù shìjiè hépíng.
column7: We must safeguard world peace.
column9: To defend or keep up something valued: 維護權利, 維護和平, and also systems and equipment: 系統維護, 設備維護. 維修 is the repair of something broken.

column3: Upkeep and repair of equipment, buildings and vehicles, as a noun (维修费, 维修站) or a verb. It is the word on signs: 电梯正在维修.
column4: 电梯正在维修，请走楼梯。
column5: 電梯正在維修，請走樓梯。
column6: Diàntī zhèngzài wéixiū, qǐng zǒu lóutī.
column7: The elevator is being repaired, please use the stairs.
column9: Upkeep and repair of equipment, buildings and vehicles, as a noun (維修費, 維修站) or a verb. It is the word on signs: 電梯正在維修.

column3: To fix a broken thing, and the object follows directly: 修理自行车, 修理电脑. A repairer is 修理工. In speech it can also mean to sort someone out: 我要修理你!
column4: 我的手机坏了，要拿去修理。
column5: 我的手機壞了，要拿去修理。
column6: Wǒ de shǒujī huài le, yào ná qù xiūlǐ.
column7: My phone is broken and has to be taken to be repaired.
column9: To fix a broken thing, and the object follows directly: 修理自行車, 修理電腦. A repairer is 修理工. In speech it can also mean to sort someone out: 我要修理你!

column3: As a noun, a device built into a larger system: 安全装置, 控制装置. More technical than 机器. As a verb, to install, it is rarer than 安装.
column4: 这台机器有一个安全装置。
column5: 這台機器有一個安全裝置。
column6: Zhè tái jīqì yǒu yī ge ānquán zhuāngzhì.
column7: This machine has a safety device.
column9: As a noun, a device built into a larger system: 安全裝置, 控制裝置. More technical than 機器. As a verb, to install, it is rarer than 安裝.

column3: The buildings and equipment that serve a purpose: 公共设施, 体育设施, 医疗设施. A collective noun, so there is no 个: say 这些设施, or 设施齐全 (fully equipped).
column4: 这个小区的设施很齐全。
column5: 這個小區的設施很齊全。
column6: Zhège xiǎoqū de shèshī hěn qíquán.
column7: This residential area is very well equipped.
column9: The buildings and equipment that serve a purpose: 公共設施, 體育設施, 醫療設施. A collective noun, so there is no 個: say 這些設施, or 設施齊全 (fully equipped).

column3: Alone it mostly means to install or fit: 安灯, 安空调. The peaceful sense lives in compounds: 平安, 安全, 安静, 晚安. A place can follow with 在.
column6: Qǐng nǐ bǎ dēng ān zài zhèlǐ.
column7: Please install the lamp here.
column9: Alone it mostly means to install or fit: 安燈, 安空調. The peaceful sense lives in compounds: 平安, 安全, 安靜, 晚安. A place can follow with 在.

column3: To find a proper place for people or things: 安置难民, 安置行李. Someone arranges it, often after a move or a disaster, and the object is usually a person or group needing housing or work.
column4: 政府安置了受灾的群众。
column5: 政府安置了受災的群眾。
column6: Zhèngfǔ ānzhì le shòuzāi de qúnzhòng.
column7: The government resettled the people hit by the disaster.
column9: To find a proper place for people or things: 安置難民, 安置行李. Someone arranges it, often after a move or a disaster, and the object is usually a person or group needing housing or work.

column3: A verb (把桌子固定住) and an adjective: 固定工作 (a steady job), 固定时间, 固定收入. 不固定 means not fixed, and a temporary job is 临时工作.
column4: 他每天在固定的时间跑步。
column5: 他每天在固定的時間跑步。
column6: Tā měitiān zài gùdìng de shíjiān pǎobù.
column7: He runs at a fixed time every day.
column9: A verb (把桌子固定住) and an adjective: 固定工作 (a steady job), 固定時間, 固定收入. 不固定 means not fixed, and a temporary job is 臨時工作.

column3: It starts many words: 决定, 一定, 规定, 稳定. As a verb it settles things: 定计划, 定时间. It also means to book: 定机票, though 订 is the usual character for that in writing.
column6: Wǒmen dìng le míngtiān de jīpiào.
column7: We have booked tomorrow's plane tickets.
column9: It starts many words: 決定, 一定, 規定, 穩定. As a verb it settles things: 定計劃, 定時間. It also means to book: 定機票, though 訂 is the usual character for that in writing.

column3: Steady, whether a thing does not wobble (开得很稳) or a person is reliable (他做事很稳). After a verb it means firmly: 站稳, 坐稳, 拿稳.
column6: Qǐng zuò wěn le, chē yào kāi le.
column7: Please sit tight, the bus is about to go.
column9: Steady, whether a thing does not wobble (開得很穩) or a person is reliable (他做事很穩). After a verb it means firmly: 站穩, 坐穩, 拿穩.

column3: An even level over time: 情绪稳定, 物价稳定, 工作稳定, and the verb 稳定下来 (to settle down). It is common for the economy, prices, a job or feelings.
column6: Tā de gōngzuò hěn wěndìng.
column7: His job is very stable.
column9: An even level over time: 情緒穩定, 物價穩定, 工作穩定, and the verb 穩定下來 (to settle down). It is common for the economy, prices, a job or feelings.

column3: For things that will not break or fall: 坚固的桥, 坚固的房子; figuratively, 坚固的友谊. Not steadiness like 稳. In everyday speech, 结实 is also used for sturdy.
column6: Zhè zuò qiáo fēicháng jiāngù.
column7: This bridge is extremely sturdy.
column9: For things that will not break or fall: 堅固的橋, 堅固的房子; figuratively, 堅固的友誼. Not steadiness like 穩. In everyday speech, 結實 is also used for sturdy.

column3: Smooth and steady, with no bumps or swings: 平稳地飞行, 价格平稳, 心情平稳. The adverb form is 平稳地.
column6: Fēijī píngwěn de jiàngluò le.
column7: The plane landed smoothly.
column9: Smooth and steady, with no bumps or swings: 平穩地飛行, 價格平穩, 心情平穩. The adverb form is 平穩地.

column3: To guard: 守门 (also to play goalkeeper), 守在门口. It also means to keep or follow: 守规矩, 守时 (be punctual), 守信用 (keep your word). In both senses you stay in place.
column6: Nǐ yào shǒu guījǔ, bùyào luàn pǎo.
column7: You must follow the rules and not run around.
column9: To guard: 守門 (also to play goalkeeper), 守在門口. It also means to keep or follow: 守規矩, 守時 (be punctual), 守信用 (keep your word). In both senses you stay in place.

column3: Formal: it suits programs, accounts and shops that shut down for good (工厂被关闭了), and notices such as 请关闭手机 and 请关闭门窗. In everyday speech a door or light is just 关.
column6: Qǐng guānbì shǒujī.
column7: Please turn off your phones.
column9: Formal: it suits programs, accounts and shops that shut down for good (工廠被關閉了), and notices such as 請關閉手機 and 請關閉門窗. In everyday speech a door or light is just 關.

column3: Written Chinese: it lives in set phrases (无法, 无人, 无关, 无意) and as a prefix meaning un- or -less (无用). Speech uses 没有 instead.
column4: 他无家可归，只好住在朋友家。
column5: 他無家可歸，只好住在朋友家。
column6: Tā wú jiā kě guī, zhǐhǎo zhù zài péngyou jiā.
column7: He had no home to go back to and had to stay at a friend's.
column9: Written Chinese: it lives in set phrases (無法, 無人, 無關, 無意) and as a prefix meaning un- or -less (無用). Speech uses 沒有 instead.

column3: Goes straight before a verb: 无法解释, 无法相信. It is the written, slightly formal cousin of spoken 没办法 and 没法儿, and you meet it in error messages (无法登录).
column6: Wǒ wúfǎ huídá zhège wèntí.
column7: I cannot answer this question.
column9: Goes straight before a verb: 無法解釋, 無法相信. It is the written, slightly formal cousin of spoken 沒辦法 and 沒法兒, and you meet it in error messages (無法登錄).

column3: The same 不起 pattern also means can't afford: 买不起, 吃不起. Here it is attitude toward a person: 看不起别人, and 被人看不起 is common. The positive 看得起 is rarer.
column4: 不要看不起任何一个人。
column5: 不要看不起任何一個人。
column6: Bùyào kànbuqǐ rènhé yī ge rén.
column7: Don't look down on anyone.
column9: The same 不起 pattern also means can't afford: 買不起, 吃不起. Here it is attitude toward a person: 看不起別人, and 被人看不起 is common. The positive 看得起 is rarer.

column3: A spoken complaint about heat, noise or a person: 热得受不了, 我受不了他. It works as a complete reply, and the positive 受得了 mostly turns up in questions. The 了 is read liǎo here, the 了 that follows 得 or 不 to express possibility, as in 忘不了.
column6: Zhèlǐ tài chǎo le, wǒ shòubuliǎo.
column7: It's too noisy here, I can't stand it.
column9: A spoken complaint about heat, noise or a person: 熱得受不了, 我受不了他. It works as a complete reply, and the positive 受得了 mostly turns up in questions. The 了 is read liǎo here, the 了 that follows 得 or 不 to express possibility, as in 忘不了.

column3: Praise for a person or an achievement: 你真了不起, 了不起的人. Said with a shrug it turns sarcastic: 有什么了不起的 means what is so great about that, and 没什么了不起 means nothing special.
column4: 他十岁就会写诗，真了不起。
column5: 他十歲就會寫詩，真了不起。
column6: Tā shí suì jiù huì xiě shī, zhēn liǎobuqǐ.
column7: He could write poems at ten, which is amazing.
column9: Praise for a person or an achievement: 你真了不起, 了不起的人. Said with a shrug it turns sarcastic: 有什麼了不起的 means what is so great about that, and 沒什麼了不起 means nothing special.

column3: About running out of time, not about ability: 来不及吃早饭, and 来不及了 alone means too late. The positive 来得及 is mostly heard in questions and in 还来得及. 及 is built as a hand grabbing a person.
column6: Kuài diǎnr, yào láibují le.
column7: Hurry up, we're running out of time.
column9: About running out of time, not about ability: 來不及吃早飯, and 來不及了 alone means too late. The positive 來得及 is mostly heard in questions and in 還來得及. 及 is built as a hand grabbing a person.

column3: Names what you depend on, a person or a thing: 孩子离不开妈妈. The same 不开 pattern gives 走不开 (can't get away from work) and 打不开 (won't open). 开 after a verb is a directional complement meaning away or off.
column4: 现在的人都离不开手机。
column5: 現在的人都離不開手機。
column6: Xiànzài de rén dōu líbukāi shǒujī.
column7: Nowadays people can't do without their phones.
column9: Names what you depend on, a person or a thing: 孩子離不開媽媽. The same 不開 pattern gives 走不開 (can't get away from work) and 打不開 (won't open). 開 after a verb is a directional complement meaning away or off.

column3: Far more common than 在乎 itself, and it takes its object directly: 不在乎钱, 不在乎别人怎么说. It is not caring about what others might mind, whereas 无所谓 is having no preference between options (吃什么都无所谓). 乎 is a classical particle similar to 於, with the sense in or at.
column4: 他一点儿也不在乎别人怎么说。
column5: 他一點兒也不在乎別人怎麼說。
column6: Tā yīdiǎnr yě bùzàihu biéren zěnme shuō.
column7: He doesn't care at all what other people say.
column9: Far more common than 在乎 itself, and it takes its object directly: 不在乎錢, 不在乎別人怎麼說. It is not caring about what others might mind, whereas 無所謂 is having no preference between options (吃什麼都無所謂). 乎 is a classical particle similar to 於, with the sense in or at.

column3: Mostly used in the negative or in questions: 你在乎吗, 我在乎你的看法. It is about whether something matters to you, while 关心 is about looking after someone. Said warmly, 我在乎你 means you matter to me.
column6: Nǐ zàihu tā de kànfǎ ma?
column7: Do you care what he thinks?
column9: Mostly used in the negative or in questions: 你在乎嗎, 我在乎你的看法. It is about whether something matters to you, while 關心 is about looking after someone. Said warmly, 我在乎你 means you matter to me.

column3: Said when you have no preference: 吃什么都无所谓, and 我无所谓 alone means whatever. A question word with 都 is the usual frame (去哪儿都无所谓). Said flatly it can sound uninterested.
column4: 去哪儿吃饭我都无所谓。
column5: 去哪兒吃飯我都無所謂。
column6: Qù nǎr chīfàn wǒ dōu wúsuǒwèi.
column7: I don't mind where we go to eat.
column9: Said when you have no preference: 吃什麼都無所謂, and 我無所謂 alone means whatever. A question word with 都 is the usual frame (去哪兒都無所謂). Said flatly it can sound uninterested.

column3: Reassures that the trouble is small (没带伞不要紧) or that something is not serious (他的病不要紧). The positive 要紧 means important or urgent: 有要紧的事. After an apology, 没关系 is the more general reply.
column4: 没带伞不要紧，我有一把。
column5: 沒帶傘不要緊，我有一把。
column6: Méi dài sǎn bùyàojǐn, wǒ yǒu yī bǎ.
column7: It doesn't matter that you didn't bring an umbrella, I have one.
column9: Reassures that the trouble is small (沒帶傘不要緊) or that something is not serious (他的病不要緊). The positive 要緊 means important or urgent: 有要緊的事. After an apology, 沒關係 is the more general reply.

column3: Colloquial: 我没法儿去. It is also a complete reply, 没法儿！, for nothing can be done. In writing, 没办法 or 无法 is safer. The 儿 is read r here, a non-syllabic suffix that adds no syllable.
column4: 雨太大了，我没法儿出门。
column5: 雨太大了，我沒法兒出門。
column6: Yǔ tài dà le, wǒ méifár chūmén.
column7: It's raining too hard, I can't go out.
column9: Colloquial: 我沒法兒去. It is also a complete reply, 沒法兒！, for nothing can be done. In writing, 沒辦法 or 無法 is safer. The 兒 is read r here, a non-syllabic suffix that adds no syllable.

column3: Agrees with someone: 你说得没错. Alone, 没错！ means exactly or sure thing, and 交给我，没错 reassures that nothing will go wrong. The shape matches 没问题 and 没关系.
column4: 你说得没错，我今天太累了。
column5: 你說得沒錯，我今天太累了。
column6: Nǐ shuō de méicuò, wǒ jīntiān tài lèi le.
column7: You're right, I'm too tired today.
column9: Agrees with someone: 你說得沒錯. Alone, 沒錯！ means exactly or sure thing, and 交給我，沒錯 reassures that nothing will go wrong. The shape matches 沒問題 and 沒關係.

column3: Introduces a surprise, often with 竟然 or 居然: 没想到你也来了. 想不到 means almost the same, and either can stand alone or open a sentence. After a verb, 到 is a complement indicating arriving at a place or reaching a point.
column6: Méixiǎngdào nǐ yě lái le!
column7: I didn't expect you to come too!
column9: Introduces a surprise, often with 竟然 or 居然: 沒想到你也來了. 想不到 means almost the same, and either can stand alone or open a sentence. After a verb, 到 is a complement indicating arriving at a place or reaching a point.

column3: Says there is still time: 现在走还来得及, and 还来得及 is a very common reassurance. It is often asked as 来得及吗, and a verb can follow: 来得及赶上火车.
column6: Xiànzài chūfā hái láidejí.
column7: There's still time if we set off now.
column9: Says there is still time: 現在走還來得及, and 還來得及 is a very common reassurance. It is often asked as 來得及嗎, and a verb can follow: 來得及趕上火車.

column3: Formal, and only for meetings and conferences: 召开会议, 召开记者招待会. The organizer is the subject, and the news often says 会议将于明天召开. A party or class takes 开 or 举办 instead. 召 was originally to call out with the mouth.
column4: 公司明天要召开记者招待会。
column5: 公司明天要召開記者招待會。
column6: Gōngsī míngtiān yào zhàokāi jìzhě zhāodàihuì.
column7: The company will hold a press conference tomorrow.
column9: Formal, and only for meetings and conferences: 召開會議, 召開記者招待會. The organizer is the subject, and the news often says 會議將於明天召開. A party or class takes 開 or 舉辦 instead. 召 was originally to call out with the mouth.

column3: A formal gathering of a whole body, bigger than a 会议: 全体大会, 股东大会. In the news it names bodies and congresses, such as 联合国大会. 会 is also the ending of 同学会 and 运动会.
column4: 大会明天上午九点开始。
column5: 大會明天上午九點開始。
column6: Dàhuì míngtiān shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ.
column7: The general meeting starts at nine tomorrow morning.
column9: A formal gathering of a whole body, bigger than a 會議: 全體大會, 股東大會. In the news it names bodies and congresses, such as 聯合國大會. 會 is also the ending of 同學會 and 運動會.

column3: Chair of a meeting or committee, and the title of the head of a body: 学生会主席, 主席先生. China's head of state is the 国家主席, while a president elsewhere is a 总统. 席 pictures a woven mat with ornament, and it also means a seat, a banquet or a place in an assembly.
column6: Tā shì xuéshēnghuì de zhǔxí.
column7: He is the chair of the student council.
column9: Chair of a meeting or committee, and the title of the head of a body: 學生會主席, 主席先生. China's head of state is the 國家主席, while a president elsewhere is a 總統. 席 pictures a woven mat with ornament, and it also means a seat, a banquet or a place in an assembly.

column3: A talk or lecture series open to the public, not a class: 听讲座, 举办讲座. Count it with 场 or 个: 一场讲座.
column4: 今天下午有一个关于健康的讲座。
column5: 今天下午有一個關於健康的講座。
column6: Jīntiān xiàwǔ yǒu yī ge guānyú jiànkāng de jiǎngzuò.
column7: There is a talk about health this afternoon.
column9: A talk or lecture series open to the public, not a class: 聽講座, 舉辦講座. Count it with 場 or 個: 一場講座.

column3: A prepared speech to an audience, as verb and noun: 做演讲, 发表演讲, 演讲比赛. As a verb it takes no object; the topic comes with 关于: 关于环保的演讲. 演 is the perform character in 演员 and 表演.
column4: 她在大会上做了一个精彩的演讲。
column5: 她在大會上做了一個精彩的演講。
column6: Tā zài dàhuì shang zuò le yī ge jīngcǎi de yǎnjiǎng.
column7: She gave a wonderful speech at the meeting.
column9: A prepared speech to an audience, as verb and noun: 做演講, 發表演講, 演講比賽. As a verb it takes no object; the topic comes with 關於: 關於環保的演講. 演 is the perform character in 演員 and 表演.

column3: Reports upward, from junior to senior, on work or progress: 向经理汇报工作. The noun is 工作汇报. A news report is 报道, and a notice going down to staff is 通知.
column6: Wǒ yào xiàng jīnglǐ huìbào gōngzuò.
column7: I have to report on my work to the manager.
column9: Reports upward, from junior to senior, on work or progress: 向經理匯報工作. The noun is 工作匯報. A news report is 報道, and a notice going down to staff is 通知.

column3: Formal and official: what you seek is almost always an opinion or consent (征求意见, 征求同意), and a draft put out for comment is 征求意见稿. The 求 is the same as in 要求 and 请求.
column6: Lǎoshī zhēngqiú dàjiā de yìjiàn.
column7: The teacher asks everyone for their opinions.
column9: Formal and official: what you seek is almost always an opinion or consent (徵求意見, 徵求同意), and a draft put out for comment is 徵求意見稿. The 求 is the same as in 要求 and 請求.

column3: Passes on a message you received, politely: 请转告他明天开会. A person follows, then the message. 转达 is close, often for thanks or greetings, while telling your own news first-hand is 告诉.
column6: Qǐng nǐ zhuǎngào tā, míngtiān kāihuì.
column7: Please tell him that there is a meeting tomorrow.
column9: Passes on a message you received, politely: 請轉告他明天開會. A person follows, then the message. 轉達 is close, often for thanks or greetings, while telling your own news first-hand is 告訴.

column3: The person reminded is the object, then what to do: 提醒我带伞. It can also warn gently (提醒大家注意安全) and appears on signs as 温馨提示, with 提示 instead.
column6: Qǐng tíxǐng wǒ míngtiān dài sǎn.
column7: Please remind me to bring an umbrella tomorrow.
column9: The person reminded is the object, then what to do: 提醒我帶傘. It can also warn gently (提醒大家注意安全) and appears on signs as 溫馨提示, with 提示 instead.

column3: Needs a person as its object: 说服他去看医生, 被说服. 有说服力 means convincing, with 力 for power. The 服 is the same as in 佩服 and 服从.
column6: Wǒ shuōfú le tā qù kàn yīshēng.
column7: I persuaded him to go and see a doctor.
column9: Needs a person as its object: 說服他去看醫生, 被說服. 有說服力 means convincing, with 力 for power. The 服 is the same as in 佩服 and 服從.

column3: Admits something true that is often unwelcome: 承认错误, 我承认, 不敢承认. It is also how a state or a result is recognized (承认这个结果), and 承担 and 承受 share the 承. 承 pictures a kneeling person with both hands, to hold or carry.
column6: Tā chéngrèn shì zìjǐ de cuò.
column7: He admitted it was his own fault.
column9: Admits something true that is often unwelcome: 承認錯誤, 我承認, 不敢承認. It is also how a state or a result is recognized (承認這個結果), and 承擔 and 承受 share the 承. 承 pictures a kneeling person with both hands, to hold or carry.

column3: Checks details and fixes them: 确认时间, 确认订单, and a 确认 button on a screen. It is neutral and has nothing to do with guilt, unlike 承认. 确定 and 确实 share the 确. 确 holds 石, rock: as certain as a rock.
column6: Qǐng zài quèrèn yīxià shíjiān.
column7: Please confirm the time once more.
column9: Checks details and fixes them: 確認時間, 確認訂單, and a 確認 button on a screen. It is neutral and has nothing to do with guilt, unlike 承認. 確定 and 確實 share the 確. 確 holds 石, rock: as certain as a rock.

column3: Informal talk about a person or an event, often gossip: 议论别人, 大家都在议论这件事. 议论纷纷 means everyone is talking. As a noun: 引起议论. 讨论 is the orderly version.
column6: Dàjiā dōu zài yìlùn zhè jiàn shì.
column7: Everyone is talking about this.
column9: Informal talk about a person or an event, often gossip: 議論別人, 大家都在議論這件事. 議論紛紛 means everyone is talking. As a noun: 引起議論. 討論 is the orderly version.

column3: A dispute that can heat up: 争论不休, 引起争论, and as a noun a debate or controversy. The topic comes first or after 为: 为这件事争论. A personal quarrel is 吵架.
column4: 他们为这件事争论了很久。
column5: 他們為這件事爭論了很久。
column6: Tāmen wèi zhè jiàn shì zhēnglùn le hěn jiǔ.
column7: They argued about this for a long time.
column9: A dispute that can heat up: 爭論不休, 引起爭論, and as a noun a debate or controversy. The topic comes first or after 為: 為這件事爭論. A personal quarrel is 吵架.

column3: A structured debate with two sides: 辩论赛, 辩论队. The 辩 also gives 辩护 (defend) and 辩解 (explain oneself). Heated, loose arguing is 争论. The doubled part of 辩 possibly symbolizes two prisoners accusing each other.
column4: 这个问题他们辩论了一个晚上。
column5: 這個問題他們辯論了一個晚上。
column6: Zhège wèntí tāmen biànlùn le yī ge wǎnshang.
column7: They debated this question all evening.
column9: A structured debate with two sides: 辯論賽, 辯論隊. The 辯 also gives 辯護 (defend) and 辯解 (explain oneself). Heated, loose arguing is 爭論. The doubled part of 辯 possibly symbolizes two prisoners accusing each other.

column3: A reporter's interview or coverage: 采访市长, 接受采访. For a job interview use 面试. The 采 gives 采用, 采取 and 采购 too. 采 shows a hand picking from a tree.
column4: 记者正在采访那位运动员。
column5: 記者正在採訪那位運動員。
column6: Jìzhě zhèngzài cǎifǎng nà wèi yùndòngyuán.
column7: The reporter is interviewing that athlete.
column9: A reporter's interview or coverage: 採訪市長, 接受採訪. For a job interview use 面試. The 採 gives 採用, 採取 and 採購 too. 採 shows a hand picking from a tree.

column3: Being involved in a matter, often its planning or decision: 参与讨论, 参与者. More formal than 参加, which fits attending an event. The 与 here is read yù, meaning to take part in.
column4: 每个人都可以参与讨论。
column5: 每個人都可以參與討論。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu kěyǐ cānyù tǎolùn.
column7: Everyone can join the discussion.
column9: Being involved in a matter, often its planning or decision: 參與討論, 參與者. More formal than 參加, which fits attending an event. The 與 here is read yù, meaning to take part in.

column3: Joining an organization means becoming a member: 加入俱乐部, 加入我们. Online it is 加入购物车 and 加入群. It also means adding something in: 往汤里加入一点盐. Attending an event is 参加.
column4: 我想加入你们的足球队。
column5: 我想加入你們的足球隊。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng jiārù nǐmen de zúqiúduì.
column7: I'd like to join your soccer team.
column9: Joining an organization means becoming a member: 加入俱樂部, 加入我們. Online it is 加入購物車 and 加入群. It also means adding something in: 往湯里加入一點鹽. Attending an event is 參加.

column3: For formal events, meetings and ceremonies: 出席会议, 出席婚礼. The opposite is 缺席, and attendance is 出席率. A class or casual party does not take it.
column4: 总统将出席明天的会议。
column5: 總統將出席明天的會議。
column6: Zǒngtǒng jiāng chūxí míngtiān de huìyì.
column7: The president will attend tomorrow's meeting.
column9: For formal events, meetings and ceremonies: 出席會議, 出席婚禮. The opposite is 缺席, and attendance is 出席率. A class or casual party does not take it.

column3: People coming to a set place and time: 在门口集合, 八点集合, and the leader's call 大家集合！ On notices it is 集合地点. In math it is a set, so the word turns up in school texts.
column4: 明天早上七点在学校门口集合。
column5: 明天早上七點在學校門口集合。
column6: Míngtiān zǎoshang qī diǎn zài xuéxiào ménkǒu jíhé.
column7: We'll meet at the school gate at seven tomorrow morning.
column9: People coming to a set place and time: 在門口集合, 八點集合, and the leader's call 大家集合！ On notices it is 集合地點. In math it is a set, so the word turns up in school texts.

column3: Common frames: 想象一下, 想象不到, 难以想象, 想象力. It is a picture formed in the mind of something not in front of you. 象 is the elephant character; it also means shape or appearance.
column4: 你想象一下，一百年以后会怎么样。
column5: 你想象一下，一百年以後會怎麼樣。
column6: Nǐ xiǎngxiàng yīxià, yībǎi nián yǐhòu huì zěnmeyàng.
column7: Imagine what things will be like in a hundred years.
column9: Common frames: 想象一下, 想象不到, 難以想象, 想象力. It is a picture formed in the mind of something not in front of you. 象 is the elephant character; it also means shape or appearance.

column3: Slower and deeper than 想: 思考问题, 独立思考, 值得思考. It takes problems, life or choices rather than a person as its object. 思 may be a fontanel plus a heart; the fontanel part later changed into 田.
column4: 遇到问题时，先要认真思考。
column5: 遇到問題時，先要認真思考。
column6: Yùdào wèntí shí, xiān yào rènzhēn sīkǎo.
column7: When you meet a problem, you first need to think seriously.
column9: Slower and deeper than 想: 思考問題, 獨立思考, 值得思考. It takes problems, life or choices rather than a person as its object. 思 may be a fontanel plus a heart; the fontanel part later changed into 田.

column3: Weighing options before deciding: 考虑一下, 考虑清楚, 值得考虑. 我考虑考虑 is a polite way to put someone off. 考虑到 means taking into account. 思考 is deeper and more abstract.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ yào kǎolǜ yīxià.
column7: I need to think this over.
column9: Weighing options before deciding: 考慮一下, 考慮清楚, 值得考慮. 我考慮考慮 is a polite way to put someone off. 考慮到 means taking into account. 思考 is deeper and more abstract.

column3: A noun for doubt or a question: 有疑问, 提出疑问, and 毫无疑问 (no doubt at all). 有什么疑问吗 is how a teacher asks if there are any questions. 疑问句 is a question sentence. 疑 began as a man with a cane looking around, mouth wide open, not knowing where to go.
column4: 如果你有疑问，可以问老师。
column5: 如果你有疑問，可以問老師。
column6: Rúguǒ nǐ yǒu yíwèn, kěyǐ wèn lǎoshī.
column7: If you have questions, you can ask the teacher.
column9: A noun for doubt or a question: 有疑問, 提出疑問, and 毫無疑問 (no doubt at all). 有什麼疑問嗎 is how a teacher asks if there are any questions. 疑問句 is a question sentence. 疑 began as a man with a cane looking around, mouth wide open, not knowing where to go.

column3: Finding out or knowing about a person, place or situation: 了解情况, 我不太了解他, 我去了解一下. For grasping a language point or what someone said, 懂 or 明白 is the word. The 了 is read liǎo here, the reading for clear in one's mind and to understand clearly.
column4: 我想了解一下这个城市。
column5: 我想瞭解一下這個城市。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng liǎojiě yīxià zhège chéngshì.
column7: I'd like to find out more about this city.
column9: Finding out or knowing about a person, place or situation: 了解情況, 我不太了解他, 我去了解一下. For grasping a language point or what someone said, 懂 or 明白 is the word. The 了 is read liǎo here, the reading for clear in one's mind and to understand clearly.

column3: Sums up what is already there: 请用一句话概括, 概括地说 (in brief). 总结 sums up experience or work. 概 also forms 大概 and 概念, and 括 forms 包括 and 括号.
column4: 请你用一句话概括这篇文章。
column5: 請你用一句話概括這篇文章。
column6: Qǐng nǐ yòng yī jù huà gàikuò zhè piān wénzhāng.
column7: Please sum up this article in one sentence.
column9: Sums up what is already there: 請用一句話概括, 概括地說 (in brief). 總結 sums up experience or work. 概 also forms 大概 and 概念, and 括 forms 包括 and 括號.

column3: Criticizes an opinion, not a person: 看问题很片面, 你的看法太片面了. The opposite is 全面 (comprehensive). 面 is the side or aspect also in 方面 and 全面.
column6: Nǐ de kànfǎ tài piànmiàn le.
column7: Your view is too one-sided.
column9: Criticizes an opinion, not a person: 看問題很片面, 你的看法太片面了. The opposite is 全面 (comprehensive). 面 is the side or aspect also in 方面 and 全面.

column3: Neglects something that matters: 忽视问题, 不能忽视. 忽略 skips something small, while 重视 is its opposite, to take seriously.
column4: 我们不能忽视孩子的感受。
column5: 我們不能忽視孩子的感受。
column6: Wǒmen bù néng hūshì háizi de gǎnshòu.
column7: We cannot overlook the children's feelings.
column9: Neglects something that matters: 忽視問題, 不能忽視. 忽略 skips something small, while 重視 is its opposite, to take seriously.

column3: Weighs several options in a considered decision: 选择专业, 做出选择, 没有选择. It can take a verb: 选择留下. 选择题 is a multiple-choice question. 挑 is a lighter, more casual pick.
column4: 我选择留在这个城市工作。
column5: 我選擇留在這個城市工作。
column6: Wǒ xuǎnzé liú zài zhège chéngshì gōngzuò.
column7: I chose to stay and work in this city.
column9: Weighs several options in a considered decision: 選擇專業, 做出選擇, 沒有選擇. It can take a verb: 選擇留下. 選擇題 is a multiple-choice question. 挑 is a lighter, more casual pick.

column3: Often in fixed phrases: 注意细节, and the saying 细节决定成败. 细 also gives 仔细 and 细心.
column4: 我们还要讨论一下计划的细节。
column5: 我們還要討論一下計劃的細節。
column6: Wǒmen hái yào tǎolùn yīxià jìhuà de xìjié.
column7: We still need to talk through the details of the plan.
column9: Often in fixed phrases: 注意細節, and the saying 細節決定成敗. 細 also gives 仔細 and 細心.

column3: Praises work or observation that is fine and thorough: 工作细致, 细致的观察. 仔细 is more about the act of looking carefully, while 细致 is about the quality of the result. In this word 致 is a bound form meaning fine, delicate and exquisite.
column6: Tā zuòshì fēicháng xìzhì.
column7: She does things very carefully.
column9: Praises work or observation that is fine and thorough: 工作細緻, 細緻的觀察. 仔細 is more about the act of looking carefully, while 細緻 is about the quality of the result. In this word 緻 is a bound form meaning fine, delicate and exquisite.

column3: What you decide at the end of a study, argument or meeting: 得出结论, 还没有结论. 下结论 means to draw a conclusion, and 现在下结论太早 or 不要急着下结论 warns against jumping to one.
column6: Xiànzài xià jiélùn hái tài zǎo.
column7: It's still too early to draw a conclusion.
column9: What you decide at the end of a study, argument or meeting: 得出結論, 還沒有結論. 下結論 means to draw a conclusion, and 現在下結論太早 or 不要急著下結論 warns against jumping to one.

column3: Basic knowledge everyone should have, not good judgment: 生活常识, 缺乏常识, 没有常识 (ignorant of the basics). Counted with 点: 一点常识. 识 is read shí, and in Taiwan shì.
column4: 这是一个生活常识，大家都应该知道。
column5: 這是一個生活常識，大家都應該知道。
column6: Zhè shì yī ge shēnghuó chángshí, dàjiā dōu yīnggāi zhīdào.
column7: This is basic everyday knowledge that everyone should know.
column9: Basic knowledge everyone should have, not good judgment: 生活常識, 缺乏常識, 沒有常識 (ignorant of the basics). Counted with 點: 一點常識. 識 is read shí, and in Taiwan shì.

column3: The inner mental side of a person: 心理健康, 心理压力, 心理学, 心理医生. 心理作用 means it is all in your head. 心情 is a passing mood, 心理 is deeper.
column4: 孩子的心理健康很重要。
column5: 孩子的心理健康很重要。
column6: Háizi de xīnlǐ jiànkāng hěn zhòngyào.
column7: Children's mental health is very important.
column9: The inner mental side of a person: 心理健康, 心理壓力, 心理學, 心理醫生. 心理作用 means it is all in your head. 心情 is a passing mood, 心理 is deeper.

column3: A hope you work toward, not the dream you have asleep (that is just 梦). It pairs with 实现 and 追求, and it also works as a verb: 梦想成为医生.
column4: 他的梦想是成为一名医生。
column5: 他的夢想是成為一名醫生。
column6: Tā de mèngxiǎng shì chéngwéi yī míng yīshēng.
column7: His dream is to become a doctor.
column9: A hope you work toward, not the dream you have asleep (that is just 夢). It pairs with 實現 and 追求, and it also works as a verb: 夢想成為醫生.

column3: A trip to see conditions on the spot, typical of officials, scholars and business people: 实地考察, 出国考察. For ordinary sightseeing visits, 参观 is the word.
column4: 他们去山区考察当地的教育情况。
column5: 他們去山區考察當地的教育情況。
column6: Tāmen qù shānqū kǎochá dāngdì de jiàoyù qíngkuàng.
column7: They went to the mountain area to study its local education.
column9: A trip to see conditions on the spot, typical of officials, scholars and business people: 實地考察, 出國考察. For ordinary sightseeing visits, 參觀 is the word.

column3: Both a verb and a noun: 暗示他, 心理暗示. The hint is indirect, in words, looks or gestures, so the listener has to read between the lines.
column6: Tā ànshì wǒ zǎodiǎn huí jiā.
column7: She hinted that I should go home early.
column9: Both a verb and a noun: 暗示他, 心理暗示. The hint is indirect, in words, looks or gestures, so the listener has to read between the lines.

column3: Written style; 也许 is the more common word in speech. It goes before the verb or opens the sentence and is weaker than 一定: 或许他已经走了.
column6: Huòxǔ tā jīntiān bù huì lái le.
column7: Perhaps he won't come today.
column9: Written style; 也許 is the more common word in speech. It goes before the verb or opens the sentence and is weaker than 一定: 或許他已經走了.

column3: Spoken, for a real possibility; it sits before the verb and is often followed by 会: 说不定他已经到了. 或许 is the more formal counterpart.
column4: 带上伞吧，说不定会下雨。
column5: 帶上傘吧，說不定會下雨。
column6: Dài shàng sǎn ba, shuōbudìng huì xià yǔ.
column7: Take an umbrella, it might rain.
column9: Spoken, for a real possibility; it sits before the verb and is often followed by 會: 說不定他已經到了. 或許 is the more formal counterpart.

column3: A gentle doubt, not a flat denial: 贵的未必好, 未必是真的. It comes before a verb or adjective and often answers a claim you only partly accept; 不一定 is a little more casual.
column6: Guì de dōngxi wèibì hǎo.
column7: Expensive things are not necessarily good.
column9: A gentle doubt, not a flat denial: 貴的未必好, 未必是真的. It comes before a verb or adjective and often answers a claim you only partly accept; 不一定 is a little more casual.

column3: Says something is bound to happen given the circumstances, usually with 会 before the verb: 难免会犯错. It can also be the complement: 错误是难免的.
column4: 学习一门新语言时，难免会犯错。
column5: 學習一門新語言時，難免會犯錯。
column6: Xuéxí yī mén xīn yǔyán shí, nánmiǎn huì fàncuò.
column7: When learning a new language, you will inevitably make mistakes.
column9: Says something is bound to happen given the circumstances, usually with 會 before the verb: 難免會犯錯. It can also be the complement: 錯誤是難免的.

column3: A written adverb for an impression without proof, before a verb or adjective: 似乎有点冷. In speech 好像 is the usual word.
column6: Tā jīntiān sìhū bù tài gāoxìng.
column7: He doesn't seem very happy today.
column9: A written adverb for an impression without proof, before a verb or adjective: 似乎有點冷. In speech 好像 is the usual word.

column3: Closes a comparison after a noun or clause, often with 像 or 好像 before it: 白得像雪似的, 好像没睡似的. It is spoken and works like 一样: 像雪一样白.
column4: 他高兴得像个孩子似的。
column5: 他高興得像個孩子似的。
column6: Tā gāoxìng de xiàng ge háizi shìde.
column7: He is as happy as a child.
column9: Closes a comparison after a noun or clause, often with 像 or 好像 before it: 白得像雪似的, 好像沒睡似的. It is spoken and works like 一樣: 像雪一樣白.

column3: Formal and written, and it sits inside a clause: 不知道他是否同意, 是否可行. In speech people say 是不是 or 有没有 instead.
column6: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā shìfǒu tóngyì.
column7: I don't know whether he agrees.
column9: Formal and written, and it sits inside a clause: 不知道他是否同意, 是否可行. In speech people say 是不是 or 有沒有 instead.

column3: Opens a sentence with a conclusion drawn from what you can see: 看来你很忙. For how something looks, use 看起来 before an adjective: 看起来很累.
column6: Kànlái míngtiān yào xià yǔ le.
column7: It looks like it will rain tomorrow.
column9: Opens a sentence with a conclusion drawn from what you can see: 看來你很忙. For how something looks, use 看起來 before an adjective: 看起來很累.

column3: As a connector it opens the second clause and draws a conclusion from the first: 每天练习，可见很努力. It also means plainly visible: 清晰可见.
column4: 他每天练习两小时，可见他很努力。
column5: 他每天練習兩小時，可見他很努力。
column6: Tā měitiān liànxí liǎng xiǎoshí, kějiàn tā hěn nǔlì.
column7: He practices two hours every day, so he is clearly hard-working.
column9: As a connector it opens the second clause and draws a conclusion from the first: 每天練習，可見很努力. It also means plainly visible: 清晰可見.

column3: A set phrase that opens a statement true in most cases, followed by a comma. Add exceptions afterward with 但是. Related openers are 总的来说 and 具体来说.
column4: 一般来说，北方的冬天比较冷。
column5: 一般來說，北方的冬天比較冷。
column6: Yībānláishuō, běifāng de dōngtiān bǐjiào lěng.
column7: Generally speaking, winters in the north are rather cold.
column9: A set phrase that opens a statement true in most cases, followed by a comma. Add exceptions afterward with 但是. Related openers are 總的來說 and 具體來說.

column3: Followed by a comma, it sums up after several points and says the details do not change the outcome. 总而言之 is the longer, more formal version.
column4: 不管怎样，总之你要小心。
column5: 不管怎樣，總之你要小心。
column6: Bùguǎn zěnyàng, zǒngzhī nǐ yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: Whatever happens, in short, you must be careful.
column9: Followed by a comma, it sums up after several points and says the details do not change the outcome. 總而言之 is the longer, more formal version.

column3: Confirms or concedes, before a verb or adjective, and often agrees with what was just said: 他的确很聪明. 确实 is the everyday near-synonym. 的 is read dí in this word, not de.
column4: 这家餐厅的菜的确很好吃。
column5: 這家餐廳的菜的確很好吃。
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài díquè hěn hǎochī.
column7: The food in this restaurant is indeed very tasty.
column9: Confirms or concedes, before a verb or adjective, and often agrees with what was just said: 他的確很聰明. 確實 is the everyday near-synonym. 的 is read dí in this word, not de.

column3: Presses a question for the real answer, before the verb: 你究竟想怎么样？ 到底 is the more colloquial equivalent. As a noun it means the outcome: 弄个究竟.
column6: Nǐ jiūjìng xiǎng qù nǎr?
column7: Where on earth do you want to go?
column9: Presses a question for the real answer, before the verb: 你究竟想怎麼樣？ 到底 is the more colloquial equivalent. As a noun it means the outcome: 弄個究竟.

column3: Unexpectedly, to my surprise: 他竟然忘了我的生日 "he actually forgot my birthday". It goes before the verb and shows that something went against expectations, good or bad. 竟 means "unexpectedly" and 然 "so". It is stronger than 居然, which is nearly the same.
column4: 他竟然忘了自己的生日。
column5: 他竟然忘了自己的生日。
column6: Tā jìngrán wàng le zìjǐ de shēngrì.
column7: He actually forgot his own birthday.
column9: Unexpectedly, to my surprise: 他竟然忘了我的生日 "he actually forgot my birthday". It goes before the verb and shows that something went against expectations, good or bad. 竟 means "unexpectedly" and 然 "so". It is stronger than 居然, which is nearly the same.

column3: Noun and verb: 做研究, 研究问题, and 研究生 for a graduate student. In speech it also means to talk something over and decide: 我们研究一下.
column6: Tā zài dàxué lǐ yánjiū lìshǐ.
column7: He studies history at the university.
column9: Noun and verb: 做研究, 研究問題, and 研究生 for a graduate student. In speech it also means to talk something over and decide: 我們研究一下.

column3: Developing something new, a drug, machine or product: 研制新药, 研制成功. It is not for studying a topic; that is 研究.
column4: 科学家们研制出了一种新药。
column5: 科學家們研製出了一種新藥。
column6: Kēxuéjiāmen yánzhì chū le yī zhǒng xīn yào.
column7: The scientists developed a new medicine.
column9: Developing something new, a drug, machine or product: 研製新藥, 研製成功. It is not for studying a topic; that is 研究.

column3: Verb and noun: 统计人数 counts people, 统计数字 are the figures. 据统计 is a standard way to open a report.
column4: 据统计，这个城市有一千万人口。
column5: 據統計，這個城市有一千萬人口。
column6: Jù tǒngjì, zhège chéngshì yǒu yī qiān wàn rénkǒu.
column7: According to statistics, this city has ten million people.
column9: Verb and noun: 統計人數 counts people, 統計數字 are the figures. 據統計 is a standard way to open a report.

column3: Material for study or reference, with no plural form: 查资料, 学习资料, 个人资料. One item is 一份资料.
column6: Wǒ zhèngzài wǎng shang chá zīliào.
column7: I'm looking up material online.
column9: Material for study or reference, with no plural form: 查資料, 學習資料, 個人資料. One item is 一份資料.

column3: Verb and noun, based on data or reasoning rather than a guess (that is 猜): 预测未来, 无法预测. The weather forecast itself is 预报.
column6: Méiyǒu rén néng yùcè wèilái.
column7: No one can predict the future.
column9: Verb and noun, based on data or reasoning rather than a guess (that is 猜): 預測未來, 無法預測. The weather forecast itself is 預報.

column3: The direction something is moving over time, in economics or society: 发展趋势, 上升的趋势.
column6: Fángjià yǒu shàngshēng de qūshì.
column7: House prices tend to go up.
column9: The direction something is moving over time, in economics or society: 發展趨勢, 上升的趨勢.

column3: What a talk, event or work is about: 今天的主题, 主题歌, 主题公园. It is broader than 题目, which is a title or an exam question.
column4: 这次会议的主题是环境保护。
column5: 這次會議的主題是環境保護。
column6: Zhè cì huìyì de zhǔtí shì huánjìng bǎohù.
column7: The theme of this meeting is environmental protection.
column9: What a talk, event or work is about: 今天的主題, 主題歌, 主題公園. It is broader than 題目, which is a title or an exam question.

column3: The setting behind an event, a picture or a person: 历史背景, 家庭背景, 背景音乐. In slang, 他有背景 means he has powerful connections.
column4: 这部电影的背景是二十年代的上海。
column5: 這部電影的背景是二十年代的上海。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng de bèijǐng shì èrshí niándài de Shànghǎi.
column7: The film is set in Shanghai in the 1920s.
column9: The setting behind an event, a picture or a person: 歷史背景, 家庭背景, 背景音樂. In slang, 他有背景 means he has powerful connections.

column3: As an adjective before a noun: 综合素质, 综合大学 (a university with many faculties). Before a verb it means taking everything together: 综合考虑.
column4: 老师会综合大家的意见做决定。
column5: 老師會綜合大家的意見做決定。
column6: Lǎoshī huì zōnghé dàjiā de yìjiàn zuò juédìng.
column7: The teacher will make a decision by bringing everyone's views together.
column9: As an adjective before a noun: 綜合素質, 綜合大學 (a university with many faculties). Before a verb it means taking everything together: 綜合考慮.

column3: An abstract, slightly philosophical word for things in general, with no measure word: 新事物, 各种事物. For physical objects in daily talk, use 东西.
column4: 我们要用发展的眼光看事物。
column5: 我們要用發展的眼光看事物。
column6: Wǒmen yào yòng fāzhǎn de yǎnguāng kàn shìwù.
column7: We should look at things with an eye to development.
column9: An abstract, slightly philosophical word for things in general, with no measure word: 新事物, 各種事物. For physical objects in daily talk, use 東西.

column3: The kind or nature of something, used in analysis: 工作性质, 问题的性质, 性质不同.
column4: 这两个问题的性质不一样。
column5: 這兩個問題的性質不一樣。
column6: Zhè liǎng ge wèntí de xìngzhì bù yīyàng.
column7: The nature of these two problems is not the same.
column9: The kind or nature of something, used in analysis: 工作性質, 問題的性質, 性質不同.

column3: A concrete sign by which something is recognized or told apart: 基本特征, 面部特征, 个人特征.
column4: 熊猫的特征是黑白两色。
column5: 熊貓的特徵是黑白兩色。
column6: Xióngmāo de tèzhēng shì hēibái liǎng sè.
column7: The characteristic of the panda is its black and white coloring.
column9: A concrete sign by which something is recognized or told apart: 基本特徵, 面部特徵, 個人特徵.

column3: The overall state of affairs and which way it is moving, heard in the news: 国际形势, 经济形势. It is not for a personal circumstance.
column6: Xiànzài de jīngjì xíngshì hěn hǎo.
column7: The economic situation is good now.
column9: The overall state of affairs and which way it is moving, heard in the news: 國際形勢, 經濟形勢. It is not for a personal circumstance.

column3: Used for conditions, not skills: 改善生活, 改善关系, 改善环境. For improving skills or scores, 提高 is the verb. Often 得到改善.
column4: 医生的工作改善了病人的生活。
column5: 醫生的工作改善了病人的生活。
column6: Yīshēng de gōngzuò gǎishàn le bìngrén de shēnghuó.
column7: The doctor's work improved the patients' lives.
column9: Used for conditions, not skills: 改善生活, 改善關係, 改善環境. For improving skills or scores, 提高 is the verb. Often 得到改善.

column3: You fix a wrong thing in behavior or in a text: 改正错误, 改正缺点. On homework the casual word is 改错.
column4: 发现错误后，他马上改正了。
column5: 發現錯誤後，他馬上改正了。
column6: Fāxiàn cuòwù hòu, tā mǎshàng gǎizhèng le.
column7: After finding the mistake, he corrected it at once.
column9: You fix a wrong thing in behavior or in a text: 改正錯誤, 改正缺點. On homework the casual word is 改錯.

column3: Shortens a time, distance or length: 缩短时间, 缩短距离. The opposite is 延长.
column4: 新的高铁缩短了两个城市的距离。
column5: 新的高鐵縮短了兩個城市的距離。
column6: Xīn de gāotiě suōduǎn le liǎng ge chéngshì de jùlí.
column7: The new high-speed railway has shortened the distance between the two cities.
column9: Shortens a time, distance or length: 縮短時間, 縮短距離. The opposite is 延長.

column3: Reduces size or scope: 缩小范围, 缩小差距, 缩小图片. The opposite is 扩大.
column6: Qǐng bǎ túpiàn suōxiǎo yīdiǎn.
column7: Please make the picture a little smaller.
column9: Reduces size or scope: 縮小範圍, 縮小差距, 縮小圖片. The opposite is 擴大.

column3: Enlarges something concrete or abstract: 扩大范围, 扩大影响, 扩大生产. The opposite is 缩小.
column6: Gōngsī dǎsuàn kuòdà shēngchǎn.
column7: The company plans to expand production.
column9: Enlarges something concrete or abstract: 擴大範圍, 擴大影響, 擴大生產. The opposite is 縮小.

column3: Spreads outward into new areas: 扩展业务, 扩展到全国. Compared with 扩大, it suggests reaching further out. In computing: 扩展名, a file extension.
column4: 这家公司的业务扩展到了全国。
column5: 這家公司的業務擴展到了全國。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de yèwù kuòzhǎn dào le quánguó.
column7: This company's business has spread across the whole country.
column9: Spreads outward into new areas: 擴展業務, 擴展到全國. Compared with 擴大, it suggests reaching further out. In computing: 擴展名, a file extension.

column3: Someone lowers a price, level, cost or risk: 降低价格, 降低成本, 降低风险. When the level falls by itself, 下降 is the usual word.
column4: 商店降低了水果的价格。
column5: 商店降低了水果的價格。
column6: Shāngdiàn jiàngdī le shuǐguǒ de jiàgé.
column7: The shop has lowered the price of fruit.
column9: Someone lowers a price, level, cost or risk: 降低價格, 降低成本, 降低風險. When the level falls by itself, 下降 is the usual word.

column3: The thing itself goes down, with no object: 气温下降, 成绩下降, 下降了百分之五. The opposite is 上升. When someone lowers it on purpose, use 降低.
column6: Zuìjìn qìwēn míngxiǎn xiàjiàng le.
column7: The temperature has dropped noticeably recently.
column9: The thing itself goes down, with no object: 氣溫下降, 成績下降, 下降了百分之五. The opposite is 上升. When someone lowers it on purpose, use 降低.

column3: Common on its own for temperatures and prices: 气温降了, 价格降了, 降到零度. In compounds: 降雨, 降温, 降价, 降落. It pictures going down a hill.
column6: Qìwēn jiàng dào le língdù yǐxià.
column7: The temperature has dropped below zero.
column9: Common on its own for temperatures and prices: 氣溫降了, 價格降了, 降到零度. In compounds: 降雨, 降溫, 降價, 降落. It pictures going down a hill.

column3: The minus verb in math: 十减三. Outside math it mostly sits in compounds: 减肥, 减价, 减轻, 减少.
column6: Shí jiǎn sān děngyú qī.
column7: Ten minus three is seven.
column9: The minus verb in math: 十減三. Outside math it mostly sits in compounds: 減肥, 減價, 減輕, 減少.

column3: Works with or without an object: 减少浪费, 人数减少了, 减少了一半. It is about quantity or number; the opposite is 增加.
column4: 我们要减少使用塑料袋。
column5: 我們要減少使用塑膠袋。
column6: Wǒmen yào jiǎnshǎo shǐyòng sùliàodài.
column7: We should use fewer plastic bags.
column9: Works with or without an object: 減少浪費, 人數減少了, 減少了一半. It is about quantity or number; the opposite is 增加.

column3: A slow, steady build-up of experience, knowledge or money: 积累经验, 积累财富. It also works as a noun: 经验的积累. In this word 累 is read lěi on the mainland and lèi in Taiwan.
column4: 学习语言需要慢慢积累。
column5: 學習語言需要慢慢積累。
column6: Xuéxí yǔyán xūyào mànmàn jīlěi.
column7: Learning a language takes gradual accumulation.
column9: A slow, steady build-up of experience, knowledge or money: 積累經驗, 積累財富. It also works as a noun: 經驗的積累. In this word 累 is read lěi on the mainland and lèi in Taiwan.

column3: Of people or things in different places, or attention that wanders: 分散注意力, 分散投资, 住得很分散. The opposite is 集中.
column4: 手机会分散学生的注意力。
column5: 手機會分散學生的注意力。
column6: Shǒujī huì fēnsàn xuésheng de zhùyìlì.
column7: Phones can distract students' attention.
column9: Of people or things in different places, or attention that wanders: 分散注意力, 分散投資, 住得很分散. The opposite is 集中.

column3: Things break up or spread out from a gathering: 散会, 散场, 散开, 分散. Also 散步, to stroll.
column4: 会议结束了，大家都散了。
column5: 會議結束了，大家都散了。
column6: Huìyì jiéshù le, dàjiā dōu sàn le.
column7: The meeting is over and everyone has dispersed.
column9: Things break up or spread out from a gathering: 散會, 散場, 散開, 分散. Also 散步, to stroll.

column3: Formal; the object is something good and usually abstract that you want to move forward: 促进发展, 促进交流, 互相促进.
column4: 运动可以促进身体健康。
column5: 運動可以促進身體健康。
column6: Yùndòng kěyǐ cùjìn shēntǐ jiànkāng.
column7: Exercise can promote good health.
column9: Formal; the object is something good and usually abstract that you want to move forward: 促進發展, 促進交流, 互相促進.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 移动, 转移, 移民, 移开. On its own it takes things you can shift a little: 把桌子移一下.
column6: Bǎ zhuōzi wǎng zuǒ yí diǎn.
column7: Move the table a bit to the left.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 移動, 轉移, 移民, 移開. On its own it takes things you can shift a little: 把桌子移一下.

column3: Changing position, even slightly: 移动桌子. It is also the word for mobile: 移动电话, 移动支付, and the carrier 中国移动.
column6: Qǐng wù yídòng zhèxiē dōngxi.
column7: Please do not move these things.
column9: Changing position, even slightly: 移動桌子. It is also the word for mobile: 移動電話, 移動支付, and the carrier 中國移動.

column3: Moves something from one place or state to another, physical or abstract: 转移注意力, 转移话题, 转移资金. Somewhat formal.
column4: 他想转移话题，不谈这件事。
column5: 他想轉移話題，不談這件事。
column6: Tā xiǎng zhuǎnyí huàtí, bù tán zhè jiàn shì.
column7: He wants to change the subject and not talk about it.
column9: Moves something from one place or state to another, physical or abstract: 轉移注意力, 轉移話題, 轉移資金. Somewhat formal.

column3: A part turning around a point: 转动钥匙, 转动方向盘, 轮子转动. A person changing direction is 转身.
column6: Tā zhuǎndòng yàoshi, dǎkāi le mén.
column7: He turned the key and opened the door.
column9: A part turning around a point: 轉動鑰匙, 轉動方向盤, 輪子轉動. A person changing direction is 轉身.

column3: Turning your body around, common in stories: 转身就走, 转过身来. It splits around other words: 转过身, 转了个身.
column4: 他转身就走了，什么也没说。
column5: 他轉身就走了，什麼也沒說。
column6: Tā zhuǎnshēn jiù zǒu le, shénme yě méi shuō.
column7: He turned and left without saying anything.
column9: Turning your body around, common in stories: 轉身就走, 轉過身來. It splits around other words: 轉過身, 轉了個身.

column3: Back-and-forth movement from a fixed point, like a pendulum: 摆动手臂, 摆动尾巴, 树枝在风中摆动.
column4: 小狗高兴地摆动着尾巴。
column5: 小狗高興地擺動著尾巴。
column6: Xiǎo gǒu gāoxìng de bǎidòng zhe wěiba.
column7: The puppy wags its tail happily.
column9: Back-and-forth movement from a fixed point, like a pendulum: 擺動手臂, 擺動尾巴, 樹枝在風中擺動.

column3: Mostly abstract: what wavers is a belief, resolve or position (立场动摇), or the word names what shakes it (动摇信心). Something that physically sways is 摇晃.
column4: 困难没有动摇他的决心。
column5: 困難沒有動搖他的決心。
column6: Kùnnan méiyǒu dòngyáo tā de juéxīn.
column7: Difficulties did not shake his determination.
column9: Mostly abstract: what wavers is a belief, resolve or position (立場動搖), or the word names what shakes it (動搖信心). Something that physically sways is 搖晃.

column3: Shaking back and forth under your own control: 摇头 for no, 摇手 to wave something off, 摇铃 for a handbell, 摇一摇 to give something a shake.
column6: Tā yáo le yáo tóu, shuō bù zhīdào.
column7: He shook his head and said he didn't know.
column9: Shaking back and forth under your own control: 搖頭 for no, 搖手 to wave something off, 搖鈴 for a handbell, 搖一搖 to give something a shake.

column3: Things that come down on their own: rain, leaves, the setting sun (太阳落山). 落在 plus a place says where something lands, 落下 is to drop down, and 落后 is to fall behind.
column6: Shùyè luò zài dì shang le.
column7: The leaves fell on the ground.
column9: Things that come down on their own: rain, leaves, the setting sun (太陽落山). 落在 plus a place says where something lands, 落下 is to drop down, and 落後 is to fall behind.

column3: A reaction to something that has just happened, so it sits in past events (急忙跑过去) and not in commands; for "hurry up!" say 赶快.
column4: 听到哭声，她急忙跑了过去。
column5: 聽到哭聲，她急忙跑了過去。
column6: Tīngdào kūshēng, tā jímáng pǎo le guòqù.
column7: Hearing crying, she hurried over.
column9: A reaction to something that has just happened, so it sits in past events (急忙跑過去) and not in commands; for "hurry up!" say 趕快.

column3: Making use of time or a chance before it slips away: 抓紧时间, 抓紧做. Called out as 大家抓紧！ it means "hurry up." It can also be a plain firm grip: 抓紧扶手.
column4: 时间不多了，大家抓紧吧。
column5: 時間不多了，大家抓緊吧。
column6: Shíjiān bù duō le, dàjiā zhuājǐn ba.
column7: There isn't much time left, so let's make the most of it.
column9: Making use of time or a chance before it slips away: 抓緊時間, 抓緊做. Called out as 大家抓緊！ it means "hurry up." It can also be a plain firm grip: 抓緊扶手.

column3: Goes before the verb and sets no exact time: "as soon as you can." Polite and common in emails and requests (尽快回复); 马上 means right now.
column4: 请您尽快回复我的邮件。
column5: 請您儘快回覆我的郵件。
column6: Qǐng nín jǐnkuài huífù wǒ de yóujiàn.
column7: Please reply to my email as soon as possible.
column9: Goes before the verb and sets no exact time: "as soon as you can." Polite and common in emails and requests (儘快回復); 馬上 means right now.

column3: A formal, written word for speed in changes, reactions and spreading: 迅速发展, 迅速反应, 消息迅速传开. In everyday speech people say 很快.
column6: Xiāoxi xùnsù chuánbiàn le quán chéng.
column7: The news spread rapidly through the whole city.
column9: A formal, written word for speed in changes, reactions and spreading: 迅速發展, 迅速反應, 消息迅速傳開. In everyday speech people say 很快.

column3: Formal, the word of notices, instructions and news: 请立即离开, 立即出发. Speech prefers 马上 or 立刻. It goes before the verb.
column4: 看到火光，他立即报了警。
column5: 看到火光，他立即報了警。
column6: Kàndào huǒguāng, tā lìjí bào le jǐng.
column7: Seeing the flames, he called the police at once.
column9: Formal, the word of notices, instructions and news: 請立即離開, 立即出發. Speech prefers 馬上 or 立刻. It goes before the verb.

column3: Doing a small thing in passing, as you go. It can be considerate (随手关门, close the door behind you; 随手关灯) or careless (随手乱扔), so the context tells which.
column6: Qǐng suíshǒu guān dēng.
column7: Please switch off the light on your way out.
column9: Doing a small thing in passing, as you go. It can be considerate (隨手關門, close the door behind you; 隨手關燈) or careless (隨手亂扔), so the context tells which.

column3: Credits someone with acting before everyone else: 率先发言, 率先完成. It goes before the verb and turns up in news reports and formal praise. 先 is built from a foot and a person, with the sense of going forward.
column4: 他率先举手回答了问题。
column5: 他率先舉手回答了問題。
column6: Tā shuàixiān jǔ shǒu huídá le wèntí.
column7: He was the first to raise a hand and answer the question.
column9: Credits someone with acting before everyone else: 率先發言, 率先完成. It goes before the verb and turns up in news reports and formal praise. 先 is built from a foot and a person, with the sense of going forward.

column3: Little by little, for a change that creeps up on its own: 天渐渐黑了, 渐渐习惯. It goes before a verb or adjective and usually looks back at what happened, not at orders.
column4: 天渐渐黑了，路上的人越来越少。
column5: 天漸漸黑了，路上的人越來越少。
column6: Tiān jiànjiàn hēi le, lù shang de rén yuè lái yuè shǎo.
column7: It was getting dark and fewer and fewer people were on the road.
column9: Little by little, for a change that creeps up on its own: 天漸漸黑了, 漸漸習慣. It goes before a verb or adjective and usually looks back at what happened, not at orders.

column3: The written partner of 渐渐, at home in reports about trends: 逐渐提高, 逐渐增多. It describes a process; for taking your time on purpose, say 慢慢来.
column4: 他的汉语水平逐渐提高了。
column5: 他的漢語水平逐漸提高了。
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng zhújiàn tígāo le.
column7: His Chinese level gradually improved.
column9: The written partner of 漸漸, at home in reports about trends: 逐漸提高, 逐漸增多. It describes a process; for taking your time on purpose, say 慢慢來.

column3: Step by step in stages, planned or controlled: 逐步实现, 逐步改善. That makes it a word for policies and projects, where 逐渐 just describes a drift.
column4: 我们会逐步改善这里的环境。
column5: 我們會逐步改善這裡的環境。
column6: Wǒmen huì zhúbù gǎishàn zhèlǐ de huánjìng.
column7: We will improve the environment here step by step.
column9: Step by step in stages, planned or controlled: 逐步實現, 逐步改善. That makes it a word for policies and projects, where 逐漸 just describes a drift.

column3: Several people or things coming or happening one after another over a stretch of time, so the subject is plural: 客人陆续到了, 陆续离开. For one thing changing slowly, use 渐渐.
column6: Kèrénmen lùxù dào le.
column7: The guests arrived one after another.
column9: Several people or things coming or happening one after another over a stretch of time, so the subject is plural: 客人陸續到了, 陸續離開. For one thing changing slowly, use 漸漸.

column3: Before a verb: the same thing keeps happening or being done. Often an insistence (一再强调, 一再提醒) or a delay (一再推迟), and usually in a report of what already happened.
column4: 老师一再提醒我们要按时交作业。
column5: 老師一再提醒我們要按時交作業。
column6: Lǎoshī yīzài tíxǐng wǒmen yào ànshí jiāo zuòyè.
column7: The teacher reminded us again and again to hand in our work on time.
column9: Before a verb: the same thing keeps happening or being done. Often an insistence (一再強調, 一再提醒) or a delay (一再推遲), and usually in a report of what already happened.

column3: Doing something over and over with care or insistence. It clusters with verbs of thinking, asking, declining and thanking: 再三考虑, 再三推辞, 再三感谢.
column4: 他再三感谢我们的帮助。
column5: 他再三感謝我們的幫助。
column6: Tā zàisān gǎnxiè wǒmen de bāngzhù.
column7: He thanked us again and again for our help.
column9: Doing something over and over with care or insistence. It clusters with verbs of thinking, asking, declining and thanking: 再三考慮, 再三推辭, 再三感謝.

column3: Many people or things doing the same thing one after another, so it needs a plural subject: 大家纷纷鼓掌, 花瓣纷纷落下. Usually before the verb, but it can follow, as in 议论纷纷, and as an adjective it describes things falling thick and fast (大雪纷纷). Not for one person.
column4: 听到这个消息，大家纷纷鼓掌。
column5: 聽到這個消息，大家紛紛鼓掌。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, dàjiā fēnfēn gǔzhǎng.
column7: On hearing the news, everyone started applauding.
column9: Many people or things doing the same thing one after another, so it needs a plural subject: 大家紛紛鼓掌, 花瓣紛紛落下. Usually before the verb, but it can follow, as in 議論紛紛, and as an adjective it describes things falling thick and fast (大雪紛紛). Not for one person.

column3: Opens a clause to say that things changed at that point and stayed changed: 从此以后, 从此再也没有. It can look back in a story or ahead in a resolution (从此以后，我要努力学习).
column4: 他搬走了，从此我们再也没有联系。
column5: 他搬走了，從此我們再也沒有聯繫。
column6: Tā bān zǒu le, cóngcǐ wǒmen zài yě méiyǒu liánxì.
column7: He moved away, and we have not been in touch since.
column9: Opens a clause to say that things changed at that point and stayed changed: 從此以後, 從此再也沒有. It can look back in a story or ahead in a resolution (從此以後，我要努力學習).

column3: The everyday word for holding in your arms, including a hug between people (抱一下, 抱抱) and carrying a child (抱孩子, 抱着书); 拥抱 is the more formal hug. It also holds feelings inside: 抱希望, 抱怨.
column4: 妈妈抱着孩子走进了房间。
column5: 媽媽抱著孩子走進了房間。
column6: Māma bào zhe háizi zǒujìn le fángjiān.
column7: The mother walked into the room carrying the child.
column9: The everyday word for holding in your arms, including a hug between people (抱一下, 抱抱) and carrying a child (抱孩子, 抱著書); 擁抱 is the more formal hug. It also holds feelings inside: 抱希望, 抱怨.

column3: Touching with the hand to feel: 摸一摸, 摸头. It also means groping in the dark (摸黑) and, in 摸不着头脑, not being able to find your way into a problem.
column6: Bié mō nà zhī gǒu, tā huì yǎo rén.
column7: Don't touch that dog, it bites.
column9: Touching with the hand to feel: 摸一摸, 摸頭. It also means groping in the dark (摸黑) and, in 摸不著頭腦, not being able to find your way into a problem.

column3: Sticking something flat onto a surface: 贴邮票, 贴海报. It also means staying right up against something (贴着墙), and 补贴 is a subsidy.
column4: 他在墙上贴了一张海报。
column5: 他在牆上貼了一張海報。
column6: Tā zài qiáng shang tiē le yī zhāng hǎibào.
column7: He put up a poster on the wall.
column9: Sticking something flat onto a surface: 貼郵票, 貼海報. It also means staying right up against something (貼著牆), and 補貼 is a subsidy.

column3: Filling a gap or a blank: 填表, 填空, 填满. For a form, the fuller 填写 is also common.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng biǎo tián yīxià.
column7: Please fill in this form.
column9: Filling a gap or a blank: 填表, 填空, 填滿. For a form, the fuller 填寫 is also common.

column3: Cutting food into pieces with a knife: 切菜, 切水果, 切成片, and 切开 for cutting something open. 切 pairs with a knife or blade, while 剪 is for scissors.
column6: Tā zhèngzài chúfáng lǐ qiē cài.
column7: She is chopping vegetables in the kitchen.
column9: Cutting food into pieces with a knife: 切菜, 切水果, 切成片, and 切開 for cutting something open. 切 pairs with a knife or blade, while 剪 is for scissors.

column3: Covering something from above: 盖被子, 盖上盖子. Pressing a seal onto a document is 盖章, and 盖房子 is to build a house.
column6: Tiān lěng le, yào gài hòu bèizi.
column7: It's cold now, so use a thick quilt.
column9: Covering something from above: 蓋被子, 蓋上蓋子. Pressing a seal onto a document is 蓋章, and 蓋房子 is to build a house.

column3: Poking or prying something out with a point: 把刺挑出来. It also stirs trouble up (挑拨) and appears in 挑战, a challenge.
column6: Tā yòng zhēn bǎ cì tiǎo le chūlái.
column7: He picked the splinter out with a needle.
column9: Poking or prying something out with a point: 把刺挑出來. It also stirs trouble up (挑撥) and appears in 挑戰, a challenge.

column3: Rowing or paddling: 划船, 划桨. It also means "worth it": 划算 is what shoppers say about a good deal, and 不划算 about a poor one.
column4: 周末我们去公园划船吧。
column5: 週末我們去公園劃船吧。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù gōngyuán huá chuán ba.
column7: Let's go rowing in the park this weekend.
column9: Rowing or paddling: 划船, 划槳. It also means "worth it": 划算 is what shoppers say about a good deal, and 不划算 about a poor one.

column3: Rolling something flat into a tube: 卷起来, 卷袖子, 卷头发. It counts rolls (一卷纸), and 内卷 is slang for a rat race of over-competition. 卷饼 is a wrap.
column4: 他把纸卷起来放进包里。
column5: 他把紙捲起來放進包裡。
column6: Tā bǎ zhǐ juǎn qǐlái fàngjìn bāo lǐ.
column7: He rolled up the paper and put it in his bag.
column9: Rolling something flat into a tube: 卷起來, 卷袖子, 卷頭髮. It counts rolls (一卷紙), and 內卷 is slang for a rat race of over-competition. 卷餅 is a wrap.

column3: A pull that leaves things open or apart: 拉开门, 拉开窗帘. It also opens a gap between people or scores (拉开距离), and 拉开序幕 raises the curtain on an event.
column4: 她拉开窗帘，让阳光进来。
column5: 她拉開窗簾，讓陽光進來。
column6: Tā lākāi chuānglián, ràng yángguāng jìnlái.
column7: She drew the curtains to let the sunlight in.
column9: A pull that leaves things open or apart: 拉開門, 拉開窗簾. It also opens a gap between people or scores (拉開距離), and 拉開序幕 raises the curtain on an event.

column3: Two everyday senses: rushing forward (冲出去, 往前冲) and rinsing or pouring water over something (冲澡, 冲咖啡). 冲突 is a conflict.
column6: Yùndòng wán, tā qù chōng le ge zǎo.
column7: After exercising, he went to take a quick shower.
column9: Two everyday senses: rushing forward (衝出去, 往前沖) and rinsing or pouring water over something (沖澡, 沖咖啡). 衝突 is a conflict.

column3: Pulling one thing out from among others or taking part from a whole: 抽出, 抽签, 抽屉. 抽烟 is to smoke, and 抽空 or 抽时间 means to find time in a busy schedule.
column4: 他从书架上抽出一本书。
column5: 他從書架上抽出一本書。
column6: Tā cóng shūjià shang chōu chū yī běn shū.
column7: He pulled a book off the shelf.
column9: Pulling one thing out from among others or taking part from a whole: 抽出, 抽籤, 抽屜. 抽煙 is to smoke, and 抽空 or 抽時間 means to find time in a busy schedule.

column3: The sharp point on a plant or a fish bone (鱼刺), and the verb to prick or stab. It also forms sensations: 刺痛 a sting, 刺眼 glaring, 刺耳 harsh to hear.
column6: Xiǎoxīn, zhè duǒ huā yǒu cì.
column7: Careful, this flower has thorns.
column9: The sharp point on a plant or a fish bone (魚刺), and the verb to prick or stab. It also forms sensations: 刺痛 a sting, 刺眼 glaring, 刺耳 harsh to hear.
