column3: A spoken word for putting your full strength into something, placed before the verb: 使劲推, 使劲跑. 用力 is the neutral way to say it.
column6: Mén tài zhòng le, nǐ děi shǐjìn tuī.
column7: The door is heavy, you have to push hard.
column9: A spoken word for putting your full strength into something, placed before the verb: 使勁推, 使勁跑. 用力 is the neutral way to say it.

column3: The top of something (山顶, 头顶); as a verb, to hold up or push against it (顶住, 顶着太阳). It is the measure word for hats.
column6: Tā dài zhe yī dǐng hóng màozi.
column7: He is wearing a red hat.
column9: The top of something (山頂, 頭頂); as a verb, to hold up or push against it (頂住, 頂著太陽). It is the measure word for hats.

column3: Mostly met inside compounds (避免, 躲避, 避开). On its own it takes a concrete threat to get out of the way of: 避雨, 避风.
column4: 下雨了，我们去那边避雨吧。
column5: 下雨了，我們去那邊避雨吧。
column6: Xià yǔ le, wǒmen qù nàbiān bì yǔ ba.
column7: It's raining, let's take shelter over there.
column9: Mostly met inside compounds (避免, 躲避, 避開). On its own it takes a concrete threat to get out of the way of: 避雨, 避風.

column3: The thing avoided is a bad outcome, often a verb follows: 避免错误, 避免浪费, 避免发生. To dodge a person you would say 躲.
column6: Kāichē shí yào bìmiǎn jiē diànhuà.
column7: You should avoid answering the phone while driving.
column9: The thing avoided is a bad outcome, often a verb follows: 避免錯誤, 避免浪費, 避免發生. To dodge a person you would say 躲.

column3: Getting free of something that clings or weighs on you: a bad state, a burden or a follower (摆脱困境, 摆脱贫穷, 摆脱烦恼). It suggests an effort, not a casual dropping.
column6: Tā xiǎng bǎituō zhè zhǒng shēnghuó.
column7: He wants to break free from this kind of life.
column9: Getting free of something that clings or weighs on you: a bad state, a burden or a follower (擺脫困境, 擺脫貧窮, 擺脫煩惱). It suggests an effort, not a casual dropping.

column3: Someone steps in to stop what is about to happen or under way, and the object is usually a person or an event: 阻止他, 阻止事故发生. It is not for stopping yourself, which is 停止.
column4: 没有人能阻止他去做这件事。
column5: 沒有人能阻止他去做這件事。
column6: Méiyǒu rén néng zǔzhǐ tā qù zuò zhè jiàn shì.
column7: No one can stop him from doing this.
column9: Someone steps in to stop what is about to happen or under way, and the object is usually a person or an event: 阻止他, 阻止事故發生. It is not for stopping yourself, which is 停止.

column3: Before a verb: circumstances left no choice (被迫离开, 被迫取消). No one is named as the forcer, and it is more formal than 只好.
column4: 因为下大雨，比赛被迫取消了。
column5: 因為下大雨，比賽被迫取消了。
column6: Yīnwèi xià dàyǔ, bǐsài bèipò qǔxiāo le.
column7: Because of the heavy rain, the match was forced to be canceled.
column9: Before a verb: circumstances left no choice (被迫離開, 被迫取消). No one is named as the forcer, and it is more formal than 只好.

column3: Bearing a heavy load of pressure, pain, loss or weight (承受压力, 承受不了). 忍受 is putting up with something unpleasant, so 承受 sounds more like carrying a load. 承 is built from a kneeling person and both hands, with the sense of holding and carrying.
column4: 他一个人承受着很大的压力。
column5: 他一個人承受著很大的壓力。
column6: Tā yī ge rén chéngshòu zhe hěn dà de yālì.
column7: He bears a lot of pressure all by himself.
column9: Bearing a heavy load of pressure, pain, loss or weight (承受壓力, 承受不了). 忍受 is putting up with something unpleasant, so 承受 sounds more like carrying a load. 承 is built from a kneeling person and both hands, with the sense of holding and carrying.

column3: Taking a responsibility, cost or risk onto yourself: 承担责任, 承担费用, 承担风险. For pressure or pain that falls on you, use 承受.
column4: 出了问题，我来承担责任。
column5: 出了問題，我來承擔責任。
column6: Chū le wèntí, wǒ lái chéngdān zérèn.
column7: If anything goes wrong, I'll take the responsibility.
column9: Taking a responsibility, cost or risk onto yourself: 承擔責任, 承擔費用, 承擔風險. For pressure or pain that falls on you, use 承受.

column3: Rare on its own; learners mostly meet it in 遇到, 遇见 and 遇险, or in 待遇 for treatment and pay. Alone, it suits a general case like 遇事.
column6: Yù shì bù yào huāng.
column7: Don't panic when something happens.
column9: Rare on its own; learners mostly meet it in 遇到, 遇見 and 遇險, or in 待遇 for treatment and pay. Alone, it suits a general case like 遇事.

column3: Running into a person or something unplanned: 遇到朋友, 遇到困难, 遇到问题. Surprises and troubles are its natural objects; an arranged meeting is 见面.
column4: 我在街上遇到了一个老朋友。
column5: 我在街上遇到了一個老朋友。
column6: Wǒ zài jiē shang yùdào le yī ge lǎo péngyou.
column7: I ran into an old friend on the street.
column9: Running into a person or something unplanned: 遇到朋友, 遇到困難, 遇到問題. Surprises and troubles are its natural objects; an arranged meeting is 見面.

column3: A neutral word for a chance meeting, mostly with people (很高兴遇见你). It can also take problems (遇见困难), but 遇到 is the usual word for those.
column4: 我昨天在地铁里遇见了老师。
column5: 我昨天在地鐵裡遇見了老師。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān zài dìtiě lǐ yùjiàn le lǎoshī.
column7: Yesterday I ran into my teacher on the subway.
column9: A neutral word for a chance meeting, mostly with people (很高興遇見你). It can also take problems (遇見困難), but 遇到 is the usual word for those.

column3: A verb to stimulate or upset (刺激经济, 别刺激他) and an adjective for thrilling (很刺激), as with roller coasters. So the same word is fun in one sentence and hurtful in another.
column6: Zuò guòshānchē zhēn cìjī!
column7: Riding the roller coaster is really thrilling!
column9: A verb to stimulate or upset (刺激經濟, 別刺激他) and an adjective for thrilling (很刺激), as with roller coasters. So the same word is fun in one sentence and hurtful in another.

column3: Noun: a hard-earned lesson from a mistake or failure (吸取教训). Verb: to lecture or scold (教训孩子). A school lesson is a different word, 课.
column4: 这次失败给了我们一个教训。
column5: 這次失敗給了我們一個教訓。
column6: Zhè cì shībài gěi le wǒmen yī ge jiàoxun.
column7: This failure taught us a lesson.
column9: Noun: a hard-earned lesson from a mistake or failure (吸取教訓). Verb: to lecture or scold (教訓孩子). A school lesson is a different word, 課.

column3: A formal complaint to someone with authority, such as a manager or an agency (向经理投诉, 接到投诉). Merely grumbling is 抱怨. Common in service settings.
column4: 我要向经理投诉这家餐厅。
column5: 我要向經理投訴這家餐廳。
column6: Wǒ yào xiàng jīnglǐ tóusù zhè jiā cāntīng.
column7: I want to make a complaint to the manager about this restaurant.
column9: A formal complaint to someone with authority, such as a manager or an agency (向經理投訴, 接到投訴). Merely grumbling is 抱怨. Common in service settings.

column3: Noun and verb. Said to clear the air between people: 别误会, 这是个误会, 误会了他的意思.
column6: Qǐng bié wùhuì, wǒ méiyǒu shēngqì.
column7: Please don't get me wrong, I'm not angry.
column9: Noun and verb. Said to clear the air between people: 別誤會, 這是個誤會, 誤會了他的意思.

column3: A written linker for verbs, adjectives and clauses, not for plain nouns (use 和). It joins similar things (年轻而有活力) or contrasting ones (大而不贵), and shows up in 不约而同. Rare in casual talk.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu piàoliang ér piányi.
column7: This piece of clothing is pretty and cheap.
column9: A written linker for verbs, adjectives and clauses, not for plain nouns (use 和). It joins similar things (年輕而有活力) or contrasting ones (大而不貴), and shows up in 不約而同. Rare in casual talk.

column3: Follows a negative and gives the true statement, usually in the pair 不是……而是……. Both spoken and written.
column4: 他不是不想去，而是没有时间。
column5: 他不是不想去，而是沒有時間。
column6: Tā bù shì bù xiǎng qù, érshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
column7: It's not that he doesn't want to go, but that he has no time.
column9: Follows a negative and gives the true statement, usually in the pair 不是……而是……. Both spoken and written.

column3: A written "however" that opens the second clause and turns against expectation. Speech uses 可是 or 但是 instead.
column4: 他很努力，然而还是没有成功。
column5: 他很努力，然而還是沒有成功。
column6: Tā hěn nǔlì, rán'ér háishi méiyǒu chénggōng.
column7: He worked hard, but he still didn't succeed.
column9: A written "however" that opens the second clause and turns against expectation. Speech uses 可是 or 但是 instead.

column3: It sits after the subject and before the verb, never at the start of a clause. 但是 or 可是 can open the clause, with 却 inside it for a stronger turn: 可是他却不来。
column4: 我等了他很久，他却没来。
column5: 我等了他很久，他卻沒來。
column6: Wǒ děng le tā hěn jiǔ, tā què méi lái.
column7: I waited for him for a long time, but he didn't come.
column9: It sits after the subject and before the verb, never at the start of a clause. 但是 or 可是 can open the clause, with 卻 inside it for a stronger turn: 可是他卻不來。

column3: It opens the second clause and names what happens if the first does not hold: 快走，否则要迟到了。 Written and slightly formal; in speech 不然 is the usual word. The 否 is the one in 是否.
column4: 快点走，否则我们要迟到了。
column5: 快點走，否則我們要遲到了。
column6: Kuài diǎn zǒu, fǒuzé wǒmen yào chídào le.
column7: Hurry up, otherwise we will be late.
column9: It opens the second clause and names what happens if the first does not hold: 快走，否則要遲到了。 Written and slightly formal; in speech 不然 is the usual word. The 否 is the one in 是否.

column3: The spoken partner of 否则, opening the second clause with the bad result. It also opens a suggestion when something is not working: 不然我们明天再去吧。
column4: 早点睡吧，不然明天起不来。
column5: 早點睡吧，不然明天起不來。
column6: Zǎodiǎn shuì ba, bùrán míngtiān qǐ bu lái.
column7: Go to bed early, or you won't be able to get up tomorrow.
column9: The spoken partner of 否則, opening the second clause with the bad result. It also opens a suggestion when something is not working: 不然我們明天再去吧。

column3: It comes with a question word or a choice (不管谁, 不管多难, 不管去不去), and the main clause almost always has 都 or 也. Spoken; the written partner is 无论.
column4: 不管多难，我都要试一试。
column5: 不管多難，我都要試一試。
column6: Bùguǎn duō nán, wǒ dōu yào shì yī shì.
column7: No matter how hard it is, I'll give it a try.
column9: It comes with a question word or a choice (不管誰, 不管多難, 不管去不去), and the main clause almost always has 都 or 也. Spoken; the written partner is 無論.

column3: The written partner of 不管, with the same pattern: a question word or a choice, then 都 or 也 in the main clause. The set phrase 无论如何 means in any case.
column4: 无论天气怎么样，我们都去。
column5: 無論天氣怎麼樣，我們都去。
column6: Wúlùn tiānqì zěnmeyàng, wǒmen dōu qù.
column7: Whatever the weather, we are going.
column9: The written partner of 不管, with the same pattern: a question word or a choice, then 都 or 也 in the main clause. The set phrase 無論如何 means in any case.

column3: It grants an extreme or unlikely case and says it changes nothing, so the second clause normally has 也 or 都. A common shape is 哪怕再难，也……. Livelier than the more formal 即使.
column6: Nǎpà xià dàyǔ, wǒ yě yào qù.
column7: Even if it rains heavily, I still want to go.
column9: It grants an extreme or unlikely case and says it changes nothing, so the second clause normally has 也 or 都. A common shape is 哪怕再難，也……. Livelier than the more formal 即使.

column3: It brings up a feared but unlikely event, usually a bad one, and the main clause says what to do: 万一下雨怎么办？ Also a noun for that mishap itself: 以防万一. Think one chance in ten thousand.
column6: Dài shàng sǎn ba, wànyī xià yǔ ne.
column7: Take an umbrella, just in case it rains.
column9: It brings up a feared but unlikely event, usually a bad one, and the main clause says what to do: 萬一下雨怎麼辦？ Also a noun for that mishap itself: 以防萬一. Think one chance in ten thousand.

column3: A written conditional for imagined or contrary-to-fact situations: 假如我是你. More formal than 如果, and the main clause often starts with 就 or 那么.
column4: 假如我是你，我就不会这样做。
column5: 假如我是你，我就不會這樣做。
column6: Jiǎrú wǒ shì nǐ, wǒ jiù bù huì zhèyàng zuò.
column7: If I were you, I wouldn't do it like that.
column9: A written conditional for imagined or contrary-to-fact situations: 假如我是你. More formal than 如果, and the main clause often starts with 就 or 那麼.

column3: Mostly used in the pair 既……又/也…… for two qualities at once, usually both good or both bad: 既便宜又好吃. The other common use is 既然. It shows a person kneeling at a bowl of rice; one reading is that the person has turned away, finished eating.
column6: Tā jì cōngmíng yòu nǔlì.
column7: She is both clever and hardworking.
column9: Mostly used in the pair 既……又/也…… for two qualities at once, usually both good or both bad: 既便宜又好吃. The other common use is 既然. It shows a person kneeling at a bowl of rice; one reading is that the person has turned away, finished eating.

column3: It starts from something both sides already accept and draws a conclusion or suggestion: 既然你累了，就早点休息吧。 The second clause often has 就 or 那么. Unlike 因为, it does not give a cause. The 然 ends many adverbs: 突然, 当然.
column4: 既然你累了，就早点休息吧。
column5: 既然你累了，就早點休息吧。
column6: Jìrán nǐ lèi le, jiù zǎodiǎn xiūxi ba.
column7: Since you are tired, get some rest early.
column9: It starts from something both sides already accept and draws a conclusion or suggestion: 既然你累了，就早點休息吧。 The second clause often has 就 or 那麼. Unlike 因為, it does not give a cause. The 然 ends many adverbs: 突然, 當然.

column3: Written. It mostly joins nouns, with the main item first, and in a list only the last item takes it: 书、杂志以及报纸. In speech people use 和.
column4: 桌子上有书、笔以及一些水果。
column5: 桌子上有書、筆以及一些水果。
column6: Zhuōzi shang yǒu shū, bǐ yǐjí yīxiē shuǐguǒ.
column7: On the table there are books, pens and some fruit.
column9: Written. It mostly joins nouns, with the main item first, and in a list only the last item takes it: 書、雜誌以及報紙. In speech people use 和.

column3: It starts a sentence or clause that adds a further point, often followed by 还 or 也. Typical of reports and essays; in speech 另外 is the usual word.
column4: 他会说英语，此外还会说日语。
column5: 他會說英語，此外還會說日語。
column6: Tā huì shuō Yīngyǔ, cǐwài hái huì shuō Rìyǔ.
column7: He speaks English, and besides that he speaks Japanese.
column9: It starts a sentence or clause that adds a further point, often followed by 還 or 也. Typical of reports and essays; in speech 另外 is the usual word.

column3: A written word that is rare in speech, where people say 这 or 这里. It lives on in set phrases such as 此时, 此外, 因此, 从此, and on signs like the one in the example.
column6: Qǐng wù zài cǐ tíng chē.
column7: Please do not park here.
column9: A written word that is rare in speech, where people say 這 or 這裡. It lives on in set phrases such as 此時, 此外, 因此, 從此, and on signs like the one in the example.

column3: It begins the second clause, which is the next step or natural result of the first, not a logical conclusion (that is 所以). The 于 is a written word for in or at, as in 由于 and 关于.
column4: 天黑了，于是我们回家了。
column5: 天黑了，於是我們回家了。
column6: Tiān hēi le, yúshì wǒmen huí jiā le.
column7: It got dark, so we went home.
column9: It begins the second clause, which is the next step or natural result of the first, not a logical conclusion (that is 所以). The 於 is a written word for in or at, as in 由於 and 關於.

column3: On its own it mostly means law, in set verbs: 犯法, 守法, 违法. As the second half of a word it means a way of doing or seeing: 办法, 做法, 说法, 看法, 想法. In 法国 and 法语 it stands for France.
column6: Tā yīdiǎnr yě bù dǒng fǎ.
column7: He doesn't know the law at all.
column9: On its own it mostly means law, in set verbs: 犯法, 守法, 違法. As the second half of a word it means a way of doing or seeing: 辦法, 做法, 說法, 看法, 想法. In 法國 and 法語 it stands for France.

column3: Counted with 位 or 名. The 官 ending names officials by their role: 警官, 军官, 外交官. In court the 律师 argues the case and the 法官 decides it.
column4: 法官宣布了最后的结果。
column5: 法官宣布了最後的結果。
column6: Fǎguān xuānbù le zuìhòu de jiéguǒ.
column7: The judge announced the final result.
column9: Counted with 位 or 名. The 官 ending names officials by their role: 警官, 軍官, 外交官. In court the 律師 argues the case and the 法官 decides it.

column3: Both the body of law and one particular law, in a formal register. Typical verbs: 遵守, 违反, 制定. A house rule or school rule is not a 法律; that is a 规定 or 规则.
column4: 每个人都应该遵守法律。
column5: 每個人都應該遵守法律。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yīnggāi zūnshǒu fǎlǜ.
column7: Everyone should obey the law.
column9: Both the body of law and one particular law, in a formal register. Typical verbs: 遵守, 違反, 制定. A house rule or school rule is not a 法律; that is a 規定 or 規則.

column3: The institution and also its building: 去法院, 起诉到法院. Lower courts are 基层/中级/高级人民法院 on the mainland and 地方法院 in Taiwan; the highest is 最高人民法院 on the mainland and 最高法院 in Taiwan.
column4: 这个案子明天在法院开庭。
column5: 這個案子明天在法院開庭。
column6: Zhège ànzi míngtiān zài fǎyuàn kāitíng.
column7: This case will be heard in court tomorrow.
column9: The institution and also its building: 去法院, 起訴到法院. Lower courts are 基層/中級/高級人民法院 on the mainland and 地方法院 in Taiwan; the highest is 最高人民法院 on the mainland and 最高法院 in Taiwan.

column3: Rules that have been set for a game, a system or traffic: 游戏规则, 交通规则. Customs of behavior are 规矩, official orders 规定. As an adjective it means regular in form, so 不规则 is irregular. The 则 is the same standard in 原则.
column6: Bǐsài yǒu zìjǐ de guīzé.
column7: The competition has its own rules.
column9: Rules that have been set for a game, a system or traffic: 遊戲規則, 交通規則. Customs of behavior are 規矩, official orders 規定. As an adjective it means regular in form, so 不規則 is irregular. The 則 is the same standard in 原則.

column3: A pattern you discover rather than one people impose (that is 规则): 自然规律, 找规律. As an adjective it describes a steady routine: 作息很规律.
column6: Tā de shēnghuó hěn yǒu guīlǜ.
column7: He lives a very regular life.
column9: A pattern you discover rather than one people impose (that is 規則): 自然規律, 找規律. As an adjective it describes a steady routine: 作息很規律.

column3: The rules a group must keep, as in a school, army or workplace: 遵守纪律, 课堂纪律. Personal self-discipline is a different word, 自律.
column6: Xuésheng yào zūnshǒu kètáng jìlǜ.
column7: Students must keep to classroom discipline.
column9: The rules a group must keep, as in a school, army or workplace: 遵守紀律, 課堂紀律. Personal self-discipline is a different word, 自律.

column3: A basic standard, for a person's morals or an organization's rules: 坚持原则, 违反原则. 原则上 often opens a general rule before the exception: 原则上可以，但是……
column4: 在原则问题上，他从不让步。
column5: 在原則問題上，他從不讓步。
column6: Zài yuánzé wèntí shang, tā cóng bù ràngbù.
column7: On matters of principle, he never gives way.
column9: A basic standard, for a person's morals or an organization's rules: 堅持原則, 違反原則. 原則上 often opens a general rule before the exception: 原則上可以，但是……

column3: Firm, official wording for signs and rules: 禁止吸烟, 禁止入内. In speech people say 不许 or 不让.
column6: Zhèlǐ jìnzhǐ tíng chē.
column7: Parking is not allowed here.
column9: Firm, official wording for signs and rules: 禁止吸煙, 禁止入內. In speech people say 不許 or 不讓.

column3: Verb and noun. It sets a ceiling but allows what stays under it, where 禁止 bans outright. 限 alone shows up in 限速, 限时 and 限量, a speed limit, a time limit and a limited quantity.
column6: Zhège yóuxì yǒu niánlíng xiànzhì.
column7: This game has an age limit.
column9: Verb and noun. It sets a ceiling but allows what stays under it, where 禁止 bans outright. 限 alone shows up in 限速, 限時 and 限量, a speed limit, a time limit and a limited quantity.

column3: A broad line of action set by a government or organization: 基本方针, 教育方针, 制定方针. It is bigger than a single step (that is a 措施). Picture a compass needle pointing the way.
column4: 国家制定了新的教育方针。
column5: 國家制定了新的教育方針。
column6: Guójiā zhìdìng le xīn de jiàoyù fāngzhēn.
column7: The country has drawn up a new education policy.
column9: A broad line of action set by a government or organization: 基本方針, 教育方針, 制定方針. It is bigger than a single step (that is a 措施). Picture a compass needle pointing the way.

column3: A concrete step taken against a problem, usually with 采取: 采取措施, 安全措施. Counted with 项: 一项措施. The general line behind such steps is a 方针.
column4: 政府采取了一些新的措施。
column5: 政府採取了一些新的措施。
column6: Zhèngfǔ cǎiqǔ le yīxiē xīn de cuòshī.
column7: The government has taken some new measures.
column9: A concrete step taken against a problem, usually with 採取: 採取措施, 安全措施. Counted with 項: 一項措施. The general line behind such steps is a 方針.

column3: Formal. The object is something written and lasting: 制订计划, 制订规则, 制订方案. Almost the same as 制定, the more common form. By itself 订 means to book or order: 订票, 订位.
column4: 我们一起制订了一个学习计划。
column5: 我們一起制訂了一個學習計畫。
column6: Wǒmen yīqǐ zhìdìng le yī ge xuéxí jìhuà.
column7: Together we drew up a study plan.
column9: Formal. The object is something written and lasting: 制訂計劃, 制訂規則, 制訂方案. Almost the same as 制定, the more common form. By itself 訂 means to book or order: 訂票, 訂位.

column3: The executive body that governs, at any level: 中央政府, 地方政府. The country itself is 国家, not 政府. In news it is often the subject of 决定, 宣布 or 规定.
column4: 政府决定增加学校的数量。
column5: 政府決定增加學校的數量。
column6: Zhèngfǔ juédìng zēngjiā xuéxiào de shùliàng.
column7: The government decided to increase the number of schools.
column9: The executive body that governs, at any level: 中央政府, 地方政府. The country itself is 國家, not 政府. In news it is often the subject of 決定, 宣布 or 規定.

column3: Noun and adjective: 关心政治, 政治问题. 政治家 is a politician, and 政治 is also a school subject. The 政 is the same as in 政府, 政策 and 政党.
column6: Tā duì zhèngzhì hěn gǎn xìngqù.
column7: He is very interested in politics.
column9: Noun and adjective: 關心政治, 政治問題. 政治家 is a politician, and 政治 is also a school subject. The 政 is the same as in 政府, 政策 and 政黨.

column3: The head of a government, not of the state. The Chinese premier is 国务院总理 on the mainland (行政院院长 in Taiwan). Germany's chancellor is 德国总理, while Japan's and Britain's prime ministers are usually 首相. 总 starts other top titles: 总统, 总经理.
column4: 新总理今天发表了讲话。
column5: 新總理今天發表了講話。
column6: Xīn zǒnglǐ jīntiān fābiǎo le jiǎnghuà.
column7: The new prime minister gave a speech today.
column9: The head of a government, not of the state. The Chinese premier is 國務院總理 on the mainland (行政院院長 in Taiwan). Germany's chancellor is 德國總理, while Japan's and Britain's prime ministers are usually 首相. 總 starts other top titles: 總統, 總經理.

column3: President of a republic: 美国总统 "the US president", 总统选举 "presidential election". 总 "overall" plus 统 "lead". It is used for the head of state of countries such as the United States and Taiwan. In the PRC, the head of state is called 主席.
column4: 美国总统明天要访问中国。
column5: 美國總統明天要訪問中國。
column6: Měiguó zǒngtǒng míngtiān yào fǎngwèn Zhōngguó.
column7: The American president will visit China tomorrow.
column9: President of a republic: 美國總統 "the US president", 總統選舉 "presidential election". 總 "overall" plus 統 "lead". It is used for the head of state of countries such as the United States and Taiwan. In the PRC, the head of state is called 主席.

column3: In modern speech 官员 is the usual word for an official; 官 alone is 当官 (to hold office) or a rank suffix: 军官, 警官, 法官. It is roughly analyzed as multiple rooms under a roof, an official building.
column6: Guān yuè dà, zérèn yuè dà.
column7: The higher the rank, the greater the responsibility.
column9: In modern speech 官員 is the usual word for an official; 官 alone is 當官 (to hold office) or a rank suffix: 軍官, 警官, 法官. It is roughly analyzed as multiple rooms under a roof, an official building.

column3: Coming from the authorities, or from a company or organization itself: 官方网站, 官方账号, 官方消息. Spoken shortening: 官网. The opposite is 民间, or 非官方.
column4: 请看官方网站上的通知。
column5: 請看官方網站上的通知。
column6: Qǐng kàn guānfāng wǎngzhàn shang de tōngzhī.
column7: Please look at the notice on the official website.
column9: Coming from the authorities, or from a company or organization itself: 官方網站, 官方帳號, 官方消息. Spoken shortening: 官網. The opposite is 民間, or 非官方.

column3: Often a modifier for things aimed at everyone: 大众文化, 大众媒体, 大众化 (made popular). 众 ends other words for groups of people: 观众, 听众, 群众, 公众.
column4: 这是一家受大众喜爱的饭店。
column5: 這是一家受大眾喜愛的飯店。
column6: Zhè shì yī jiā shòu dàzhòng xǐ'ài de fàndiàn.
column7: This is a restaurant loved by the public.
column9: Often a modifier for things aimed at everyone: 大眾文化, 大眾媒體, 大眾化 (made popular). 眾 ends other words for groups of people: 觀眾, 聽眾, 群眾, 公眾.

column3: Verb: bringing separate things under one standard, as in 统一管理, 统一标准. Adjective before a noun or 的: all alike, as in 统一价格, 统一的校服.
column4: 同学们穿着统一的校服。
column5: 同學們穿著統一的校服。
column6: Tóngxuémen chuān zhe tǒngyī de xiàofú.
column7: The students are wearing the same school uniform.
column9: Verb: bringing separate things under one standard, as in 統一管理, 統一標準. Adjective before a noun or 的: all alike, as in 統一價格, 統一的校服.

column3: A king ranks below an emperor (皇帝). Compounds: 国王, 王子 (prince), 王后 (queen consort), 女王 (queen in her own right). It may have begun as a picture of a ritual axe, possibly of jade, a symbol of the king's power.
column6: Shīzi shì bǎi shòu zhī wáng.
column7: The lion is the king of beasts.
column9: A king ranks below an emperor (皇帝). Compounds: 國王, 王子 (prince), 王后 (queen consort), 女王 (queen in her own right). It may have begun as a picture of a ritual axe, possibly of jade, a symbol of the king's power.

column3: A job title, counted with 名 or 位: 当外交官. A senior one is an 大使 (ambassador); the ministry is 外交部. The 官 ending is the same as in 警官, 军官 and 法官.
column4: 她的爸爸是一名外交官。
column5: 她的爸爸是一名外交官。
column6: Tā de bàba shì yī míng wàijiāoguān.
column7: Her father is a diplomat.
column9: A job title, counted with 名 or 位: 當外交官. A senior one is an 大使 (ambassador); the ministry is 外交部. The 官 ending is the same as in 警官, 軍官 and 法官.

column3: Sounds exactly like 权力, which is power held over others; 权利 is what you are entitled to. Verbs: 享有, 放弃, 保护. It pairs with 义务: 权利和义务. 人权 is human rights.
column4: 每个人都有受教育的权利。
column5: 每個人都有受教育的權利。
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yǒu shòu jiàoyù de quánlì.
column7: Everyone has the right to be educated.
column9: Sounds exactly like 權力, which is power held over others; 權利 is what you are entitled to. Verbs: 享有, 放棄, 保護. It pairs with 義務: 權利和義務. 人權 is human rights.

column3: The other half of 权利和义务. Verbs: 尽义务, 履行义务. Before a noun it means unpaid or required by law: 义务劳动, 义务教育. A volunteer is an 义工 in Taiwan and a 志愿者 on the mainland.
column4: 纳税是每个公民的义务。
column5: 納稅是每個公民的義務。
column6: Nàshuì shì měi ge gōngmín de yìwù.
column7: Paying tax is every citizen's duty.
column9: The other half of 權利和義務. Verbs: 盡義務, 履行義務. Before a noun it means unpaid or required by law: 義務勞動, 義務教育. A volunteer is an 義工 in Taiwan and a 志願者 on the mainland.

column3: One battle or fight, not the whole war (that is 战争); counted with 场. Figurative for any hard struggle. Family: 战斗机 (fighter plane), 战斗力 (fighting strength).
column4: 战士们勇敢地投入了战斗。
column5: 戰士們勇敢地投入了戰鬥。
column6: Zhànshìmen yǒnggǎn de tóurù le zhàndòu.
column7: The soldiers bravely threw themselves into the battle.
column9: One battle or fight, not the whole war (that is 戰爭); counted with 場. Figurative for any hard struggle. Family: 戰鬥機 (fighter plane), 戰鬥力 (fighting strength).

column3: A whole war as a historical event, bigger than one 战斗; counted with 场. Verbs: 发动, 爆发, 结束. 战 alone ends other war words: 冷战, 内战, 世界大战.
column4: 战争给人们带来了很多痛苦。
column5: 戰爭給人們帶來了很多痛苦。
column6: Zhànzhēng gěi rénmen dàilái le hěn duō tòngkǔ.
column7: War brought people a lot of suffering.
column9: A whole war as a historical event, bigger than one 戰鬥; counted with 場. Verbs: 發動, 爆發, 結束. 戰 alone ends other war words: 冷戰, 內戰, 世界大戰.

column3: A respectful word for service members, especially in the PLA, and for people who fight for a cause: 和平战士. The plain word for an enlisted soldier is 士兵. Counted with 名 or 位.
column4: 这位战士受了很重的伤。
column5: 這位戰士受了很重的傷。
column6: Zhè wèi zhànshì shòu le hěn zhòng de shāng.
column7: This soldier was badly wounded.
column9: A respectful word for service members, especially in the PLA, and for people who fight for a cause: 和平戰士. The plain word for an enlisted soldier is 士兵. Counted with 名 or 位.

column3: Alone it is the speech word for a rank-and-file soldier: 当兵 (to do military service), 当兵的. 士兵 is the fuller, more formal word. Added to a branch or status: 步兵, 骑兵, 新兵, 老兵. In Chinese chess it is also the pawn.
column6: Tā dāng le liǎng nián bīng.
column7: He did two years of military service.
column9: Alone it is the speech word for a rank-and-file soldier: 當兵 (to do military service), 當兵的. 士兵 is the fuller, more formal word. Added to a branch or status: 步兵, 騎兵, 新兵, 老兵. In Chinese chess it is also the pawn.

column3: Someone who means to harm you; a rival in a game or contest is a 对手. It also works for things: 健康的敌人. 敌 starts 敌军 and 敌国, the enemy army and enemy country. The opposite is 朋友.
column6: Áoyè shì jiànkāng de dírén.
column7: Staying up late is the enemy of health.
column9: Someone who means to harm you; a rival in a game or contest is a 對手. It also works for things: 健康的敵人. 敵 starts 敵軍 and 敵國, the enemy army and enemy country. The opposite is 朋友.

column3: Used for people and places, and figuratively: 征服高山, 征服观众. The 服 is the one meaning to submit or be convinced, as in 说服, 服从 and 佩服.
column4: 他成功地征服了这座高山。
column5: 他成功地征服了這座高山。
column6: Tā chénggōng de zhēngfú le zhè zuò gāoshān.
column7: He successfully conquered this high mountain.
column9: Used for people and places, and figuratively: 征服高山, 征服觀眾. The 服 is the one meaning to submit or be convinced, as in 說服, 服從 and 佩服.

column3: Gives orders to troops or traffic, and leads an orchestra: 指挥交通, 乐队指挥. The noun is the person doing it. A commanding officer is a 指挥官. 挥 alone is to wave: 挥手.
column6: Jǐngchá zhèngzài zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
column7: The police officer is directing the traffic.
column9: Gives orders to troops or traffic, and leads an orchestra: 指揮交通, 樂隊指揮. The noun is the person doing it. A commanding officer is a 指揮官. 揮 alone is to wave: 揮手.

column3: The object follows directly: 战胜对手, 战胜困难, 战胜疾病. Used for wars and sport, but most often figuratively for overcoming something hard. In casual talk about a game people say 赢. The 胜 is also in 胜利 and 获胜.
column4: 他战胜了病魔，重新站了起来。
column5: 他戰勝了病魔，重新站了起來。
column6: Tā zhànshèng le bìngmó, chóngxīn zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: He overcame his illness and stood up again.
column9: The object follows directly: 戰勝對手, 戰勝困難, 戰勝疾病. Used for wars and sport, but most often figuratively for overcoming something hard. In casual talk about a game people say 贏. The 勝 is also in 勝利 and 獲勝.

column3: The one beaten is the object: 我们打败了对手. If you are the loser, say 输 or 败给. Other 打 plus result words: 打赢, 打破, 打倒. Potential forms: 打得败, 打不败.
column6: Wǒmen duì dǎbài le duìshǒu.
column7: Our team beat the opponents.
column9: The one beaten is the object: 我們打敗了對手. If you are the loser, say 輸 or 敗給. Other 打 plus result words: 打贏, 打破, 打倒. Potential forms: 打得敗, 打不敗.

column3: Mostly found in compounds: 失败, 战败, 打败. As a lone verb it sounds written or newsy, as in 败给对手; for losing a game, speech uses 输. It can also mean to decay: 败坏.
column4: 这场比赛我们败给了对手。
column5: 這場比賽我們敗給了對手。
column6: Zhè chǎng bǐsài wǒmen bài gěi le duìshǒu.
column7: We lost this match to our opponents.
column9: Mostly found in compounds: 失敗, 戰敗, 打敗. As a lone verb it sounds written or newsy, as in 敗給對手; for losing a game, speech uses 輸. It can also mean to decay: 敗壞.

column3: The plain, neutral word for an enlisted soldier of any army; 战士 sounds respectful. 军人 covers anyone in the armed forces, officers included. Counted with 名.
column4: 广场上站着一名年轻的士兵。
column5: 廣場上站著一名年輕的士兵。
column6: Guǎngchǎng shang zhàn zhe yī míng niánqīng de shìbīng.
column7: A young soldier stands on the square.
column9: The plain, neutral word for an enlisted soldier of any army; 戰士 sounds respectful. 軍人 covers anyone in the armed forces, officers included. Counted with 名.

column3: Praising and somewhat written, for courage in danger: 英勇作战, 英勇牺牲, in speeches and news. Everyday bravery is 勇敢. 英 begins 英雄, and 勇 is also in 勇气.
column4: 消防员英勇地冲进了火场。
column5: 消防員英勇地衝進了火場。
column6: Xiāofángyuán yīngyǒng de chōngjìn le huǒchǎng.
column7: The firefighters heroically rushed into the fire.
column9: Praising and somewhat written, for courage in danger: 英勇作戰, 英勇犧牲, in speeches and news. Everyday bravery is 勇敢. 英 begins 英雄, and 勇 is also in 勇氣.

column3: Introduces what an attitude, view or effect is about, before or after the subject: 他对于这件事很满意. The frame 对于……来说 means "for ..., as far as ... goes". Unlike 关于, it needs an opinion or reaction to follow, not just a topic.
column4: 对于这件事，我没有意见。
column5: 對於這件事，我沒有意見。
column6: Duìyú zhè jiàn shì, wǒ méiyǒu yìjiàn.
column7: As for this matter, I have no objection.
column9: Introduces what an attitude, view or effect is about, before or after the subject: 他對於這件事很滿意. The frame 對於……來說 means "for ..., as far as ... goes". Unlike 關於, it needs an opinion or reaction to follow, not just a topic.

column3: Names the subject matter of a book, talk or question. A 关于 phrase either opens the sentence or becomes a modifier with 的: 关于环保的文章. Unlike 对于, no attitude is involved; it is only "on the topic of".
column4: 我买了一本关于中国历史的书。
column5: 我買了一本關於中國歷史的書。
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī běn guānyú Zhōngguó lìshǐ de shū.
column7: I bought a book about Chinese history.
column9: Names the subject matter of a book, talk or question. A 關於 phrase either opens the sentence or becomes a modifier with 的: 關於環保的文章. Unlike 對於, no attitude is involved; it is only "on the topic of".

column3: Takes a specific problem, group or situation as its target: 针对这个问题采取措施, 针对儿童的节目. The noun 针对性 means "being targeted". It can also mean aimed against someone: 这话不是针对你的.
column4: 这个活动是针对小学生的。
column5: 這個活動是針對小學生的。
column6: Zhège huódòng shì zhēnduì xiǎoxuéshēng de.
column7: This activity is aimed at elementary school students.
column9: Takes a specific problem, group or situation as its target: 針對這個問題採取措施, 針對兒童的節目. The noun 針對性 means "being targeted". It can also mean aimed against someone: 這話不是針對你的.

column3: Opens a sentence or comes before a verb to name the evidence or rule behind it: 根据规定, 根据调查结果. As a noun it is the grounds for a claim: 有根据 is well-founded, 没有根据 groundless.
column4: 根据天气预报，明天有雨。
column5: 根據天氣預報，明天有雨。
column6: Gēnjù tiānqì yùbào, míngtiān yǒu yǔ.
column7: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.
column9: Opens a sentence or comes before a verb to name the evidence or rule behind it: 根據規定, 根據調查結果. As a noun it is the grounds for a claim: 有根據 is well-founded, 沒有根據 groundless.

column3: Opens a sentence with a role and then says what follows from it: 作为老师, 我有责任……. As a noun it is conduct or achievement: 有作为 is "to make something of oneself".
column4: 作为学生，你应该认真学习。
column5: 作為學生，你應該認真學習。
column6: Zuòwéi xuésheng, nǐ yīnggāi rènzhēn xuéxí.
column7: As a student, you should study seriously.
column9: Opens a sentence with a role and then says what follows from it: 作為老師, 我有責任……. As a noun it is conduct or achievement: 有作為 is "to make something of oneself".

column3: A written way to name the essential point or deciding factor, mostly in fixed openers: 关键在于, 区别在于, 问题在于. It names a point or factor, not a place.
column6: Chénggōng de guānjiàn zàiyú jiānchí.
column7: The key to success lies in persistence.
column9: A written way to name the essential point or deciding factor, mostly in fixed openers: 關鍵在於, 區別在於, 問題在於. It names a point or factor, not a place.

column3: The everyday way to do something on someone's behalf, with the person right after it: 替我拿一下, 替孩子高兴. The same 替 is in 代替 and 替换.
column6: Nǐ néng tì wǒ mǎi yī zhāng piào ma?
column7: Can you buy a ticket for me?
column9: The everyday way to do something on someone's behalf, with the person right after it: 替我拿一下, 替孩子高興. The same 替 is in 代替 and 替換.

column3: As "from" it is written style and sits in set phrases: 来自 (comes from), 自古 (since ancient times), 自从. As "self" it is the first half of 自己, 自学, 自由, 自动.
column6: Zhè wèi kèrén zì Běijīng lái.
column7: This guest has come from Beijing.
column9: As "from" it is written style and sits in set phrases: 來自 (comes from), 自古 (since ancient times), 自從. As "self" it is the first half of 自己, 自學, 自由, 自動.

column3: What bears down on you is a challenge, danger or decision: 面临困难, 面临挑战, 面临选择. The subject is a person, group or country, and the tone is formal. 面对 is how you actively face it; 面临 is that it has arrived at your door.
column4: 我们面临着很大的困难。
column5: 我們面臨著很大的困難。
column6: Wǒmen miànlín zhe hěn dà de kùnnan.
column7: We are facing great difficulties.
column9: What bears down on you is a challenge, danger or decision: 面臨困難, 面臨挑戰, 面臨選擇. The subject is a person, group or country, and the tone is formal. 面對 is how you actively face it; 面臨 is that it has arrived at your door.

column3: A written way to say where a place is, in descriptions and textbooks: 位于北京, 位于河边. The subject is a city, building or region, never a person, and no 在 goes before it.
column6: Wǒ jiā wèiyú shì zhōngxīn.
column7: My home is in the city center.
column9: A written way to say where a place is, in descriptions and textbooks: 位於北京, 位於河邊. The subject is a city, building or region, never a person, and no 在 goes before it.

column3: Followed by a state, position or stage, usually abstract: 处于领先地位, 处于危险之中, 处于发展阶段. It is formal.
column4: 他现在处于很危险的状态。
column5: 他現在處於很危險的狀態。
column6: Tā xiànzài chǔyú hěn wēixiǎn de zhuàngtài.
column7: He is in a very dangerous state now.
column9: Followed by a state, position or stage, usually abstract: 處於領先地位, 處於危險之中, 處於發展階段. It is formal.

column3: The replacer comes first and the replaced is the object: 机器代替人. It takes a person or a thing, and often 不了: 谁也代替不了你.
column6: Méiyǒu rén néng dàitì tā.
column7: No one can take his place.
column9: The replacer comes first and the replaced is the object: 機器代替人. It takes a person or a thing, and often 不了: 誰也代替不了你.

column3: Stresses something being superseded over time, especially by new technology: 被替代, 替代品 (a substitute product), 无法替代. It is used far more for things than for people.
column4: 电子书正在慢慢替代纸质书。
column5: 電子書正在慢慢替代紙質書。
column6: Diànzǐshū zhèngzài mànmàn tìdài zhǐzhì shū.
column7: E-books are slowly replacing paper books.
column9: Stresses something being superseded over time, especially by new technology: 被替代, 替代品 (a substitute product), 無法替代. It is used far more for things than for people.

column3: The object can be a person, a tool or your own effort: 依靠自己, 依靠科技. As a noun it is the support itself: 他是我们唯一的依靠. In speech 靠 alone does the same job: 靠自己.
column6: Wǒmen zhǐ néng yīkào zìjǐ.
column7: We can only rely on ourselves.
column9: The object can be a person, a tool or your own effort: 依靠自己, 依靠科技. As a noun it is the support itself: 他是我們唯一的依靠. In speech 靠 alone does the same job: 靠自己.

column3: Where something comes from: 消息来源 (a news source), 经济来源 (source of income), 资料来源. As a verb it takes 于: 知识来源于实践.
column4: 这个消息的来源是什么？
column5: 這個消息的來源是什麼？
column6: Zhège xiāoxi de láiyuán shì shénme?
column7: What is the source of this news?
column9: Where something comes from: 消息來源 (a news source), 經濟來源 (source of income), 資料來源. As a verb it takes 於: 知識來源於實踐.

column3: How the parts of something fit together, whether a building, a sentence, an essay or an economy: 句子结构, 年龄结构, 结构复杂.
column4: 这个句子的结构很复杂。
column5: 這個句子的結構很複雜。
column6: Zhège jùzi de jiégòu hěn fùzá.
column7: This sentence has a complicated structure.
column9: How the parts of something fit together, whether a building, a sentence, an essay or an economy: 句子結構, 年齡結構, 結構複雜.

column3: Works in two directions: B 由 A 构成 (B is made up of A), or A 构成 B (A forms or amounts to B), which is how 构成威胁 and 构成犯罪 work.
column6: Shuǐ shì yóu qīng hé yǎng gòuchéng de.
column7: Water is made up of hydrogen and oxygen.
column9: Works in two directions: B 由 A 構成 (B is made up of A), or A 構成 B (A forms or amounts to B), which is how 構成威脅 and 構成犯罪 work.

column3: The way something physical is built, especially a machine, organ or rock layer: 人体构造, 地质构造. Compared with 结构 it is more concrete and technical.
column4: 这台机器的构造很简单。
column5: 這台機器的構造很簡單。
column6: Zhè tái jīqì de gòuzào hěn jiǎndān.
column7: This machine is simply built.
column9: The way something physical is built, especially a machine, organ or rock layer: 人體構造, 地質構造. Compared with 結構 it is more concrete and technical.

column3: Spoken, for fastening something you wear or knot: 系鞋带, 系领带, 系围巾, 系安全带. To tie up a package or someone's hands, use 绑 instead.
column4: 上车以后，请系好安全带。
column5: 上車以後，請繫好安全帶。
column6: Shàng chē yǐhòu, qǐng jì hǎo ānquándài.
column7: After getting in the car, please fasten your seat belt.
column9: Spoken, for fastening something you wear or knot: 繫鞋帶, 繫領帶, 繫圍巾, 繫安全帶. To tie up a package or someone's hands, use 綁 instead.

column3: On its own it is a knot (打结, 蝴蝶结). In compounds it is "to form or to conclude": 结婚, 结账, 结束, 结冰, 结果.
column4: 他在绳子上打了一个结。
column5: 他在繩子上打了一個結。
column6: Tā zài shéngzi shang dǎ le yī ge jié.
column7: He tied a knot in the rope.
column9: On its own it is a knot (打結, 蝴蝶結). In compounds it is "to form or to conclude": 結婚, 結帳, 結束, 結冰, 結果.

column3: Order as a sequence, never as a command: 按顺序, 打乱顺序, 先后顺序. The 顺 in 笔顺 (stroke order) is the same one.
column4: 请按顺序排队，不要着急。
column5: 請按順序排隊，不要著急。
column6: Qǐng àn shùnxù páiduì, bùyào zháojí.
column7: Please line up in order and don't be impatient.
column9: Order as a sequence, never as a command: 按順序, 打亂順序, 先後順序. The 順 in 筆順 (stroke order) is the same one.

column3: Things are set out in a fixed order or pattern: 排列整齐, 按字母顺序排列. The thing arranged is the object (排列座位); for people lining up, say 排队.
column4: 请把这些词按顺序排列。
column5: 請把這些詞按順序排列。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē cí àn shùnxù páiliè.
column7: Please arrange these words in order.
column9: Things are set out in a fixed order or pattern: 排列整齊, 按字母順序排列. The thing arranged is the object (排列座位); for people lining up, say 排隊.

column3: Describes how animals, plants, people or resources are spread over an area: 分布在, 分布广泛, 分布不均. It is not for handing out goods; that is 分发 or 分配.
column4: 大熊猫主要分布在四川。
column5: 大熊貓主要分佈在四川。
column6: Dàxióngmāo zhǔyào fēnbù zài Sìchuān.
column7: Giant pandas live mainly in Sichuan.
column9: Describes how animals, plants, people or resources are spread over an area: 分佈在, 分佈廣泛, 分佈不均. It is not for handing out goods; that is 分發 or 分配.

column3: Divides a whole into named parts: A 分为 B 和 C, 分为三个部分. It is written style; speech prefers 分成.
column6: Zhè běn shū fēnwéi sān ge bùfen.
column7: This book is divided into three parts.
column9: Divides a whole into named parts: A 分為 B 和 C, 分為三個部分. It is written style; speech prefers 分成.

column3: Formal news and notices: something is put in a category or rank, often with 被: 被列为世界遗产, 列为重点.
column4: 这座古城被列为世界文化遗产。
column5: 這座古城被列為世界文化遺產。
column6: Zhè zuò gǔchéng bèi lièwéi shìjiè wénhuà yíchǎn.
column7: This ancient city is listed as a World Cultural Heritage site.
column9: Formal news and notices: something is put in a category or rank, often with 被: 被列為世界遺產, 列為重點.

column3: Puts something on a formal list, plan or agenda: 列入名单, 列入计划, 列入议程. Passive with 被 is common, and 黑名单 is a blacklist.
column4: 他的名字被列入了名单。
column5: 他的名字被列入了名單。
column6: Tā de míngzi bèi lièrù le míngdān.
column7: His name was put on the list.
column9: Puts something on a formal list, plan or agenda: 列入名單, 列入計劃, 列入議程. Passive with 被 is common, and 黑名單 is a blacklist.

column3: A measure word for trains and for lines of people or vehicles: 一列火车, 一列队伍. With a verb it means to list: 列出, 列表. In a data table, 列 is a column on the mainland (a row is 行), but in Taiwan 列 is a row and a column is 栏.
column4: 一列火车从远处开了过来。
column5: 一列火車從遠處開了過來。
column6: Yī liè huǒchē cóng yuǎnchù kāi le guòlái.
column7: A train came from a distance.
column9: A measure word for trains and for lines of people or vehicles: 一列火車, 一列隊伍. With a verb it means to list: 列出, 列表. In a data table, 列 is a column on the mainland (a row is 行), but in Taiwan 列 is a row and a column is 欄.

column3: Counts how many kinds there are, for goods, animals and plants: 种类很多, 种类繁多. One kind is 一种, and 种类 is the whole range.
column4: 这家商店的水果种类很多。
column5: 這家商店的水果種類很多。
column6: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn de shuǐguǒ zhǒnglèi hěn duō.
column7: This store has many kinds of fruit.
column9: Counts how many kinds there are, for goods, animals and plants: 種類很多, 種類繁多. One kind is 一種, and 種類 is the whole range.

column3: A group that shares features, such as a film genre or a data type: 电影类型, 数据类型, 性格类型. Counted with 种: 这种类型.
column4: 你喜欢哪种类型的电影？
column5: 你喜歡哪種類型的電影？
column6: Nǐ xǐhuan nǎ zhǒng lèixíng de diànyǐng?
column7: What type of film do you like?
column9: A group that shares features, such as a film genre or a data type: 電影類型, 數據類型, 性格類型. Counted with 種: 這種類型.

column3: Mostly before a noun: 系列产品 (a product line), 系列活动. 一系列 before a noun means "a whole string of": 一系列问题.
column4: 这个系列一共有五本书。
column5: 這個系列一共有五本書。
column6: Zhège xìliè yīgòng yǒu wǔ běn shū.
column7: This series has five books in all.
column9: Mostly before a noun: 系列產品 (a product line), 系列活動. 一系列 before a noun means "a whole string of": 一系列問題.

column3: The cause is the subject, and the result is almost always bad: 导致事故, 导致失败, 导致交通堵塞. For a good result, use 带来 or 促进.
column4: 大雨导致了严重的交通堵塞。
column5: 大雨導致了嚴重的交通堵塞。
column6: Dàyǔ dǎozhì le yánzhòng de jiāotōng dǔsè.
column7: The heavy rain led to serious traffic jams.
column9: The cause is the subject, and the result is almost always bad: 導致事故, 導致失敗, 導致交通堵塞. For a good result, use 帶來 or 促進.

column3: Takes a person as its object, then a verb: 这件事促使我改变了想法. The 使 is the same causing 使 as in 使人高兴. The tone is formal, and the push is toward an action or change.
column4: 这次失败促使他更加努力。
column5: 這次失敗促使他更加努力。
column6: Zhè cì shībài cùshǐ tā gèngjiā nǔlì.
column7: This failure spurred him to work even harder.
column9: Takes a person as its object, then a verb: 這件事促使我改變了想法. The 使 is the same causing 使 as in 使人高興. The tone is formal, and the push is toward an action or change.

column3: The object is a reaction, feeling or problem: 引起注意, 引起兴趣, 引起误会. Both good and bad outcomes fit, unlike 导致.
column4: 他的话引起了大家的注意。
column5: 他的話引起了大家的注意。
column6: Tā de huà yǐnqǐ le dàjiā de zhùyì.
column7: His words attracted everyone's attention.
column9: The object is a reaction, feeling or problem: 引起注意, 引起興趣, 引起誤會. Both good and bad outcomes fit, unlike 導致.

column3: Gentle, indirect guidance of someone's thinking or behavior, from a teacher or parent: 引导学生思考. For physically leading a group, say 带领.
column4: 老师引导学生自己找答案。
column5: 老師引導學生自己找答案。
column6: Lǎoshī yǐndǎo xuésheng zìjǐ zhǎo dá'àn.
column7: The teacher guides students to find the answers themselves.
column9: Gentle, indirect guidance of someone's thinking or behavior, from a teacher or parent: 引導學生思考. For physically leading a group, say 帶領.

column3: Brings in something from outside, such as technology, equipment, talent or foreign capital: 引进技术, 引进人才. A formal word, typically for companies and institutions.
column4: 公司从国外引进了新设备。
column5: 公司從國外引進了新設備。
column6: Gōngsī cóng guówài yǐnjìn le xīn shèbèi.
column7: The company brought in new equipment from abroad.
column9: Brings in something from outside, such as technology, equipment, talent or foreign capital: 引進技術, 引進人才. A formal word, typically for companies and institutions.

column3: The attractor is the subject, and the people drawn are the object: 吸引游客, 吸引注意. 被吸引 is "be drawn in", and 有吸引力 is "attractive".
column4: 这座城市吸引了很多游客。
column5: 這座城市吸引了很多遊客。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì xīyǐn le hěn duō yóukè.
column7: This city attracts many tourists.
column9: The attractor is the subject, and the people drawn are the object: 吸引遊客, 吸引注意. 被吸引 is "be drawn in", and 有吸引力 is "attractive".

column3: Works for the physical (a sponge, plants) and the abstract (knowledge, experience), and for a group taking in members: 吸收水分, 吸收经验, 吸收新成员.
column6: Hǎimián kěyǐ xīshōu hěn duō shuǐ.
column7: A sponge can absorb a lot of water.
column9: Works for the physical (a sponge, plants) and the abstract (knowledge, experience), and for a group taking in members: 吸收水分, 吸收經驗, 吸收新成員.

column3: Used for abilities, roles and strengths: 发挥作用 (play a role), 发挥才能. In exams and matches, 发挥得好 or 发挥不好 says how someone performed on the day.
column4: 他在比赛中发挥得很好。
column5: 他在比賽中發揮得很好。
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng fāhuī de hěn hǎo.
column7: He performed very well in the match.
column9: Used for abilities, roles and strengths: 發揮作用 (play a role), 發揮才能. In exams and matches, 發揮得好 or 發揮不好 says how someone performed on the day.

column3: Putting learned knowledge, skills or methods to practical use: 运用知识, 灵活运用. It is more formal than 用 and stresses applying what you have learned.
column4: 你要学会运用学到的知识。
column5: 你要學會運用學到的知識。
column6: Nǐ yào xuéhuì yùnyòng xuédào de zhīshi.
column7: You should learn to apply the knowledge you've gained.
column9: Putting learned knowledge, skills or methods to practical use: 運用知識, 靈活運用. It is more formal than 用 and stresses applying what you have learned.

column3: Describes things with real daily use, as opposed to merely pretty: 实用的礼物, 很实用, 实用性. It is positive, and fits objects, skills and books.
column4: 这本书很实用，我每天都用。
column5: 這本書很實用，我每天都用。
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn shíyòng, wǒ měitiān dōu yòng.
column7: This book is very practical, and I use it every day.
column9: Describes things with real daily use, as opposed to merely pretty: 實用的禮物, 很實用, 實用性. It is positive, and fits objects, skills and books.

column3: Answers "what is it used for?": 有很多用途, 主要用途, 用途广泛. It is about things, not people.
column6: Zhè zhǒng gōngjù yǒu hěn duō yòngtú.
column7: This tool has many uses.
column9: Answers "what is it used for?": 有很多用途, 主要用途, 用途廣泛. It is about things, not people.

column3: Goes with something abstract: 作出决定, 作出贡献, 作出回应, 作出努力. 做出 is the same word, and 作出 is the written form.
column4: 公司作出了一个重要的决定。
column5: 公司作出了一個重要的決定。
column6: Gōngsī zuòchū le yī ge zhòngyào de juédìng.
column7: The company made an important decision.
column9: Goes with something abstract: 作出決定, 作出貢獻, 作出回應, 作出努力. 做出 is the same word, and 作出 is the written form.

column3: On its own it is written, for quoting a line, as in the example; in speech "to cite" is 引用. Most of the time it is a building block, starting 引起, 引导, 引进 and ending 吸引.
column6: Tā yǐn le yī jù gǔshī.
column7: He quoted a line of old poetry.
column9: On its own it is written, for quoting a line, as in the example; in speech "to cite" is 引用. Most of the time it is a building block, starting 引起, 引導, 引進 and ending 吸引.

column3: Names parts inside a whole, often with examples: 价格包括早餐, 包括我在内. The subject is the whole, and 在内 closes the list. In Taiwan 括 is read guā.
column6: Jiàgé bāokuò zǎocān hé wǎncān.
column7: The price includes breakfast and dinner.
column9: Names parts inside a whole, often with examples: 價格包括早餐, 包括我在內. The subject is the whole, and 在內 closes the list. In Taiwan 括 is read guā.

column3: Something is held inside as an element, often abstract or hidden: 包含意思, 包含着很多信息. Unlike 包括, it does not list the parts one by one.
column4: 这句话包含着很深的意思。
column5: 這句話包含著很深的意思。
column6: Zhè jù huà bāohán zhe hěn shēn de yìsi.
column7: This sentence contains a deep meaning.
column9: Something is held inside as an element, often abstract or hidden: 包含意思, 包含著很多信息. Unlike 包括, it does not list the parts one by one.

column3: On its own it is for the mouth: 含着糖, 含在嘴里. In compounds it is "to contain" or "to hold back": 含水, 含笑, 含糊 (vague), 包含, 含有.
column6: Háizi zuǐ lǐ hán zhe yī kuài táng.
column7: The child has a candy in his mouth.
column9: On its own it is for the mouth: 含著糖, 含在嘴裡. In compounds it is "to contain" or "to hold back": 含水, 含笑, 含糊 (vague), 包含, 含有.

column3: Said of substances in food, water and goods, as on an ingredient label: 含有糖分, 含有毒素. It is followed by a thing or an amount.
column6: Zhè zhǒng yǐnliào hányǒu hěn duō táng.
column7: This drink contains a lot of sugar.
column9: Said of substances in food, water and goods, as on an ingredient label: 含有糖分, 含有毒素. It is followed by a thing or an amount.

column3: Meets a standard, requirement or situation exactly; the object is almost always abstract: 符合要求, 符合条件, 符合实际.
column4: 他的条件完全符合要求。
column5: 他的條件完全符合要求。
column6: Tā de tiáojiàn wánquán fúhé yāoqiú.
column7: His qualifications fully meet the requirements.
column9: Meets a standard, requirement or situation exactly; the object is almost always abstract: 符合要求, 符合條件, 符合實際.

column3: Formal. It takes conditions and abilities, not physical objects: 具备条件, 具备能力. The negative 不具备 is common in notices and reports.
column4: 做这份工作要具备一定的能力。
column5: 做這份工作要具備一定的能力。
column6: Zuò zhè fèn gōngzuò yào jùbèi yīdìng de nénglì.
column7: To do this job, you need to have a certain ability.
column9: Formal. It takes conditions and abilities, not physical objects: 具備條件, 具備能力. The negative 不具備 is common in notices and reports.

column3: An adjective that follows its subject: 意见一致, 前后一致. As an adverb it means "unanimously": 一致同意. The opposite is 不一致.
column6: Dàjiā de kànfǎ wánquán yīzhì.
column7: Everyone's views are completely in agreement.
column9: An adjective that follows its subject: 意見一致, 前後一致. As an adverb it means "unanimously": 一致同意. The opposite is 不一致.

column3: Both a verb and a noun: 对比一下 is a quick side-by-side comparison, while 形成对比 and 鲜明的对比 name the contrast itself. Use it when two things are set side by side to show their differences. One old dictionary reads 比 as two things set side by side.
column4: 把这两张照片对比一下。
column5: 把這兩張照片對比一下。
column6: Bǎ zhè liǎng zhāng zhàopiàn duìbǐ yīxià.
column7: Compare these two photos.
column9: Both a verb and a noun: 對比一下 is a quick side-by-side comparison, while 形成對比 and 鮮明的對比 name the contrast itself. Use it when two things are set side by side to show their differences. One old dictionary reads 比 as two things set side by side.

column3: Opposite to something is 与A相反 or 和A相反, and 正好相反 or 恰恰相反 says it is exactly the reverse. At the start of a sentence it means "on the contrary": 相反，他很高兴。
column4: 他和我的想法正好相反。
column5: 他和我的想法正好相反。
column6: Tā hé wǒ de xiǎngfǎ zhènghǎo xiāngfǎn.
column7: His idea is the exact opposite of mine.
column9: Opposite to something is 與A相反 or 和A相反, and 正好相反 or 恰恰相反 says it is exactly the reverse. At the start of a sentence it means "on the contrary": 相反，他很高興。

column3: After a verb it says something was done backward or inside out: 穿反了, 放反了, 说反了. As a prefix it gives "anti-" or "against": 反对, 反战. 反面 is the reverse side.
column6: Nǐ de yīfu chuān fǎn le.
column7: You've put your clothes on inside out.
column9: After a verb it says something was done backward or inside out: 穿反了, 放反了, 說反了. As a prefix it gives "anti-" or "against": 反對, 反戰. 反面 is the reverse side.

column3: Two everyday uses: a thing reflects something (反映现实, 反映出问题), and a person reports a problem or opinion upward (向领导反映情况, 反映意见), so someone can act on it.
column4: 这部电影反映了现实生活。
column5: 這部電影反映了現實生活。
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng fǎnyìng le xiànshí shēnghuó.
column7: This film reflects real life.
column9: Two everyday uses: a thing reflects something (反映現實, 反映出問題), and a person reports a problem or opinion upward (向領導反映情況, 反映意見), so someone can act on it.

column3: The object is usually a difficult person or problem: 不好对付 or 很难对付 describes someone tough to handle, and the sense is neutral (对付敌人, 对付困难). Only 对付一下, to get by with something makeshift, is colloquial.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn bù hǎo duìfu.
column7: This child is hard to handle.
column9: The object is usually a difficult person or problem: 不好對付 or 很難對付 describes someone tough to handle, and the sense is neutral (對付敵人, 對付困難). Only 對付一下, to get by with something makeshift, is colloquial.

column3: Stresses a meaning held inside a word, phrase or gesture, deeper or less obvious than 意思. Typical: 词的含义, 深刻的含义, and counted with 种 or 层, as in 有两层含义.
column4: 这个词有两种不同的含义。
column5: 這個詞有兩種不同的含義。
column6: Zhège cí yǒu liǎng zhǒng bù tóng de hányì.
column7: This word has two different meanings.
column9: Stresses a meaning held inside a word, phrase or gesture, deeper or less obvious than 意思. Typical: 詞的含義, 深刻的含義, and counted with 種 or 層, as in 有兩層含義.

column3: Put the substance before it: 含糖量, 维生素含量, 蛋白质含量, then 高 or 低. The pattern 含X量 builds terms for how much X is in something, on food labels and in science.
column4: 这种水果的维生素含量很高。
column5: 這種水果的維生素含量很高。
column6: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ de wéishēngsù hánliàng hěn gāo.
column7: This fruit is high in vitamin content.
column9: Put the substance before it: 含糖量, 維生素含量, 蛋白質含量, then 高 or 低. The pattern 含X量 builds terms for how much X is in something, on food labels and in science.

column3: Formal: what you gain is valuable and often abstract: 获得成功, 获得奖学金, 获得帮助, 获得好评. In everyday speech 得到 is the more common word. 获 has the dog 犭 in it: one dictionary explains the old form as hunting and catching animals with a dog.
column4: 她在比赛中获得了第一名。
column5: 她在比賽中獲得了第一名。
column6: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng huòdé le dì-yī míng.
column7: She won first place in the competition.
column9: Formal: what you gain is valuable and often abstract: 獲得成功, 獲得獎學金, 獲得幫助, 獲得好評. In everyday speech 得到 is the more common word. 獲 has the dog 犭 in it: one dictionary explains the old form as hunting and catching animals with a dog.

column3: You go and get it from a source, especially information, data or resources: 获取信息, 获取数据, 获取权限. Common with technology: 获取密码. Prizes and results go with 获得 instead.
column4: 我们可以在网上获取很多信息。
column5: 我們可以在網上獲取很多資訊。
column6: Wǒmen kěyǐ zài wǎng shang huòqǔ hěn duō xìnxī.
column7: We can get a lot of information online.
column9: You go and get it from a source, especially information, data or resources: 獲取信息, 獲取數據, 獲取權限. Common with technology: 獲取密碼. Prizes and results go with 獲得 instead.

column3: Takes back what you had given out: lent money (收回借出的钱), territory, or your own words and decisions (收回刚才的话, 收回成命). The object is always something you released first.
column4: 他想收回借给朋友的钱。
column5: 他想收回借給朋友的錢。
column6: Tā xiǎng shōuhuí jiè gěi péngyou de qián.
column7: He wants to get back the money he lent to his friend.
column9: Takes back what you had given out: lent money (收回借出的錢), territory, or your own words and decisions (收回剛才的話, 收回成命). The object is always something you released first.

column3: Literally the harvest, and figuratively what you take away from an experience: 这次旅行收获很大, 有很多收获. "What did you get out of it?" is 有什么收获？ It works as a noun and as a verb.
column6: Zhè cì lǚxíng wǒ shōuhuò hěn dà.
column7: I gained a lot from this trip.
column9: Literally the harvest, and figuratively what you take away from an experience: 這次旅行收獲很大, 有很多收獲. "What did you get out of it?" is 有什麼收獲？ It works as a noun and as a verb.

column3: What is provided is help, a service, information, evidence or conditions, often by an organization (提供证据, 提供服务). Usual frame: 为/给 + person + 提供 + thing, as in 为客人提供免费早餐.
column4: 酒店为客人提供免费早餐。
column5: 酒店為客人提供免費早餐。
column6: Jiǔdiàn wèi kèrén tígōng miǎnfèi zǎocān.
column7: The hotel provides free breakfast for its guests.
column9: What is provided is help, a service, information, evidence or conditions, often by an organization (提供證據, 提供服務). Usual frame: 為/給 + person + 提供 + thing, as in 為客人提供免費早餐.

column3: A continuing supply of goods and utilities: 供应热水, 二十四小时供应, 本店供应早餐. 供应商 is a supplier, and 供不应求 says supply cannot meet demand.
column4: 这里二十四小时供应热水。
column5: 這裡二十四小時供應熱水。
column6: Zhèlǐ èrshísì xiǎoshí gōngyìng rèshuǐ.
column7: Hot water is supplied here around the clock.
column9: A continuing supply of goods and utilities: 供應熱水, 二十四小時供應, 本店供應早餐. 供應商 is a supplier, and 供不應求 says supply cannot meet demand.

column3: Stresses both sides giving and receiving, and is more formal than 换, which also means to swap and to replace one thing with another (换衣服, 换钱). Typical: 交换礼物, 交换意见, 交换电话号码, 交换生. 交 began as a picture of a person with crossed legs.
column4: 我们互相交换了电话号码。
column5: 我們互相交換了電話號碼。
column6: Wǒmen hùxiāng jiāohuàn le diànhuà hàomǎ.
column7: We exchanged phone numbers with each other.
column9: Stresses both sides giving and receiving, and is more formal than 換, which also means to swap and to replace one thing with another (換衣服, 換錢). Typical: 交換禮物, 交換意見, 交換電話號碼, 交換生. 交 began as a picture of a person with crossed legs.

column3: Send by mail or courier: 寄信, 寄包裹, 寄快递, with 给 for the receiver (寄给他). It does not cover email, which is 发. It also means to entrust, as in 寄希望于, "to pin hopes on". The roof 宀 fits an older idea of living away from home.
column6: Wǒ gěi péngyou jì le yī fēng xìn.
column7: I sent my friend a letter.
column9: Send by mail or courier: 寄信, 寄包裹, 寄快遞, with 給 for the receiver (寄給他). It does not cover email, which is 發. It also means to entrust, as in 寄希望於, "to pin hopes on". The roof 宀 fits an older idea of living away from home.

column3: As a verb, to put in time, money or effort: 投入时间, 投入资金, 投入使用 (put into service). As an adjective, fully absorbed: 工作很投入, 演得很投入. A noun too: an investment.
column6: Tā zuòshì zǒngshì fēicháng tóurù.
column7: He is always fully absorbed in what he does.
column9: As a verb, to put in time, money or effort: 投入時間, 投入資金, 投入使用 (put into service). As an adjective, fully absorbed: 工作很投入, 演得很投入. A noun too: an investment.

column3: Two everyday senses: to go back (回归, 归来, 归还 to give back) and to belong to or be someone's responsibility: 这些书归你, 这件事归我管. The second is common in speech.
column6: Zhèxiē shū yǐhòu dōu guī nǐ le.
column7: From now on these books are all yours.
column9: Two everyday senses: to go back (回歸, 歸來, 歸還 to give back) and to belong to or be someone's responsibility: 這些書歸你, 這件事歸我管. The second is common in speech.

column3: The object is a goal or ideal: 追求梦想, 追求幸福, 追求完美, 追求真理. Positive and a bit formal. With a person as the object it means to court them: 他在追求她.
column4: 他一直在追求自己的梦想。
column5: 他一直在追求自己的夢想。
column6: Tā yīzhí zài zhuīqiú zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
column7: He has always been pursuing his own dream.
column9: The object is a goal or ideal: 追求夢想, 追求幸福, 追求完美, 追求真理. Positive and a bit formal. With a person as the object it means to court them: 他在追求她.

column3: More formal than 找 and suggests a longer search, often for something abstract or lost: 寻找答案, 寻找机会, 寻找失踪的人. For keys or a phone, say 找.
column4: 我们正在寻找新的办法。
column5: 我們正在尋找新的辦法。
column6: Wǒmen zhèngzài xúnzhǎo xīn de bànfǎ.
column7: We are looking for a new way.
column9: More formal than 找 and suggests a longer search, often for something abstract or lost: 尋找答案, 尋找機會, 尋找失蹤的人. For keys or a phone, say 找.

column3: Sends something toward a target or into a slot: 投票 vote, 投篮 shoot a basket, 投币 insert a coin, 投资 invest, 投诉 complain. For tossing something away, the everyday word is 扔.
column6: Wǒ tóu le tā yī piào.
column7: I cast a vote for him.
column9: Sends something toward a target or into a slot: 投票 vote, 投籃 shoot a basket, 投幣 insert a coin, 投資 invest, 投訴 complain. For tossing something away, the everyday word is 扔.

column3: Praises people and their work: 优秀学生, 成绩优秀, 优秀作品. Stronger than 好, and common in awards, evaluations and school grades, where it ranks above 良好.
column4: 她是班里最优秀的学生。
column5: 她是班裡最優秀的學生。
column6: Tā shì bān lǐ zuì yōuxiù de xuésheng.
column7: She is the best student in the class.
column9: Praises people and their work: 優秀學生, 成績優秀, 優秀作品. Stronger than 好, and common in awards, evaluations and school grades, where it ranks above 良好.

column3: Written and formal; praises lasting qualities such as a tradition, a variety or a record: 优良传统, 品质优良, 优良品种. For a person the usual word is 优秀.
column6: Zhōngguó yǒu hěn duō yōuliáng chuántǒng.
column7: China has many fine traditions.
column9: Written and formal; praises lasting qualities such as a tradition, a variety or a record: 優良傳統, 品質優良, 優良品種. For a person the usual word is 優秀.

column3: A formal adjective for conditions and habits: 良好的习惯, 关系良好, 状态良好, 良好的态度. As a school grade it sits just below 优秀.
column4: 他从小养成了良好的习惯。
column5: 他從小養成了良好的習慣。
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo yǎngchéng le liánghǎo de xíguàn.
column7: He developed good habits from childhood.
column9: A formal adjective for conditions and habits: 良好的習慣, 關係良好, 狀態良好, 良好的態度. As a school grade it sits just below 優秀.

column3: A gentle, refined beauty that you see or hear: 风景优美, 优美的音乐, 动作优美, 优美的文字. Not for a pretty face (that is 漂亮 or 好看), but fine for a person's figure, posture or movement: 舞姿优美.
column4: 这里风景优美，空气新鲜。
column5: 這裡風景優美，空氣新鮮。
column6: Zhèlǐ fēngjǐng yōuměi, kōngqì xīnxiān.
column7: The scenery here is beautiful and the air is fresh.
column9: A gentle, refined beauty that you see or hear: 風景優美, 優美的音樂, 動作優美, 優美的文字. Not for a pretty face (that is 漂亮 or 好看), but fine for a person's figure, posture or movement: 舞姿優美.

column3: Stands out among others, beyond just good: 表现出色, 非常出色, and with 地 before a verb, 出色地完成. Said of work, performance and people. 出 shows a foot stepping out of a cave.
column4: 他出色地完成了这个任务。
column5: 他出色地完成了這個任務。
column6: Tā chūsè de wánchéng le zhège rènwu.
column7: He did an outstanding job on this task.
column9: Stands out among others, beyond just good: 表現出色, 非常出色, and with 地 before a verb, 出色地完成. Said of work, performance and people. 出 shows a foot stepping out of a cave.

column3: Says how an event or task ends, with nothing lacking: 圆满成功, 圆满完成, 圆满结束. Mostly for events, meetings and tasks, often in 取得圆满成功.
column6: Huìyì yuánmǎn jiéshù le.
column7: The meeting ended with complete success.
column9: Says how an event or task ends, with nothing lacking: 圓滿成功, 圓滿完成, 圓滿結束. Mostly for events, meetings and tasks, often in 取得圓滿成功.

column3: An adjective and a noun: 典型例子, 典型的北方人, and as a quick comment, 很典型 or 太典型了. It can be praise or criticism, depending on what is typical. 型 has the earth 土 because it was an earthen mold, hence a form or pattern.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge diǎnxíng de lìzi.
column7: This is a typical example.
column9: An adjective and a noun: 典型例子, 典型的北方人, and as a quick comment, 很典型 or 太典型了. It can be praise or criticism, depending on what is typical. 型 has the earth 土 because it was an earthen mold, hence a form or pattern.

column3: Different from the usual, often for a reason, and not praise: 特殊情况, 特殊待遇, 特殊原因. Common in rules and notices (特殊情况除外). Unlike 特别, it is never an adverb.
column4: 这种情况比较特殊，需要特别处理。
column5: 這種情況比較特殊，需要特別處理。
column6: Zhè zhǒng qíngkuàng bǐjiào tèshū, xūyào tèbié chǔlǐ.
column7: This situation is rather special and needs special handling.
column9: Different from the usual, often for a reason, and not praise: 特殊情況, 特殊待遇, 特殊原因. Common in rules and notices (特殊情況除外). Unlike 特別, it is never an adverb.

column3: Praises something as unlike any other, with its own character: 独特的风格, 独特的味道, 独特的魅力. Positive, unlike the neutral 特殊. 特 has the ox 牛 because it seems to have meant a large bull first; "single; unique" may be an extension of that.
column4: 这家店的菜有独特的味道。
column5: 這家店的菜有獨特的味道。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de cài yǒu dútè de wèidào.
column7: The food at this shop has a unique taste.
column9: Praises something as unlike any other, with its own character: 獨特的風格, 獨特的味道, 獨特的魅力. Positive, unlike the neutral 特殊. 特 has the ox 牛 because it seems to have meant a large bull first; "single; unique" may be an extension of that.

column3: Clear and unmistakable, for colors, contrasts, stances and traits: 色彩鲜明, 立场鲜明, 对比鲜明, 个性鲜明. Nothing about it is in doubt.
column4: 这幅画的色彩非常鲜明。
column5: 這幅畫的色彩非常鮮明。
column6: Zhè fú huà de sècǎi fēicháng xiānmíng.
column7: The colors in this painting are very vivid.
column9: Clear and unmistakable, for colors, contrasts, stances and traits: 色彩鮮明, 立場鮮明, 對比鮮明, 個性鮮明. Nothing about it is in doubt.

column3: Formal, for a change or effect that is easy to notice: 显著提高, 效果显著, 显著的变化. It pairs with 提高, 进步 and 增长, and in statistics means "significant".
column4: 他的汉语水平有了显著的提高。
column5: 他的漢語水平有了顯著的提高。
column6: Tā de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng yǒu le xiǎnzhù de tígāo.
column7: His Chinese level has improved markedly.
column9: Formal, for a change or effect that is easy to notice: 顯著提高, 效果顯著, 顯著的變化. It pairs with 提高, 進步 and 增長, and in statistics means "significant".

column3: Before a verb it shows a fondness or habit: 好学, 好动, 好客, 好奇, and 爱好 hobby. Mostly in such compounds; in plain speech "to like" is 喜欢 or 爱.
column6: Tā hào guǎn xiánshì.
column7: He likes to meddle in other people's business.
column9: Before a verb it shows a fondness or habit: 好學, 好動, 好客, 好奇, and 愛好 hobby. Mostly in such compounds; in plain speech "to like" is 喜歡 or 愛.

column3: Before a noun it says nothing else is mixed in: 纯棉, 纯金, 纯水, 纯牛奶 (plain milk), and 纯正 for an accent or taste that is authentic. It also builds 单纯 simple and 纯真 innocent.
column4: 这瓶蜂蜜很纯，没有加糖。
column5: 這瓶蜂蜜很純，沒有加糖。
column6: Zhè píng fēngmì hěn chún, méiyǒu jiā táng.
column7: This honey is pure, with no sugar added.
column9: Before a noun it says nothing else is mixed in: 純棉, 純金, 純水, 純牛奶 (plain milk), and 純正 for an accent or taste that is authentic. It also builds 單純 simple and 純真 innocent.

column3: Light passes through it: 透明玻璃, 透明塑料袋. Figuratively it means open to scrutiny, as in 价格透明 and 信息透明. The 透 also follows verbs for "through": 看透, 想透.
column6: Zhège bēizi shì tòumíng de.
column7: This cup is transparent.
column9: Light passes through it: 透明玻璃, 透明塑料袋. Figuratively it means open to scrutiny, as in 價格透明 and 信息透明. The 透 also follows verbs for "through": 看透, 想透.

column3: A negative word for routines, jobs, colors and a repeated sound: 生活单调, 声音单调, 颜色单调, 太单调了. Its opposite is 丰富, rich and varied.
column4: 每天做同样的事，生活太单调了。
column5: 每天做同樣的事，生活太單調了。
column6: Měitiān zuò tóngyàng de shì, shēnghuó tài dāndiào le.
column7: Doing the same thing every day, life is too monotonous.
column9: A negative word for routines, jobs, colors and a repeated sound: 生活單調, 聲音單調, 顏色單調, 太單調了. Its opposite is 豐富, rich and varied.

column3: Three jobs: strange (奇怪, 怪事), to blame (怪我, 不能怪他), and in speech "rather" before an adjective, warmly: 怪可爱的. 怪不得 means "no wonder".
column6: Zhè bù néng guài tā, shì wǒ de cuò.
column7: You can't blame him, it was my fault.
column9: Three jobs: strange (奇怪, 怪事), to blame (怪我, 不能怪他), and in speech "rather" before an adjective, warmly: 怪可愛的. 怪不得 means "no wonder".

column3: Mostly in compounds (严格, 严重, 严肃, 严厉). After a verb it means shut tight with no gaps: 关严, 盖严. 严父 is a stern father.
column4: 门没有关严，风吹进来了。
column5: 門沒有關嚴，風吹進來了。
column6: Mén méiyǒu guān yán, fēng chuī jìnlái le.
column7: The door wasn't closed tight and the wind blew in.
column9: Mostly in compounds (嚴格, 嚴重, 嚴肅, 嚴厲). After a verb it means shut tight with no gaps: 關嚴, 蓋嚴. 嚴父 is a stern father.

column3: Strict about rules, standards and people: 严格要求, 管理严格, 严格执行. Before a verb it is "strictly": 严格遵守, 严格按照. The opposite is 宽松.
column4: 老师对我们的要求很严格。
column5: 老師對我們的要求很嚴格。
column6: Lǎoshī duì wǒmen de yāoqiú hěn yángé.
column7: The teacher is very strict with us.
column9: Strict about rules, standards and people: 嚴格要求, 管理嚴格, 嚴格執行. Before a verb it is "strictly": 嚴格遵守, 嚴格按照. The opposite is 寬鬆.

column3: Only for bad things such as illness, damage, mistakes or problems: 病情严重, 严重的问题, 严重影响. A person's stern manner is 严肃, not this.
column6: Tā de bìngqíng hěn yánzhòng.
column7: His illness is very serious.
column9: Only for bad things such as illness, damage, mistakes or problems: 病情嚴重, 嚴重的問題, 嚴重影響. A person's stern manner is 嚴肅, not this.

column3: A noun, the secret itself (告诉你一个秘密, 小秘密, 保守秘密), and an adjective: 秘密会议, 秘密地. The same 秘 is in 秘书, a secretary.
column4: 我告诉你一个秘密，你别说出去。
column5: 我告訴你一個秘密，你別說出去。
column6: Wǒ gàosu nǐ yī ge mìmì, nǐ bié shuō chūqù.
column7: I'll tell you a secret, don't tell anyone.
column9: A noun, the secret itself (告訴你一個秘密, 小秘密, 保守秘密), and an adjective: 秘密會議, 秘密地. The same 秘 is in 秘書, a secretary.

column3: An adjective only: something unexplained, with wonder or unease: 神秘的人, 神秘感, 很神秘. Unlike 秘密, it is never the secret itself. 别这么神秘 teases someone for being cagey.
column4: 山里有一个神秘的小村子。
column5: 山裡有一個神秘的小村子。
column6: Shān lǐ yǒu yī ge shénmì de xiǎo cūnzi.
column7: There is a mysterious little village in the mountains.
column9: An adjective only: something unexplained, with wonder or unease: 神秘的人, 神秘感, 很神秘. Unlike 秘密, it is never the secret itself. 別這麼神秘 teases someone for being cagey.

column3: A verb plus object, so it can split (保了密), and degree or scope words go before it: 严格保密, 对外保密 (keep it from outsiders). Typical: 请保密 as a polite request, and 保密协议, a confidentiality agreement. 保 began as a person carrying a child on the back.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì qǐng nǐ yīdìng bǎomì.
column7: Please keep this matter strictly secret.
column9: A verb plus object, so it can split (保了密), and degree or scope words go before it: 嚴格保密, 對外保密 (keep it from outsiders). Typical: 請保密 as a polite request, and 保密協議, a confidentiality agreement. 保 began as a person carrying a child on the back.

column3: Closeness of relations, contact and attention, not of physical distance: 关系密切, 联系密切, 密切合作, 密切关注. For things that are near each other, say 靠近.
column4: 这两个国家的关系非常密切。
column5: 這兩個國家的關係非常密切。
column6: Zhè liǎng ge guójiā de guānxi fēicháng mìqiè.
column7: The relations between these two countries are very close.
column9: Closeness of relations, contact and attention, not of physical distance: 關係密切, 聯繫密切, 密切合作, 密切關注. For things that are near each other, say 靠近.

column3: A person can be independent of parents (独立生活, 他很独立), a country of another (国家独立), and a thing can stand alone: 独立思考, 独立完成. As a verb it takes no object. 立 is a picture of a person standing on the ground.
column4: 他十八岁就开始独立生活了。
column5: 他十八歲就開始獨立生活了。
column6: Tā shíbā suì jiù kāishǐ dúlì shēnghuó le.
column7: He started to live independently at eighteen.
column9: A person can be independent of parents (獨立生活, 他很獨立), a country of another (國家獨立), and a thing can stand alone: 獨立思考, 獨立完成. As a verb it takes no object. 立 is a picture of a person standing on the ground.

column3: On its own: thickly packed. 头发很密, 树林很密. Its opposite is 稀 or 疏. It also appears in words about secrecy and closeness: 密码 password, 秘密, 保密, 密切. The mountain 山 inside it is explained as something hidden in the mountains.
column4: 这片树林很密，很难走进去。
column5: 這片樹林很密，很難走進去。
column6: Zhè piàn shùlín hěn mì, hěn nán zǒu jìnqù.
column7: This wood is dense and hard to walk into.
column9: On its own: thickly packed. 頭髮很密, 樹林很密. Its opposite is 稀 or 疏. It also appears in words about secrecy and closeness: 密碼 password, 秘密, 保密, 密切. The mountain 山 inside it is explained as something hidden in the mountains.

column3: Ties with no gaps, between people, groups or parts: 紧密合作, 联系紧密, 紧密结合. It stresses tightness, while 密切 is the usual word for relations and attention. Written style.
column4: 两个公司的合作越来越紧密。
column5: 兩個公司的合作越來越緊密。
column6: Liǎng ge gōngsī de hézuò yuè lái yuè jǐnmì.
column7: The cooperation between the two companies is getting closer and closer.
column9: Ties with no gaps, between people, groups or parts: 緊密合作, 聯繫緊密, 緊密結合. It stresses tightness, while 密切 is the usual word for relations and attention. Written style.

column3: Officials close off roads, areas and buildings: 封闭道路, 封闭管理, a closed campus where no one comes or goes. Of a person, 思想封闭 means cut off from new ideas. Alone, 封 is also the measure word for letters, as in 一封信.
column4: 因为下雪，高速公路被封闭了。
column5: 因為下雪，高速公路被封閉了。
column6: Yīnwèi xià xuě, gāosùgōnglù bèi fēngbì le.
column7: The expressway was closed because of snow.
column9: Officials close off roads, areas and buildings: 封閉道路, 封閉管理, a closed campus where no one comes or goes. Of a person, 思想封閉 means cut off from new ideas. Alone, 封 is also the measure word for letters, as in 一封信.

column3: As an adjective, cautious and not open to change: 思想保守, 比较保守, 保守的人. Mild criticism, but neutral in politics and in 保守估计, "a conservative estimate". As a verb it mostly goes with 秘密.
column4: 我爷爷的想法比较保守。
column5: 我爺爺的想法比較保守。
column6: Wǒ yéye de xiǎngfǎ bǐjiào bǎoshǒu.
column7: My grandfather's ideas are rather conservative.
column9: As an adjective, cautious and not open to change: 思想保守, 比較保守, 保守的人. Mild criticism, but neutral in politics and in 保守估計, "a conservative estimate". As a verb it mostly goes with 秘密.

column3: To be particular about something: 讲究卫生, 讲究礼貌, 吃得很讲究, 穿着讲究. As a noun, 有讲究 means there is a rule or reason behind it, common for food and customs.
column4: 她吃饭很讲究，只吃新鲜的菜。
column5: 她吃飯很講究，只吃新鮮的菜。
column6: Tā chīfàn hěn jiǎngjiu, zhǐ chī xīnxiān de cài.
column7: She is particular about her food and eats only fresh dishes.
column9: To be particular about something: 講究衛生, 講究禮貌, 吃得很講究, 穿著講究. As a noun, 有講究 means there is a rule or reason behind it, common for food and customs.
